schedule.desc: Considering that you are all stars, meet at the hotel lobby for a leisurely 45-minute stroll around the venue. Get some fresh air, exercise, and chat with authors, editors, and artists in an informal setting. Hear about the interesting, fun, and maybe even unbelievable features of Anaheim.
schedule.title: Stroll with the Stars

schedule.desc: Join us for the official announcement of the 2026 Nommo Awards Shortlist, celebrating the best in African speculative fiction. The Nommo Awards, presented by the African Speculative Fiction Society (ASFS), honour outstanding works of speculative fiction by African writers across the continent and diaspora.
schedule.title: Nommo Awards 2026: Celebrating African Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: From the page to the screen, queer characters are driving some of our most beloved stories. Enjoy celebrating the characters, relationships, and narratives that are bringing us joy and elevating queer experiences across books and media.
schedule.title: More Than Subtext: Celebrating Queer Characters in SF/F (Virtual)

schedule.desc: How can STEM and storytelling enrich each other, and how do we build futures grounded in African science, lived experience, and cultural knowledge? This practice-based workshop explores how to use science as raw material for fiction: not to limit imagination, but to expand it. Participants will create characters, build speculative worlds, and develop frameworks for original stories that link science and storytelling. Themes include AI, climate, marine life, fisheries, water, pollution, food, currency, smart cities, and health and care. The workshop draws on the Applied African SF Toolkit, which provides guided activities, sample texts, and discussion frameworks to help users think differently about research, technology, and the futures we're shaping. No-one is expected to be a scientist or a novelist: all you need is curiosity and imagination. By the end of this session, each participant will understand how science can enrich creative ideas; know how to blend cultural knowledge with scientific logic; and have the beginnings of a speculative world or story to build on.
schedule.title: Creative Worldbuilding: A Workshop from Applied African SF

schedule.desc: Beatrice Erkers is Program Director of Existential Hope at Foresight Institute, where she works on building vivid, positive visions of the future through worldbuilding, film, and events. Come chat about what it takes to imagine AI going right, how storytelling and worldbuilding can shape technological futures, or the challenges of building optimism into serious AI discourse.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Beatrice Erkers

schedule.desc: Ada Palmer, historian, novelist, author of Terra Ignota and the forthcoming Norse Myth duology Hanged God's Game, Best Related Work Hugo finalist this year for Inventing the Renaissance: Myths of a Golden Age. Recently published an essay collection co-authored with Jo Walton: Trace Elements: Conversations on the Project of Science Fiction and Fantasy. Scholar of the Renaissance, Enlightenment, radical thought and censorship. Podcaster (Ex Urbe Ad Astra), educational LARP designer, filker (Sassafrass, Norse Myth music), costumer, anime/manga expert (Osamu Tezuka, shoujo, post-war manga).
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Ada Palmer

schedule.desc: The Suburban Hellscape of Technology: Writing Horror at Home. Tiffani Angus, co-author of the multi-award-shortlisted Spec Fic for Newbies series, will take you on a journey into the development of the subgenres of suburban horror and techno horror and look at how they evolved side by side and even overlap. The workshop will culminate in an activity that’ll get you started creating a whole new horror story.
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: Writing Horror at Home

schedule.desc: African graphic storytelling is flourishing but creators often work in isolation across countries and platforms. Borderless is a new initiative of the African Speculative Fiction Society (ASFS) to connect these energies and create a collaborative ecosystem for African graphic novel creators. Building on conversations from Worldcon 2025, this panel brings together writers, illustrators, editors, and publishers in the area of African graphic novels.
schedule.title: Borderless: Building an Ecosystem for African Graphic Novels

schedule.desc: Join us for an interview with Dilman Dila. He is a Ugandan writer, film maker and social activist and was nominated for the Philip K. Dick Award in 2024.
schedule.title: An Entire World in a Screen: Dilman Dila (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Understandings of what justice is, what it means, and how to systematize it, varies across cultures past and present. From anarchistic to restorative, collective to corportate, there have been a wide variety of justice systems portrayed throughout science fiction books and media. This panel explores justice systems in science fiction and fantasy that may be very different from the ones we see in societies today.
schedule.title: Justice Systems in SFF (Virtual)

schedule.desc: See some of the best films shown at the Seattle 2025 Worldcon Film Festival, here in Anaheim!
schedule.title: Best of Seattle Worldcon Film Festival

schedule.desc: Brittany Otto is a paper artist known for combining hand cut layered paper and light into shadow box sculptures that she calls Oneiroframes. From farm life in New Hamphire as a child and now in Seattle, she explored a variety of artistic media through intense cosplay costumes before finding her passion for paper sculpture. Creative, a gamer, and nerdy to the bone, come on by to chat with her about all kinds of things from art to fairy tales and beyond!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Brittany Otto

schedule.desc: Is cannibalism the oldest taboo? It's fascinating, that’s for sure, from the refined palate of Hannibal Lecter to its use as the ultimate othering. Whether it’s being deployed as an ugly cliché of man-eating rednecks and hungry jungle natives, or used in films like Society, cannibalism has thrilled audiences for hundreds of years. Horror has always been on the menu.
schedule.title: Cannibalism Can Be Fun: In Literature

schedule.desc: Over the years we learned that some of the “big names” in science fiction and fantasy were, and are, behaving in a very unethical way. Their works, however, may be important to us. Is it possible to separate the art from the artist? Should we try doing so, and if yes how can we achieve it? And last, but not least: how can we ethically enjoy such pieces of art?
schedule.title: Can We Enjoy the Art of Unethical People? (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Following in the tradition of L.A.con III and L.A.con IV, we will discuss how Worldcon has changed since the previous L.A. Worldcon. How did the bidding and conrunning processes change? Are the membership demographics the same or different? Let's look to the past and the future of Worldcon and try to predict how it will develop.
schedule.title: 20 Years of Worldcon Organizing

schedule.desc: The film Contagion (2011) provided an eerily prescient vision of the COVID-19 pandemic. Let’s look at the portrayal of pandemics in television and film, which have loved a good medical thriller for decades now. Which ones do we look back on now and think accurate versus the ones that seem much more science fictional? Is the difference in the portrayal of the medical condition or in the way that society responds?
schedule.title: Contagion and COVID

schedule.desc: The central ambiguity of George RR Martin’s Tales of Dunk and Egg is routinely overlooked: there is no reliable evidence that Ser Arlan of Pennytree ever knighted Duncan. Dunk claims the title, performs the role, and is accepted. This paper reads that ambiguity as the organizing problem of the series. What does it mean that the most honorable knight in Westeros was never knighted at all?
schedule.title: Fraud and Knightly Identity in Dunk and Egg

schedule.desc: Adapting science fiction and fantasy novels to the stage is a vastly different process than adapting to film. We have seen fannish and professional adaptations, such as the recent examples of Dune: The Musical at Glasgow 2024 and the National Theatre’s Frankenstein. What are the challenges inherent in adapting science fiction and fantasy to the stage? What characteristics lead to a better chance of success?
schedule.title: Adapting SFF for the Stage

schedule.desc: Fairies. The Sidhe. The Little People. The Kindly Ones. Fairy tales and folklore have long been a powerful influence on the fantasy genre, but how do you go about writing fey creatures in such a way that they feel like the stories you loved as a child? Where do you source your inspiration? How do you create something new that feels like something old? And most importantly, how do you avoid giving offence to the oft-capricious Lord and Ladies?
schedule.title: Writing the Fey

schedule.desc: The concept of a found family often emerges in the conversations about the first steps in fandom. It may be phrased differently including wording such as “my people”, but the meaning stays similar; many of us just "click" when meeting the fandom. We will take a look at that idea and we’ll try to answer questions as to whether fandom is really a found family and how this perception differs between the fans.
schedule.title: Fandom as a Found Family

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss how classical music has influenced SFF or been used effectively in speculative fiction. This topic will also cover extrapolations of where “classical” music might go in the future, and definitions of classical music versus other forms of music.
schedule.title: Classical Music and SFF

schedule.desc: Be dazzled by the variety of massive murals, paintings, props, sets, and sculptures created for films, television, theater, and theme parks by two top scenic artists from the Art Directors' Guild. Bridget Duffy and Cathy Koon will present artwork which they created by painting “Godzilla Style” (i.e., really big!) This will be followed by the Large Scale Mural and Backdrop Painting workshop on Saturday.
schedule.title: Monumental Art in Hollywood

schedule.desc: Non-Sherlock Holmes mysteries set in historical time periods are always a crowd favorite. Come listen to authors who love this genre talk about the benefits and restrictions of the form and find some new favorites along the way.
schedule.title: Sleuthing Through History
New and Indie Autographing: Makana Yamamoto

schedule.desc: Brooks Peck is a pop culture museum curator and writer, specializing in all things nerdy especially SFF, video games, and comics. He's currently very focused on vampires. Want to talk vampires? Come and let's discuss our favorite vampire works, favorite vampires, and favorite vampire hunters. Undoubtedly The Lost Boys is the greatest vampire movie ever made--fight me!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Brooks Peck

schedule.desc: Join Tim, Colleen, and Stan as they sit down together for an engaging, free-flowing conversation, sharing stories, influences, and creative journeys.
schedule.title: In Conversation - Colleen Doran, Tim Kirk, and Stan Sakai

schedule.desc: Tactics may win battles, but logistics wins wars. Yet so much of military science fiction is focused mostly on the front lines. This panel will discuss the nuts and bolts of getting supplies to the front lines. What are the challenges faced when you need to get self-sealing stem bolts out to the Delta Quadrant?
schedule.title: The Logistics of Galactic War

schedule.desc: Denise Gendron is a cheerful singer/songwriter/bassist/music teacher from Massachusetts who loves to write and perform filk songs of joy and inspiration. Audience participation is both welcome and encouraged!
schedule.title: Concert: Denise Gendron

schedule.desc: Congress’ withdrawal of funding for NASA’s Mars Sample Return may have you feeling blue about the future of Mars exploration. However, there are still multiple hardworking spacecraft at the Red Planet. In addition, several countries have missions under development. This panel of space scientists and engineers will talk about the ongoing work at Mars and what they dream we might discover next.
schedule.title: What’s Next for the Exploration of Mars?
New and Indie Autographing: Justin C. Key

schedule.desc: It's the most purrrrrrfect meetup to start the con! Come meet other people who love their cats and kittens. Show off pictures of your fur babies. Trade stories about your adorable fuzzy murder machines, er, companions. (Please do not bring your actual cats or kittens. Pictures, tattoos, or paintings are all cool.)
schedule.title: Meetup: Fans of Cats and Kittens

schedule.desc: Two decades ago, Aang caught the imagination of teens and young adults around the world. Its influence is still being felt today. Come hear about how the show captures our attention from the found family/chosen one dynamic to the adorable animals you can't help but love. (This panel is for teens)
schedule.title: Then the Fire Nation Attacked: Avatar the Last Airbender

schedule.desc: Panels are often the backbone of convention’s program. To have a successful panel one needs to have great panellists, but it is equally important to find a moderator who would take care of the panel to run smoothly and be interesting. It is not only about asking questions, but also about making sure everyone have the chance to speak, and catch threads that may appear in the responses, and are worth pursuing. But how to do that well?
schedule.title: How to Moderate a Panel

schedule.desc: Los Angeles in the 1930s and 1940s wasn't just a hub of fandom, it was a magnet for prominent SF professionals whose work helped define the Golden Age. This program focuses on Robert A. Heinlein, whose move to LA immersed him in local fandom and war-era research culture, and the meetings of his Manana Literary Society. It will also highlight the editors, illustrators, and pulp authors who made SoCal a pressure point for modern SF.
schedule.title: Heinlein and the Professionals of Early LA Science Fiction

schedule.desc: In recent years, manga and graphic novels have surged in popularity among middle grade and young adult readers, captivating them with their dynamic storytelling and visual appeal. This panel brings together authors and educators to explore the factors driving this boom. Panelists will examine current trends shaping the genre and discuss how these illustrated narratives differ from traditional prose.
schedule.title: The Rise of the Middle Reader/YA Graphic Novel

schedule.desc: Looking back 50 years: which SFF films have stood the test of time ,and which ones now cause us to cringe?
schedule.title: The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly of 1976 Movies

schedule.desc: Cristián Londoño Proaño is an Ecuadorian novelist, editor of the SF magazine Omicron Theory, and creator of the Andean fantasy subgenre. Come chat about Ecuadorian science fiction — its history, its wild diversity, and the authors and books you’ve probably never heard of but should. Andean myth meets biotech, volcanoes, and speculative futures! This table talk will be held in Spanish. ¡Curiosos y colegas, bienvenidos!
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Cristián Londoño-Proaño

schedule.desc: Eris Young is a transgender writer of speculative fiction. Their debut lesbian horror novel Hunger in the Blood is publishing in 2027. Their stories have appeared in StarShipSofa, Extra and other publications. They are fiction editor at Shoreline of Infinity Science Fiction Magazine. Chat about what queer speculative fiction really means and writing from a marginalized perspective. Bonus points for fungus, food in fiction, and Byzantine eunuchs.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Eris Young

schedule.desc: Craig Miller, Lucasfilm's original Director of Fan Relations, gives a slide show on the early days of Lucasfilm and marketing Star Wars and The Empire Strikes Back to fandom and the rest of the world. Stories may include Lucas's original explanation for the Falcon's 12 parsec Kessel Run, picking Leigh Brackett to write Empire, the wrap party Carrie Fisher threw, Underwear That’s Fun To Wear, taking Droids to Sesame Street, and more.
schedule.title: Star Wars Memories

schedule.desc: Vinyl records, DVDs, paper zines, and other forms of physical media are growing in popularity, even with digital natives. What will be the next thing to be revived? What does this mean for fandom and other communities in a world where we assume everyone gets information through online channels?
schedule.title: The Rediscovery of Physical Media

schedule.desc: Let’s talk audiobooks! What does it take to create one as an independent author. Gabrielle is a veteran audiobook director, publisher and narrator. Let’s examine the myriad production options, casting and costs. If you are a fan, voice talk your likes and dislikes, and maybe hear a few “insider” stories. If your interests lie in story podcasts, we can chat about It’s Storytime with Will Wheaton, which she produces. If time runs short, we can continue our chat at Skyboat’s table in the Dealers’ Room!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Gabrielle de Cuir

schedule.desc: From the grim reaper to a dark angel, death is featured in many fantasy novels. What are the similarities and differences of these personifications? And what media does it well?
schedule.title: Personifications of Death

schedule.desc: Create yourself some elf ears, a funny nose, or a lovely tail
schedule.title: Noses, Ears, and Tails! Oh My!

schedule.desc: Fannish Hugo Award categories are as old as the Award itself. Over the years their number and scope have changed, and currently we are voting on four fannish statuettes: Best Fanzine, Best Fancast, Best Fan Writer, and Best Fan Artist. What is the meaning and importance of those categories for both the winners and fandom as a whole? Why do we need them? Let’s discuss the importance of Hugo Awards for fans.
schedule.title: The Fan Hugo Categories

schedule.desc: Join us for a stroll through the garden of poisons to learn about toxic, intoxicating and narcotic plants and their historic uses. How do these toxins help plants survive? What effects do they have on the human body? And what should you do if you find yourself on the wrong side of a poisoning?
schedule.title: Poisonous Plants: When “Natural” is not very good for you

schedule.desc: E.G. Condé, author of the Ignyte-nominated novella, Sordidez, reads from the next installment of his pioneering Taínofuturism series, Caciques (Stelliform Press). Set in near-future Puerto Rico, Caciques (2027) imagines indigenous heroes at the height of their power as they contend with ghosts from their colonial past.
schedule.title: Reading: E.G. Condé

schedule.desc: You’ve workshopped your writing and received constructive feedback. Are you ready to revise? Do the critiques fit with your vision? Do you know how to move forward? The facilitator will offer advice for speeding up the revision process and tips for reverse outlining, synopsizing, and annotating as well as opening discussion for attendees to share their tips for getting to that final draft.
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: What Happens After the Workshop? The Path to Revision

schedule.desc: There is some new research and discussion about this very old topic. Robert Sapolsky’s Determined and Daniel Dennett’s I’ve Been Thinking look at the topic from different directions. Can we really make our own decisions? What does it even mean to have or not have free will?
schedule.title: Free Will: Well? Do We Have Free Will or Not?
New and Indie Autographing: Henry Lien

schedule.desc: A demonstration and lesson on balloon sculpting for kids. We will also make balloon animals via request for the Camp Fuzzy members! (Allergy warning: balloons contain latex.)
schedule.title: Balloon Animal Sculpting Workshop (Kids’ Edition)

schedule.desc: Children's Programming Staff Members will take the kids with parents/guardians through the Dealers Room. We might even find a few dealers who are members of the Adventurers Club and have stops for the kids to collect stamps for their Adventurers Club Passports and possibly a cool item.
schedule.title: Kids' Tour the Dealers Room

schedule.desc: Bring out your inner Trekkie with this networked computer game experience! 6–8 players take control of the spaceship Artemis, assuming various crew jobs: Helm, Weapons, Science, Communications, Engineering, Fighter Pilot(s), and Captain. The ship’s missions require the crew to work together to overcome challenges such as combat, puzzle-solving, diplomacy, and exploration. An educational (space science) teambuilding experience!
schedule.title: Artemis Space Bridge Simulator (Thursday)

schedule.desc: Christopher Caldwell reads a selection from his Ursula K. Le Guin Prize for Fiction nominated, William L. Crawford Award winning collection of short stories, Call and Response: Stories of the Fantastic
schedule.title: Reading: Christopher Caldwell

schedule.desc: Stories about the end of the world have always captured our imagination. But how do you go about designing your own? Using my latest novel Ash Land as an example, I’ll go through the step-by-step process I used to create my own dystopia. I’ll discuss how to come up with an idea, how to refine your concept through research, and the ten pillars needed to build any fictional world.
schedule.title: Designing a Dystopia Using Real Science

schedule.desc: Caitlin Rozakis, New York Times bestselling author of Dreadful and The Grimoire Grammar School Parent Teacher Association, reads from her latest contemporary fantasy/office comedy Startup Hell.
schedule.title: Reading: Caitlin Rozakis

schedule.desc: Merav Hoffman wears a lot of hats, including singer, songwriter, filk archivist, and President of Interfilk. In 2021 Merav was inducted into the Filk Hall of Fame. She’s also a founding member of the bands Lady Mondegreen, The Funny Things, Goldberry, and The Goat Rodeo. Merav sings her own songs and those by friends. You can stay up to date with her work at https://www.ladymondegreen.com/merav.
schedule.title: Concert: Merav Hoffman

schedule.desc: On Our Skin (Nigeria), The Herbal Witch (Switzerland), The Parking Ticket Fairy (USA), The Planet That Doesn't Exist (Israel), The Roots Within (UK), The Screenwriter (Italy), Work from Home (Netherlands), ΠΙΕΣ (Germany, Greece)
schedule.title: Fantasy Films from Around the World

schedule.desc: Shay Kauwe writes speculative fiction through the lens of the Pacific. Her books include The Killing Spell and the forthcoming House of Salt. Drop in to chat land and water rights, working with “the big 5,” Hawaiian mythology, diverse SFFH, the evil of pineapples, worldbuilding and magic systems, language learning, ghost stories, and her hot take that Westerns and Gothics are kissing cousins.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Shay Kauwe

schedule.desc: A meetup for gender diverse creators to be in community. Discuss topics, and address challenges faced specifically by gender diverse creators of all mediums.
schedule.title: Meetup: Gender Diverse Creators for Gender Diverse Creators

schedule.desc: It can be hard when your brain gives you TOO MANY cool ideas. Writing advice often suggests outlining, but ND brains can be rule-resistant and still have a hard time squeezing things down to something plot-shaped. Instead, let's make it fun! We'll run through some methods and exercises to help yoke your creative drive, including visual mind mapping, decision making with random chance and rubber ducks, and much more
schedule.title: Outlining Stories While ADHD

schedule.desc: Before writing existed, we spoke our truths. How has oral storytelling influenced the written word, and how has the resurgence of oral storytelling and bards impacted the way we are recording history?
schedule.title: A Long Time Ago: Oral Traditions (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Dustin Adair, an Emmy-nominated character animator with a quarter century’s experience of animating some of the most high-profile Sci-Fi characters in television, film and videogames, presents a retrospective lecture. It will include a behind-the-scenes view of his work animating Cylons, Terminators, Transformers and many, many more. There will also be a discussion of the future of the VFX industry and the inclusion of AI.
schedule.title: 25 Years of Animating Sci-Fi Characters

schedule.desc: Before writing existed, we spoke our truths. How has oral storytelling influenced the written word, and how has the resurgence of oral storytelling and bards impacted the way we are recording history?
schedule.title: A Long Time Ago: Oral Traditions

schedule.desc: Want to take your adventuring to the next level? Explore how to write and build a Live-Action Role Playing game for you and your friends! (This workshop is for teens)
schedule.title: Gather Your Party: Teen LARP Writing Workshop

schedule.desc: Conventions are exciting, chaotic, and sometimes… a bit much. For the more introverted guests, navigating the crowds and constant activity can take some strategy. Listen to con-goers share the tricks and survival tactics they’ve developed to help introverts not just get through conventions, but have a great time doing it.
schedule.title: An Introvert’s Guide to Surviving Conventions (Virtual)

schedule.desc: A century after Amazing Stories debuted in April 1926, its impact on science fiction and fandom remains profound. More than a magazine, it built a community, connecting readers through letters, inspiring clubs and fanzines, and helping create organized fandom. This panel explores how it shaped fan identity and laid the groundwork for the participatory culture that defines SF today.
schedule.title: 100 Years Later: The Impact of Amazing Stories Magazine

schedule.desc: Science fiction has seemed to be dying for nearly as long as it has existed. Briefly examining the grounds and history of the phenomena—including laments and complaints within genre communities, material changes in publishing patterns, and academic & critical works I argue that the constant apparent death of SF is tied up with its relation to time and possibility.
schedule.title: Time and Ongoing Death of Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Satellites, doorbells, smart glasses, smart phones, and maybe even your smart TV can all watch you. Who can see what, and what is it being used for? How transparent is that data? On the flip side, citizens are using cell phones to record people abusing power. Can we protect that right in the wake of Federal pushback? How can we use modern technology to continue holding powerful people accountable?
schedule.title: Surveillance Tech: Who Can Watch You? Who Can You Watch?

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss the pleasures and perils of co-writing. Do you both work up a contract first? Do you get an agent to represent both? What is your method of writing together, and how do you resolve the inevitable clashes when two creative minds are passionate about their way of doing things? Each panelist has published at least one co-written work.
schedule.title: Collaborative Writing

schedule.desc: Time to rally the Pokemon Go! players - make friends in game with other players from around the world and get reaquainted with players you have met at previous Worldcons. We can also touch base about any in game events happening over the weekend. We will meet in the lobby and then head out together to explore the area.
schedule.title: Meetup: Pokemon Go! (Thursday)

schedule.desc: Meet several 2026 debut authors, indie and traditional, who talk about getting their first project into print.
schedule.title: Meet Debut Authors of 2026! 1st Edition

schedule.desc: In the rapidly evolving landscape of space science and exploration, defining ethical norms is of acute concern. How will we protect other worlds against contamination and exploitation for resources? How do we ensure all voices are heard and a vision of global cooperation and benefit is made reality? Come consider how scientists and writers can partner to manifest an ethical approach to exploring space.
schedule.title: Ethics of Space Research and Exploration

schedule.desc: Techbros (and many readers) have forgotten the essential core of cyberpunk: rebellion and defiance. How do we write cyberpunk when we are living in it? What does it have to say about our techno-dystopian present?
schedule.title: The Punk in Cyberpunk

schedule.desc: Local conventions struggle with many issues including graying of fandom, lack of resources, and difficulty attracting new fans. Yet, some cons and local groups thrive. How do they do it? Is there a secret we can all learn? Let’s discuss what solutions different groups applied and which of them worked and why.
schedule.title: Achieving Local Convention Success

schedule.desc: Children's Programming Staff Members will take the kids with parents/guardians through the Exhibits Hall. We might even find a few Specific Exhibits to stop to collect stamps for their Adventurers Club Passports.
schedule.title: Kids' Tour the Exhibits Hall

schedule.desc: Neil Clarke is the editor of Clarkesworld Magazine, Forever Magazine, and several anthologies, including The Best Science Fiction of the Year series. He is also a 2026 Hugo Award finalist for Best Editor Short Form. Join him for a chat about short fiction, art, publishing, and whatever else you (and the others) want to ask him about. The conversation goes where you lead it... within reason.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Neil Clarke

schedule.desc: Michael Solis is the author of the Deficient series, founder of Mintaka Press, and Executive Director of the nearly 50-year-old literary nonprofit Writers & Books in Rochester, NY. A former humanitarian worker who spent many years living across Africa and Latin America, he loves chatting about queer speculative stories, worldbuilding, superpowers, the journey from small press to indie publishing, audiobook narration, nonprofit leadership, and anything else you'd like to discuss!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Michael Solis

schedule.desc: Henry Lien reads a true story about two judgy cousins and the literal end of the world from his acclaimed writing craft book Spring, Summer, Asteroid, Bird: The Art of Eastern Storytelling.
schedule.title: Reading: Henry Lien

schedule.desc: Scientists discuss games that riff on actual science, such as Wingspan, Turing Machine, SETI, Search for Planet X and Leaving Earth.
schedule.title: Depictions of Science in Board Games

schedule.desc: Masquerades, or costuming competitions, have a long history at Worldcon. Whether you're entering for the first time or just planning to sit in the audience, our panel will share a little masquerade history, explain how judging works, and tell tales of their own masquerade entries. What is the ICG? What are skill divisions? Can anyone enter? Come find out!
schedule.title: My First Masquerade

schedule.desc: In science fiction, the future often comes with miracle cures that “solve” disabilities such as blindness, deafness, limb difference and other illnesses. Is a world without disability really a utopia? Panelists will dive into questions about humanity, prioritized normalcy, and identity, and will explore how stories of the future can include disabled people as vital parts of the world, not something to erase.
schedule.title: Accessing Futures: Disability, Transhumanism, and Utopias

schedule.desc: Andrew Rubin, author of Hell or High Winter (Rare Bird Books / Simon & Schuster), reads from his contemporary fantasy reimagining of the Greek god Hermes, answering the age-old question: What's a Messenger of the Gods supposed to do in the age of email?
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Andrew Rubin

schedule.desc: One Thousand and One Nights is one of the most influential speculative fiction stories with a global impact. How has this story shaped other stories? What's new in Middle Eastern speculative fiction now that it's 1001 years later?
schedule.title: 1001 Years Later

schedule.desc: What if the worlds you imagine could exist? In this interactive workshop, participants will create bold future scenarios, identify the barriers that stand in the way, and design breakthrough ideas to overcome them. Using the XPRIZE model, you’ll explore how visionary ideas can take shape in the real world.
schedule.title: Inventing the Future: Designing Moonshots

schedule.desc: Marketing for an author can take many forms. In this panel, we will explore opportunities to market yourself and your books through social media platforms. These include text and multi-media platforms, such as Instagram, X, YouTube, TikTok, Reddit, and more. In addition, we'll discuss building community through Discord, reviewing books, blogger groups, review sites, and indie contests.
schedule.title: Marketing your Indie Book through Social Media and Community Building

schedule.desc: The world feels heavy, the future uncertain. But it is not time to accept the inevitable. It’s time to light the fires, build our own suns and rewrite our future. Are cli-fi, hopepunk, and solarpunk the answer? It can be hard to build a better future if we dont know how to picture it. Let’s take a look at the world through the lens of science fiction genres that are letting their hope shine through in their work.
schedule.title: Climate Future Fiction, Hopepunk, and Solarpunk

schedule.desc: Terese Mason Pierre is an award-winning writer, poet, and editor. Join her for a discussion on everything from editing at a magazine, doing an MFA, and applying for grants (in Canada), to attending residencies, teaching creative writing and balancing writing with life.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Terese Mason Pierre

schedule.desc: Descriptors such as pale and bloodless have often led audiences to perceive the vampire as white by default. Productions like Sinners join a rich written tradition of disregarding this rendition. We will explore the portrayal of the immortal vampire, the considerations behind these creative choices, and how broadening who is imagined, or condemned, as a vampire introduces dynamic narratives around this enduring icon of fear and desire.
schedule.title: Faces of the Vampire: Blood and Power

schedule.desc: The fictional substance adamantium is best known as the material in Wolverine’s skeleton, Ultron’s shell, and X-23’s claws. But as physicist and exotic materials expert Sara Callori (California State University, San Bernardino) will describe, superstrong materials like adamantium have a long history going back to ancient folklore and are the subject of research by modern-day scientists. Come to have your mind expanded (but not your skeleton replaced)!
schedule.title: Adamantium: From Myth to Material

schedule.desc: Come and make a game! We’ll provide the materials if you provide the ideas. You can bring your game to the playtesting workshop later in the con, and completed concepts could be published in the con newsletter or Discord!
schedule.title: Tabletop Game Design Jam

schedule.desc: Children can be creative! Come build a sock monster, sock zombies, or anything else from socks, cotton balls, and other materials. Children may need help from a parent or guardian with sewing.
schedule.title: Build Your Own Monster

schedule.desc: From climate change to mass incarceration, democratic collapse to rising authoritarianism, and other dystopian worries, things feel more dire than ever before. How do we continue to find hope? How do we continue to write stories full of wonder or that can speak to our present when feeling crushed by the weight of the world? Our panelists talk about the importance of hope, finding it when things seem rough, and writing through difficult times.
schedule.title: Writing a Way Out of This Mess

schedule.desc: Alien's tag line was "In space, no one can hear you scream." There's been a recent revival of the space horror subgenre in publishing, and it's right on time. Can we have more gothic spaces in space? What about the bright and colorful body horror of Scavengers Reign? Let's stop debating whether Alien is sci fi or horror. It's clearly both, and we love it!
schedule.title: Horror in Space

schedule.desc: How did Babylon 5’s five-year arc, planned narrative threads, and season-long storytelling anticipate modern prestige television patterns?
schedule.title: Babylon 5’s Revolution: Serialized Storytelling Before Peak TV

schedule.desc: John Picacio is nominated for two Hugo Awards this year -- Best Professional Artist and Best Graphic Story (for The Invisible Parade with Leigh Bardugo). Everyone who attends scores a signed promo card for The Invisible Parade. Come ask how The Invisible Parade was created, and how cover art is made. Ask about Picacio works past and future, and about forthcoming Lotería cards. We'll walk to the Art Show in time for the 2pm Opening.
schedule.title: Table Talk: John Picacio

schedule.desc: Alasdair Stuart, professional enthusiast and occasional supernatural menace, reads from frequent fanzine finalist The Full Lid and may have a surprise for fans of The Magnus Archives...
schedule.title: Reading: Alasdair Stuart

schedule.desc: Wole Talabi, Hugo, Nebula and Locus award nominated author of Shigidi and the Brass Head of Obalufon reads from his new first-contact SF thriller The Fist Of Memory - about a Nigerian assassin, a South African astronomer and a strange alien object heading towards Earth. Part John Wick meets Arrival by way of The Three Body Problem, it’s also a story of balance, redemption, interconnectedness & the ways in which memory shapes us.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Wole Talabi

schedule.desc: Though the tendency is to regard apocalyptic or future noir scenarios as “dystopian,” in most cases they actually provide a degree of freedom and even success for their protagonists. So what makes them “dystopian”? For that matter, they can be viewed as fulfilling a shadowy form of the American Dream. So is dystopia just subjective?
schedule.title: From Mad Max to Cyberpunk: Agency in Hostile Spaces

schedule.desc: Come see Pegasus Award winner Paul Kwinn play tunes both silly and otherwise.
schedule.title: Concert: Paul Kwinn

schedule.desc: This panel discusses the best sources for current criticism and reviews for books, media and more. Come hear about the big names and the little hidden gems!
schedule.title: Good Reviews Are Hard to Find

schedule.desc: One of the most popular British imports into the U.S. for over half a century, Doctor Who enjoyed a renaissance beginning in the mid 2000’s. However, with the collapse of its American partnership with Disney, the future of the show hasn’t been as bleak as this in decades. Or has it? This panel will discuss the status of the series, its prospects, and its promise for a new generation of fans.
schedule.title: Doctor Who at the Crossroads

schedule.desc: Join our panelists as they discuss how they recognize implicit biases in their writing. They will explore how to make intentional decisions about what to challenge, subvert, or consciously include within their imagined worlds.
schedule.title: Authorial Bias and Worldbuilding

schedule.desc: Post-traumatic stress disorder is finally a widely recognized issue among not only battle veterans but anyone who experiences an acute or chronic trauma. How can we present PTSD and similar responses to trauma in speculative fiction with grace and empathy?
schedule.title: From Shell Shock to Mind-Burn: PTSD in Sci-Fi

schedule.desc: In the near future, a plague infests La Gran Colombia. Ingrid Bolívar is the only one who knows that the plague is carried by young women of the streets, whom she has claimed as her army. Policarpa is meant to be Ingrid's greatest weapon, but when she falls in love with a top government official, she instead tries to become a savior. Rooted in Latin American magical realism, the world of Policarpa exists in a Colombia that is just around the corner.
schedule.title: Policarpa: Apocalypse Sur Amerikkka

schedule.desc: Smilodon fatalis, with its elongated saberteeth, has fascinated both scientists and the public since its discovery in 1869. We took a multidisciplinary approach, combining information on the recently found Homotherium latidens cub mummy, Panthera leo (lion) cub, Felis catus (cat), Homo sapiens (human), tissue depth measurements, and forensic techniques to determine what Smilodon fatalis might have looked like.
schedule.title: CSI: Sabertooth Edition

schedule.desc: From The Alan Parsons Project to Bad Omens, bands have drawn heavily from SFF, horror, anime, and literature to create “concept” albums. How have these albums and music impacted audiences through the years, created fascinating imagery, videos, and merch, and drawn younger bands and their fans into geek culture?
schedule.title: Concept Albums

schedule.desc: Andrew Rubin is the author of the contemporary urban fantasy Hell or High Winter, in which the Greek god Hermes struggles to find purpose in the modern world. Let's chat about why we still crave mythology in the age of AI, adapting ancient legends for today's tech-obsessed world, writing across novels and screenplays, the state of Hollywood, publishing a debut fantasy, or whatever rabbit hole our conversation tumbles into.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Andrew Rubin

schedule.desc: Costumers and parents discuss some easy things that you can do and things you can use for costuming for your kids.
schedule.title: Easy Costuming Tricks for Kids

schedule.desc: Some fandoms have a longer "life cycle" than others: some rise and fall according to the accessibility/production of new content, but some have a surprising shelf life, continuing on long after the source media ends. What are the hallmarks of a fandom with more longevity than others? What are signs that a fandom is in its "death throes," and can it come back from that? How does fanwork (fanfiction, fanart, fanzines, etc) contribute to all this?
schedule.title: The Rise and Fall of Fandoms

schedule.desc: What’s it like to live within the Pacific Rim? Authors based in the Pacific Rim share their thoughts on the greatest ocean of all, including how it features in their stories.
schedule.title: Enchanting the Pacific

schedule.desc: Many television series have great beginnings and middles but the end flops. What makes for a perfect ending? Let’s look at series that stuck the landing, and others that… didn’t. How can screenwriters write endings that bring closure, satisfaction, and resonance?
schedule.title: A Satisfying Ending

schedule.desc: Advanced humanoid robots are already in development. How far are we, really, from having a robot integrated with artificial intelligence? How would our new robotic companions help us? What physical dangers would they pose? What social and ethical dangers would they create? What kind of social pushback would they inspire, and why? How deep will the uncanny valley be?
schedule.title: Humanoid Robots

schedule.desc: "Care and Feeding of the Writer/Artist 101"--sometimes literally. What happens when your artist roomie or partner goes into hibernation? Dealing with the depression when a project doesn't work, or flops. Dealing with the highs. Panelists offer insight and suggestions for those who are in it for the long haul living with a creator. This can also apply to two writers or artists living together!
schedule.title: Living with a Writer/Artist

schedule.desc: Everyone is welcome to help celebrate Guest of Honor Barbara Hambly’s birthday! Since Barbara loves a good tea, we are throwing her a birthday tea party on LAcon V’s opening day!
schedule.title: Barbara Hambly’s Birthday Tea Party

schedule.desc: Celebrate science fiction in film with five shorts and one feature-length movie. Shorts: Before The Sky Took Him (USA), Kontaminate You (USA), Lunar Dark (USA), NIXIE (USA), The Astronaut (USA). Feature: Zero Existence (Italy, directed by Matteo Scarfò).
schedule.title: An Afternoon of Science Fiction Movies

schedule.desc: LangTime Studio is a language creation live stream hosted on YouTube by David and Jessie Peterson (conlangers from Game of Thrones, Dune, Supergirl, and many more). In this special episode of their live stream David and Jessie will introduce audience members to their shared universe—the setting of the board game Sovála—and demonstrate the name creation process by creating names for the anthropomorphic bats of Námuo Káámie.
schedule.title: Live Podcast: LangTime Studio

schedule.desc: We no longer really accept the 19th century anthropological and psychoanalytical idea that all cultures have the same fairy tales with the same underlying meanings, but we do still see recurring tropes, and flashes of familiarity. This panel will explore their favorite tales and think about how fairy and folk tales in the cultures they have experienced express local cultural concerns, and shape and are shaped by the fantastic.
schedule.title: Fairy Tales and How They Connect Us

schedule.desc: A meetup for Hispanic and Latine creators to be in community. Discuss topics and address challenges faced specifically by community creators of all mediums.
schedule.title: Meetup: Hispanic and Latine Creators for Hispanic and Latine Creators

schedule.desc: Cyber-professionals and other experts will help you understand how the bad guys are using AI tools to harm you. They will talk about deepfakes, social engineering, data theft, AI-crafted lies and more.
schedule.title: Real Villains and AI: AI as a Hacker Tool

schedule.desc: John Wardale can make dozens of animals and other objects from long skinny balloons. These include dogs, dragons, giraffes, elephants, ninja turtles, mermaids, aliens, hats, motorcycles, and the starship Enterprise. He will talk about how to do balloon sculpting, and teach everyone to make their own dog. (Allergy warning: balloons contain latex.)
schedule.title: Balloon Animal Sculpting Workshop (Thursday)

schedule.desc: Panelists will address the purely business side of a writing career, from investing in your own projects (should you record an audiobook?) to investing for your future, including taxes and other nitty gritty nuts and bolts.
schedule.title: The Business Side of a Writing Career

schedule.desc: The new Vera C. Rubin Observatory is running the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, the most ambitious survey of the universe so far. It sweeps the sky over and over, looking for changes. It may just ruin astronomers' sleep. If you told VRO "Text me every time you notice an asteroid moving," your phone might be beeping ALL NIGHT LONG. The panel discuss what kind of science can we expect this torrent of data to bring?
schedule.title: Vera Rubin Observatory: Tracking Changes in the Sky

schedule.desc:
He’s just spoiled rotten. Thin IC thinks he’s got some kind of—I dunno—dissociative mental disorder or something. And maybe he does. But that just ain’t right. If eyes are indeed the window to the soul, I think that thing sitting in the other room is straight from the depths of hell itself. Join us playing this legendary game!

Character sheets, dice and pencils provided.
schedule.title: Shadowrun: Spoiled Rotten

schedule.desc: Lee is an Executive Editor with Tor Publishing Group (Macmillan) and started his formal editing career with HarperCollins. He’s published such luminaries as Martha Wells, Kate Elliott, Nnedi Okorafor, Adrian Tchaikovsky and Becky Chambers. He also writes and performs. He was the first British editor to ever be nominated for the Hugo Award for Best Editor (Long Form) and is the only one to have ever been nominated in the Short Form category.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Lee Harris

schedule.desc: Before he was a Grand Master, Ray Bradbury was an active science fiction fan in the lively Los Angeles scene of the 1930s and 1940s. The Earliest Bradbury is a deep dive into his work, life, and antics before he became a professional author; it's also a unique look at the community of fans, artists, and writers from which he emerged.
schedule.title: The Earliest Bradbury

schedule.desc: Join us for a panel discussion with the creators of the cross-platform MAYA universe which encompasses books, films, video games, graphic novels and more!
schedule.title: MAYA Narrative Universe

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss science fails in media and books, and enlighten the audience on how this stuff actually works.
schedule.title: Oops . . . Fails in SF and Science Writing

schedule.desc: Marvel and DC continue to release superhero films and fans continue to flock to the theatres. Some fans, though, think that the market is oversaturated, and it is too hard for newcomers to dive in. Where could the DCU and MCU look for new content that would bring more excitement for more people? What suggestions are there for newcomers who want to catch up? Is the end of these universes upon us, and if so, where else should we go for superhero content?
schedule.title: Are We Really Tired of Superhero Movies?

schedule.desc: You may be a master wordsmith alone at your desk, but public speaking will make you doubt your prowess? Come get tips from Gabrielle de Cuir, a veteran director of stage, audiobooks, and public speaking, on how to excel at reading excerpts from your book before an audience. She'll tell you how to create the best presentation of your brand and select an excerpt, explore delivery styles, and employ relaxation techniques. The fear of public speaking is real. Approach your next reading with a whole new boost in confidence.
schedule.title: What?! You Want Me to Read My Own Book ... in Public?

schedule.desc: Thomas Ha is a Nebula and Locus award-winning author of speculative short fiction and the author of the debut short story collection Uncertain Sons and Other Stories. Come join an informal discussion about writing and submitting short fiction, general writing craft, the mechanics of short stories, and other miscellany.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Thomas Ha

schedule.desc: Somto Ihezue is a Nigerian writer and filmmaker. His work has won the Locus Award and has been a finalist for the Nebula Award, the British Fantasy Award, the ALCS Tom-Gallon Trust Award, and the Ignyte Award. Come along to chat about fireflies, longing, ukpaka, boyhood, Igbo spirits, and everything in between.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Somto Ihezue

schedule.desc: Online platforms differ in terms of norms, type of material presented, algorithms, and audiences. How has the architecture of varying platforms shaped our behaviors in these spaces? Are some platforms more hospitable or hostile towards specific kinds of fan activity than others?
schedule.title: How Does Internet Architecture Shape Fandom Behavior?

schedule.desc: Do you love masterful criminals and clever detectives? Explore ways to plant clever clues, create intrigue and keep your readers guessing until the very end. (This workshop is for teens)
schedule.title: The Butler Did It: Teen Mystery Workshop

schedule.desc: Astro Boy, Speed Racer, Battle of the Planets, Robotech, Star Blazers. All were edited, adjusted and even added to: but with over 60 years of anime being appreciated by US audiences, and comics being released based on some of the franchises, which series are still worth watching? And with which should viewers revert to the originals?
schedule.title: Americanized Anime

schedule.desc: Theodora Goss is the award-winning author of the Athena Club series of novels about girl monsters in Victorian London, as well as short stories, essays, and poems. She has also taught creative writing in an MFA program and numerous workshops. Come talk about gothic fiction, monsters, fairy tales, heroine's journeys, anything witchy, and the challenges of writing while teaching.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Theodora Goss

schedule.desc: How do the worst of the worst become the best of the best? Small and scheming, titanic and brutal, cold-hearted, and somehow, rather stylish, or at least complex--join this lively discussion about why some villains become undeniably unforgettable, and get readers to root for them.
schedule.title: Villains You Root For

schedule.desc: Sara Felix is a Hugo award winning artist who makes abstract space art as well as tiaras. She is also the president of ASFA, the Association of Science Fiction and Fantasy Artists, mom and cat admirer. Come join her to discuss tips and techniques on making your own tiara, where to get supplies, talk about the state of fantasy art, how she gets anything done while parenting, or just to discuss your admiration of her cat Cheeto.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Sara Felix

schedule.desc: Emboss, stamp, color notecards to give them to family & friends or save them for your own scrapbook
schedule.title: Personalize a Card

schedule.desc: Daryl Gregory will be reading from The Porcelain Sisters, a horror comedy novella coming out this fall.
schedule.title: Reading: Daryl Gregory

schedule.desc: The history and complexity of dog breeding offers a practical lens into how one might approach the ethics and logistics of futuristic breeding programs. Emerging computational tools may provide additional insight, but are not a silver bullet. The imprecision of genetic modeling risks selection cutoffs that narrow the gene pool and lead to unintended consequences.
schedule.title: Dogs as a Template for Your Futuristic Breeding Program

schedule.desc: Robert J. Sawyer, author of Hugo-winner Hominids, reads from his brand-new nonfiction collection Sawyer on Science Fiction, which Amazing Stories calls “Incisive and startlingly frank.”
schedule.title: Reading: Robert J. Sawyer

schedule.desc: As the boundaries of speculative fiction are pushed every year in novels, similar growth is experienced in comics. This panel will discuss where we, as fans and creators of comics and graphic novels, find ourselves in the SFF landscape.
schedule.title: Current Landscape of Speculative Fiction Comics and Graphic Novels

schedule.desc: When are games a good tool for education? How/what do games teach their players? What can we learn from studying, playing, or designing games? How do we, or should we, distinguish games from simulation and/or role playing?
schedule.title: Games as Pedagogy

schedule.desc: Join us for today’s feedback session. This is the best way to connect with the convention organizers and ask any questions you have about the con. Your participation will help us to address current issues and capture new opportunities that we might otherwise miss. Your feedback matters and will be heard by future Worldcon organizers as well!
schedule.title: Feedback Session - Thursday

schedule.desc: Many TTRPG supplements exist to help us play our favorite stories at the table, but what if you want to play a story that nobody’s adapted? Bring your favorite work—short story, novel, TV episode, movie, or video game—and we’ll explore how to deconstruct it and play it at the table.
schedule.title: Playing Our Favorite Stories (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Celebrating twenty years of audio fiction, join Escape Artists veterans discussing two decades of podcast industry changes, what they would do differently, the path to becoming a nonprofit, and what the future holds for EA.
schedule.title: Escape Artists Foundation: 20 Years of Podcasting

schedule.desc: Dungeons and Dragons (D&D) is the default ruleset for many tabletop roleplaying game groups. While it works well, it isn’t built for every story. This workshop explores how other systems handle similar ideas, support different genres and settings, and shape play in new ways. Bring your scenario, your ruleset, your questions, and we'll discuss the practical ways to choose or adapt a ruleset that fits the game you want to run.
schedule.title: Beyond D&D: Choosing the Right Ruleset

schedule.desc: Regenerative agriculture is the new buzzy method for healthy farming. What is it? Why does it matter? How is it linked to indigenous practices? Can you do it in your garden? It’s largely about soil linked to nutrients in our food.
schedule.title: Regenerative Agriculture: Good soil, clean water, and more

schedule.desc: Although tabletop roleplaying games (TTRPGs) are only about 50 years old, the scandals that have dogged the industry since inception have forced the culture of players, game masters, and designers to change every decade. From the D&D co-writers suing each other to a massive public outcry over proposed changes to default fair use contracts, the industry has been rocked by decisions that prove how lucrative and how beloved tabletop roleplaying games are.
schedule.title: A History of Tabletop Roleplaying Games in Seven Scandals

schedule.desc: Dennis K. Crosby is an award-winning author, editor, and former private investigator. Since 2020 he has published three urban fantasy novels and twenty-two short stories in various publications, including Weird Tales Magazine and Creepshow: 13 Tales of Terror. Chat with him about the craft of writing, indie publishing, horror, fantasy, mythology, P.I. tips and tricks, and how to make it in this extraverted world as a card-carrying introvert.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Dennis K. Crosby

schedule.desc: Sunday Times bestselling author Micaiah Johnson will read short excerpts from her upcoming horror novel, The Unhaunting, as well as her previously published novels, which have been named best of the year by New York Times, best of the decade by National Public Radio, and best of the 21st Century by Bookriot.
schedule.title: Reading: Micaiah Johnson

schedule.desc: Book clubs are a great way to connect with other fans and discuss the works you love. Panelists will discuss how to start and sustain a book club, and strategies to help your book clubs flourish.
schedule.title: Book Clubs: Strategies to Create, Run, and Sustain Them

schedule.desc: During this panel, poets will delve into poetry to explore meaning with an eye towards utility in speculating with wonder while encouraging community.
schedule.title: Black, Queer, and Speculating in Verse

schedule.desc: How do composers imagine and create music in non-human environments? Panelists will discuss and compare instruments and soundscapes used in various alien cultures depicted in media.
schedule.title: Exomusicology: Creating the Music of Alien Civilizations

schedule.desc: What info really needs to be in a cover or query letter? Does the story need a blurb or synopsis? Our panelists will discuss the best method for cover letters today, taking into particular account the tired-eyed editor or agent who might see dozens in a single work session.
schedule.title: Writing Cover or Query Letters

schedule.desc: Magical Realism is not solely the province of English and Latinx authors. Come hear from and about authors slipping just a little bit of wonder into their stories.
schedule.title: Cross-Cultural Perspectives on Magical Realism (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Traditional publishing across the board seems to focus on finding and promoting young authors and their debut novels. As an older person seeking a late-in-life career change, rejection after rejection from agents and the few publishers open to unrepresented writers can make it feel like no one is interested. Is self-publishing the only road for the older author with a story to share? This panel busts some myths and looks at the many possible roads to publication for older writers wanting to break in.
schedule.title: Breaking Into Traditional Publishing As a New, Older Author

schedule.desc: Come join those of Jewish background, religion, and/or culture for discussion, interaction, and community.
schedule.title: Meetup: Jewish Genre Fans

schedule.desc: Join Richard Man, winner of the Hugo Award for Best Fan Artist, for a guided docent tour of the art show.
schedule.title: Art Show Docent Tour: Richard Man

schedule.desc: This workshop will focus on different forms of hair braiding: four strand “round” braids, classic (three-strand) French and (three-strand) Dutch (or inverted-French or underhand), crown braid (a modified three-strand French braid), and five and seven-strand fingering techniques. We might work on hearts, spirals and pullup-weaves. Which we use will be tailored to the desires and abilities of the participants.
schedule.title: Fancy Hair Braids Workshop (Thursday)

schedule.desc: Come play Jackbox games this evening with other teens!
schedule.title: Jackbox Games for Teens

schedule.desc: In any conflict where causality and the butterfly effect mean that any tactical action can have unintended consequences, there are significant ethical questions. Was it a genocide when the Twelfth Doctor erased the Daleks from history? Does the past have a right to have happened the way it did?
schedule.title: Causality Violations: The Ethics of a Time War

schedule.desc: The modern science fiction and fantasy community often refers to J. R. R. Tolkien and Ursula K. Le Guin as the "grandparents" of SFF. What do today's creatives think about their legacies and the most recent adaptations of their work?
schedule.title: The Legacy of Tolkien & Le Guin Today

schedule.desc: Neurodiverse authors and readers often experience storytelling in ways that reflect how they process the world around them. Join writers as they come to explore how reading and writing fiction can help them navigate and engage with content. They’ll share practical writing advice for neurodivergent creators on how to integrate their perspectives into their process, as well as how to write characters unlike themselves into their narratives.
schedule.title: Neurodiverse Approaches to the Art of Stories

schedule.desc: The most recent Predators movie: Badlands is set on the Predators' home-world, focusing on the culture of their species. A written and verbal language Yautja for the Predators - Yautja - was developed by linguist Britton Watkins, drawing influence from previous depictions of the Predators language, as well as the type of sound a Predator's mouth design could realistically make, including their typical clicking noises. Come hear about how Britton developed this fascinating language - and learn to speak a few words and phrases!
schedule.title: Yautja - the language of the movie Predator

schedule.desc: What’s coming in future transportation? Will either solar or hydrogen fuel cell-based technology power our planes? What about personal transportation?
schedule.title: Future Transportation: Thinking Beyond Autonomous EVs

schedule.desc: Yume Kitasei is a Japanese and American writer of genre-blending science fiction. She is the author of three novels, The Deep Sky, The Stardust Grail, and Saltcrop. She lives in Brooklyn with two cats, Boondoggle and Filibuster, and balances writing with a career in city government. Join if you want to chat and/or commiserate about science fiction, publishing, plotting novels with spreadsheets, how science fiction and public policy could or do intersect, and how to navigate the "work-work" balance of writing while working a day job sixty hours a week. Ask her why clones aren't creepy.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Yume Kitasei

schedule.desc: Bring the kids for a special filk concert geared to them.
schedule.title: Children’s Filk Concert

schedule.desc: John Scalzi is America's foremost Hugo-winning DJ. Also, he's written some books.
schedule.title: Table Talk: John Scalzi

schedule.desc: In March 1859, a massive coronal mass ejection hit the Earth, causing a geomagnetic storm known as the Carrington Event. It caused brilliant aurora all the way down to Cuba, and induced three-inch sparks (100,000 volts) in telegraph lines. When a storm this large, or larger, hits Earth again, what will the impacts be? What does space weather preparedness look like?
schedule.title: A Carrington Event: What if the Sun Destroys our Satellites?

schedule.desc: Navajo leader shares the Navajo emergence story in Navajo, with English translation provided
schedule.title: Navajo Emergence Story

schedule.desc: Do you cut on a table raised by paint cans to ergonomic height? Use memory foam mats to cushion your knees while crawling on the floor? Have a custom closet-turned-cosplay-shop? Our panel will discuss designing physical spaces for creation, whether you’ve got a permanent maker space or a system for setting up only as needed. Bring your questions and our experts will share their experiences finding ways to make your spaces work.
schedule.title: Creating Craft Spaces

schedule.desc: We've heard about cozy mysteries, but how in the world can horror be "cozy"? Balancing scary and cosy is no easy task. How do writers strike the balance between humour and horror, the cosy and the creepy? Join our panel as they discuss this new subgenre.
schedule.title: What the Heck is 'Cozy Horror'?

schedule.desc: Dustin Adair founded his videogame company, Scary Robot, in 2011 and has successfully released eight titles. This talk will focus on what it takes to develop videogames as a lone-wolf, by yourself. He will also share tips and tricks to help increase your chances of successfully completing your first game and then continuing to develop more titles.
schedule.title: The Highs and Lows of a Lone-Wolf Videogame Developer

schedule.desc: LGBTQ+ themes have appeared in anime and manga since the 1950's. We will provide an overview of terminology and subgenres, discuss works that are done well, and talk about how the works have influenced the anime fandom community.
schedule.title: LGBTQ+ Representation in Anime and Manga

schedule.desc: Let's decorate a journal: What type of journal? River Song's, Tardis, Indiana Jones adventures, Princess, poetry, songs, or private thoughts
schedule.title: Journal Making

schedule.desc: John Brunner died mid-Worldcon and Iain M Banks died before he could attend Loncon 3. There is a tendency to invite GoHs to Worldcons late in their lives. This ensures that fans and pros who are invited have decades of activity behind them. On the flip side, we may be waiting too late to honor some of them. How do we find the balance between honoring people with career long enough to be well-established while not delaying that honor for too long?
schedule.title: Do We Honor People Too Late?

schedule.desc: From Isaac Asimov to Martha Wells, robots have fascinated readers and writers alike. We’ll try to gather as many SF writers depicting robots as we can, and have a great discussion about how SF robots get designed, what they say about us and the future, and more. What are the best robot stories?
schedule.title: Robots in Science Fiction: Who’s Writing What in Robotics?

schedule.desc: Philip K. Dick Award-winning author Carrie Vaughn will read from a brand-new, forthcoming Cormac and Amelia novella, Infernal Spark. Ghost hunting enters the digital age!
schedule.title: Reading: Carrie Vaughn

schedule.desc: Foz Meadows, author of A Strange and Stubborn Endurance and All the Hidden Paths, reads from his next novel, Godburned, forthcoming in January 2027.
schedule.title: Reading: Foz Meadows

schedule.desc: Join award-winning authors Jessica Maison and Matt Harry as they welcome a guest, choose two monsters, then pit them against each other in an epic, improvised encounter! MvM is fun, informative, and always unexpected.
schedule.title: Live Podcast: Monster v. Monster

schedule.desc: Indigenous voices keep rising, from indigenous futurism to fantasy epics rooted in their culture and mythos. Hear how these authors are inspired by their history as they look to the future.
schedule.title: We Are Still Here: Indigenous Voices in Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: Online content creation is a relatively new way to make a living. It's one thing to make the art; it's an entirely different skill set to teach someone else how to make it, along with creating videos, managing an online community, providing tech support, etc. Come hear our panelists describe how they function as content creators and how they figured it out.
schedule.title: The Art of Content Creation

schedule.desc: Let's geek out about our favorite SFF musicals from television, stages, and movies. Spontaneous sing-a-longs may occur!
schedule.title: Geek Out About: SF/F Musicals

schedule.desc: Can you survive the POETRY DEEEAATTTHMATTCCHHH?! *cough* Sorry, don't know where that came from. Join us as professional poets and random audience members face off in front of an audience of judgmental amateurs and pros who will vote for the winner of this game of wits!
schedule.title: Poetry Deathmatch!

schedule.desc: Effie Seiberg is a Nebula-winning and Hugo- and Sturgeon-nominated short story writer, specializing in satire and social commentary, especially about disability. Come chat about anything from humor in SFF, humor as a tool against authoritarianism, writing and publishing while disabled, the power of stories, activism via urinal stickers, being the Emotional Support Human for a small dog, baking weird things, or anything else!
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Effie Seiberg

schedule.desc: From surveillance states to corporate overlords, SFF loves to imagine systems of power gone wrong. Panelists with legal, tech, and policy backgrounds discuss what fiction gets right (and wrong) about how institutional power actually works—and how to make your dystopia more chillingly plausible.
schedule.title: Law, Corporations, and Dystopia in SFF

schedule.desc: Mari Ness is a poet and short fiction writer - and now, a Nebula finalist and a two-time Hugo finalist! Come chat about poetry, short fiction, the submission process, fairy tales, cats, animation, wheelchairs, alligators, and a host of other not exactly random to entirely random topics.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Mari Ness

schedule.desc: Sex scenes in fiction can reveal character, shift power, advance plot, deepen relationships, or expose emotional truths. However, they can also stall a story or exist only as spectacle. This panel explores the narrative function of intimacy in speculative fiction, from fade-to-black implications to explicit depictions.
schedule.title: Another Sex Scene Already? Pacing Intimacy in Romantasy (Virtual)

schedule.desc: The TV adaptation of the Murderbot series offers us the chance to interact with our favorite snarky, pessimistic, paranoid SecUnit in a whole new way. Murderbot's quest offers insight into individuality, identity, neurodivergence, found family, and the love of entertainment media. Hack your governor module, download your feed, and join us as we get to know Murderbot better.
schedule.title: Finding One's Own Sanctuary Moon: Inside Murderbot's Mind

schedule.desc: In visual media, we can rely on everyone agreeing on what’s being shown. But when we’re reading a novel or a short story, writing a fanfic, or playing a roleplaying game, we’re all using our imaginations, and our imaginations will differ. How does that affect our shared experience of these artworks? And when we transform them, whether through fanfic, through play, or something else, how can we make sure we’re all sharing the same world?
schedule.title: Collaborative Visualizations

schedule.desc: When recording or performing a cover of someone else's song or a parody of their original material, there are legal things to consider to keep yourself out of trouble, as well as just practicing good manners about using other people’s work. What do you need to know before putting your versions of these songs on public display?
schedule.title: But It’s Not Mine: Cover Song and Parody Legalities

schedule.desc: Bisexual identity in media is too often erased or misrepresented. Explore how bisexual representation is portrayed in storytelling, why authentic imagery matters, and how creators can move beyond stereotypes to depict bisexual characters with nuance and respect.
schedule.title: The Bi Standard: Respecting Bisexual Identity in Storytelling

schedule.desc: Excerpt from Threads, a non-linear magical realist novel, set primarily in the Pennsylvania coal region (1868-1999). A bloodline of women based on biblical female archetypes (e.g. Eve and Hagar), who traditionally had little or no voice, speak out and act. Their struggles, failures and triumphs are woven into an old rug by the family’s first mother, creating links among past and future generations.
schedule.title: Reading: Sally Wiener Grotta

schedule.desc: Long before the internet, SFF fandom experimented with a universal communication system: Esperanto. In the 1930s and 1940s, many fans believed that a shared global language would help build the peaceful, cooperative future. Nowhere was this enthusiasm stronger than in Los Angeles fandom, where figures like Forrest J Ackerman and Charles D. Hornig championed Esperanto as part of their vision of a truly international SFF community.
schedule.title: SFF Fandom and Esperanto

schedule.desc: A meetup for Asian creators to be in community, discuss topics, and address challenges faced specifically by Asian creators of all media.
schedule.title: Meetup: Asian Creators for Asian Creators

schedule.desc: Join us for two films: Time Helmet (Canada), Voidance (UK - Zoe Cunningham)
schedule.title: Not So Late Night Science Fiction Double Feature

schedule.desc: Eric Linus Kaplan, writer for Futurama, Big Bang Theory, and others, will chat with Eric Schwitzgebel about alien and robot consciousness, along with many related subjects.
schedule.title: Alien and Robot Consciousness

schedule.desc: Jake Casella Brookins is a critic and independent scholar; he’s the publishing editor at the Ancillary Review of Books and the host and producer of the podcast A Meal of Thorns (both Hugo finalists). Come chat about the fine art of reviewing, tips on pitching nonfiction essays, and what goes into editing nonfiction work about speculative fiction! He’s also always keen to talk about philosophy & SF, translated SF, and the state of the field.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Jake Casella Brookins

schedule.desc: 2026 saw the first-ever medical evacuation from the International Space Station. The panel will discuss how real astronauts prepare for health emergencies, the risks of near-earth orbit, and what new dangers they expect for the upcoming lunar missions.
schedule.title: SOS on the ISS: Medical Emergencies in Orbit

schedule.desc: It's elementary, dear Watson, that Sherlock Holmes is one of the greatest, and certainly best known, detectives of all time. Portrayals of Holmes have included gender bending, alternate timelines, and more. Our panelists will discuss the various depictions of Conan Doyle's detective through the years, and using their powers of deduction, may even decide upon which ones worked best!
schedule.title: Sherlock Holmes Through Time and Space

schedule.desc: Kamilah Cole is the USA Today & national indie bestselling Jamaican-American author of So Let Them Burn, This Ends in Embers, An Arcane Inheritance, and the upcoming Wicked Endeavors. Join her to talk about classic anime like Sailor Moon and Cowboy Bebop, how to juggle writing fiction and fanfiction, how to juggle writing books and having a day job, cancelled TV shows like Once Upon a Time and Sleepy Hollow, and anything else your beautiful mind can come up with.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Kamilah Cole

schedule.desc: Black Gothic, also called Afro-Gothic, blends classic Gothic fascinations like horror, mystery, and the uncanny with the lived realities of the Black American experience and the African diaspora. Join authors as they explore history, folklore, religion, and storytelling traditions, and how the genre utilizes elements such as mythology, religion, and traditions both oral and written, to engage with Black trauma and avenues of processing.
schedule.title: The Black Gothic in America

schedule.desc: In 1930s Los Angeles, a small group of passionate readers began meeting in living rooms and borrowed back rooms, laying the foundation for LASFS. When fandom was young and the mimeograph was king, writers, artists, letterhacks, and eccentric personalities of every sort gathered here. This panel will explore how they shape the emerging culture of science fiction. Join us to find out.
schedule.title: LASFS: Building the World's Oldest Active SF Club

schedule.desc: With dozens of anime shows rushing at us every few months, it's easy for good stuff to be overlooked. What are your favorite less-discussed anime shows of recent years?
schedule.title: Hidden Gems of Anime

schedule.desc: You've pitched a project to an editor who is interested. Yay! But. They want to see an outline. You're a pantser! You like letting the story evolve through experimental writing! What are you going to do? Our panelists are those who outline plus those who usually don't outline but have learned to as they discuss strategies for developing an outline: How to keep the idea fresh in your mind, how to approach structure, how to infuse the outline with the passion you feel when pantsing the story, etc.
schedule.title: How to Change your Writing Process--When Pantsers have to Outline

schedule.desc: This panel of scientists is here to answer your questions about space and space travel. Soothe your curiosity and pick up some new ideas for stories along the way! (This panel is for teens)
schedule.title: Wandering the Stars: Space Science for Teens

schedule.desc: Disabled characters have been part of speculative fiction for a long time: from Dr. Jekyll to Miles Vorkosigan and more. For many fans, those stories offer powerful moments of recognition. Take a look at disability across SFF, discussing the characters that have shaped readers and writers and the representations they want to see more of.
schedule.title: Disabilities Within the Genre

schedule.desc: The panel will explore how to make horror, the supernatural, and other speculative theatre work in a live performance setting. How does it set itself apart from films or books? From Paris's Grand Guignol to Clive Barker, from high school productions of Alien to Sweeney Todd, we'll discuss our favorite dark corners of theater and how to make your dramaturgy deliciously ghoulish.
schedule.title: Horror on Stage

schedule.desc: N.E. Davenport writes SFF novels with bold and unapologetic heroines who stand firmly in their own power, sexual freedom, and agency. Enemies-to-lovers, found family, morally grey characters, and villainous love interests are common to her story worlds. Join her for a table talk about fierce heroines, feminine rage, weaving romance and spice into SFF, why villains and anti-heroes make for sexy love interests, and all things morally grey.
schedule.title: Table Talk: N.E. Davenport

schedule.desc: With the recent rise in popularity of horror and horror tropes within traditionally non-horror genres, body horror is experiencing a renaissance. Panelists will examine what body horror symbolizes in both historic and contemporary works.
schedule.title: Body Horror as Symbolism

schedule.desc: Food descriptions can bring an imagined world to life, establishing culture, revealing inspiration, and depicting settings through a single bite. On this panel, authors will explore how food can showcase culture and give their stories that little extra kick.
schedule.title: Food for Thought: Worldbuilding Through the Delectable

schedule.desc: Fan Artists use many forms of expression – from drawing, through painting, sculpture, jewellery, to anything else one can use to create art. Let’s do a deep dive into the realm of Fan Artists, their works, their motivations, even their favourite item in their Hugo portfolio!
schedule.title: What It Means to Be a Fan Artist

schedule.desc: Mur Lafferty, author of Six Wakes, will be reading from her upcoming cozy fantasy, Second Best Heroes.
schedule.title: Reading: Mur Lafferty
