schedule.desc: Scott Edelman has published 135+ short stories, many of which have been gathered in collections such as These Words Are Haunted, What Will Come After (which was a finalist for the Shirley Jackson Memorial Award), Tell Me Like You Done Before, and Things That Never Happened (about which Publishers Weekly wrote, "his talent is undeniable"). He will be reading a sampling from his most recent collection, 101 Things to Do Before You're Downloaded.
schedule.title: Reading: Scott Edelman

schedule.desc: Miguel O. Mitchell (he/him) is a speculative poet, SFF author, visual artist, and retired chemist. He loves talking about the power of speculative poetry to enrich us, is fascinated by the possibilities of extraterrestrial sentience, consumes lots of SFF and H (Get Out! Sinners!) in all media and enjoys urban fantasy worldbuilding. Come ask about his work, talk about SFFH, inquire about crazy scientific discoveries, and see some of his SFF art.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Miguel O. Mitchell

schedule.desc: Sex scenes in fiction can reveal character, shift power, advance plot, deepen relationships, or expose emotional truths. However, they can also stall a story or exist only as spectacle. This panel explores the narrative function of intimacy in speculative fiction, from fade-to-black implications to explicit depictions.
schedule.title: Another Sex Scene Already? Pacing Intimacy in Romantasy

schedule.desc: Marshall Ryan Maresca is a writer, the author of the 19 novels and novellas of fantasy series The Maradaine Saga, as well as the dieselpunk novel The Velocity of Revolution. He’s also the co-host of six-time Hugo Finalist podcast Worldbuilding for Masochists, discussing the craft of creating sci-fi and fantasy worlds. Come chat with him about writing giant series, worldbuilding, spreadsheets, 80s movies he saw too many times and culinary opinions.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Marshall Ryan Maresca

schedule.desc: The first science fiction fan clubs emerged in 1929 by young kids corresponding with other fans of Hugo Gernsback’s Amazing and Wonder Stories. In July 1939 both the first Worldcon was held and the science fiction golden age started. Join us for a 10 year journey following these young fans as they create the first clubs, fanzines, and engage in fandom drama and politics. They shaped what fandom and conventions would become.
schedule.title: The Wrath of Con - First Fandom and the Rise of Worldcon

schedule.desc: Filmmaker and author Anand Gandhi reads from his forthcoming epic science-fantasy novel MAYA: Seed Takes Root. Maya is the highest-funded debut novel in crowdfunding history. Immerse yourself in a world where the internet grows from trees and billionaire-gods govern with a "nudge".
schedule.title: Reading: Anand Gandhi

schedule.desc: Flash fiction, short story, novelette, novella. What makes a story work at a particular length? How does a writer know how long a story should be? Once a story is written, how does the length affect the author's marketing strategy? Panelists will compare these, and also how best to market each.
schedule.title: Crafting Novellas, Novelettes, Short Stories, and Flash/Micro Fiction

schedule.desc: If you identify as part of the LGBTQIA+ community, this meetup is for you!
schedule.title: Meetup: LGBTQIA+

schedule.desc: Prof. Matt Malkan (University of California Los Angeles (UCLA)) will share some of the recent discoveries about the origin of the universe that have been keeping him up at night. In recent years the big surveys of the sky have been delivering surprise after surprise on dark matter, black holes, dark energy, our origins and the future of our universe. Come be amazed and get your burning questions answered!
schedule.title: How the Early Universe Keeps Delivering New Surprises

schedule.desc: Convention Chair Joyce Lloyd welcomes you all at the official opening of LAcon V. Join our toastmaster, amazing Guests, and staff for the convention will be present to open the convention to all of our attendees, both in-person and virtual.
schedule.title: Opening Ceremony

schedule.desc: Tropes have been around as long as fanfiction has, many of which were lifted/adapted from the source material, and some of which are wholly unique to fandom (see: Omegaverse). But in recent years, tropes have skyrocketed to popularity, even "crossing over" into traditional publishing and marketing spaces. What's the appeal of our favorite tropes, and are there some that have fallen out of favor?
schedule.title: Tropes in Transformative Works

schedule.desc: While the Spider-Verse films in recent years developed an excited fan base, the concept of the Spider-Verse in comics has been around for decades. Join us for a panel all about celebrating the multiverse and as many Spideys as our time allotment will allow!
schedule.title: Exploring the Spider-Verse!

schedule.desc: Heather will be reading from an in-process short story “Expiration Date” about an author with writer’s block and a harpy moonlighting as a muse. If there’s additional time, she may share some excerpts from the next Alpennia book, Mistress of Shadows.
schedule.title: Reading: Heather Rose Jones

schedule.desc: Alex Pheby, author of the Cities of the Weft trilogy, reads from his forthcoming historical fantasy epic The House of Spiders.
schedule.title: Reading: Alex Pheby

schedule.desc: Come dance with Dublin 2029 and Stepwise! Stepwise is a traditional Celtic folk band consisting of Liam Lewis (mandolin, guitar, fiddle, voice), Olivia Breidenthal (fiddle and voice) and All-Ireland Champion bones player James Yoshizawa (percussion). They perform a mixture of traditional Irish songs with tight vocal harmonies and traditional Irish tune sets. Find them at https://stepwiseband.com.
schedule.title: Dublin 2029 Ceilidh (Featuring Stepwise)

schedule.desc: Octavia Butler once explained that Earthseed, the religion created in her novel Parable of the Sower, was a collection of poems she wrote to break through writer's block. In this open session, poets and writers discuss what techniques, textures, and forms can create beliefs that motivate new possibilities.
schedule.title: Parables For New Sowers

schedule.desc: Elizabeth Sandifer takes a break from stressing about whether she’s gonna get a Hugo for a chapter of Last War in Albion, her sprawling critical history of British comic books, in order to read an excerpt from the forthcoming chapter on Grant Morrison’s The Invisibles. Probably the bit where they get high and are abducted by aliens. That one’s pretty fun.
schedule.title: Reading: Elizabeth Sandifer

schedule.desc: The Oasis is a calm, welcoming place where you can rest and recharge at your own pace. You don’t have to talk to anyone unless you want to. You’ll find simple activities like coloring, short readings, and self-care supplies. If you need something, just ask—we’re here to help.
schedule.title: The Oasis - Thursday

schedule.desc: Sue Burke is an author and translator who wrote the trilogy Semiosis, Interference, and Usurpation; Immunity Index and Dual Memory, as well as short stories, poetry, journalism, and essays. Do your houseplants hate you? No. Do they want to take over the world? Yes. Do our machines want to take over the world? Maybe, and what could stop them? Do you want to save the galaxy, or are you tired of trying? Let’s talk about all this.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Sue Burke

schedule.desc: Filk music started out with people getting together in a circle in some random place at a convention to swap songs. We're official now and in a larger space, but it's still the same supportive tradition of sharing music together late into the night. All voices, instruments, and styles including a cappella welcome. Come by to sing or to listen!
schedule.title: Thursday Open Filk

schedule.desc: Join fellow pagans of all traditions as we welcome the full moon and the opening of LAcon V. We will cast a circle and welcome everyone for discussion, interaction and community. Share your favorite pagan authors, artists and stories. Blessed Be.
schedule.title: Meetup & Ritual: Pagan Genre Fans

schedule.desc: Join Dr. Theresa Jean Tanenbaum ("Tess")—ex-professor of interactive storytelling, multidisciplinary artist, and disabled neurospicy transgender witch activist—as she reads new speculative poetry and poems from her chapbook Abominations: Poems of Feminine Monstrosity, Speculation, & Horror, and a selection from her forthcoming cozy sapphic T4T romance + fictional-magical-girl-anime eggfic novel: The Egg Prime Directive.
schedule.title: Reading: Tess Tanenbaum

schedule.desc: Eboni Dunbar, winner of the 2024 Ignyte Award for best novelette reads from her recently released short story, "The Butcher of Zed" featured in the anthology, Shatter The Sun.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Eboni J. Dunbar

schedule.desc: Clarion alum Chelsea Sutton will read from her new "weird, big-hearted little nightmare" horror/fantasy novella Krackle's Last Movie, out this year from Split/Lip Press.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Chelsea Sutton
Virtual Table Talk: Charusheel Manikrao Mane

schedule.desc: Mysticism and the blending of Sci-Fi and fantasy in African SF stories is perhaps still new for western audiences. The panel will discuss why this is the case, give examples of African SF with mystic elements, and recommend follow up.
schedule.title: Mysticism and the Supernatural in African Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Join multi-award winning horror playwright. and one-time movie monster, Kevin Glover, for a peak behind the curtain at writing horror for the stage. This panel was recorded live at Crypticon in May 2026, in Seattle, and will be screened as part of the virtual program.
schedule.title: Stage Frights: Playwriting 101

schedule.desc: S. M. Hallow is a speculative fiction author who loves history, fairy tales, and Frankenstein. She is the author of Indie Ink Award finalist How To Survive This Fairytale and gothic horror romance novel The Halls of the Dead. Join her for a virtual chat about her books, our favorite monsters, the books we loved when we were twelve, queer retellings, self pub & trad pub, and resurrecting your gays in fiction.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: S. M. Hallow

schedule.desc: This presentation challenges prevailing stigmas surrounding gaming and offers a research-based perspective on the positive effects of video games on mental health and societal well-being. We will discuss stigmatization and moral panic, gaming disorder, mental health benefits, and the PERMA-V model. This presentation aims to reframe gaming as a legitimate beneficial activity that can support mental health, strengthen community, and promote personal development.
schedule.title: Gaming Does Good (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Caroline Hardaker, writer, poet, playwright, and explorer of all things uncanny and speculative, reads from her latest illustrated novel, Mothtown.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Caroline Hardaker

schedule.desc: Joan Slonczewski, author of the classic hard-SF novel A Door into Ocean, reads from her forthcoming novel Forevertree, a world where ambisexual humans live upon giant intelligent trees and rescue enslaved AIs.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Joan Slonczewski

schedule.desc: Refining your prose so that it sings can be a daunting task. CL Hellisen, author of The Shape of Monsters, shows you how using all your senses when revising will help deepen and enrich your writing. With exercises and examples, this interactive workshop will give you the tools to use sensory description that supports your world-building, deepens characterisation, and heightens your narrative tension.
schedule.title: Making Your Words Sing, a Sensory Workshop

schedule.desc: Ada Palmer tells wild tales of papal history in the (in)glorious Renaissance days of warrior popes, raging feuds, Inquisition drama, and extreme nepotism. Learn about the days of Machiavelli through Palmer’s historical research, and her (in)famous papal election live action role playing (LARP) Temptemus Papam which has now run many parallel simulations of the most corrupt papal election in the historical record, a test kitchen that reveals Machiavelli’s ideas in action.
schedule.title: The Papal Election of 1492/2016

schedule.desc: Luis Barragán, Colombian author and illustrator, is one of the rising stars of the New Weird wave that is sweeping across Latin America. By blending indigenous philosophy with a cosmopolitan aesthetic, he's redefining the possibilities of science fiction written in Spanish.
schedule.title: Holy Worms and Techno-Shamans: Luis Barragán (Virtual)

schedule.desc: These magazines have been bringing us delightful content for years, sometimes decades! Listen to these Hugo Award Finalists for Best Semiprozine talk about running a zine from how to keep it going year after year to finding and showcasing the best of the best.
schedule.title: Labor of Love: Hugo Best Semiprozine Finalists (Virtual)

schedule.desc: A. L. Kaplan, author of Mark of the Goddess and other short stories, reads from her novel, Star Touched. She is a member of the Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers Association, is the past president of the Maryland Writers’ Association, and holds an MFA in sculpture. When not writing or indulging in her fascination with wolves, this proud mom lives in Maryland with her husband and dog. Learn more at ALKaplanAuthor.com.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: A. L. Kaplan

schedule.desc: From surveillance states to corporate overlords, SFF loves to imagine systems of power gone wrong. Panelists with legal, tech, and policy backgrounds discuss what fiction gets right (and wrong) about how institutional power actually works—and how to make your dystopia more chillingly plausible.
schedule.title: Law, Corporations, and Dystopia in SFF (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Considering that you are all stars, meet at the hotel lobby for a leisurely 45-minute stroll around the venue. Get some fresh air, exercise, and chat with authors, editors, and artists in an informal setting. Hear about the interesting, fun, and maybe even unbelievable features of Anaheim.
schedule.title: Stroll with the Stars

schedule.desc: Cristián Londoño Proaño, Ecuadorian novelist, editor of the SF magazine Omicron Theory, and creator of the Andean fantasy subgenre, reads “El paquete,” a finalist for Tec de Monterrey’s HERO science fiction prize and published in Chile, Ecuador, and Hungary. On a banana hacienda where climate change has wiped out the cacao, a young man turns to biotech to revive it: a story of roots, family, and hope. Read in its original Spanish. Free download link to come!
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Cristián Londoño-Proaño

schedule.desc: Join a live Virtual Visit to the ATLAS Experiment at CERN and meet the scientists exploring the fundamental building blocks of the universe. Streaming live from CERN, the session offers an inside look at the largest experiment in the world, and the discoveries of modern particle physics. Participants will also have the opportunity to ask questions directly to the experts. Hosted by ATLAS physicist Dr. Steven Goldfarb.
schedule.title: Virtual CERN Tour

schedule.desc: Whether you are a fan or a pro working within our genre, you may “Level up”. Gaining experience can give you more “power”. The question is how to use responsibly and without harming others? Let’s discuss responsible levelling up as creators and community members, including both the pitfalls and benefits that come with greater experience and visibility in fandom.
schedule.title: Leveling Up Responsibility in Speculative Genres

schedule.desc: Fashion - including clothes, accessories hairstyles, and makeup - can provide significant information about group belonging, socioeconomic status, politics, and personality. As a tool for building new worlds, descriptions of fashion can be a powerful indicator to the audience. Join our panelists as they discuss their favorite ways costuming has been used as part of worldbuilding in speculative fiction, and learn from their key considerations when building your own worlds.
schedule.title: Fashion as Worldbuilding in Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: Speculative fiction got lucky with its fanbase; they are one creative and dedicated bunch! They can turn out amazing material about the many facets of SF/F, as shown by the Hugo Award Finalists for Best Fanzine. These fanzine folks will be talking about creating, running, and loving the work and community.
schedule.title: Fans Know Best: Hugo Best Fanzine Finalists

schedule.desc: Loads of different coloring pages, with pages for each day’s theme.
schedule.title: Coloring Time

schedule.desc: “Show, don’t tell,” is one of the first “rules” new writers hear from all sides. But what happens when you have to tell? Panelists will discuss voice, point of view, unreliable narrators, Bickham’s “scene” and “sequel” and other writing book advice, as well as tricks for balancing both sides of writing’s most famous rule of thumb.
schedule.title: Don’t Show Your Story, Tell It!

schedule.desc: Author and musician Henry Lien takes us on a musical journey through all the campy science fiction and fantasy theme songs that he has written and performed for the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association (SFWA), Clarion West, and his own books.
schedule.title: Concert: Henry Lien

schedule.desc: Our panelists will discuss the specific journeys that writers follow to research for a particular book or short story. We will explore their unexpected discoveries, odd twists and turns, or hilarious encounters.
schedule.title: Research Stories

schedule.desc: Joe Haldeman has been writing sf (and a little fantasy) since 1969, and has won almost every sf/f award given since then, including a plastic banana. He was a (drafted) soldier before he was a writer, and much of his work has been related to war.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Joe Haldeman

schedule.desc: The Gothic has a long and venerable tradition. Many agree that it began with Horace Walpole's The Castle of Otranto, but the Gothic has evolved many subgenres and niches now. Panelists will discuss elements of a Gothic tale: mood, structure, character, and of course the Gothic world.
schedule.title: Gothic Writing and Worldbuilding

schedule.desc: None of us knows everything about everyone, or every instance in history from every perspective. We can, and do, get things wrong. Sensitivity readers can help us, providing a service for writers based on lived experience and expertise. This panel will address finding sensitivity readers, and the vexing issues of representation, appropriation, and how writers can express themselves through their fiction without tripping over their own blinkers.
schedule.title: Why You Need Sensitivity Readers

schedule.desc: The maiden voyage of the space shuttle Endeavour led to the creation of a unique piece of art. Artist Bridget Duffy was asked by General Kevin P. Chilton (USAF Ret.) to create a special painting commemorating his first mission: STS-49, the maiden voyage of the then-newest space shuttle Endeavour. Duffy will talk about how Chilton decided to work with her, and will walk the audience through her process in creating the final work.
schedule.title: Art in Space: Bridget Duffy

schedule.desc: Latinx Futurism finds a way to the future, speculates past dystopias, dreams of utopias, and builds alternatives. Our panelists will discuss pathways to promote new insights, grow and preserve the Cal State Fullerton Archive, and enhance the Archive’s reach throughout the campus community and beyond. ¡Latinxfuturism Ahora!
schedule.title: Latinx Futurisms: The Cal State Fullerton Archive

schedule.desc: As Worldcon becomes more global, expanding to new areas of the world’s genre community, what does the current landscape look like? What have been some of the challenges in expanding? And, what do we have to look forward to?
schedule.title: Is Worldcon Finally Becoming A World SF Convention?

schedule.desc: Join R.P. Singletary for the launch of his new book, Speak Softly Among Icebergs. According to publisher Parlyaree, a queer indie press, “A stunning exploration of family, ecology, addiction, life, and what we leave behind. His writing, told from multiple voices and perspectives within the same page or paragraph, is like poetic theater: meant to be read aloud.”
schedule.title: Book Launch: R.P. Singletary

schedule.desc: SciFi fans tend to see space exploration as an unmitigated good, but exploration carries risks and, if not done carefully and intentionally, can cause serious harm to communities on Earth and perpetuate inequalities that still challenge humankind. This session will discuss how human beings can better prepare for an interplanetary future that can actually make humanity's future a better place.
schedule.title: The Ethical Exploration of the Solar System

schedule.desc: The Bible is a major cornerstone for Christianity and other religions, but what if you viewed it as a fantasy novel? Explore elements of fantasy in the Bible in this panel. Our panelists discuss how epic quests, side adventures, and heroic feats play a part in this religious text.
schedule.title: The Bible as a Fantasy Novel

schedule.desc: Tracy Drain is a flight systems engineer who has spent the last two-and-a-half decades helping to develop and operate deep space missions. She thinks that humor, kindness and patience can be aaaalmost as important as technical know-how, when guiding teams through stressful, high stakes, technical shenanigans. Come hear some stories of what it’s like helping baby spacecraft take their first steps out into the great unknown.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Tracy Drain

schedule.desc: African speculative fiction faces a critical threat: fragmentation and lack of institutional preservation. Seminal works are scattered across physical anthologies, defunct blogs, and social media, risking permanent loss. This panel launches the African Speculative Fiction Society (ASFS)’s Digital Archive: a comprehensive initiative to preserve 500+ African speculative fiction works and 50 oral history interviews.
schedule.title: Archiving the Future: Preserving African Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: In 1933, ambitious teenage fans convinced some of the era's biggest SF writers to participate in a wild experiment: a round-robin serial novel called Cosmos. The result was uneven, chaotic, and groundbreaking. This session examines how this fan-driven stunt shaped early fandom culture and helped John W. Campbell Jr. and Raymond A. Palmer secure two of the most important editorial jobs in SF history.
schedule.title: The Ultimate Cosmos: The Fan Experiment That Changed SF

schedule.desc: Using folklore, fairy tales and supernatural elements in your fiction, from fantasy to contemporary, exploring different ways of using myths and folktales to build worlds, flesh out your writing and inject magic.
schedule.title: Delving Deep: Using Folklore in Your Worldbuilding

schedule.desc: In 2026, Mel Brooks will (we hope) turn 100 years old. This panel will discuss his genre films (such as Young Frankenstein, Dracula: Dead and Loving It, Spaceballs) and explore why some of them work and some don't, and how Brooks' love and understanding of the genre (or lack thereof) impact his success.
schedule.title: The SFF of Mel Brooks

schedule.desc: We run cons because of our love of the genre and community, but also because we like to do it. Yet, there are times when one needs to take a step back. This may happen as our lives require more of our time, but it may also be a way to avoid burnout. How can we be aware of when we do too much? When should we step down, take a break, or even abandon conrunning?
schedule.title: When It's Time to Stop Convention Work

schedule.desc: Experienced musicians will help kids to write the LAconV Camp Fuzzy filk song.
schedule.title: Writing Filk Songs with Kids

schedule.desc: Some of the most pivotal tabletop games have been based on other people’s settings. There was a period where a franchise tie-in was generally seen as a mark against a game, whether in the video or tabletop realm; more recently, some very well-regarded games are based on franchises. How do we go about playing in other people’s worlds, and what are the benefits and drawbacks?
schedule.title: Playing in Someone Else’s World

schedule.desc: Women and other marginalized genders are part of historical fantasies, but how have they changed over time? What books and shows showcase historical these folks realistically?
schedule.title: Women and Nonbinary Folks in Historical Fantasy

schedule.desc: Military science fiction has long been associated with rigid hierarchies, imperial expansion, and nationalist narratives, but what happens when the genre is reimagined through an explicitly leftist lens? From worker-led space fleets to post-capitalist defense forces, this panel explores stories that center collective struggle, anti-imperial resistance, and revolutionary politics within futuristic armed conflicts.
schedule.title: The Red Army: Leftist Military Science Fiction

schedule.desc: There are as many ways to write songs as there are songwriters! Our experienced songwriters discuss and answer your questions about joining words and music and explore techniques and tricks to spark creativity.
schedule.title: Songwriting 101

schedule.desc: Tips on how to create a furry sidekick in stories: developing personalities, how to make readers feel attached to animal characters, and how to avoid the whiff of slavery, where the companion apparently exists only to nurture the protagonist without any life of their own. Examples will, of course, be provided.
schedule.title: Writing Loyal Companions in SF/F

schedule.desc: When a writer and artist find their vibe, something beautiful happens. Join John Picacio and Leigh Bardugo in this discussion / presentation about their collaboration on The Invisible Parade, what their journey through the graphic story space looked like, and what lessons they learned for new creatives to the graphic story format.
schedule.title: Welcome to THE INVISIBLE PARADE

schedule.desc: Ready to bring a dragon to life? Join Guest of Honor and Disney artist Tim Kirk to learn how. Learn tips, techniques, and creative secrets from a master illustrator as you create your own legendary creature. (This workshop is for adults.)
schedule.title: Draw a Dragon with Tim Kirk: Adults’ Workshop

schedule.desc: Los Angeles. Hollywood. Beverly Hills. Southern California—known as the land of endless sunshine and glamour. So why is this iconic region so perfectly suited for imagining the end of the world? Join panelists to explore the unique landscapes, cultural symbolism, and visual contrasts that make Southern California an irresistible setting for stories of collapse.
schedule.title: It's the End of the World: Southern California Dystopia

schedule.desc: Angela Liu, 2025 Astounding Award Finalist and author of the 2026 Hugo Award-nominated poem, “The Mourning Robot,” will be reading an excerpt from her cozy short story, “Fernie,” about a time traveling little girl and her mind-reading fern, along with a brand new poem.
schedule.title: Reading: Angela Liu

schedule.desc: This panel examines specific cases where ideas from science fiction have anticipated real technologies. Writers, engineers, and academics will discuss how the speculative can inspire innovation and critical thinking.
schedule.title: Science Fiction as a Driver of Scientific Innovation (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Gentle morning Tai Chi session.
schedule.title: Morning Tai Chi - Friday

schedule.desc: Emily Hockaday (she/her) is the acquiring editor for Asimov’s Science Fiction Magazine. Emily worked for both Analog Science Fiction and Fact and Asimov’s Science Fiction Magazine for over fifteen years, most recently as the senior managing editor and poetry editor. Please join Emily to talk about short fiction, publishing, poetry, Asimov’s, Analog, writing, or any SF related topic.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Emily Hockaday

schedule.desc: Since 2012, we have been showing our love to the Hugo Award for Best Fancast. Come hear this year's finalists talk about the ins and outs of running a fancast, what that entails, and how you, too, could be sharing your work out there for all to hear.
schedule.title: Hear Me Out: Hugo Best Fancast Finalists

schedule.desc: Foz Meadows is a queer trans author of SFF works, most recently of The Tithenai Chroicles, an M/M romantasy duology; his next novel, Godburned, is due out in January 2027. Join him to chat about worldbuilding, queerness, the politics of art, why AI sucks, the perils of being a terminally online elder millennial, and various other things that spark joy, potentially including (but by no means limited to) cats, K-Pop, danmei and TV dramas.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Foz Meadows

schedule.desc: Jennifer Brozek, a multi-talented author, editor, and media tie-in writer, reads from her most recent release, Shadowrun: Imre Grey, a cyberpunk with magic thriller.
schedule.title: Reading: Jennifer Brozek

schedule.desc: In Always Coming Home, Le Guin explores how a communalistic future might reshape our perceptions of property and nationhood. According to Benedict Anderson, our conception of “nation” comes from print capitalism, which allowed citizens to conceptualize themselves in community with those they had never met. Therefore, the nation is an imagined community.
schedule.title: True Communities in Imagined Futures

schedule.desc: David Gerrold, author of the award winning The Martian Child, will read from his recent work, but he hasn't decided what yet.
schedule.title: Reading: David Gerrold

schedule.desc:
You’ve never practiced Santeria yourself. If you did, you’d have all the Nyugen. You know you have been hired to find Sancho and her and put an end to him. Join us playing this legendary game!

Character sheets, dice and pencils provided.
schedule.title: Shadowrun: Santeria

schedule.desc:
An original adventure for Monster of the Week (Powered by the Apocalypse), a rules-light tabletop role playing game drawing from the fiction of television horror (Buffy, Supernatural, X-Files, etc).The system and the game master are both very friendly to new players!

Content warning: body and/or plant horror.
schedule.title: Sir, This is a Harby's

schedule.desc: Bring out your inner Trekkie with this networked computer game experience! 6–8 players take control of the spaceship Artemis, assuming various crew jobs: Helm, Weapons, Science, Communications, Engineering, Fighter Pilot(s), and Captain. The ship’s missions require the crew to work together to overcome challenges such as combat, puzzle-solving, diplomacy, and exploration. An educational (space science) teambuilding experience!
schedule.title: Artemis Space Bridge Simulator (Friday)

schedule.desc: Got a spare pint? Following long-standing L.A. tradition, we will be having the Southern California and San Diego Blood Bank join us, and they are ready to help you save some lives by donating your blood. The Bloodmobile will be parked outside the Anaheim Hilton, either right in front or off to the side on Hotel Way.
schedule.title: Blood Drive for the SoCal Blood Bank

schedule.desc: Fictional portrayals of extraterrestrial mining frequently depict far more labor-intensive operations of a type which is no longer common in the richer countries on Earth and now only continues in the global South. However, any successful extraterrestrial mining startups will develop into companies that have far more in common with today’s giant mining conglomerates than with fictional Belters.
schedule.title: Economics of Extraterrestrial Mining in Fact and Fiction

schedule.desc: It’s hard to know which tech companies to trust, if any. Where should you store your data, your texts, your communications? How do you keep your data out of governments’, as well as hackers’, hands? The parallel rise of AI and authoritarian governments poses serious risks. Writers and artists have had work stolen. Hackers abound. People have lost jobs over social media posts. Come explore the dangers of powerful tech meeting fragile privacy laws.
schedule.title: Data and Privacy: Keeping Your Data Safe

schedule.desc: It’s a fact that for the most part, no series can run forever. Sometimes some of our favorite titles get canceled. Usually it’s an issue with a title not making a certain sales threshold, but sometimes it can be editorial shakeups. Often sales levels aren’t directly related to overall quality or our own tastes. What were your favorite canceled comics? Which defunct titles would you like to see revived?
schedule.title: Canceled Comics: Celebrating Lost But Not Forgotten Comics

schedule.desc: Travel back to 1966 to explore why Star Trek felt boldly futuristic from day one. How did its optimism, diverse cast, and social questions challenge television norms of the time? Which creative and cultural choices helped it speak not only to its moment, but to decades beyond it?
schedule.title: 1966 Time Capsule: What Made Star Trek Ahead of its Time?

schedule.desc: If you're self-published in the SFF genre or an author at a small press, let's meet each other! The format goes like this: Each author brings two of their own books, one to give away, the other to keep. For two minutes, you will talk one-on-one with another author. At the bell, you will move to another author. You'll keep one of your own books to use to introduce yourself to the other authors. The book you give away will be traded away at each conversation and travel around the room. During each two-minute period, there will be four 30-second conversations: 1 - about your book, 2 - about their book, 3 - about one of the exchanged books, 4 - about the other exchanged book. Bell rings, move to the next person. When the session ends, whatever book is in your hand, you get to keep. Let's go!!
schedule.title: Indie Author Meetup and Book Exchange

schedule.desc: Science fiction often asks the biggest questions about humanity's future. The debates will explore ethical dilemmas that often occur in science fiction, such as artificial intelligence, space exploration, and human identity with a two-minute 1v1 flash debate battle format! (This panel is for teens.)
schedule.title: 1v1 Flash Debate Battle: Ethical Dilemma in Sci-Fi

schedule.desc: Sometimes you need to make your characters suffer without going over the top, having them survive the unsurvivable, or be unconscious the whole time. How can you write that sweet spot of pain and misery that can be endured or powered through while still being gut-wrenching to the reader? Which injuries lend themselves best to being healed and cared for by someone else, for the other side of hurt/comfort?
schedule.title: Best Whump Options: Injuries for Fiction

schedule.desc: This panel will discuss ways to envision a hopeful future. We explore the power of imagination in creating new realities, share examples of hopeful works we have enjoyed reading, recommend books, and share steps to create your own positive realities.
schedule.title: Narratives for a Hopeful Future

schedule.desc: Technology, AI, robotics, virtualization, and politicized curriculum have deeply impacted schools everywhere at all levels. American universities are being pressured on DEI. How can we deliver great global education in the future? Will technology give us new tools, or will we use less of it? What will be most important for future students to learn? How do we make education fairer and more inclusive?
schedule.title: Future Schooling: What Will Education Be Like in the Future?

schedule.desc: Panelists discuss how the world in which we set our stories is a character. Do our choices about setting drive the story? How does the setting shape culture and characters? How can we add the lived-in detail that makes a setting feel real? How do we know if our setting and story don’t work together?
schedule.title: Choose Wisely: Our Setting is Our First Character

schedule.desc: The use of puppetry as a theatrical technique has been seen around the world for thousands of years. We have seen it used in science fiction storytelling on stage, television, and in film. Let's look at some of our favorite SFF puppets and how stories would have been vastly different without them.
schedule.title: Puppetry for Storytelling

schedule.desc: Morag and Erin write queer speculative fiction, usually under the penname MK Hardy. Novels: The Needfire, The Haunting of Avis Lovelock, Splasher (as Billie Host). Join them for a virtual chat about any old thing - long-term collaborative partnerships, working with a 'big indie' press, IP work, writing multiple genres, maintaining equilibrium in a mad business... or if you prefer we could talk foraging, cocktails, cats, choirs, film, or DIY.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: MK Hardy

schedule.desc: Viable Paradise is a one-week residential workshop in writing and selling commercial SF/F. The workshop is intimate, intense, and features extensive time spent with best-selling and award-winning authors and professional editors currently working in the field. Instructors and alums will discuss the unique qualities of this collegial, mutually-supportive workshop that includes both long-form and short story writers.
schedule.title: Viable Paradise: A Residential Writing Workshop

schedule.desc: The writing process isn’t a binary, it’s a wide open universe. Panelists discuss different ways they approach story creation and the many metaphorical descriptions that people may find useful, including gardening, exploration, architecture, musical structures, outlining, “night driving,” and more.
schedule.title: Beyond the Pantsers and Plotters Spectrum (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Beth Tabler and Adrian Collins would love to have a chin wag with you about publishing Grimdark Magazine each quarter. Commissioning Editor Beth procures, finds, and contracts all the stories, reprints, articles, interviews, and book reviews our readers love each quarter. EiC Adrian is responsible for the logistics of the print magazine going through layout, to print, distribution, publicity and marketing, and commercials.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Beth Tabler & Adrian Collins

schedule.desc: Stan Sakai has spent more than four decades crafting stories that blend action, humor, folklore, and history into one of the medium's most beloved series. A master cartoonist, writer, and historian, his work has earned multiple Eisner, Harvey, and Inkpot Awards and inspired generations of readers and creators. He is joined in conversation by editor and comics historian Scott Dunbier, to take us through his career, his inspirations, and his iconic creation of wandering ronin Usagi Yojimbo.
schedule.title: Stan Sakai: A Comics Legend in Conversation

schedule.desc: The creation and meaning of tattoos in genre art and in fictional cultures can serve to enrich an image or a story. Our panelists will also discuss the use of genre symbols in tattoos as community signifiers.
schedule.title: The Role of Tattoos and Tattooing in SFF

schedule.desc: Running a Worldcon takes a lot of time. It is true in both the time span of the work and the actual amount of it. This endeavor can take even a decade from the initial idea to the end of a convention, and it happens in addition to our usual lives. How can we survive on such journey, and come out of it with happiness and satisfaction and not a burnout?
schedule.title: The 13th Labor of Hercules: Surviving Working on a Worldcon

schedule.desc: Why did we get social media instead of five hour workweeks as technology advanced? Where is the leisure the Jetsons promised? These authors all have opinions they can't wait to share.
schedule.title: Science Fiction and The Economics of Technology

schedule.desc: Robert Jackson Bennett writes genre-mixing secondary world fantasy with a strong focus on character, theme, and worldbuilding. Do you want to talk about why people flock to legalistic, loophole-riddled magic systems, but absolutely loathe "beams of light shooting out of my hands" powers? Or do you want to discuss why certain characters stick with you long after you forget where they were or what they did? Then you've come to the right place!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Robert Jackson Bennett

schedule.desc: You've completed your 2D or 3D masterpiece or maybe just printed another copy of something that's in demand, and now it's time to ship it to the customer. What are the cost-effective strategies and techniques for making sure that it arrives undamaged? What are your shipping horror stories?
schedule.title: Ship It Safely

schedule.desc: The term “bleed” means that we identify with our characters in roleplays and mix our emotions with theirs. Yet, as James D’Amato notes in The Ultimate RPG Gameplay Guide, sometimes the most interesting moments in fiction come from characters’ failures. In this workshop we’ll explore how to separate player from character and really put our characters through the ringer in the name of good play!
schedule.title: Playing to Fail: Interesting Decisions in TTRPGs

schedule.desc: Join Guest of Honor Colleen Doran for a guided docent tour of her exhibit in the Art Show.
schedule.title: Art Show Docent Tour: Colleen Doran

schedule.desc: Mythology exists in all areas of the world. How do you respectfully retell a myth? What if the myth is not from your culture? Is there a way to retell a story while also being respectful to it's origin? How do you avoid cultural appropriation? Can you? Panelists discuss this sensitive topic and how they've approached the topic in the past.
schedule.title: Respectful Retellings

schedule.desc: Fans of the books and the television show are invited to meet up and socialize!
schedule.title: Geek Out About: The Expanse

schedule.desc: When re-creating a look from visual media, costumers can reference a wealth of images to put together an ensemble. But what about when the source material is the written word? Panelists will discuss how they approach designing a costume from written descriptions, successful adaptations they've created or seen from others, and characters still on their costuming wish list.
schedule.title: Fashioning Words: Creating Costumes Based on Books

schedule.desc: Poet Brian U. Garrison finds honeybush tea preferable to rooibos, Ceylon (Sri Lankan) cinnamon > cassia, Ceres > Pluto, Jupiter > any exoplanet, hammer dulcimer > harp > ukulele, time travel > staying put, ultimate frisbee > soccer, polka dots > stripes, antifascism > authoritarianism. Is it (nearly) all personal preference? Probably, but we can still talk about it! Tell him about your favorite musical, vegan recipe, or neuroscience factoid.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Brian U. Garrison

schedule.desc: Muay Thai is the national martial art of Thailand and one of the fastest-growing combat sports in the world. Learn the basics of stance, footwork, and basic strikes with author and Muay Thai coach Marshall J. Moore in this safe, fun introductory class! Participants should wear comfortable athletic clothing and be able to perform moderate exercise. There will be no physical contact between participants.
schedule.title: Introduction to Muay Thai

schedule.desc: One of the oldest poetic forms is having resurgence, this beginner level workshop will cover the history of the sonnet, analyze examples of contemporary sonnets, and provide a generative prompt for a first draft.
schedule.title: Try a Sonnet!

schedule.desc: Kids who play video games also express interest in creating their own video games. This panel for kids will help give them some ideas on how they can take their ideas and turn them into stories that would make a good video game.
schedule.title: How to Write Stories for Video Games

schedule.desc: Since their modern forms emerged in Japan in the last century, anime and manga have become a global phenomenon, whose influence can be found in every corner of genre fiction today. Panelists will discuss the influence of manga and anime on their own work and the work of others, and how both art forms continue to influence new generations of writers today.
schedule.title: Books Inspired By Anime and How Anime Inspires Your Creative Work

schedule.desc: For about as long as there has been science fiction and fantasy literature, there has also been science fiction and fantasy art. Our panelists will discuss the roots of this art, how it has grown and evolved, and who from outside the field has influenced some of the greats.
schedule.title: SFF Art History

schedule.desc: Love can be its own form of magic, and not all expressions of love looks the same for everyone. What can demisexual and asexuality representation bring to the fantasy genre, and how do these narratives reshape the genre’s approach to love, connection, and overall relationships?
schedule.title: A Deeper Magic: Demisexuality and Asexuality in Fantasy

schedule.desc: This panel explores the moral dimensions at the heart of any consequential work of horror. Beyond the moral collapse and contradiction at the heart of H.P. Lovecraft’s fiction, we discuss historic and contemporary works of horror in literary fiction, film and video, and podcasting. Why do some still love the Lovecraftian vibe even after we’ve lost our faith in the man himself?
schedule.title: Bring Me the Head of Howard Phillips Lovecraft

schedule.desc: In this session, children aged 6–12 years old will harness the power of their imaginations to construct a world from the raw materials around them.
schedule.title: All Kids Are Worldbuilders

schedule.desc: Come hear the Hugo Best Novella finalists talk about their stories and how they all worked at subverting the usual expectations in their respective narratives. Dark retellings, peaceful war robots, mysteries abounding; these are not stories to skip!
schedule.title: Subverting Expectations: Hugo Best Novella Finalists

schedule.desc: Lots of birders are also science fiction and fantasy nerds. Why the overlap? Join for a discussion of favorite bird facts, latest bird-related discoveries, and how to get involved in local birding groups. Depending on the weather, there may be a fieldwork element.
schedule.title: Birds for Nerds: An Outdoorsy Hobby for Introverts

schedule.desc: How do you turn the impossible into the achievable? For 30 years, XPRIZE has used incentive competitions to transform bold ideas into breakthrough innovations across climate, health, space, and beyond. This session explores how the prize model works and why it succeeds where traditional approaches fall short, and features an alumni panel sharing firsthand insights on turning ambitious ideas into real-world solutions.
schedule.title: From Science Fiction to Reality: The XPRIZE Model

schedule.desc: Artists, art experts, and enthusiasts discuss how to build and curate an art collection, how to keep and care for artwork from prints to sculpture, and what to think about when furnishing a space with art. So whether you have more prints than you have wall space or are staring down that blank apartment wall, this panel will have some guidance for you.
schedule.title: How to Start an Art Collection

schedule.desc: Benjamin Rosenbaum, who has lost a great many awards (Hugo, Nebula, World Fantasy, BSFA, Locus, Sturgeon, Otherwise, Ennie, etc.) reads his weird Second-Temple-era cosmically heterodox historical-mystical fantasy, "The Gospel of Barabbas."
schedule.title: Reading: Benjamin Rosenbaum

schedule.desc: Science fiction radio plays demonstrate how adaptations can expand audiences and create generational legacies for authors and their publics. Audiofuturism unearths how radio drama brought fantastic modes of literature and sound rooted in African American culture to new audiences in the 20th century. Through the analysis of radio adaptations, I will offer an account of radio drama that re-articulates the significance of race and genre in mass culture.
schedule.title: Audiofuturism: The Black History of SF Radio Drama

schedule.desc: Christopher J. Garcia will show some of his favorite films from the Silicon Valley Science Fiction Short Film Festival.
schedule.title: Best of the Silicon Valley Science Fiction Short Film Festival

schedule.desc: Sarah be reading from her upcoming novel, Trad Wife (S&S September 29). It's the story of a down on her luck reporter, who's been assigned to write a trad wife hit piece. But the longer she stays on Black Swan Farm, the further her investigation takes her into the uncanny.
schedule.title: Reading: Sarah Langan

schedule.desc: In the midst of perennial fears about the genre publishing world, speculative criticism is having a renaissance. There’s an ever-increasing number of popular and academic writing that takes speculative fiction seriously. They are new and old and have an increasingly broad audience. Our panelists talk about trends, challenges, and themes in the reviewing and criticism scene, and share some of their favorite topics, writers, and venues.
schedule.title: A Golden Age of Speculative Criticism (Virtual)

schedule.desc: This applies to new authors seeking traditional publication as well as to indie authors. Getting feedback on your story prior to pitching, submitting, and publishing is necessary, even vital. Panelists will define alpha readers, beta readers, other people who give you feedback, and the benefits they offer. How do you choose the right people to help you? What happens when your beta readers insist you're great, but nothing sells?
schedule.title: Alpha, Beta, ARC Readers, and Editors: Know the Differences

schedule.desc: We're living in "interesting" times: between climate change, political upheavals, pandemics, AI, and, soon, quantum computing, what's a fan to do? How do we talk about this time of polycrisis? For example, do we prioritize political action or climate action, or try to make whatever we do do double duty? Is this as bad as it feels? How can we frame our thinking to pull a positive future that we want to live in out of these troubling times?
schedule.title: Polycrisis: Living Through Many Challenges At Once

schedule.desc: Children's Programming Staff Members will take the kids with parents/guardians through the Art Show. We might bump into members of the Adventurers Club and have a spot for the kids to collect a stamps for their Adventurers Club Passports.
schedule.title: Kids Tour of the Art Show

schedule.desc: Imagine a D&D group of one thousand people. How do you tell stories for such large, active groups of people and what do we learn about storytelling from such events? Join Stewart Hotston, author and owner of one of the United Kingdom’s largest LARPs, as he talks about what their writing teams have learned about story telling from running their games and why romance remains an essential part of what’s important.
schedule.title: Worldbuilding for Thousands: What LARP Tells Us About Storytelling, Agency and Romance

schedule.desc: Are you someone who plays tabletop RPGs and would like to get better at improvisation at the table? Whether you’re a seasoned GM or a newer player, this workshop is for you.
schedule.title: Improvisation for the Tabletop Gamer

schedule.desc: Trip Galey is a writer, an editor, a (very smol) publisher, and a researcher obsessed with bargains, deals, and agreements of a fairy nature. Come along to chat about fairy tales and fantastic fiction, 80s SFF, writing and publishing while queer, worldbuilding, the power of stories, tea addiction, growing up on the rodeo circuit, collaborative writing, and a plethora of other random stuff!
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Trip Galey

schedule.desc: Hugo finalist editors discuss the often-invisible craft behind great books. Challenging myths about “fixing” authorial voice, they explore how editors guide rather than rewrite, contributing far beyond the page. From shaping projects to navigating publishing realities, this panel asks: how do we recognise excellence in a role defined by subtlety? What myths would they dispel?
schedule.title: Stet or Cut? The Invisible Craft of the Editor

schedule.desc: This panel introduces participants to two story structures: Kishotenketsu, the four-part Asian narrative, and the Fictean Curve, the three-part narrative used in mystery and pulp fiction. Time permitting, we’ll bring those into discussion with the “Hollywood 8” paradigm shift in film storytelling!
schedule.title: Beyond Save the Cat: Alternative Story Structures for Adventurous Writers

schedule.desc: From armored rabbits mounted on snails to scribbled pointing hands, what's going on in the margins of medieval manuscripts? Join our panelists as they discuss the many forms of marginalia, including doodles and notes, and why it still has such enduring appeal today.
schedule.title: Medieval Marginalia

schedule.desc: How will SF fans look 100 years from now? In this workshop, teens will write a short letter to SF fans and Worldcon participants in the year 2126. They can reflect on the hopes, anxieties, technologies, and communities that shape fandom today, while imagining how SF and fan culture may evolve over the next century. They will seal the message in a “Worldcon Time Capsule”.
schedule.title: Letters to the Future: Messages to the Fans of 2126

schedule.desc: Come hear from the Hugo for Best Novelette finalists as they talk about writing stories for that hard-to-publish length of fiction. Do they choose the length or did the length choose them? How do they fit stories into that size while balancing complexity and story arc? What tips do they have for others who find themselves gravitating towards this form?
schedule.title: The Awkward Length: Hugo Best Novelette Finalists

schedule.desc: What is cozy fantasy? What elements and tropes does it use? Why is it so popular?
schedule.title: Cozy Fantasy

schedule.desc: Nearly all known human societies throughout history have had some form of religion, and according to a 2025 global survey, it remains an important part of the lives of more than two thirds of the people world. Panelists will discuss what religion is and isn't; how religions reflect the cultures that foster them; how to avoid the Evil Church of Evil cliché; and how to create interesting cults, sects, philosophies, and theologies within a religion.
schedule.title: Is Religion A Necessary Part Of Worldbuilding?

schedule.desc: Herbert’s Dune universe posed the Butlerian Jihad as a crusade against computers, thinking machines, and conscious robots. The use of AI (aka generative AI, LLMs) is built upon intersectionality biased power structures: there is no neutral thinking machine. We are in a time of real and justified rage at extensive damages, all badged as progress and efficiency. If we fail to govern AI, can we outright reject it? Should we?
schedule.title: Rage Against The Machine

schedule.desc: Many works feature intelligent non-human life, but often those characters are written as humans in disguise. They may have different physical abilities, but their drives and desires are basically human ones. Sophonts with truly alien motivations are more often off-stage or secondary characters, foils for the plucky human Main Character. But it doesn't have to be that way. What are our favorite examples of truly inhuman protagonists?
schedule.title: Truly Inhuman Characters

schedule.desc: Plenty of women and non-binary warriors have existed throughout history but they tend to get short shrift in literature. Listen to storytellers who have embraced these incredible people and have written about them or used them as inspiration.
schedule.title: Anything You Can Do: Women and Non-Binary Warriors

schedule.desc: Taking literature in one language and transforming it into a new work in another language is an art with plenty of tension and high stakes in terms of transmitted meaning. Come hear the translators and the translated bemoan and celebrate the pitfalls and powers of translation.
schedule.title: Translation Tightrope

schedule.desc: The Kingdom of Caid, the SCA’s Southern California branch, brings its fighters to Worldcon for live combat demonstrations. See armored combat with rattan swords and rapier fencing in Renaissance style, both at full speed. Between bouts, fighters share how their armor and weapons are made, how bouts are won, and why honor is at the center of it all. Stop by, ask questions, and find out how you can try it yourself.
schedule.title: SCA Combat Demo - Friday #1

schedule.desc: Queer people have often only seen themselves in comics through metaphorical stories, like Marvel’s mutants. There is a clamor for explicitly queer people to be included, and furthermore, included outside of tragic narratives and integrated into the stories beyond focusing on their queerness. Is there still a place for metaphor? What comics have queerness done well? How are comics unique in combining representation with metaphor?
schedule.title: Queerness in Comics: Representation vs. Metaphor

schedule.desc: Though the native people of the Pacific have often been erased or misrepresented in SFF, the indigenous groups of Moananuiākea, "the great expansive ocean," have long been storytellers. Learn how authors from Pacific Island communities and their stories have shaped science fiction and fantasy, and the ways that the ocean has influenced their works.
schedule.title: Moananuiākea: The Influence of the Pacific on SFF

schedule.desc: Taunya Gren is a long time actor, film maker and screenwriter who is also an avowed nerd. She'll get you chatting about movies (especially action films), what it’s like on set, herbal medicine, filk music, women in film, cryptids and the value of failure as the flip side of success. You may accidentally come away with a fire to be in or make film of your own.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Taunya Gren

schedule.desc: Let's look at the evolution of L.A.’s world-renowned entertainment industry, from Old Hollywood to the Golden Age to Disneyland to Tinseltown to Silicon Beach.
schedule.title: A Tour of ‘The Industry’

schedule.desc: Explore the psychology behind fear and how horror writers tap into primal anxieties. From cultural phobias to universal terrors, what makes readers' skin crawl—and how can we harness it in ways that are diverse, exciting and novel?
schedule.title: Writing the Anatomy of Fear: What Really Scares Us?

schedule.desc: Alasdair Stuart and Marguerite Kenner are a genre power couple who never met a medium they didn't love. He's a professional enthusiast, pop culture analyst, narrative designer and award winning voice actor. She's a lawyer and publisher of the Escape Artists Foundation. They've won several genre awards, write The Full Lid, and have been Hugo Award nominees 19 times. Come chat with them about why creating and liking things is awesome.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Marguerite Kenner and Alasdair Stuart

schedule.desc: Make and decorate a cape, shawl, scarf or create your own wearable item!
schedule.title: Capes, Cloaks, and Shawls

schedule.desc: As the meme says, the current titular trend of “A ___ of ___ and ___” is running roughshod through the fantasy romance genre right now. What other trends are running rampant? Which are on the rise and which are dying out? Panelists explore the ins and out of these trends.
schedule.title: A ___ of ___ and ___: Trends in Romantasy

schedule.desc: Hugo Award-winning fanzine editor Geri Sullivan welcomes you to her Guest of Honor exhibit space in ACC North. She would love to meet you!
schedule.title: In Residence: Geri Sullivan

schedule.desc: Inua Ellams, screenwriter of "The Story And The Engine" (Doctor Who) reads from "The Half God of Rainfall," awarded the Hay Festival Medal for Poetry, and a selection of poems from his first poetry collection, The Actual.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Inua Ellams

schedule.desc: J.R. Dawson will be reading from her Hugo, Nebula, and Sturgeon nominated short story, "Six People to Revise You".
schedule.title: Reading: J.R. Dawson

schedule.desc: We all adore writers who find a world or character they love and keep running with them, giving us fix after fix of narrative goodness. How do they do it? What keeps a series running? What keeps it feeling fresh and new while still giving us the comfort of the known world and characters? Most importantly, when is the next one coming out?
schedule.title: The Stories That Just Keep Giving: Hugo Best Series Finalists

schedule.desc: The Expanse is just one example of the Noir genre getting comfy in space. What other stories do we love that come out of this sepia-toned mashup? Who does it well, and who does it campy? Come hear from authors who play in this hardboiled world of crime.
schedule.title: Hardboiled Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Discover the strange alchemy between music and storytelling in this workshop run by The Write Song Podcast host Kat Kourbeti. Whether this is something you already do in your creative life or are new to the idea of using music as inspiration, this workshop will spark new insights and options to explore. Through guided writing sprints and group discussions, you’ll get the chance to explore the inspiring power of different music genres and maybe even come up with your next big idea.
schedule.title: Find the Write Song: A Writing Workshop With Tunes

schedule.desc: How do you write about places you both belong to and stand apart from—and how does SFF explore displacement, belonging, and identity? Come together with authors with immigrant and diasporic identities to discuss creating speculative fiction shaped by their intersectional identities.
schedule.title: Writing Between Worlds: Diasporic Influence in SFF

schedule.desc: What truly defines family? Join these writers as they unpack the meaning of family and the many ways we search for and discover acceptance and support in the absence of family by blood.
schedule.title: Found Family: Who We Call Home

schedule.desc: Come join other fans who identify as atheist, humanist, skeptic, secular, and/or freethinker for discussion, interaction, and community.
schedule.title: Meetup: Atheist Genre Fans

schedule.desc: Applying the academic definition of science fiction as thought experiment entertainment provides a new perspective on how the genre does, and can contribute to the scientific enterprise. This panel introduces the Science Fiction and SETI crowd-sourced bibliography project and the panelists discuss both the specifics of how scientists might use such a bibliography.
schedule.title: Science Fiction as Thought Experiment and SETI

schedule.desc: SF author Ted White led a panel at LA Con II in 1984 with this same title. Forty-two years later and it’s worth asking the question again. Today, historians, archivists, and fans preserve and share fandom’s past in many ways. But what is the value of fan history, and who needs it? Does it simply record it, or does it shape the future of fandom? Join us as we examine the relationship between modern fandom and its history.
schedule.title: Who Needs Fan History?

schedule.desc: Join Hugo winning Sara Felix in learning to make your own tiara. Sara will teach us beginner-friendly methods to create beautiful tiaras from filigree and shinies. Please note that this technique involves wire wrapping, which requires a measure of hand strength and dexterity.
schedule.title: Tiara Workshop with Sara Felix

schedule.desc: Join Christine Valada for a special conversation with her friend and colleague of more than 30 years: our wonderful Guest of Honor, Barbara Hambly. A master of fantasy, mystery, horror, and historical fiction, Hambly has delighted readers for decades with her richly imagined worlds and unforgettable characters. Together, they’ll explore her writing journey, creative inspirations, publishing experiences, and memories from a remarkable career in speculative fiction.
schedule.title: Barbara Hambly: A Life in Fantasy, Mystery, and History

schedule.desc: It's been said that any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic. But is it? Are advanced magic systems actually based upon "scientific" principles? Where is the line between them, can we tell the difference - and ultimately, does it matter?
schedule.title: Science vs. Magic

schedule.desc: Marshall Ryan Maresca, Cass Morris, & Natania Barron co-host the 6-time Hugo Finalist podcast Worldbuilding for Masochists, discussing the craft of creating sci-fi and fantasy worlds. Between them, they have a chaotic spectrum of skills and interests, so come nerd out about worldbuilding, historical fashion, food and cooking, oenophilia, perfumes, languages, spreadsheets, the publishing industry, running a podcast, or whatever else comes to mind!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Worldbuilding for Masochists

schedule.desc: For as long as humans have told stories, they’ve invented imaginative, often unusual, ones about the creation of the world: some divine, some demonic. We consider how writers have used, expanded, sometimes exploded, those stories in their own works. How do creators balance respect with invention? And what unforgettable detail from a creation myth has stayed with you?
schedule.title: Gods Did WHAT?! Creation Stories from Around the World (Virtual)

schedule.desc: John McDaid is a SF writer and singer-songwriter from Portsmouth, RI. He brings a Sturgeon Award-winning writer’s eye to songs. The New York Times described him as “a mischievous guitarist and vocalist with a gift for the inimitable phrase.” A four-time Pegasus Award nominee for Best Writer/Composer, his debut studio album Trail of Mars received the John Culkin Award from the Media Ecology Association. His music is available at https://johnmcdaid.bandcamp.com.
schedule.title: Concert: John McDaid

schedule.desc: Do you like dark academia? Do you like horror? Do you like the horrors of academia? Leigh Bardugo, number one New York Times bestselling author, reads from Dead Beat, the not-yet-released final book in her Ninth House Trilogy—a raucous tale of the occult set amid the very real secret societies of Yale University.
schedule.title: Reading: Leigh Bardugo

schedule.desc: See some up and coming filmaker's films, so you can say you saw them before they made it big. 2389: Coming Home (USA), Being of Problem (South Korea), Love Machine (USA), My Name Is Ringo (USA), Pishtaco (Peru), Tomorrow (USA)
schedule.title: Student Short Films

schedule.desc:
Your group of goblins is in trouble. You've totally beefed the job the Dark Lord gave you. Now you're gonna have to scramble to fix things before someone finds out! Accidentally shoot yourself out of your own siege weapon. Pull strange and dangerous things out of your pockets. Set the Dark Lord's summer home on fire... again. Have a blast in this silly little game of goblin hijinks!

Players should be 13+ years old.
schedule.title: ShenaniGoblins

schedule.desc: With more and more dark romance novels providing warning labels that read like a shopping list of harder kinks, this panel explores why they are flying off the shelves. What makes a dark romantasy a success? How dark is too dark? Come for the discussion, leave with a wishlist as these authors happily stare into the darkest hearts and find love.
schedule.title: Morally Gray in a Pitch Black World: Dark Romantasy

schedule.desc: A must for all aspiring authors, our panelists will discuss the intricacies of publishing contracts. They will talk about pitfalls to avoid, strategies to get windfalls, and other details about publishing contracts.
schedule.title: The Legal Intricacies of Publishing Contracts

schedule.desc: Funding for the sciences is under the most severe attack in decades. Thanks to focused grassroots action, some of the worst cuts have been averted. Come join The Planetary Society’s Director of Government Relations, Jack Kiraly, in this online talk to find out how you can effectively defend space science, space exploration, and NASA.
schedule.title: How Can You Help Save Space Science?

schedule.desc: Many famous creators came from fandom, and many actively participate in the community. At the same time, other authors prefer to have a distance from the fans. How those interactions work in different media? To what extent fans can impact the creation process?
schedule.title: How Authors and Creators Interact With Their Fandoms

schedule.desc: Carmilla Jo is a Bay Area cosplayer, model, and Masquerade Judge for WorldCon 2026. Featured on magazine covers, she has worked with brands including Adult Swim, Riot Games, T-Mobile and Penguin Teen. Writing as Jo Wu, her debut picture book A Village Made of Rainbows arrives in 2027 from Alvina Ling Books. Drop by to chat about cosplay, especially if you're a masquerade contestant!
schedule.title: Table Talk: CARMILLA JO

schedule.desc: What makes a magic system convincing? Panelists will dig into the craft behind fantastical systems, be they wondrous magic or impressive advanced tech. Whether you want tightly ruled mechanics, vaguebut mysterious forces, or sheer whimsy, come learn what conventions you should follow and which you can break.
schedule.title: Designing Convincing Magical Systems

schedule.desc: Writers have feelings and fears about AI seeping into our tools, bringing with it multifold biases and skills erosion. Like it or not, everyday writing software is being AI‑ified. Is Grammarly now too AI‑driven to trust? Is it okay to use LLMs for research or reverse outlining? The panel discusses the costs, concerns, and compromises being made when AI enters the frame - even with our unconscious engagement.
schedule.title: Generative AI and Writing: Navigating Tool AI‑ification

schedule.desc: It’s a in-person AMA! Marie Brennan writes series, novels, short stories, RPG adventures, and poetry, all across the spectrum of fantasy and occasionally dipping into SF, sometimes as one half of M.A. Carrick (with Alyc Helms). She also practices karate, plays tabletop games, loves photography and travel, drinks far too much tea, and goes weak in the knees for cats. Come for an informal, small-group chat about whatever you like!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Marie Brennan

schedule.desc: Akua Lezli Hope, a SFPA Grand Master of Fantastic Poetry, invites listeners into a shared field of imagination where Afrofantastic visions, consciousness, and connection are offered through poems from her recently released collection, Telepath and other new works that explore transformation and wonder.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Akua Lezli Hope

schedule.desc: Are you a big fan of D&D but looking to branch out into other games? Or maybe you tried it once and it wasn’t what you hoped it would be? Come to this panel and learn about the indie RPGs that are taking the industry by storm, from Alice is Missing to Mothership and from CY_BORG to Signal to Noise. This panel will discuss a range of indie RPGs, from solo and two-player games to epistolary games and text-only games.
schedule.title: What’s Hot in Indie Tabletop Role Playing Games? (Virtual)

schedule.desc:
The Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association (SFWA) will announce the 2027 SFWA Grand Master during a special fireside chat. SFWA President Kate Ristau will sit down for a conversation with the newly announced Grand Master, with a special introduction by Operations Director Russell Davis.
Join us as we celebrate the work, wisdom, and lasting contributions of the 2027 SFWA Grand Master.
schedule.title: Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers Assoc (SFWA) Fireside Chat

schedule.desc: Samantha Mills is the multiple award-winning author of The Wings Upon Her Back and Rabbit Test and Other Stories, as well as one of this year’s Hugo nominees for short story. Join her to talk about short fiction, long fiction, genre mashups, getting an agent, navigating debut year, or writing while parenting, while ADHD, while the world is going to pieces! Sam wants all of your reading recommendations.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Samantha Mills

schedule.desc: In this workshop, kids get to build their own fantasy worlds with help from world builders, song writers, and teachers. Facilitators will go around the room giving each person a chance to say one action they want to take - adventures that work like an old-style text adventure or modern-day escape room but as theater of the mind.
schedule.title: Fantasy Worldbuilding For Kids

schedule.desc: Microcontrollers are tiny single-board computers that can take inputs from switches and sensors, and output signals to activate LEDs and other electronic devices. If you want to learn how to add lighting and other digitally controlled effects to your projects, this is the panel for you. Our panelists will discuss the different types and brands of microcontroller, how to hook them up and power them, how to program them, (even if you've never done any programming before) and what pitfalls to avoid.
schedule.title: Getting Started With Microcontrollers

schedule.desc: For over half a century, Star Trek has entertained, educated, and surprised us with tales of daring exploration, scientific discovery, ethical quandaries, and hope. Our panelists talk about the enduring legacy of Star Trek, why it continues to hold weight today, and what Star Trek's new "class" is doing to connect the franchise to new audiences.
schedule.title: Star Trek Is 60!

schedule.desc: Create wings which can make any costume/cosplay magical
schedule.title: Wing Making

schedule.desc: David D. Levine is a Hugo- and Nebula-winning SF writer who's been active in SF fandom since 1977 and a professional SF writer since 2000. He is also a podcast/audiobook narrator, space technology and astronomy nerd, theatre geek, and teacher about writing, sexuality, and many other topics. He welcomes your questions on the craft of writing, workshopping, critique and critique groups, the differences between short stories and novels, the challenges of breaking in as an older writer, and topics ranging from user interface design to Napoleonic spacefaring technology.
schedule.title: Table Talk: David D. Levine

schedule.desc: Children's Programming Staff Members will take the kids with parents/guardians through the Dealers Room. We might even find a few dealers who are members of the Adventurers Club and have stops for the kids to collect stamps for their Adventurers Club Passports and possibly a cool item.
schedule.title: Kids' Tour the Dealers Room

schedule.desc: Whether you are a midlist trad-pub author or self-published, being published can be satisfying--and frustrating. While everyone aspires to be that breakthrough author with millions in sales and hordes of adoring fans, the vast majority hover somewhere between midlist survival and total obscurity. We will explore the life of an author regardless of how many books you sell, and how to enjoy the process. We will also address the many activities you can participate in, and ways to showcase your work once you've published your first book.
schedule.title: Finding Satisfaction as an Author Apart from Sales (or Lack Thereof)

schedule.desc: If your entire society consists of nobles, soldiers, and peasants, you don’t have a world—you have a Renaissance Fair brochure. This panel digs into who actually makes a society run, the people who exist outside neat class boxes. History offers a vast array of social structures that can enrich professions, status systems, and character dynamics in fictional worlds.
schedule.title: Populating Fantasy: More Than Kings, Knights, and Smallfolk (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Janet Forbes is a writer, game writer and the co-founder of World Anvil, the 3.5 million strong worldbuilding platform with integrated novel writing software and role playing game campaign management tools! Join this table talk to chat about all things worldbuilding, World Anvil, plus her work on youtube/instagram, short fiction, and the Dark Crystal role playing game. Or just come to share your favourite archaeological site or dinosaur Janet has snuck both into every intellectual property she's ever worked on, including the post-apocalyptic space opera, Vast Grimm!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Janet Forbes

schedule.desc: Jewish culture and people have contributed so much to the horror genre. From folkloric entities like golems and Lilith, to novelists like Ira Levin and R L Stine, to the works of Rod Serling and Sam Raimi, the Jewish perspective is inextricable from the modern horror genre. Come and kibbitz with us about our favorite genre.
schedule.title: Jewish Horror

schedule.desc: Young adult literature continues to grow, as evidenced by the overwhelming support for the Lodestar Award. The Lodestar Award finalists will discuss writing for a younger audience, how these books came about, and what they have coming up next.
schedule.title: For the Youth! Lodestar Award Finalists

schedule.desc: Impact events are massive explosions powered by tremendous kinetic energy. In spite of this, impacts in the solar system are not only destructive events, they are responsible for creation as well. From the origin of the planets, to the advent of life on earth, to our current assessments of impact hazards to human civilization, this presentation by a professional planetary scientist will provide a look at planetary impacts for all space fans.
schedule.title: Planetary Impacts: Harbingers of Creation and Destruction

schedule.desc: Join us for today’s feedback session. This is the best way to connect with the convention organizers and ask any questions you have about the con. Your participation will help us to address current issues and capture new opportunities that we might otherwise miss. Your feedback matters and will be heard by future Worldcon organizers as well!
schedule.title: Feedback Session - Friday

schedule.desc: Make a starry night scene using watercolors. Allergy warning: latex in use.
schedule.title: Learn watercolor wash technique

schedule.desc: There's more to Doctor Who than what’s on television. You can read books and comics, listen to audio plays, and engage with multiple spinoffs. Let’s dive into the expanded Whoniverse!
schedule.title: A Traveler’s Guide Through the Whoniverse

schedule.desc: Our panelists will discuss how commercial art differs from other forms of art and how they succeed at creating and selling it, especially for book and magazine covers.
schedule.title: Balancing Art and Commercial Appeal

schedule.desc: This year we are celebrating the 51st anniversary of the first Australian Worldcon. Aussiecon 1 members, let's gather and reminisce about this fascinating journey.
schedule.title: Meetup: Aussiecon 1 Members

schedule.desc: As anyone who's ever tried to create something knows, the biggest hurdle is starting in the first place. How do you create and maintain the motivation to go from talking about what you want to make (armchair making) to actually building things?
schedule.title: Making Makers Make

schedule.desc: Where is the line between appreciation and appropriation? Join these creators as they share how they’ve navigated this question for their audiences within their own work, the mistakes and insights they’ve encountered along the way, and the lessons they’ve learned about writing to include while minimizing harm.
schedule.title: Cultural Appreciation or Appropriation

schedule.desc: Time to rally the Pokemon Go! players - make friends in game with other players from around the world and get reaquainted with players you have met at previous Worldcons.
