We can also touch base about any in game events happening over the weekend. We will meet in the lobby and then head out together to explore the area.
schedule.title: Meetup: Pokemon Go! (Friday)

schedule.desc: Imagine sitting in a darkly lit room and listening to horror stories. These stories don't deal with ghosts or monsters, but they are more scary because they deal with things that went wrong at conventions! We will share our convention catastrophe stories and, maybe, find solutions to them.
schedule.title: Conrunner Horror Stories

schedule.desc: How do we define 'voice' in fiction? Is it a case of 'you have it or you don't'? Does it come naturally, or is it something you can learn? In this interactive workshop, you'll explore your own authorial voice in a series of guided discussions and exercises through analysis to practice. (This workshop will contain short writing exercises but there is no obligation to share your work unless you are comfortable doing so.)
schedule.title: Finding Your Voice

schedule.desc: Many authors bracket the transmission of scientific knowledge from scenes of lived body experience. We live in bodies, we learn in our bodies; nothing known is separate from our physical situation in the world. This talk suggests ways to access embodied physicality while simultaneously communicating accurate scientific knowledge
schedule.title: Using Body Experience to Communicate Science

schedule.desc: From the bugs of Klendathu to the Tyranids of Warhammer 40,000, military science fiction often imagines enemies as beings unworthy of empathy or compassion. This panel explores how depicting sentient others as subhuman, as worth less, normalizes real‑world dehumanization. When fiction frames some lives as “acceptable casualties,” how does that affect the way we respond to real world conflicts?
schedule.title: Acceptable Casualties: Military SFF’s Empathy Deficit

schedule.desc: Writing Excuses is a fast-paced, educational podcast for writers, by writers. Our goal is to help our listeners become better at their craft. Whether they write for fun or for profit, whether they’re new to the domain or old hands, Writing Excuses has something to offer. Join our live panel for a half hour Q&A then a podcast episode with the topic chosen from YOUR questions
schedule.title: Live Podcast: Writing Excuses

schedule.desc: Join our panelists as they discuss writing about women who fight off the labels of hero and villain. They'll explore what makes morally complex female characters. They will talk about creating women characters who are not only willing to do whatever it takes to survive and reach their goals but leave readers cheering for them.
schedule.title: Ruthless Women: Fierce Women in SFF

schedule.desc: As book bans become more common and as reports suggest that publishers are avoiding certain demographics in fiction because they are seen as too “risky,” what does it mean to write characters whose identities experience erasure by gatekeepers, even when reader demand and sales encourage the opposite? How can writing serve as a form of resistance and what does it mean to engage in a long history of authorial defiance?
schedule.title: Authors in Defiance: Writing as Resistance

schedule.desc: Plagues have been used in literature since before the Bible. Now that we’ve seen one in person, how does that change the way we view tropes around illness and human responses to disasters? What stood up to reality, and which were absolute lies? How has this changed how we write about disease and disaster?
schedule.title: Epidemics and Pandemics: Truth vs. Fiction

schedule.desc:
Ellen Datlow has been acquiring and edited short fiction for a very long time, especially horror.
She's got a couple of cats, lots of intriguing collections of "stuff" and is willing to answer questions
about her life as an editor and most everything else.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Ellen Datlow

schedule.desc: John Wardale makes dozens of animals and other objects from long skinny balloons. These include dogs, dragons, giraffes, elephants, ninja turtles, mermaids, aliens, hats, motorcycles, and the starship Enterprise. He will teach us how to do balloon sculpting by helping everyone to make their own dog. (Allergy warning: balloons contain latex.)
schedule.title: Balloon Animal Sculpting Workshop (Friday)

schedule.desc: Don't know where to begin your writing, but want to explore options? Explore Storymatic with us, a card game providing building tools and ideas to help your stories take shape. (This is a workshop for teens)
schedule.title: Storymatic: Teen Idea Generating Workshop

schedule.desc: K-Pop Demon Hunters was an unexpected hit in 2025. Come geek out about Huntri/x, Saja Boys, and Bobby with other fans!
schedule.title: Geek Out About: K-Pop Demon Hunters

schedule.desc: A common criticism of both fantasy and science fiction is that the genre can be oblivious to the nuances of social class, and the way class influences how one experiences technological change or magical opportunities. Panelists will discuss the depiction of class, how the experience of class can vary from culture to culture, and the role of money, culture, education, and ideology in the experience and writing of class in SF and fantasy.
schedule.title: Social Classes in SF and Fantasy

schedule.desc: Effie Seiberg, author of the Nebula-winning and Hugo- and Sturgeon-nominated satire "Laser Eyes Ain't Everything" will read a few of her most recent short satires. Come for the lols, stay for the scathing commentary on current events.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Effie Seiberg

schedule.desc: Popular fiction often slots female-identifying characters into one of the traditional three stages of womanhood: maiden, mother or crone, missing the decade-long span between mother and crone. We explore this phase, discover its insights into the universal experience of change, and explore how to create characters – not necessarily female or even human – who incorporate the natural chaos of this period of aging, loss and transformation.
schedule.title: Menopause as Template for Character Change

schedule.desc: Elizabeth Bear, author of the currently Hugo-nominated White Space series and many other works of speculative fiction, will read something brand new! It's a mystery that can only be solved by attending!
schedule.title: Reading: Elizabeth Bear

schedule.desc: A.T. Greenblatt is a Nebula Award winning writer and mechanical engineer. She has published over forty short stories, and has been a finalist for a Hugo, Locus, World Fantasy, and Sturgeon Award. Her stories have been translated into twelve languages, taught in universities around the world, and included in multiple year's best anthologies. Her fiction and essays can be found in Reactor, Uncanny, Slate, and Clarkesworld as well as many other publications.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: A. T. Greenblatt

schedule.desc: Does a dog know what Tuesday is? What would it be like to see in four dimensions? Can two people experience time differently? How might aliens perceive time? Panelists discuss how science or literature might help us understand alternative perceptions of time, and what works of literature have already done exactly that.
schedule.title: Time: Do People, Animals & Aliens Experience it Differently?

schedule.desc: It’s time for the workers to take to the streets (and skies!) to fight for their rights. This panel will explore how authors have used collective worker action in SFF. Our panelists will suggest some of the best ways to go about including collective workers’ rights in stories.
schedule.title: Collective Workers’ Rights Actions in Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: Spicy books come in a variety of spice levels, from just a smidge of eroticism to "I'm gonna need a fan". What are some workable rules for these various levels? Our panelists look at varying degrees of spicing books, and share suggestions for writers and readers alike.
schedule.title: The Scoville Scale of Spicy Books

schedule.desc: Thrones, dragons, and hedge knights, oh my! Join fellow fans of the ASOIAF books and shows for a lively discussion.
schedule.title: Geek Out About: A Song of Ice and Fire

schedule.desc: Odin will read Cat of Thunder by John Taloni to kids.
schedule.title: Story Time with Odin: Cat of Thunder

schedule.desc: Jeff is an award-winning artist, illustrator, writer and game designer. Jeff was part of the first wave of computer game artists hired in 1990, having worked notably for Electronic Arts for several years. He is also the creator of Jeff Sturgeon's Last Cities of Earth, a post-apocalyptic world jeff created, the anthology vol. One was released in 2022; a second is planned as well as a graphic novel with Jim Wright. Jeff is an avid outdoorsman with a film project underway, concerning unexplained events in a remote place in the mountains of northern CA.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Jeff Sturgeon

schedule.desc: AI is poised to change every aspect of democracy. Join longtime fan and security technologist Bruce Schneier for a deep dive into current AI technologies and how they will change how we vote, pass laws, adjudicate disputes, and interact with government at every level.
schedule.title: AI and Democracy

schedule.desc: More academics are studying transformative works and fandoms through the lens of anthropological and media studies. Who are the tentpoles of this field, who is doing the most exciting contemporary work, and where can we find their published research? How many of them are coming to this study with their own experience, and how many are studying us from the outside in? What insights can we obtain from their perspectives?
schedule.title: Acafandom: the Academic Study of Fandoms

schedule.desc: A meetup for creators with disabilities to be in community. Discuss topics, and address challenges faced specifically by creators with disabilities of all media.
schedule.title: Meetup: Creators with Disabilities for Creators with Disabilities

schedule.desc: Robin Hobb and Kat Ogden encourage younger writers not to wait, but to write their stories and get them out there now. (This panel is for teens.)
schedule.title: Writer Here, Right Now

schedule.desc: Over Earth’s history, five mass extinction events—brought about by vastly different causes—have threatened life on our planet as we know it. However, mass extinctions, and extinctions in general, remain rare in speculative fiction. This overview will cover cataclysms that wiped out up to 80% of all animal genera, current biodiversity crisis, depictions of life—and the loss of it—in SFF.
schedule.title: Mass Extinctions and Speculative Biology

schedule.desc: Sophie Burnham is an author, screenwriter, futurist, general queer menace, and finalist for the Astounding Award. Novels: Sargassa and Bloodtide. Come hang out with them to chat about worldbuilding, juggling 5+ POVs, the Roman Empire, your personal Roman Empire, films, screenwriting, Shakespeare, folkloristics, queer temporality, Marxist feminism, the specific aesthetic of the Owens house in Practical Magic, very good dogs, or whatever else comes up!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Sophie Burnham

schedule.desc: Solarpunk Futures is a card-based, rules-lite collaborative storytelling game where we imagine a better future together. The game guides players to exercise their roleplaying and creative thinking skills, dream big about the future, and then outline the steps towards building that future. Players will practice consensus decision making, learn from each other's perspectives, and perhaps even rediscover a capacity for hope. Bring a method of taking notes and an open mind!
schedule.title: Solarpunk Futures: a Utopian Storytelling Game

schedule.desc: Dr. Anita Sengupta has spent her career turning science fiction into science fact. A former NASA aerospace engineer who helped deliver the Curiosity rover to Mars and led pioneering space technology projects, she now heads Hydroplane, developing hydrogen-electric aviation for a sustainable future. Professor, commercial pilot, and lifelong SF fan, Anita joins us to discuss innovation, exploration, and her drive to boldly go where few have gone before.
schedule.title: From Star Trek to Sustainable Aviation: Dr. Anita Sengupta

schedule.desc:
Getting some herbs and spices sounds like a milk run. No big deal, they are offering you a fair amount of cred. What’s the worst that could happen? Join us playing this legendary game!

Character sheets, dice and pencils provided.
schedule.title: Shadowrun: Top Shelf Seattle

schedule.desc: From super fans to popular authors to legendary editors, women have helped shape and define science fiction since its inception. Leigh Bracket, Myrtle R. Douglas (aka Morojo), Edythe Eyde (aka Tigrina), Doris Baumgardt (aka Leslie Perri), Dorothy McIlwraith and more: our panelists will discuss the prominent female fans, authors, and editors of early science fiction and the role they played in creating the science fiction community and industry we know today.
schedule.title: Leading Ladies: Women in Early Science Fiction and Fandom

schedule.desc: Want to try your hand at writing speculative romance? Come learn the tropes and expectations of the genre. This class is for 18+.
schedule.title: Writing a Happily Ever After

schedule.desc: From drones to Big Dog, robots are being used as weapons of war. For example, Ukraine is using robotic soldiers. Foundation Robotics is designing the Phantom MK-1 specifically for combat. What is the state of the art of robotic war? How autonomously can robotic weapons act on today's battlefields, and what might happen in the future? What are the moral and social repercussions of robots at war?
schedule.title: Robots at War: Drones, Big Dogs and Other Robots in Combat

schedule.desc: Revolutions and resistance don’t just happen in the real world—they happen on the page, too. From dystopias to the magical, Latinx authors are using storytelling to show how imagination can be used to resist, rebuild, and re-envision what’s possible.
schedule.title: Latinx Worlds of Resistance

schedule.desc: Margaret Owen will be reading an excerpt from her Mythopoeic-nominated YA fairy tale heist Little Thieves, the beginning of a trilogy whose third installment, Holy Terrors, happens to be up for the Lodestar.
schedule.title: Reading: Margaret Owen

schedule.desc: In this workshop participants will enjoy facilitated discussion around the complex ideas around who is considered a hero versus the villain. Samples for this workshop will be centered around Marvel and DC chracters. After discussion, we participants will do a writing exercise focused on thought provoking story telling in poetry. There will opportunity for sharing at the end.
schedule.title: Grey Matters: Writing Poems that Nuance Heroes and Villains

schedule.desc: A panel on how to incorporate medicine into fiction. Whether it's sci-fi with a medical plot, a field medic in military SFF, or a healer in fantasy, how much hand-holding is necessary for the reader? How much lingo does the writer need to translate for the reader for it to work? How accurate must it be? How much detail to go into?
schedule.title: Writing Medical Fiction (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Come watch a psychological science fiction romance: The Living Tree (USA), directed by Anthony J. James.
schedule.title: An Afternoon at the Movies: The Living Tree

schedule.desc: From Gloomhaven to Blood Raven, nerds are passionate about a lot of things. Yet, there's one thing they love above all else: correcting people. Um, Actually presents you with statements about the fictional worlds of popular movies, TV shows, and books. They all sound right, but listen carefully, because each one has a mistake hidden in it! It's your job to figure out what's wrong and say it loudly and clearly and, of course, beginning with the magic phrase: “Um, actually...”
schedule.title: Um, Actually…The Gameshow

schedule.desc: Come create with beads! Make jewelry to wear or trinkets to attach to a backpack.
schedule.title: Beaded Creations

schedule.desc: Dystopias got you down? Let's turn that frown upside down with a discussion about humor in science fiction and what examples stand out in contemporary publishing.
schedule.title: In Space, No One Can Hear You Laugh: Humor in Sci-fi (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Have you noticed the flurry of activity on BookTok, BookTube, Bookstagram, etc. and feel like you may be missing out? How do you get your feet wet in these new seas of author-reader interaction? Experienced and newish creators discuss their own social media journeys and share their candid advice.
schedule.title: Being Social: Bookstagram, BookTok, BookTube, Podcasting

schedule.desc: Haunted houses, decaying opulence, and...cypress trees? The gothic can take place in many settings. Join panelists for a discussion on gothic traditions, reimagining them across diverse backdrops and communities, and breathing new life into a subgenre that will have you yearning for more.
schedule.title: The Global Gothic

schedule.desc: Angela Liu is a Chinese-American writer/poet based in NYC and Tokyo. She is a three-time Nebula Award and 2025 Astounding Award Finalist. Her work has also been nominated for Hugo, Locus, Ignyte, and Rhysling Awards. She previously researched mixed reality at Keio University in Japan. Come chat about writing and publishing short fiction/poetry, anime/manga, writing horror and SFF, living/eating in Japan, and worldbuilding across multiple stories.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Angela Liu

schedule.desc: “I liked it” may make the creator happy, but it’s not very actionable. How do you provide a kind but useful critique?
schedule.title: How to Give Dang Good Feedback

schedule.desc: Panelists will begin by identifying harmful tropes and then identifying the commonalities between them to understand what it means for a trope to be harmful. Do we all recognize the same ones? And how can writers and artists defuse or subvert them in their work?
schedule.title: Subverting Harmful Tropes in Spec Fic

schedule.desc: Humanity will eventually spread to the stars, but travel between these systems will take years if not decades. Is there anything that will be worth physically transporting from one star system to another? Will trade be exclusively in information transmitted at light speed? How will prices be negotiated, given the years-long delays? Will systems simply send information out there and trust that others will do the same?
schedule.title: Interstellar Life: Trade in a Sublight Universe

schedule.desc: William Rotsler is the name behind the Rotsler Award for fan art and Rotsler's Rules for Masquerades, but he also had a varied professional career as a sculptor, writer, filmaker, and photographer, with an emphasis on the erotic. What are the many faces of William Rotsler, and what is his legacy in fandom?
schedule.title: The Many Faces of LA-area Fan William Rotsler

schedule.desc: Join Guest of Honor Tim Kirk for a guided docent tour of his exhibit in the Art Show.
schedule.title: Art Show Docent Tour: Tim Kirk

schedule.desc: Intrepid cosplay adventurers have a difficult challenge: how do you get to the costume to the con? Join our panel of wayfaring creators for tales of prior travel and shipping exploits to walk away tips on transporting costumes of your own.
schedule.title: Traveling with Costumes

schedule.desc: Aspiring authors are bombarded with advice, guidelines, and hard-and-fast rules they supposedly must follow in order to be “accepted” by publishers and readers. At what point does well-meaning advice turn from helpful to demoralizing? Many first-time SF/F authors end up stressing about...everything. Let’s discuss these “rules,” and when you might choose to break them.
schedule.title: You Must Adhere to the Rules! (Not.)

schedule.desc: Hobbits! Elves! Wizards! Dwarves! Join us in Middle Earth, where all come together for a ball. Community-style dances will be taught on the spot, some bouncy and lively, others slower and lyrical. Come to the party and dance with us. Costumes, cosplay, and Middle-Earth inspired garb encouraged, but all are welcome to come as you are.
schedule.title: The Middle-Earth Ball

schedule.desc: What might the world look like if today’s boldest ideas succeed? This session journeys into a future shaped by breakthroughs in climate, health, space, and society—grounded in real innovations from XPRIZE competitions. From deep-sea exploration and planetary habitation to interspecies communication and holographic realities, we’ll explore the global challenges XPRIZE is tackling—and the breakthroughs that could help build a more abundant future.
schedule.title: XPRIZE: Designing the World of Tomorrow

schedule.desc: Carole Parker leads a dye workshop that teaches crystal wash. This is an easy-to-do technique where you stuff fabric or a garment into a container and get abstract patterns.
schedule.title: Crystal Wash

schedule.desc: We love good reviews and scathing reviews. What makes a negative review good criticism instead of troll baiting? What use is the negative review to writers, readers, and the industry? What do we need to keep in mind when reading negative reviews, whether focused on other people's work or our own?
schedule.title: The Value of the Negative Review (Virtual)

schedule.desc: We love good reviews and scathing reviews. What makes a negative review good criticism instead of troll baiting? What use is the negative review to writers, readers, and the industry? What do we need to keep in mind when reading negative reviews, whether focused on other people's work or our own?
schedule.title: The Value of the Negative Review

schedule.desc: Book banning is on the rise, along with widespread misinformation about what it is and how it impacts the book world. This panel will break down what book banning really looks like today, how it affects authors, libraries, publishers, and readers, and what storytellers and audiences can do to stand up for the freedom to read and the right to access information and the stories we love.
schedule.title: Stories For All: Confronting the Reality of Book Bans

schedule.desc: Are you a fan of Gail Carriger's Parasol Protectorate series? Join other fans of this world to geek out about it!
schedule.title: Meetup: Parasol Protectorate Fans

schedule.desc: Our oceans and seas span the globe and so do our stories. Join these acclaimed SF/F authors from a range of backgrounds as they dive into books inspired by water, ocean, and the seas both imagined and real. Let's talk pirates, ships, mermaids, swashbuckling, and the magic of water.
schedule.title: On Deck: Inclusive Perspectives from SF/F on the Seven Seas

schedule.desc: One of the pleasures of fantasy writing is imagining the sumptuous clothing worn by those with means. What are those means, and who is making the materials that go into the sumptuous clothing? What do the fashions say about the culture wearing them? These and other questions will be addressed by the panel, who will demonstrate how fashionable frippery is actually code for so very much about characters and their world.
schedule.title: Fashion and Frippery in Fantasy

schedule.desc: Kamilah Cole, USA Today and national bestselling author of So Let Them Burn and This Ends in Embers, reads from her most recent release, the adult dark academia romantic fantasy, An Arcane Inheritance.
schedule.title: Reading: Kamilah Cole

schedule.desc: The narrative tropes of living fossils, lost worlds, and last humans have long foreshadowed the contemporary discourse around concepts such as biodiversity loss, ecological collapse, and human extinction. This presentation delves into the enduring popular relevance (in science and fiction) of survivors, relicts, and revenants—particularly living fossils as remnant species, lost worlds as remnant spaces, and last humans as remnant peoples.
schedule.title: The Science and Fiction of Population and Extinction

schedule.desc: In the near future, everyone, including you, gets three months of Digital Life Extension. That’s three months to live digitally after death - unless you can afford more. ROOT is a Mixed Reality play, and you have the option of using your smartphones during the ceremony to view digital characters. If you don’t have a smartphone, you can still experience this play. You will need a newer phone running Chrome or Safari, and it should be at least 80% charged. There will be people to help connect you to the experience.
schedule.title: "ROOT (Running Out Of Time)"

schedule.desc: Magneto and Frankenstein’s monster make important points. Darth Vader and Jaime Lannister steal the show. Discuss joining the Devil’s party, and why it's something we explore again and again.
schedule.title: Join the Dark Side.

schedule.desc: Jason Sanford is a science fiction and fantasy writer on the autistic spectrum who’s also a passionate advocate for fellow authors, creators, and fans, in particular through reporting in his Genre Grapevine column (for which he's a finalist for this year's Hugo Award for Best Fan Writer). Come talk about Jason's fiction, the items he covers in his Genre Grapevine column, or about neurodiverse issues as they relate to being either a SF/F writer or fan. Jason has published dozens of stories in magazines such as Beneath Ceaseless Skies, Asimov’s Science Fiction, and Interzone and along with appearances in various “year’s best” anthologies and The New Voices of Science Fiction. His first novel Plague Birds was a finalist for both the Nebula Award and the Philip K. Dick Award. His website is www.jasonsanford.com.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Jason Sanford

schedule.desc: Flash is over in the time it takes to smoke a cigarette. Flash is big feeling mood pieces, experimental forms, or traditionally-plotted stories writ small. Flash is surprisingly diverse, as are the markets purchasing it. In this generative seminar, we’ll explore the expansive genre of flash fiction, unpack pro markets’ wish lists, analyze a few deep-yet-brief science fiction and fantasy stories, and set goals for our future flash projects.
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: Brief Illuminations – Experimenting with Flash Fiction

schedule.desc: The lower the budget, the more precious the penny. What you can do to get the most out of the least when making your movie.
schedule.title: Low and No-Budget Film Making

schedule.desc: What role does joy, optimism, and “coziness” play in speculative fiction centered on queer and trans experiences—especially at a time when these communities are increasingly politically targeted? Join panelists as they discuss what it means to depict queer and trans characters finding joy and coziness in stories within the context of our broader societal climate.
schedule.title: Queer and Cozy: Comfort in Queer SFF Narratives

schedule.desc: With the rousing success of MurderBot due in part to readers being able to identify with the 'Bot's neurodiversity, what other work has addressed the neurospicy folks and situations in a science fiction context? Who does it well? What are you tired of seeing? This panel will have a list of recommendations a mile long.
schedule.title: Uh-oh, Eye Contact: Neurodiversity in Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Join Geri in conversation with Pat Virzi. This will be a conversation illuminating how fandom can bring rich friendships into our lives, and how it can provide a framework where friendship can flourish.
schedule.title: Celebrating Friendship: Geri Sullivan GoH Dialog

schedule.desc: From the AT-AT walkers in Star Wars to the Jaegers of Pacific Rim, science fiction is filled with giant robots that are piloted into combat. Why do giant robots loom large in the imaginations of military science fiction aficionados? This panel will discuss the subtext offered by such stories, as well as the ways in which robotic avatars of individual combatants make military stories more visceral.
schedule.title: Mechs and Balances: A Philosophy of Giant Robots

schedule.desc: This mix of two genres has long been popular. Panelists will discuss how to plot a the SFnal mystery, avoiding the pitfalls of a murder mystery with SFnal window dressing, or a hard SF novel shaped around a murder, with robotically bland characters ticking through the clues with all the passion and emotional engagement of a desk clock. How to balance both? Panelists will offer examples of SFnal mysteries that enhance both aspects of the story.
schedule.title: Writing the Science Fiction Murder Mystery

schedule.desc: Quantum computing. If you know what a Qbit is, join us. Quantum methods are creating highly secure communications, and quantum sensors are improving medical imaging, navigation, and environmental monitoring. Science fiction still goes far beyond what is currently possible, but real advances in quantum science are already reshaping how we think about information, technology, and even reality itself. Let’s explore.
schedule.title: Sci fi or Real? How are Quantum Technologies Used Today?

schedule.desc: This workshop will focus on different forms of hair braiding: four strand “round” braids, classic (three-strand) French and (three-strand) Dutch (or inverted-French or underhand), crown braid (a modified three-strand French braid), and five and seven-strand fingering techniques. We might work on hearts, spirals and pullup-weaves. Which we use will be tailored to the desires and abilities of the participants.
schedule.title: Fancy Hair Braids Workshop (Friday)

schedule.desc: The concept of vampires has been around for centuries, most notably entering literature as Dracula in 1897. Since then we’ve had vampires with telepathy, shape-shifting, sparkling skin, garlic allergies, and more. How has the vampire evolved in modern literature, and what might still be coming?
schedule.title: Tasty Mortals: History of Vampires in Fiction

schedule.desc: A meetup for Black creators to be in community, discuss topics, and address challenges faced specifically by Black creators of all media.
schedule.title: Meetup: Black Creators for Black Creators

schedule.desc: Create a magic wand or sonic screwriver
schedule.title: Wands & Sonic Screwdrivers

schedule.desc: Fungus is fascinating: from the "wood-wide web" of mycelial networks, to the new psychedelic boom, to the fears of living decay and zombification, humans cannot get enough. There's likely more fiction written about mushrooms and molds than nonfiction, but science is catching up to science fiction. Let's talk about the real science, the fun fantasy, and the imagined horrors of these organisms that are already inside you.
schedule.title: Mycology in Spec Fic: Separating Fact From Fiction

schedule.desc: Elizabeth Bear is an award-winning author of novels and short fiction. She has taught at multiple well-known genre workshops. Come talk to her about art, cool science facts. horses, and anything else your heart desires (within reason). Ask me anything!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Elizabeth Bear

schedule.desc: Mona Tewari reads from her debut novel Burn the Sea. An instant Independent Press Top Forty Bestseller, Burn the Sea reimagines the life of Abbakka Chowta, a queen who ruled in South India in the 1500s, as she defended her shores against monstrous would-be colonizers.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Mona Tewari

schedule.desc: Gary K. Wolfe is an award-winning science fiction critic. His books include Soundings, Bearings, Sightings, Evaporating Genres, The Known and the Unknown, Harlan Ellison (with Ellen Weil), and American Science Fiction: Nine Classic Novels of the 1950s. His lecture series How Great Science Fiction Works is available from The Great Courses, his reviews appear in Locus magazine, and he co-hosts the Coode Street Podcast with Jonathan Strahan.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Gary K Wolfe

schedule.desc: Tap into the narrative patterns that echo through ancient epics and modern blockbusters to bring your story to life. Whether you’re a planner, seat-of-your-pants write, or battling your way through revisions, this workshop (for teens) offers guideposts for building plots that deliver satisfying narratives, dynamic character arcs, and compelling themes. Learn to incorporate different formats, from the hero’s cycle to four-act beat sheets and more!
schedule.title: And Then What? Plotting for Planners, Pantsers, and Revisers

schedule.desc: Though advances in technology have brought us closer than ever to the kind of future envisioned in the Star Trek franchise, soaring economic inequality, climate change, illegal wars, ideological extremism and polarization makes that future feel further and further away every day. Panelists will discuss how we might still be able to get to a society like Star Trek’s from here.
schedule.title: Can We Still Build Star Trek’s Utopian Society?

schedule.desc: There has always been an overlap between science fiction and crime fiction, because one of the first uses of any new technology is to commit a crime. This panel will discuss the growing trend of murder mystery in fantasy, science fiction, and horror including how to integrate worldbuilding with a mystery, build narratives that satisfy a diverse cross-section of fans, and which are their favorite speculative crime stories.
schedule.title: Speculating on a Crime: Murder Mystery in Spec-fic (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Our panelists from different professions discuss the misconceptions and errors in the depiction of their coworkers in SF. Hijinks ensue.
schedule.title: What Science Fiction Gets Wrong about my Profession

schedule.desc: Artists race to create a piece of science fiction, fantasy, and/or horror art while the audience watches. The subject of the artwork will be provided The fastest way in the universe to have fun!
schedule.title: The 20 Minute Masterpiece Competition!

schedule.desc: David Gerrold began his career with "The Trouble with Tribbles" and hasn't slowed down for six decades. He won the Hugo, Nebula and Locus awards for his semi-autobiographical The Martian Child. He has been his son's imaginary playmate ever since.
schedule.title: Table Talk: David Gerrold

schedule.desc: Lavanya Lakshminarayan is an award-winning novelist and game designer. Novels: The Ten Percent Thief, Interstellar MegaChef, Intergalactic Feast. Come chat about world-building and creating believable cultures, futurism and sustainable cities, structural experiments and craft, game design, inventing fictional cocktails and music, falling down research rabbit holes, writing from South Asia, and more! Also fair game: comics, anime, music, travel, and books from around the world.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Lavanya Lakshminarayan

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss magical animals in literature for the kids.
schedule.title: Magical Animals in Literature for Kids

schedule.desc: Chris Kluwe is a former NFL player, author, tabletop game designer, musician, and troublemaker extraordinaire. He’s available to chat about reading, writing, but not rithmatic, or you can ask him about football, running for political office, or whatever else happens to be on your mind. He might even have a Commander M:tG deck with him if time permits a game or two.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Chris Kluwe

schedule.desc: What “fanfic” means has changed throughout the course of its existence. Where once it was all non-published media created by fans, now it has a specific inflection of being work that relates to existing media. How did this change come about? How has it changed how fanfic writers interact with the source media or each other in our community spaces?
schedule.title: Defining “Fanfic”: A History

schedule.desc:
Academy Award®-winning filmmaker George Pal transformed fantasy and science fiction in motion pictures creating landmark classics such as Destination Moon, The War of the Worlds, and The Time Machine. Earlier, Pal pioneered the groundbreaking three-dimensional animated shorts known as the Puppetoons. Join producer-director Arnold Leibovit for a cinematic journey through Pal’s extraordinary imagination, beginning with the visionary feature films that influenced generations of storytellers and tracing back to the landmark Puppetoons where it all began.

Using restored film excerpts, rare imagery, and behind-the-scenes history, this program explores the innovation of Pal’s animation techniques, the enduring impact of the Puppetoons on modern visual storytelling, and the lasting sense of wonder that continues to shape the movies today.
schedule.title: George Pal's Oscar-Winning Puppetoons (Virtual)

schedule.desc: The horror genre has a sordid history of portraying anyone on the margins. The villains and monsters have so often been disfigured or disabled, and the murderers are usually some nonspecific kind of unstable. It’s not only prejudice, it is also lazy, unimaginative writing. Let us get beyond these clichés and discuss ways that disabled characters can be much more than a collection of scars or a deranged mind. Yes, even the monsters.
schedule.title: Ableism and Horror: A Match Made in Hell

schedule.desc: Writing sex scenes is as or more difficult than writing combat sequences, as these authors will happily tell you. Keeping track of everyone's body parts and desires can require complex stick-figure tracking and even spreadsheets! Come learn the pitfalls and tricks to making sex scenes work well and keep your readers engaged.
schedule.title: Wait, How Many Arms Does That Make? Writing Sex Accurately (Virtual)

schedule.desc: What really happens between a first draft and a finished book? Editing is both a craft and a creative partnership. Join a panel of experienced editors as they explore how manuscripts are shaped into finished books and sharing insights into their processes. Discover what happens behind the scenes and why great editing is an art form in itself.
schedule.title: The Art of Editing Returns/Editing as an Art Form

schedule.desc: Join this relaxed space for podcasters at all stages to connect, share experiences, and swap ideas. How do you find your audience, keep momentum, or collaborate with others? Join fellow creators to discuss what’s working, what’s changing, and how we can learn from each other.
schedule.title: Meetup: Podcasters

schedule.desc: One reason The Expanse is beloved by so many scientists and engineers is that it just gets so many things right that it starts to feel real. Our panelists will weigh in on what aspects of the world of The Expanse are within sight of being real, and which are grounded in science but further away.
schedule.title: Could The Expanse Represent our Future?

schedule.desc: Ai Jiang, Nebula and Bram Stoker-award winning author reads from her forthcoming Chinese opera-inspired science-fantasy novel An Empire in the Clouds!
schedule.title: Reading: Ai Jiang

schedule.desc: If your entire society consists of nobles, soldiers, and peasants, you don’t have a world—you have a Renaissance Fair brochure. This panel digs into who actually makes a society run, the people who exist outside neat class boxes. History offers a vast array of social structures that can enrich professions, status systems, and character dynamics in fictional worlds.
schedule.title: Populating Fantasy: More Than Kings, Knights, and Smallfolk

schedule.desc: Censorship is rife these days, but authors keep writing anyway. Come hear from authors who have worked through censorship to share their stories.
schedule.title: ████████ : Writing Through Censorship

schedule.desc: We all know fandom is full of brilliant people. It’s also full of older people. How do older fans stay brilliant? Come learn about the neuroscience of aging and the current research about aging well.
schedule.title: Fandom Needs Its Brains: How Do We Keep Them Healthy?

schedule.desc: From maps of Narnia and Middle Earth to the solar system in Firefly, maps can strongly contribute to storytelling. What makes some maps more compelling and iconic than others? What basics of cartography should a storyteller or illustrator know in order to create a successful and memorable map?
schedule.title: Cartography in SFF

schedule.desc: Join these authors writing vibrant futurisms such as Afrofuturism, Africanfuturism, Taíno futurism, Arab futurism, Latinx futurism, and Indigenous Futurisms for a discussion on their genres. Let's dive into visions of tomorrow shaped by fantasy, humor, the absurd, and political insight, all while reimagining what the future could be.
schedule.title: Inventing Tomorrow: Futurism In Science-Fiction

schedule.desc: Are you a big fan of D&D but looking to branch out into other games? Or maybe you tried it once and it wasn’t what you hoped it would be? Come to this panel and learn about the indie RPGs that are taking the industry by storm, from Alice is Missing to Mothership and from CY_BORG to Signal to Noise. This panel will discuss a range of indie RPGs, from solo and two-player games to epistolary games and text-only games.
schedule.title: What’s Hot in Indie Tabletop Role Playing Games?

schedule.desc: This paper argues that Daniel Paul Schreber’s Memoirs of My Nervous Illness and Barbara O’Brien’s Operators and Things share a structural and thematic architecture with foundational fantasy series. This offers valuable paths forward for contemporary science fiction and fantasy writing and the role of neurodiverse writers and writing.
schedule.title: Atypical Phenomenologies: Secondary World Building

schedule.desc: Bring a current handwork project for a casual meetup of communal crafting and conversation.
schedule.title: Craft and Chat (Friday)

schedule.desc: Cecilia Tan, author of Bound by the Blood, reads from her recently published sapphic time-travel Chinese fantasy novella, The Mystery of the Bitten Peach (Neon Hemlock Press).
schedule.title: Reading: Cecilia Tan

schedule.desc: Joyce Chng, author of Wolf's Path, reads an excerpt from their Southeast Asian pirate fantasy Sailing The Golden Chersonese.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Joyce Chng

schedule.desc: African eco-spiritual traditions position forests as sacred, animate spaces shaped by ancestral presence and ecological knowledge. Historically, forests have served as sites of refuge and ritual, yet colonial and extractive systems recast them as exploitable resources and sites of “pagan” danger, erasing their spiritual significance. This research investigates storytelling as a method of reclaiming these landscapes.
schedule.title: African Eco-Spirituality: Reclaiming Forested Spaces

schedule.desc: Romance readers want that Happily Ever After (HEA) or, at least, a happy for now. But what happens when romance is blended with speculative genres like gothic, horror, historical fantasy, or dystopia? Does this create stories where that result may not be what the reader expects? Is it all in the ending or is romance the love we create along the way? Join an inclusive group of authors as they discuss how romance operates within these stories and communities, and whether an HEA should always be in the cards.
schedule.title: Happily Ever After: New Takes on Romance

schedule.desc: For years fanzines were used to discuss ideas, share opinions, even argue. They provided a vehicle for creators to express themselves - their passion, opinions, ways of thinking. Our panellists will discuss how fanzines were, and are, functioning as means of self-expression for editors, article writers, LOCcers, and artists.
schedule.title: Fanzines as a Means of Self-Expression

schedule.desc: Some people want to be on the stage...and some people want to run the show. Learn about what it takes to run an incredible Masquerade, hearing behind the scenes stories, tips, and tricks from experienced Masquerade runners.
schedule.title: So You Want To Run A Masquerade - How To Make It Awesome!

schedule.desc: A language which has lost its native speakers is called a "sleeping language". Other languages are considered "endangered". How do you awaken a sleeping language? How do you bring an endangered language back to a thriving language? Language keepers of the Navajo, Comanche, Arapaho, and other nations discuss the joys and challenges of indigenous language revitalization, including its impact on their own communities and the wider world.
schedule.title: Indigenous Language Revitalization

schedule.desc: Step into the shadows and ignite our imagination in our scary story writing workshop! Explore chilling settings, craft eerie twists and unforgettable characters in a fun space, but only if you dare. (This workshop is for teens.)
schedule.title: A Scream is Worth 1000 Words: Teen Horror Writing Workshop

schedule.desc: Margaret Owen is the New York Times bestselling author of critically acclaimed young adult fantasy including the Lodestar-nominated Little Thieves series, The Merciful Crow duology, and Disney's Rootbound: A Tangled Novel. She is also a professional yapper and would love to chat with you about writing for teens and adults, publishing with the Big Five, surviving her horrible cats, and more
schedule.title: Table Talk: Margaret Owen

schedule.desc: Do you like Critical Role or Dimension 20? Are you into D&D? Are you interested in tabletop roleplaying games? Join us for a live D&D adventure with author and long-time Dungeon Master Gregory A. Wilson. He will lead a band of intrepid explorers into the depths of a thrilling and dangerous adventure, interacting with the audience as they go!
schedule.title: D&D Actual Play at LAcon V!

schedule.desc: In this unique episode with your favorite Ditch Diggers, Mur Lafferty sits down with Ursula Vernon (T. Kingfisher) to explore a career that has successfully crossed comics, illustration, children’s publishing, fantasy, and horror. They’ll discuss creative choices, weird discoveries, convention stories, and the unexpected turns that led Ursula to be LAcon V’s Toastmaster extraordinaire.
schedule.title: Ditch Diggers: What Even Is a Toastmaster?

schedule.desc: Womanhood is an intersectional experience. Creators explore its portrayal in speculative fiction—from wrongs, rights, rage, and redefinitions of strength to aging, bodily change, and beauty standards. They will discuss how womanhood is experienced inclusively across diverse identities and backgrounds, and how creators can confidently depict honest experiences beyond what is framed as “normative.”
schedule.title: Womanhood in the Speculative

schedule.desc: It's important to have a place to put things. Our panel will discuss a brief history of pockets, why women's clothing is so often missing them, and practical ideas on adding pockets into your outfits.
schedule.title: Thanks, It Has Pockets!

schedule.desc: How exactly should you set up your will before you join the ranks of the undead? Or, exactly how long can you collect your pension after becoming a lich? Bring your burning legal questions to our panel of experts, and we'll take you through all the permutations to the lawyer's favorite answer: it depends.
schedule.title: Werewolf Torts And Undead Tax Liabilities

schedule.desc: Writing sex scenes is as or more difficult than writing combat sequences, as these authors will happily tell you. Keeping track of everyone's body parts and desires can require complex stick-figure tracking and even spreadsheets! Come learn the pitfalls and tricks to making sex scenes work well and keep your readers engaged.
schedule.title: Wait, How Many Arms Does That Make? Writing Sex Accurately

schedule.desc: Many writers find that writing trauma helps them process the world and their experiences. The panelists will discuss how writers can process trauma through their work.
schedule.title: Writing As Healing

schedule.desc: For a broader Worldcon audience interested in global trends, this presentation explores how strong intellectual property frameworks and creative industries shape economic growth, cultural influence, and soft power. Drawing on research from my thesis on the creative economy, this talk highlights why storytellers, publishers, and creative entrepreneurs matter not just culturally, but geopolitically.
schedule.title: Creative Economies Rising: How Storytelling Drives Cultural and Economic Influence

schedule.desc: While you’re waiting for that first “yes,” get yourself ready for what comes next: a publishing agreement. Learn the basic terminology, the elements to look for in a solid contract, and key red flags to be on the lookout for. Sure, legal language sounds strange, but it’s words, and words are a writer’s superpower. We’ll make it fun—and a little funny—so be not afeared! Empower yourself to discuss your pub agreement and advocate for yourself with editors, publishers, and—if you are so lucky—your agent and IP attorney.
schedule.title: Contracts 101: What You Don’t Want to Not Know About Publishing Agreements

schedule.desc: Lang Belta, created by Nick Farmer and Eric Armstrong, is from The Expanse, based on the James S. A. Corey novels. In this friendly workshop, you’ll learn to speak and understand basic Lang Belta, interacting with basic phrases and building your own sentences. You’ll leave ready to join a crew of rockhoppers, represent your interests in the Transport Union, or go dancing on Tycho Station!
schedule.title: Languages of Resistance: An Introduction to Lang Belta

schedule.desc: Two movies that will scare you and make you laugh. Dead Media (USA), Ding, Dong, Die (Canada)
schedule.title: Not So Late Night Horror Double Feature

schedule.desc: Heather is an author, blogger, and podcaster, focusing on queer and historic topics. Check out her Lesbian Historic Motif Project blog and podcast! Talk to her about her queer Regency-era fantasy series, researching sexuality in history, or diving headlong into geeky analysis of SFF award history.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Heather Rose Jones

schedule.desc: Food! A vital part of life and an integral component of worldbuiding. Panelists will discuss which books do food well, and why. Writers among the panelists illustrate how they use food to enhance their settings, which traditions they draw on, and how they invented futuristic foods. They'll also discuss how what characters eat or don't eat contributes to the world of the story or book.
schedule.title: Food in Science Fiction and Fantasy (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Where can I get specialized fasteners if I only need a few of them? What’s the best glue for my project? How do I work with this material? Which specialty retailers (brick-and-mortar or online) are hobbyist & newbie-friendly? Ideally, the panelists will collaborate to create a resource list.
schedule.title: Ask a Maker

schedule.desc: Robin Hobb is a fantasy novelist. We can talk about the sixteen novels in the Realms of the Elderlings, from the The Farseer Trilogy to The Fitz and the Fool Trilogy. Let’s chat about how to start writing now despite school, children, and careers. Or we can talk about the environment in fantasy and the real world. Gardening to feed your family, raising chickens, how real life affects what you know and write.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Robin Hobb

schedule.desc: Rachanee Lumayno is an actress, voiceover artist, award-winning fantasy author, avid gamer, video game writer, and amateur dodgeball player. Come chat about all things fantasy, fairy tales, gaming, or whatever else comes to mind!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Rachanee Lumayno

schedule.desc: From J.R.R. Tolkien's Quenya to Suzette Haden Elgin's Láadan, what roles can linguistic creativity, diversity and sensitivity play in the making of a compelling science fiction or fantasy novel? Join our panel of authors and linguists as they explore the potential of linguistics and language creation to expand the boundaries of our genre.
schedule.title: Languages and Linguistics in Science Fiction & Fantasy

schedule.desc: Fonda Lee is the New York Times and USA Today bestselling, World Fantasy and Locus award-winning author of a dozen books, including the epic urban fantasy Green Bone Saga and the new science fiction novel The Last Contract of Isako. Come chat with Fonda about the craft of writing, the business of publishing, favorite anime, food experiences, tea, travel destinations, and Kurosawa movies.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Fonda Lee

schedule.desc: We explore modern roguelike video games (Blue Prince, Hades II, Ball x Pit, Balatro, etc) and how they tell unique stories through repetitive play while generating deeper playstyles.
schedule.title: Roguelikes: The Art of Repetitive Play in Storytelling

schedule.desc: A meetup for neurodiverse creators to be in community. Discuss topics, and address challenges faced specifically by neurodiverse creators of all mediums.
schedule.title: Meetup: Neurodiverse Creators for Neurodiverse Creators

schedule.desc: The “Big Two” comic book publishers control 75% of the market and get plenty of attention. If you’re curious about who makes up the independent comics market and where you fit in as a fan, this might be the panel for you!
schedule.title: The Indie Comics Panel: The Big 25%

schedule.desc: Join professional creators of constructed languages (conlangs) as they share anecdotes, provide tips, compare constructed languages, and more. Meet Paul Frommer (Na’vi for Avatar) and Britton Watkins (Yautja for Predator) who also directed the 2017 documentary Conlanging: The Art of Crafting Tongues.
schedule.title: Constructed Languages: The Inside Scoop!

schedule.desc: Since their modern forms emerged in Japan in the last century, anime and manga have become a global phenomenon, whose influence can be found in every corner of genre fiction today. Panelists will discuss the influence of manga and anime on their own work and the work of others, and how both art forms continue to influence new generations of writers today.
schedule.title: Books Inspired By Anime and How Anime Inspires Your Creative Work (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Cooperation and collaboration are not necessarily what people think of when they think of board games, but both have been a key part of tabletop gaming in recent years. Four of the last five Spiel des Jahres winners have been co-operative titles. What makes us want to play co-op games instead of competing against each other, and why is this mode of play becoming more and more popular in recent times?
schedule.title: A Golden Age of Cooperative Board Games

schedule.desc: Guillermo del Toro's 2025 Frankenstein reinterprets Mary Shelley's 1818 novel. After more than 200 years, how have our perceptions of the themes and characters changed? What does del Toro add to the discussion of this classic work of SF?
schedule.title: Guillermo del Toro's 2025 Frankenstein film

schedule.desc: Do you want to include queer characters in your stories, but you aren't sure exactly how? What counts as good representation? What's up with pronouns? What does queernorm mean? What the heck is the bury your gays trope and is it always bad to kill off an LGBTQ+ character? Do you need a sensitivity reader? Is it okay to include characters—even main characters—who have identities that aren't yours? And how do we market queer stories--must it always be small press? Let's talk representation, starting at the very basics!
schedule.title: Queer/Trans Representation 101: Authors, Characters, POV, and Marketing

schedule.desc: Choose your own chose-your-own-adventure! Matt Youngmark reads a Chooseomatic book with choices made by audience vote, and the very first choice is which book to read; Zombie apocalypse bunnies? Superhero shenanigans? Time traveling dinosaurs? You decide! PG-13: these are written toward adults and safe for teens, but there’s drinking and stuff, just for your information.
schedule.title: Reading: Matt Youngmark

schedule.desc: Our Best Poem finalists read their nominated poems and have space to discuss them.
schedule.title: Recital: Best Poem Finalists

schedule.desc: How does a poet explore the infinite vastness of space and fear in short poems? In this writing workshop, you will get to learn about the blend of brevity and expansiveness in writing about our infinite universe and the ever changing landscapes of fear
schedule.title: Haiku & Then Some: Writing SciFiKu and HorrorKu

schedule.desc: Toxic Masculinity is a dangerous yet common trope in real life, but also in literature for reasons. Panelists will examine these reasons: whether it is biological imperative or cultural shaping, why it sells, how toxic masculinity turns up in various cultures, and the elements that push against it. They will discuss how writers can avoid creating yet more predictably toxic male characters.
schedule.title: Toxic Masculinity: Writing Men

schedule.desc: Tabitha Lord, award-winning author of the Horizon series, reads from her soon-to-be published fantasy romance novel titled The Dragon Dancer of Krysh.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Tabitha Jorgensen

schedule.desc: Rachel Unger is happy to write stories of both wonder and dread, whimsy and entrails. She’ll read a modern Gothic set in South Carolina, originally published in the Tenebrous Press anthology In Somnio. You can find more of her work at www.rachelunger.com. Oh, and tell your cat she said hi.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Rachel Unger

schedule.desc: Justin C. Key, a horror author who went to medical school, performs a dramatic reading from his debut sci-fi thriller that LeVar Burton called "stunning": The Hospital at the End of the World.
schedule.title: Reading: Justin C. Key

schedule.desc: If you are a fan of great art, you don't want to miss the Art Show Reception! Come meet the artists and talk about the wonderful work they do. Enjoy a convivial evening with fellow fans of art and other like minded folks in a relaxed atmosphere at the Art Show.
schedule.title: Art Show Reception: Meet the Artists!

schedule.desc: Superman is the character that inspired and launched the entire industry of American Superhero Comics. Why were we fascinated by him, and why are we still effectively in his orbit today?
schedule.title: It's a Bird, It's a Plane, It's the Superman Panel!

schedule.desc: What will Worldcon look like in another 20+ years? In this interactive workshop, teens would imagine and design the Worldcon of 2050. Participants explore how technology, storytelling, and global fan communities might evolve and what conventions could look like in a future shaped by AI, virtual worlds, and new forms of creativity.
schedule.title: Design Your Own Worldcon: Fandom in 2050

schedule.desc: Women who’ve found success in the space industry will share their experiences and talk about their many successes. All this in a field that can be described as the highest glass ceiling of them all with institutional misogyny. Our panelists will also talk about their tactics and coping mechanisms.
schedule.title: Women in Space

schedule.desc: Isolation has always been a popular trope in horror. From Gothic castles to rural killer families, it's just easier to terrorize characters if they have nowhere to run. From the open sea to the desert, underground caves to high-tech highrises, to outer space and beyond, this panel explores all the ways to isolate characters physically, socially, and mentally.
schedule.title: Isolation Horror

schedule.desc: What if the past had turned out differently? From Indigenous nations that were never subject to colonialist exploitation to revolutions that succeeded—or failed—alternate history lets us rewrite power itself. This panel dives into the craft and responsibility of changing history on the page: research, plausibility, moral choices, and what-if speculation that reveals hidden truths. We’ll look at how authors can balance creative freedom with respect for real people and cultures, using the past not as nostalgia but as a living conversation with the present.
schedule.title: Rewriting History — The Art and Ethics of Alternate Timelines

schedule.desc: Join us for a pub quiz as Dave O’Neill prepares the questions. Either come in a team of your own or we’ll help you find a team to join!
schedule.title: Pub quiz

schedule.desc: Fandom’s favourite mixologist Tammy Coxen is known for leading cocktail crawls at conventions. Now she'll take you on one through Worldcon history! You'll time travel to past Worldcon locations to learn about the history and stories of the famous cocktails and spirits that come from those places.
schedule.title: The Cocktail History of Worldcon

schedule.desc: From a corner in a one-bedroom apartment to a 1000+ square foot industrial workshop, our panelists will discuss how to safely set up a space for whatever you're trying to make, whether it's 2D art or 3D art.
schedule.title: Making Space for Making

schedule.desc: Latinx creatives discuss the pressure they feel to create in English and the challenges they face in creating Latinx-themed art, film, books, and other projects.
schedule.title: Being Latinx and Creative in an English-Speaking Medium

schedule.desc: Understandings of what justice is, what it means, and how to systematize it, varies across cultures past and present. From anarchistic to restorative, collective to corportate, there have been a wide variety of justice systems portrayed throughout science fiction books and media. This panel explores justice systems in science fiction and fantasy that may be very different from the ones we see in societies today.
schedule.title: Justice Systems in SFF

schedule.desc: Fanfic often centers erotic escapism - and that's a feature, not a bug! Let's discuss the power of exploring sexuality & eroticism, physical vulnerability & emotional intimacy, and the wild imaginative catalysis happening in fanfic. What kinds of new subgenres and tropes have arisen in these fandoms? Whose desires are being collectively nurtured in these spaces, and is there room for them to become even more radical and inclusive?
schedule.title: Why is Fanfic So Sexy?

schedule.desc: Somto Ihezue, Locus Award winner and Nebula, Ignyte, and British Fantasy Award finalist, reads from his forthcoming novelette, When Trees Laugh, It Sounds Like This.
schedule.title: Reading: Somto Ihezue

schedule.desc: Please join us for an egalitarian, Kabbalt Shabbat with singing and both traditional and non-traditional tunes.
schedule.title: Shabbat Services

schedule.desc: If you identify as a goth and want to meet other SFF fans who are also goths, this is the meetup for you!
schedule.title: Meetup: Goths

schedule.desc: Dystopias got you down? Let's turn that frown upside down with a discussion about humor in science fiction and what examples stand out in contemporary publishing.
schedule.title: In Space, No One Can Hear You Laugh: Humor in Sci-fi

schedule.desc: I’ve been a published writer since 1964. Anthropic owes me awesome money. If you read me you know me. I do love to talk shop, but I also listen.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Larry Niven

schedule.desc: One core notion in fantasy is a hero confronting the supernatural, demanding a better deal. From Gilgamesh and Odysseus to Faust and Daniel Webster, fascinating characters tried arguing with fate or divine will…or the Devil. In The Escape, David Brin serves up a modernist, sci-fi’ish – and fun – update of that theme, along with fresh takes on Genesis and Babel, destiny and randomness, reshuffling the deck and challenging the Grand Order of Things.
schedule.title: The Escape: A Confrontation on Four Scenes

schedule.desc: Learn how Paul Frommer created the language we know today as Na’vi for Avatar.
schedule.title: Creating the Na’vi Language for Avatar

schedule.desc: There are some who think of classic films from Hollywood's golden age and earlier as creaky and old-fashioned, if not irrelevant to today's world. They should think again: there's a lot of subtext, hidden messages and neurodivergent representation in some of those films that may not be obvious to most viewers – but which can speak to those who are frequently "othered". Let's examine which classic films do this well.
schedule.title: Outsider Representation in Classic Films

schedule.desc: Take a walk down memory lane as we review Guy Lillian’s long journey through fandom. Well known as a letter-writing comics fan, Guy discovered west coast science fiction fandom in his college years, followed by northeast and southern fandoms. He started personal and general fanzines that ultimately garnered multiple Hugo nominations, serving as a DUFF delegate along the way. Come share your stories about Guy!
schedule.title: Memorial Panel for Guy H. Lillian III

schedule.desc: In the 1930s and 1940s, some science fiction fans saw their hobby as more than escapism. They treated it as a space for political expression and engagement. This panel explores an anti-fascist movement within early fandom, tracing the debates among the Futurians in New York and their uneasy dialogue with Los Angeles fans. Join us as we explore how activism, ideology, and community intersected in the genre's formative years.
schedule.title: The Anti-Fascist Science Fiction Fan Movement of the 1930s

schedule.desc: Henry Spencer is a software guy who managed to wander into satellite engineering. In his all-software days, he was one of the pioneers of open-source software. Notably, he wrote the first freely-redistributable library for "regular expressions" (text pattern-matching), and its descendants and derivatives are numerous; there is probably at least one in your computer today. Nowadays, he writes more specialized code that is running on dozens of satellites in orbit, and also works in satellite design. He has broader interests in a wide range of science and technology, including spaceflight history, military aviation, pre-computer computing, and battleships.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Henry Spencer

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss the ins and outs of switching hats between author and editor: if you are a writer but editing an anthology, should you include your own work? If so, who will edit it? Editors often serve as gatekeepers, requiring certain changes for a work to be published. How do writer-editors handle communication with a fellow author who disagrees with edits for an indie-pubbed anthology? This and other related questions will be discussed.
schedule.title: Switching Hats Between Author and Editor

schedule.desc: Blending history, mythology, and magic can be an award winning combination. This panel will discuss mixing research with imagination, turning legends into magic systems, and exploring the responsibilities and freedom of East and South East Asian authors writing fantasy inspired by the nations of Eastern and South East Asia.
schedule.title: Reimagining the Dragon: Fantasy Worlds of East and SE Asia

schedule.desc: A lot of fannish history was, and still is, passed through word of mouth. Yet there are many individuals who research the history and preserve it in a more substantial way. Those may be fanzines, books, academic research, portals archiving the older works, preservation of artifacts, and more. How is all of this done? How each of us can engage in both research and preservatio of fannish history?
schedule.title: Researching and Preserving the Fannish History

schedule.desc: Do you prefer the slow burn or the hotter than hot? These high-spice romantasy authors are here to discuss why they embrace an open door policy for their characters and never shy away from the chance to bare it all.
schedule.title: When Yearning Isn't Enough: Open Door Scenes in Romantasy

schedule.desc: In most of its guises over geologic history, Earth has been more alien than most authors' "alien" planets! Come learn from geologists how Earth through all its eras can inspire strange new worlds.
schedule.title: The Most Alien Planet: The Ancient Earth

schedule.desc: Tia Tashiro writes and reads science fiction and fantasy of all sorts. Stop by to talk about the ins and outs of short fiction craft and publishing, the behind-the-scenes process of stories like “The Temporary Murder of Thomas Monroe”, or anything else, from World Cup opinions to best road trip songs. Or learn about the inkless pen drawing challenge, how to make a playing card disappear, or how to roll a coin over your knuckles (coin provided).
schedule.title: Table Talk: Tia Tashiro

schedule.desc: Shiraki Press invites you to join them at a book launch for author Ian Patterson, with several other Shiraki Press authors.
schedule.title: Book Launch: Shiraki Press

schedule.desc: Geoffrey A. Landis writes science-fiction. He’s mostly known for hard SF, and is also a rocket scientist. As a SF writer, he’s won the Hugo, Nebula and Heinlein awards; as a scientist, he works developing technology for future space missions and works with a spacecraft design group at NASA Glenn. I’m up to talk about anything, but odds are we’ll talk about science and science fiction. Or maybe about swordfighting. You never know.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Geoffrey A. Landis

schedule.desc: Kylie Lee Baker, USA Today bestselling horror author of Japanese Gothic and Bat Eater and Other Names for Cora Zeng reads from her forthcoming snarky, anti-capitalist, haunted New York City apartment horror Hell to Pay.
schedule.title: Reading: Kylie Lee Baker

schedule.desc: What makes anime music so incredible? To find out, we take a soul fusion orchestra and play energetic music from anime, as well as the funk, hip hop, and soul that inspired it. Dr. Marcus Norris and South Side Symphony invite you to the Anime Juke Jam, covering classics from Cowboy Bebop, Samurai Champloo, The Boondocks, and more! Sing, dance, learn, and cosplay together through storytelling, live performance, and original hand-drawn animations.
schedule.title: South Side Symphony: Anime Juke Jam

schedule.desc: Rosemary Claire Smith, Sidewise Award-winning author, reads from her new book, Saurotopia. A scientist gave the dinosaurs life. The corporation left them to freeze to death. Years later, she returns to the abandoned space habitat to find the dinosaurs survived. One dinosaur remembers her. One trusts her. Inside Saurotopia, trust gets people killed. Can she save the species she gave life to? Or will she watch them tear each other apart?
schedule.title: Reading: Rosemary Claire Smith

schedule.desc: Brandon O'Brien, author of the SFPA Elgin Award-winning poetry collection Can You Sign My Tentacle?, Poet Laureate of Seattle Worldcon, and 2026 Hugo Award Best Poem Finalist, reads from their poetry collection in progress, tentatively titled An Outline of Injuries.
schedule.title: Reading: Brandon O'Brien

schedule.desc: Thomas Ha, Nebula and Locus award-winning author of Uncertain Sons and Other Stories, reads one of his dark short stories.
schedule.title: Reading: Thomas Ha

schedule.desc: Laura Anne Gilman is a writer and editor of multiple genres, with over thirty years of publishing scars. But she is also a history nerd, an animal shelter volunteer, an avid kayaker, patron goddess of MaltCon, and new-minted cancer survivor. Join the virtual chat (and bring your pets!) and learn about publishing pratfalls, the perils of puppies, and more, including why everything they say about GenXers is both true, and a lie.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Laura Anne Gilman

schedule.desc: Filk music started out with people getting together in a circle in some random place at a convention to swap songs. We're official now and in a larger space, but it's still the same supportive tradition of sharing music together late into the night. All voices, instruments, and styles including a cappella welcome . Come by to sing or to listen!
schedule.title: Friday Open Filk

schedule.desc: Hockey romance has taken the industry by storm, and bookstores are even shelving it in its own section separate from general sports romance. Everything from contemporary stories like Heated Rivalry to a whole fantasy monster hockey league, the audience is lapping it up. What makes this subgenre so successful, especially in comparison to other sports romance? Come find out!
schedule.title: High Sticking: Romance on the Ice

schedule.desc: Funny animal characters have held a history representing society and culture at a slant, but within speculative fiction, the anthropomorphic animal has allowed for authors to consider themes including difference, community, and structural inequalities. Join this panel discussion that looks at the furry fandom and anthropomorphic animals as they have allowed for cognitive estrangement.
schedule.title: Weird And Wild: Furry’s Speculative Mode

schedule.desc: In this classic panel game, our panelists try to speak extemporaneously for sixty seconds on a subject they're given without hesitation, repetition or deviation.
schedule.title: Just a Minute

schedule.desc: The Oasis is a calm, welcoming place where you can rest and recharge at your own pace. You don’t have to talk to anyone unless you want to. You’ll find simple activities like coloring, short readings, and self-care supplies. If you need something, just ask—we’re here to help.
schedule.title: The Oasis - Friday

schedule.desc: The Fabulist presents new books by three modern weird fiction masters. The Failure of the Century: A Play Concerning H.P. Lovecraft, by Nick Mamatas, picks apart the foibles of the influential pulp author. Bruce McAllister dissects the inconstant human heart in The Very Rare Thing: Tales of Yearning and Transgression. Reckoning's Michael J. DeLuca debuts The Paladin in the Forest of Thorns, an alchemical collection of ecofictions.
schedule.title: Book Launch: The Fabulist – Nick Mamatas, Bruce McAllister, and Michael J. DeLuca

schedule.desc: She erupted swinging from the same minds that created Hercules, and soon found herself standing on the broad shoulders of pop-culture giants like Wonder Woman and the Bionic Woman. How did this warrior princess redefine the role of the heroic lead, and how did she influence the TV we watch today?
schedule.title: How Xena Changed the World

schedule.desc: Emily Paxman, author of Fantasy Hive's Best Debut Novel of 2025, Death on the Caldera, reads from her latest novel, All We Have Left, a cozy, post-apocalyptic romance.
schedule.title: Reading: Emily Iris Paxman

schedule.desc: Latinx directors will show original short indie horror films (some in Spanish with English subtitles, some in English) for 60-90 minutes, followed by a discussion by the directors with question and answer session.
schedule.title: Latinx Horror Film Fest

schedule.desc: Nero is a Mexican/Panamanian cartoonist who has been working in erotic webcomics for almost 20 years. Join in to talk about the modern webcomic sphere, organizing for creators rights, censorship in the internet age, or just to yap about what pens we're all using.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Nero Villagallos O'Reilly

schedule.desc: Joyce Chng writes sff and things in between. Come and join them to chat about dragons, werewolves, cosy fiction, wrangling articles and fiction, fibre arts, plus other random things.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Joyce Chng

schedule.desc: An overview of the Quenya and Sindarin languages, created by J.R.R. Tolkien. Learn to speak a few words and phrases in the language of the elves of Middle Earth!
schedule.title: Aiya! Learn “Hello” and More in Quenya

schedule.desc: Several of our pros have stories set in historical time periods or have created alternate timelines for their work. Find out how they tackled the research, how they decided what to change, and where history might take them in the future.
schedule.title: Where to Start? Researching History for Writing (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Come learn how to make a sci-fi snack that glows! Elle Beck speaks both the international languages of food and Esperanto. Watch as she demonstrates how easy it is to use Esperanto and make a fun glow-in-the dark rice noodle salad. This bi-ligual presentation will be fun and engaging. As it is virtual, we recommend you don't come hungry.
schedule.title: Cooking in Esperanto

schedule.desc: The concept of a found family often emerges in the conversations about the first steps in fandom. It may be phrased differently including wording such as “my people”, but the meaning stays similar; many of us just "click" when meeting the fandom. We will take a look at that idea and we’ll try to answer questions as to whether fandom is really a found family and how this perception differs between the fans.
schedule.title: Fandom as a Found Family (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Explore urban fantasy and sci-fi inspired by Asian heritage and culture where traditional elements meet modern streets and futuristic skylines.
schedule.title: Heart of the City: Asian Urban SFF (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Susie Williamson is a speculative fiction writer, artist and poet. Fantasy novels: Return of the Mantra, The Warder. Come along to chat about fantastic inspiration, worldbuilding, and dragons; and/or representation of disability, gender, and queer in fantasy; or we could talk favourite authors, favourite reads, the power of stories, working across artforms, self-care, nature walks, cats and hedgehogs!
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Susie Williamson

schedule.desc: In this panel discussion, we will explore the profound and extensive psychological effects of fictional characters on our overall well-being. Often seen as negative influences, these characters also embody positive traits that we should recognize and embrace. By understanding and adopting these positive qualities, individuals undergoing therapy can see substantial improvements in their mental and emotional health.
schedule.title: Fictional Characters and Geek Therapy (Virtual)

schedule.desc: We've had a bunch of new Star Trek options lately, in particular Which ones feel the most "Trek-like" and which take the franchise in new and interesting directions? This virtual discussion circle will give you a space to express your opinions and engage with other fans of the franchise.
schedule.title: Geek Out About: New Star Trek! (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Dr. Tiffani Angus will discuss how the English cottage garden style represents a nation’s pursuit of identity during the long nineteenth century and into the twentieth. Through paintings, poems, and even clothing, this talk explores the history of the English cottage garden style and how it's based on a fantasy idea of the past.
schedule.title: A Cottage Garden Conundrum: Fantastical Garden Re-Creation

schedule.desc: This talk argues for assigning AI systems presumptive personhood. Brain organoids and AI models show us the potential of artificial cognition, but also the impossibility of defining self-aware sentience. Many commentators urge us to restrain AI in order to preserve what is distinct about the human mind. But, paradoxically, attempts to limit AI only narrow the sphere of what makes us human.
schedule.title: AI Personhood: Now?

schedule.desc: These writers express their love for speculative fiction and its community by writing about the genres, works, fandom, and more!. They may be taking an academic, fan, or fun lens to those topics. These Hugo Award Finalists for Best Fan Writer will talk about what it's like to be a fan writer, what kinds of opportunities exist for said work, and what they want to write about next.
schedule.title: Love in Words: Hugo Best Fan Writer Finalists (Virtual)

schedule.desc: From a podcast for Spanish language learners, Yana, of Colibrí Tutoring, discusses the book Yo, Bruja by Isidora Chacón, which inspired the Netflix series Siempre Bruja. The protagonist, born with gifts, learns to hide them to blend into society.
