We will discuss themes such as self-acceptance, intuition, dreams as a literary device, modern stereotypes around “witches”, ritual, and the magic found in each person.
schedule.title: ¡espaÑolismo! Spanish Podcast: Yo, Bruja – The Story of a Bruja (Witch) in the Modern World

schedule.desc: Worldcons started in 1939 in New York City. As we approach 100th anniversary, there are many stories to share – both good and bad. Back in 1939 we established Masquerade, but also infamous Yellow Pamphlet was published which led to the First Exclusion Act. Some years later we started Hugo Awards, that are with us till today. And later on… Yes – there are many stories to tell, so let’s listen to at least some of those!
schedule.title: Memories of the Worldcons Past

schedule.desc: This is a hands-on and interactive virtual workshop where participants construct detailed scenarios of positive futures. We will explore how to use worldbuilding methods to imagine positive, evidence-based futures with AI and other emerging technologies. Participants will learn to construct evidence-based scenarios of futures worth building by drawing on science fiction and foresight methods.
schedule.title: Existential Hope: Envisioning Real World Futures Workshop

schedule.desc: From the curious microscopic structures found in the Martian meteorite ALH84001, to the “canals” on Mars, and the WOW! signal; the search for life beyond Earth has felt tantalizingly close to success, only to be proven wrong multiple times. Why is the search so hard?
schedule.title: The Times We Found Alien Life... Almost (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Considering that you are all stars, meet at the hotel lobby for a leisurely 45-minute stroll around the venue. Get some fresh air, exercise, and chat with authors, editors, and artists in an informal setting. Hear about the interesting, fun, and maybe even unbelievable features of Anaheim.
schedule.title: Stroll with the Stars

schedule.desc: Ada Palmer reads from the beginning of And Loki in His Prison, the first of her new historical fantasy duology Hanged God's Game, based on Norse Mythology, which comes out from Tor Books in June 2027. Closely based on the original Medieval sources, and mixing mythology with real history, the novel weaves between the lives of the Norse gods, the giants, and the humans who live in the cosmos they dominate, focusing on the mystery of Loki's true nature and relationship with Odin and the cosmos.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Ada Palmer

schedule.desc: Henry Lien is a writer and writing instructor originally from Taiwan and now living in Hollywood, CA. His hobbies include writing theme songs for all of his books and losing Nebula awards. He is also the world’s leading authority on kung-fu figure skating. He also knows a lava-hot secret regarding author promotion for introverts and impostors. He speaks with authority on that because he is a painful introvert in extrovert drag who feels most comfortable talking about himself in the third person as demonstrated here.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Henry Lien

schedule.desc: Editors don't hate you. While the moment you open a critique and you find it covered in markups is never comfortable, editors are trying to make your work stronger. How can you establish a good working relationship with your editor? What sort of boundaries are healthy? When and where should you push back? Come find out!
schedule.title: Working with an Editor (Virtual)

schedule.desc: The children of LACon V make their choices of the best of the Art Show! Each child will make their own choices with the help of the staff, parents/ or guardians. Then as a group the children will choose the top three works overall which will be awarded the LACon V Kids' Choice Award.
schedule.title: Kids' Choice Awards

schedule.desc: What makes older women's "Heroine's Journey" unique and more complex than those of younger adults, and why aren't there more of them starring as wise, badass protagonists in today's Science Fiction and Fantasy? No more being invisible or relegated to the role of supporting cast -- panelists will discuss how now is the time for older women protagonists to save the world (or take it over, one reader at a time...).
schedule.title: Older Women in SF and Fantasy

schedule.desc: This panel is made up of neurodivergent panelists and medical professionals dedicated to writing neurodivergent characters and the unique struggles they deal with. Panelists will address writing ND characters, approaches for neurodivergent writers, and writers trying to understand and faithfully depict neurodivergence.
schedule.title: Writing Neurodivergence

schedule.desc: Science fiction’s past is preserved in libraries as well as memories. How did major SF archives come into being, and what unexpected paths brought writers like Philip K. Dick and Octavia Butler into academic collections? Archivists discuss what they collect, why it matters, and how fans can engage with and use these remarkable resources to explore the history of the field.
schedule.title: From Fanzines to Archives: Where SF History Lives

schedule.desc: NASA’s mission to Jupiter’s moon Europa is scheduled to arrive in 2030, and we’re all waiting to know: could Europa have currently habitable conditions in an ocean below its icy surface? This panel of scientists and engineers will discuss why we think Europa might have an ocean, and how the Europa Clipper spacecraft has been designed to study this moon in detail.
schedule.title: Europa Clipper: Mission to an Icy Ocean World

schedule.desc: Composer Nikhil Koparkar shares the process of writing this musical number for "The Wheel of Time" series.
schedule.title: Writing "The Hills of Tanchico"

schedule.desc: This workshop will explore a variety of “liquid magic” used on sets in Hollywood, including basic scenic painting and faux finish techniques. Participants will learn how to make false surfaces look real using marbleizing and wood grain techniques, and how to make a panel look like an old castle wall with aging techniques, and others. Participants may keep the panels they create. As a finale, participants will learn how to simulate a horror “kill scene.”
schedule.title: Scenic Art and Paint Wizardry

schedule.desc: Everyone has a geeky t-shirt (or ten) that they no longer wear. Bring a gently loved (no stains, rips or tears) t-shirt for this meetup! During this hour you can drop off your t-shirt(s) so they can be sorted for actual swap, which starts at 10:30am today.
schedule.title: T-Shirt Swap Drop Off

schedule.desc: Vampires have never stayed out of the spotlight for long. In predictable cycles, we see popular stories of sexy vampires, followed by a backlash of grittier vampires, then a brief lull before the media boom starts over. Panelists discuss why vampires have such staying power in the global imagination, some of their favorite vampire stories, vampires beyond the European canon, and lesser known bloody masterpieces you may have missed.
schedule.title: Vampires Never Die

schedule.desc: Ask folks whether Star Wars is fantasy or sci-fi and you will get a broad range of answers averaging to somewhere in the middle of the two. This goes doubly for stories like Gideon the 9th, and Dune. What's the draw of mixing science and magic? Is using magic in sci-fi 'cheating' or do we agree with Thor that any sufficiently advanced science can appear to be magic? Come join the discussion and bring your recommendations!
schedule.title: Midichlorians and Quantum Fields: Magic in Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Hear from the upcoming Worldcon (Montreal 2027) and future Worldcon bids. First up, the only bid on this year’s site selection ballot, Brisbane in 2028! You'll then hear from bid representatives from Dublin in 2029, Edmonton in 2030, Texas in 2031, and Glasgow in 2034. Come prepared with your burning questions before site selection voting closes on Saturday.
schedule.title: Future Worldcons Question and Answer

schedule.desc: A key element of what takes a costume from good to great are the layers beyond the garment itself. Shoes, jewelry, headpieces, props, and more can elevate a look from fun to totally transformative. Our panel will talk through their steps of breaking down a design and share tips and tricks for adding in all those key little details.
schedule.title: Accessorize! Taking Looks to the Next Level

schedule.desc: For the first time in years, the Star Wars television presence seems to be at a crossroads: The Mandalorian has gone on to films, and multiple shows like Obi Wan Kenobi, The Acolyte, and Skeleton Crew were one-season wonders. Even the crown jewel of Star Wars TV, Andor, was a critical darling, but its ratings just didn't match. Are we at a saturation point? Or are we looking for something new in our tales from a galaxy far, far away?
schedule.title: The Future of Star Wars on Television

schedule.desc: The Ray Bradbury Center is more than an archive: it’s a team of people working at the intersection of science fiction, community, and public imagination. This roundtable invites Worldcon participants to meet the Center’s staff, ask questions, share ideas, and explore how institutions and fandom can collaborate to keep speculative futures alive and accessible.
schedule.title: A Conversation with the Ray Bradbury Center

schedule.desc: Phoebe Barton is a Canadian queer trans science fiction writer of short and interactive fiction who has written about trans vengeance, space, giant queer ladies, and public transit, and she's also an editor! Come visit virtually for a chat about these or other things like interactive fiction, film photography, or her cat.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Phoebe Barton

schedule.desc: As with most media formats, music plays a key role in anime productions. The soundtrack supports and even directs the plot and characters, and is highly influenced by the animation style chosen. What of some of the best anime soundscapes and how have they impacted the show?
schedule.title: The Music of Anime (Virtual)

schedule.desc: The X-Men started as a way to break the mold for what could be considered a “superhero comic book” but, over time, became a standard which spoke to millions of fans all over the world. How did they come to speak for generations of fans and become a phenomenon? Let’s talk about their history and celebrate what makes them both endearing and enduring!
schedule.title: The X-Men Phenomenon

schedule.desc: Join retired STEM teacher and award-winning geek rock star Tim Griffin for wacky (but peer-reviewed) songs about physics, physiology, and that weird stain on the lab floor.
schedule.title: Concert: Tim Griffin

schedule.desc: Daryl Gregory is a Seattle writer who's published eleven books and can't stay in one genre. His last three novels were the Nebula nominee When We Were Real (SF), Dragon award nominee Revelator (Appalachian horror), and Nebula nominee Spoonbenders (a comedy about a family of psychics). He's happy to talk about writing novels and short fiction, as well as writing for comics, television, and games. He's also a frequent teacher at workshops (Viable Paradise, Clarion West, Aspen Words, and more) so bring your questions on those.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Daryl Gregory

schedule.desc: All contestants, or at least one member of a group entry, must attend for the entry to be qualified for the masquerade. We will do entry check-ins and verify release forms, meet the workmanship judges, emcee, staff, and go over the basics of the masquerade rules and processes. Contestants interested in workmanship judging can also turn in their documentation at that time.
schedule.title: Pre-Masquerade Meeting for Contestants

schedule.desc: The Second World War reshaped every corner of American life, and Los Angeles fandom was no exception. Fans enlisted, relocated, and were pulled into technical and classified war work. Fanzine culture adapted. LASFS struggled to hold together. How did the community survive and how did the war transform the future direction of science fiction itself? Join us to explore.
schedule.title: LA Fandom in the War Years: Transformation on the Home Front

schedule.desc: If you want to be a successful YouTuber, it's more than just filming yourself and putting it on the site. Our panelists will discuss establishing and maintaining a YouTube presence, including choosing your niche, production tips, and monetization.
schedule.title: Get Started as a YouTube Creator

schedule.desc: Games Workshop was founded in 1975 and has been with us for over fifty years. It brought D&D to the United Kingdom for the first time, and co-founders Steve Jackson and Ian Livingstone are also responsible for the Fighting Fantasy gamebooks. However, Games Workshop’s biggest impacts have been through Warhammer and Warhammer 40,000, which are still going strong. What is the legacy of Games Workshop, and where can we expect it to go from here?
schedule.title: 50 Years of Games Workshop
New and Indie Autographing: Emily Skrutskie

schedule.desc: Stefan Rudnicki, veteran narrator, producer and/or publisher of over 3,000 audiobooks, will regale you with anecdotes about the legendary authors with whom he has collaborated, while exploring opportunities for indie authors via Skyboat Media. Happy also to answer questions about the art and craft of audiobook creation. Might even offer an introduction to Warframe’s Albrecht Entrati.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Stefan Rudnicki

schedule.desc: With one European Space Agency and two NASA spacecraft missions in the works to explore Venus, it wasn’t too long ago that the future of exploration of Earth’s sibling planet seemed sunny. However, funding cuts are imperiling the US efforts to send spacecraft to Venus. On this panel, scientists and engineers will discuss how these three missions have been designed to complement each other and why it is important to try to save both the DAVINCI and VERITAS missions.
schedule.title: What’s Next for the Exploration of Venus?

schedule.desc: Some define purple prose as sentences and situations larded with high-emotion tropes, others as sentences with too many no-calorie adjectives and adverbs, such as "literally" when nothing in the text is literal. Bland prose is often the extreme that writers swing to in order to avoid the purple problem. What's the happy medium? Panelists will define their views on how much is too much and too little, and how to find that sweet spot between them.
schedule.title: Purple vs Windowpane Prose: Navigating Between Two Extremes

schedule.desc: Klingon has no word for "Hello" - the closest to a greeting is "nuqneH?" which means "What do you want?" Join our language workshop where you will hear an overview of the Klingon language from Star Trek, and also learn to speak a few words and phrases in one of the galaxy's most popular languages!
schedule.title: nuqneH? How to "Greet" Someone In Klingon

schedule.desc: Shock: Social Science Fiction, Fantasy Map Maker, For the Queen, and others are games that are to some extent explicitly for building worlds, or parts of a world. We can play to build worlds with games not designed for this, too: James D’Amato used Star-Crossed to inform the world of his actual play podcast Campaign Skyjacks, for instance. How can we build worlds through play?
schedule.title: Worldbuilding Is the Point: Building Universes Through Play

schedule.desc: There’s something fascinating about fungi, a whole different kingdom of life, as evidenced by its prevalence in speculative fiction - see Star Trek’s Spore Drive, The Last of Us’ hive mind zombies, and the whole situation in What Moves the Dead. Hear from experts about the latest research on fungi, including new uses for mushrooms and how fungal diseases are evolving. Despite no longer being classified in the same kingdom, slime molds can join the party too.
schedule.title: Fungus Among Us: Mushrooms for Good and Evil

schedule.desc: Katie Wu does the inaugural reading of her highly anticipated debut, Madder Lake, a dark academia fantasy about two rivals who fall in love at magic painting university, forthcoming from Harper Voyager in Fall 2027.
schedule.title: Reading: Katie Wu

schedule.desc: Trip Galey, author of the Mythopoeic-shortlisted A Market of Dreams and Destiny reads from his forthcoming queer science-fantasy extravaganza The Fall of the House of Valenziaga!
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Trip Galey

schedule.desc: What does work look like in African futures? How do AI, automation, climate change, and economic transformation reshape labour, dignity, and community across the continent? Part of the Applied African SF initiative, this panel follows up on the successful "Ask the Scientist" series from Worldcon 2025, bringing together authors and researchers who are exploring the future of work through speculative fiction.
schedule.title: The Future of Work in the Age of AI: Applying African Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: From ancient myths to future galaxies, South Asian speculative fiction is bursting with dynamic new worlds that are shaped by the diverse histories and cultures of the region. Explore the magic, mystical creatures, and imaginative possibilities driving SFF inspired by South Asian cultures.
schedule.title: Story Alchemy: South Asian Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: Science fiction has long envisioned intelligence demanding planetary energy: from Asimov’s Multivac to the matrioshka brains of Robert J. Bradbury’s hard SF. Today, that speculation has collided with the physical limits of the electrical grid. We will examine the “hidden physics” of the gigawatt-scale era. Why are traditional electrical grids failing to support the cloud, and how are Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) turning tech campuses into SF city-states?
schedule.title: Data Centers and the Death of the Grid?

schedule.desc: Dr. Tiffani Angus, co-author of the multi-award-shortlisted Spec Fic for Newbies series, will introduce you to the history of this fascinating subgenre and how it can be broken down into a series of elements that create the “chain” to help you better understand it and even write it. The workshop will culminate in an activity that’ll get you started creating a whole new folk horror story.
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: Writing Folk Horror – Linking the Chain

schedule.desc: When writers bring their whole selves to the page, characters get to be dynamic and readers get a lesson in true acceptance. Even when characters are challenged, honest conversations and realities can be expressed by the authors writing them. This panel will discuss and celebrate writing gender-diverse characters and how these characters can model self-acceptance for readers and writers regardless of identity.
schedule.title: As You Are: Identity Acceptance in SFF

schedule.desc: Watch the short film The Stooge based on a story by Christopher Priest, starring Robert Picardo, followed by a Q & A with the filmmaker.
schedule.title: THE STOOGE Screening and Q & A

schedule.desc: Clarion faculty and alumni will answer your questions about the long-standing writing program for science fiction and fantasy writers that takes place on the lovely campus of the University of California San Diego for six weeks each summer. Get answers to questions such as how to apply, the timing of application to acceptance, where you will eat and live, the cost, the availability of scholarships, and more. Come find out how it can advance your writing goals!
schedule.title: Welcome to Clarion San Diego!

schedule.desc: Hollywood and your favorite authors can often get injury and trauma wrong. Come to this presentation to learn the do's and don'ts of depicting injury and trauma in your fiction!
schedule.title: Murder and Mayhem - Writing Realistic Injuries for Authors

schedule.desc: Turn the tedium of map making into a delight! Explore map making tools and techniques while building some new worlds of your own. (This workshop is for teens)
schedule.title: Where in the World? Teen Map Making Workshop

schedule.desc: Felicia Martinez, author of The Other Lives of Altagracia Sanchez, reads from her forthcoming sci-fi, multiverse reimagining of the myth of Phaedra and Hippolytus,These Bright and Perilous Designs. Asexual love, neurodivergence, and found family abound!
schedule.title: Reading: Felicia Martinez

schedule.desc: Star Trek’s production history spans the great gulf between Desilu Studios (headed at the time by Lucille Ball) and present day Paramount Skydance Corporation. The creative leadership of Gene Roddenberry, who took great pleasure in presenting cutting edge progressive issues but today, the undisguised politics of billionaire Paramount Skydance owner David Ellison may threaten the franchise’s future.
schedule.title: Paramount: Pitfalls of Kleptocratic Corporatacracy

schedule.desc:
Hey chummer, they’ve had it up to here, and you have been enlisted to shut down a riot. Join us playing this legendary game!

Character sheets, dice and pencils provided.
schedule.title: Shadowrun: April 29th, Where Were You?

schedule.desc: Bring out your inner Trekkie with this networked computer game experience! 6–8 players take control of the spaceship Artemis, assuming various crew jobs: Helm, Weapons, Science, Communications, Engineering, Fighter Pilot(s), and Captain. The ship’s missions require the crew to work together to overcome challenges such as combat, puzzle-solving, diplomacy, and exploration. An educational (space science) teambuilding experience!
schedule.title: Artemis Space Bridge Simulator (Saturday)

schedule.desc: Make a rocket to launch. How high will it go?
schedule.title: Create a Rocket to Launch

schedule.desc: At different times throughout history, pivotal technological changes have changed the course of history. Panelists will choose an interesting piece of tech or scientific knowledge and explain its development and importance.
schedule.title: Technology through the Ages: a History of Science (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Terraforming often takes place on faraway planets. But LA's thirst for water emptied lakes, drained rivers, and reshaped the flow of water across California. Some people suggest we need to geoengineer our way out of climate change. What stories have explored the costs of humans changing environments, whether real or fictional? What aspects aren't we exploring? What have we overexplored? Is it inevitable?
schedule.title: Terraforming California, Earth, and beyond

schedule.desc: In recent years, more and more crafty fans are turning to the fine art of printing and binding their own or favorite fanfiction, with incredible results. How do they do it? Let’s explore the rise and craft of fanbinding and the ethical nuances of working in this corner of fandom.
schedule.title: Fanbinding: Book-Binding for Fanfic

schedule.desc: Many writers are making the jump to game writing. Panelists will discuss how to do it, what skills are needed, and how it differs from story or book writing.
schedule.title: Getting into Game Writing

schedule.desc: The nineteenth century was a great age of science, but until anaesthesia, antiseptic and antibiotics came along, surgery remained limited and dangerous. Drugs were few, experimental protocols were near zero, and contagion was poorly understood: while TB was known to be a contagious disease in the East, the belief it was hereditary led to its rapid spread in the West. The panel will discuss what was known, what was guessed at, what was flat out wrong, and what was fashionable.
schedule.title: Nineteenth Century Medicine

schedule.desc: Games have explored apocalyptic settings for years. The Fallout franchise is possibly the most well-known, but there are many other games and franchises that play with this concept. Why do we love playing in the apocalypse, and how do games approach this subject matter differently?
schedule.title: Playing in the Apocalypse

schedule.desc: Children's Programming Staff Members will take the kids with parents/guardians through the Dealers Room. We might even find a few dealers who are members of the Adventurers Club and have stops for the kids to collect stamps for their Adventurers Club Passports and a cool item.
schedule.title: Kids' Tour the Dealers Room

schedule.desc: Come join those of Christian faith for discussion, interaction, and community.
schedule.title: Meetup: Christian Genre Fans

schedule.desc: Occasionally a story starts as prose, but sometimes the idea would do better as poetry. Come practice your speculative poetry writing skills with professional poets there to offer their wisdom and advice! (This workshop is for teens)
schedule.title: Line by Line: Teen Poetry Workshop

schedule.desc: The Sauúti Collective represents a new model for collaboration in African speculative fiction—one that centres African voices, ownership, and sustainability. Moving beyond extractive relationships with global publishers and institutions, Sauúti is building cooperative structures that keep value, rights, and creative control within African communities.
schedule.title: The Sauúti Collective: A New Model for Creative Worldbuilding

schedule.desc: Hallowed school halls, pleated skirts, tea, murder: is the mere aesthetic of academia enough, or must the story engage with certain themes and tropes to truly be considered dark academia? If so, which tropes and themes? Join this inclusive group of authors as they discuss the hallmarks of this dynamic sub-genre and where, if at all, subversion and reinterpretation come into play.
schedule.title: Dark Academia: More Than the Aesthetic

schedule.desc: For as long as humans have told stories, they’ve invented imaginative, often unusual, ones about the creation of the world: some divine, some demonic. We consider how writers have used, expanded, sometimes exploded, those stories in their own works. How do creators balance respect with invention? And what unforgettable detail from a creation myth has stayed with you?
schedule.title: Gods Did WHAT?! Creation Stories from Around the World

schedule.desc: Speculative fiction has a long history of combining the fantastic with the political. This genre is anything but apolitical. Authors will discuss the political themes they explore on the page and how these themes impact identity.
schedule.title: Reading Is Political: SFF as Political Conversation

schedule.desc: While Frankenstein's Monster might seem more magic than science these days, at the time of publication, Mary Shelley's defining work was undeniably science fiction. What other women helped define the genre? How is their influence still seen today? And how can we honor them moving forward?
schedule.title: From Cavendish to Shelley: Historical Female SF Authors

schedule.desc: Explore how SFF authors use heritage, inherited stories, traditions, and ancestral connections in their work—creating speculative fiction inspired by lineage and cultural markers rather than nation-states.
schedule.title: Roots on the Page: Writing Shaped by Heritage

schedule.desc: This panel examines specific cases where ideas from science fiction have anticipated real technologies. Writers, engineers, and academics will discuss how the speculative can inspire innovation and critical thinking.
schedule.title: Science Fiction as a Driver of Scientific Innovation

schedule.desc: Shibori is a Japanese dyeing technique that results in rich patterns. This workshop ncludes a series of historical stitch resist dye techniques found around the world. Workshop members will learn at least two techniques.
schedule.title: Shibori Stitch Resist

schedule.desc: Costumers and parents discuss some easy things that you can do and things you can use for costuming for your kids.
schedule.title: Exploring Easy Tricks for Costuming Kids

schedule.desc: Anthropic’s unauthorized use of over seven million books highlights how writers are forced to protect their work, especially with AI creeping into every corner of the digital world. Panelists will discuss author advocacy, publishing challenges, and developing support. We will look at lessons from small presses, rights reversion, and how organizations like SFWA, Writer Beware, and the Authors Guild help writers protect their careers.
schedule.title: Post Anthropic Rights Grab--Getting the Support Authors Need

schedule.desc: BIPOC Poetry editors come together to discuss the current state of poetry, what editors are looking for, which markets publish poetry, and market-related questions. They'll share their favorites poets, what are their favorites bodies of work, and, in the time of techno-fascism, why speculative poetry can be a tool of resistance.
schedule.title: What Editors Look For In Speculative Poetry

schedule.desc: Follow the pull of a golden key toward a treasure under the sea, then stay and listen to stars snarling, candles sobbing, skeletons emerging in dark barns, foxes building temples to unfathomable gods, and women liberating themselves through transformation. Tara Campbell, author of 2025 PKD finalist City of Dancing Gargoyles, will read from her new chapbook All the Wayward Angels: Dream Sestinas. In sixteen poems, Campbell creates a swirling dreamworld of falling angels, rough beasts, and creatures “using hope to dowse for rain.”
schedule.title: Reading: Tara Campbell

schedule.desc: You've brought your gently loved t-shirts, and now it's time to find a new love to take home! Browse the selection of geeky shirts brought by other attendees, grab something new-to-you, and be proud for doing a little bit for sustainability!
schedule.title: T-Shirt Swap!

schedule.desc: Were you a dragonology and dinosaur kid? Fascinated by the ocean deep and by what Eldritch creatures may lie beneath? Come to lore dump, share animal facts, and talk about how we can create resonant stories, not just super sick concepts. Malachi Lily is a worldbuilder, a SFWA-recognized writer, a career illustrator, and amateur naturalist. Stims and crafts provided! Tangents welcome!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Malachi Lily

schedule.desc: Long before AI became a product, SF writers and computer scientists wrestled with how machines express ethics. What happens if AI ethics are very different from human ethics? Is it okay for AIs to make life and death decisions in war or in medicine? Are lapses in AI ethics already doing harm?
schedule.title: What Is Ethical AI?

schedule.desc: Whether it's the horrors of the dark web, early message boards for X-Files fans, or the SCP project, the internet perfectly combines subject and medium into one big scare. Add to this the boom in horror video gaming, the backrooms phenomenon, and the digital nostalgia of analog horror, and it's no wonder why so many fans live online. Does "I Have No Mouth And I Must Scream" count as proto-internet horror?
schedule.title: The Internet of Horrors

schedule.desc: Join Robert J. Sawyer for the launch of Sawyer on Science Fiction. This is a 250,000-word collection of essays, speeches, articles, reviews, and columns about science fiction literature, science fiction fandom, and Canadian science fiction by Robert J. Sawyer, Hugo and Nebula Award-winner and Guest of Honor at the 2023 Worldcon.
schedule.title: Book Launch: Robert J. Sawyer

schedule.desc: Ready to bring a dragon to life? Join Guest of Honor and Disney artist Tim Kirk to learn how. Learn tips, techniques, and creative secrets from a master illustrator as you create your own legendary creature. (This workshop is for kids.)
schedule.title: Draw a Dragon with Tim Kirk: Kids’ Workshop

schedule.desc: Practice speaking the Klingon language. All levels of fluency are welcome!
schedule.title: Conversation Practice in Klingon

schedule.desc: So you've written and edited your manuscript and are ready for the next steps: it's time to talk query letters! This interactive workshop will take you through the basics of composing a query letter, breaking down metadata, plot pitches and comps. Bring a draft of your query to workshop or get started writing with support.
schedule.title: Writing a good query letter

schedule.desc: What makes a great review? What makes a gloriously scathing critique? Our panelists dig into the art of SFF criticism from a fan perspective: zines, blogs, social media, and beyond. We’ll share tips for reviewing well, explore how fan criticism shapes fandom culture, and tackle the tricky stuff: bias, spoilers, and beloved-but-flawed works.
schedule.title: Critiquing the Critics

schedule.desc: Despite modern transformative works spaces being more visible and accessible, and fans in this space being more likely to be open about their "wallet names," there's still a strong tendency to create fan work under pseudonyms. What is the appeal of creating and sharing work anonymously? What freedoms and restrictions can be found in working this way and engaging in community while "hidden"?
schedule.title: Freedom in Anonymity: Having an Alias for Your Fanfic

schedule.desc: Join Guest of Honor Stan Sakai for a guided docent tour of his exhibit in the Art Show.
schedule.title: Art Show Docent Tour: Stan Sakai

schedule.desc: Join this year’s Best Pro Artist Hugo Award finalists for a lively roundtable on the state of speculative art, their creative process, and the works that defined their year. From technique to storytelling, hear how they bring imagined worlds to life in a discussion designed to engage artists, writers, and fans alike.
schedule.title: Closeup: The 2026 Hugo Award Best Professional Artist Roundtable

schedule.desc: What if the past had turned out differently? From Indigenous nations that were never subject to colonialist exploitation to revolutions that succeeded—or failed—alternate history lets us rewrite power itself. This panel dives into the craft and responsibility of changing history on the page: research, plausibility, moral choices, and what-if speculation that reveals hidden truths. We’ll look at how authors can balance creative freedom with respect for real people and cultures, using the past not as nostalgia but as a living conversation with the present.
schedule.title: Rewriting History — The Art and Ethics of Alternate Timelines (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Filk Hall of Fame inductees and Pegasus Award-winning duo TJ and Mitchell Burnside Clapp have over 80 years of filking experience between them. They will perform songs of space, science, and silliness, both old and new. They are happy to share their own songs along with those of their friends and collaborators covering topics from space, science fiction, and artificial intelligence, to dragons, vampires, and Bob Dylan.
schedule.title: Concert: TJ & Mitchell Burnside Clapp

schedule.desc: Most of us agree that libraries are a vital component of civilization. Panelists will discuss how authors envision the future of libraries and what they might look like.
schedule.title: The Future of Libraries

schedule.desc: Language both shapes culture and is shaped by it, making fantasy and speculative fiction fertile ground for exploring meaning and perception. This session examines how writers can use linguistic structures to build worlds, drawing on examples like Swahili dialects that emphasize certain senses, or Eastern Congolese expressions that ask whether one “hears” meaning, revealing new possibilities for storytelling.
schedule.title: The Bantu Languages And Cultures

schedule.desc: Writers and artists have used personifications of death throughout history to impart meaning to our conception of the state of death. This presentation will provide an examination of six modern personifications of death and their commonalities and differences. While they remain in conversation with previous iterations, how do they contextualize death for a modern reader? Do they offer a new focus on what it means to be truly alive, for however long that may last?
schedule.title: Contextualizing Death Personifications

schedule.desc: Movies and TV seem to have only three ideas about how to portray culture and art in the future. Either humans ceased to develop art after the 20th/21st Century, they ignore art completely (which seems unrealistic), or they create their own often surreal and weird future art. What shows/movies do this well and which make things feel strangely anachronistic? Why is it so tough to envision future art?
schedule.title: Imagining How Art Will Look In The Future

schedule.desc: From the curious microscopic structures found in the Martian meteorite ALH84001, to the “canals” on Mars, and the WOW! signal; the search for life beyond Earth has felt tantalizingly close to success, only to be proven wrong multiple times. Why is the search so hard?
schedule.title: The Times We Found Alien Life... Almost

schedule.desc: Do you love seeing Science Fiction and Fantasy (SFF) theatrical works? What about SFF musical theater? If you said yes to either, then this is the meetup for you!
schedule.title: Meetup: Fans of SFF Theater

schedule.desc: Voyager 1 and 2 discovered volcanoes on Io, performed the only fly-bys of Uranus and Neptune, created the iconic Pale Blue Dot image and are now returning invaluable data from interstellar space. Join members of the Voyager Flight Team as they review highlights from the mission and discuss the current engineering challenges of operating humanity’s farthest ambassadors as they approach Voyager’s 50th Anniversary since launch.
schedule.title: Voyager at 50

schedule.desc: Fonda Lee, author of the Green Bone Saga, reads a special unpublished cut scene from her new science fiction novel, The Last Contract of Isako.
schedule.title: Reading: Fonda Lee

schedule.desc: Ruth Frances Long, award-winning author of the Locus recommended The Book of Gold, reads from her forthcoming alt-renaissance historical fantasy The God of Bronze, the final part of The Feral Gods Trilogy. Join her on one last trip to Amberes, where the gods walk the narrow streets and revolution is about to boil over.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Ruth Frances Long / Jessica Thorne

schedule.desc: Join us for seven short films: After Link (Portugal, UK), All the Money in the World (USA), FutureGaze (UK), I Made The Invisible Man (UK), Paracosm (USA), Pocket Change (USA), The Essence (Russian Federation)
schedule.title: Science Fiction Short films

schedule.desc: Musk names his drone ships after vessels from Iain M. Banks' Culture novels. Bezos tried to bring Consider Phlebas to Amazon Studios. Zuckerberg put The Player of Games in his book club. They understand the Culture as, at minimum, libertarian. Critics object that the billionaires are misreading the Culture's political philosophy, which is socialism. This paper argues both are wrong.
schedule.title: Understanding The Culture: Misunderstanding Banks
“Cringe Culture is Dead”: Being Open About Fanfic

schedule.desc: Many poets are first published in a chapbook or zine. This panel discusses that option over a full book collection and explores the benefits of indie and self-publishing poetry in modern times.
schedule.title: Chapbook: The Poetry Mixtape

schedule.desc: Join award-winning professional artist Vincent Di Fate for a guided docent tour of the art show.
schedule.title: Art Show Docent Tour: Vincent Di Fate

schedule.desc: Combining speculative and mystery genres is common: who doesn’t love a good mystery set in a fantastical world or in outer space? How do you catch a fantastic criminal? What can speculative mystery writers (and readers) learn from modern forensics? How would you autopsy an alien? What would serve for identification (like a fingerprint). What if an AI committed the murder? Panelists will address all these and go from there!
schedule.title: Catching a Criminal: Forensics for SF/Mystery Writers

schedule.desc: Xan van Rooyen is an autistic and non-binary author originally from South Africa, now living in Finland where they are a music teacher. They are a hybrid author writing strange, dark fiction that blends and defies categories but always features complicated queer and neurodivergent characters. Join them for a chat about writing dark tales, heavy metal, tattoos, writing and publishing while neuroqueer, collaborative writing and world-building, how to balance work and writing as a part time author, why peanut butter is life, and loads of other fun and quirky topics!
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Xan van Rooyen

schedule.desc: Romantasy is taking over the shelves. How can romance and the fantastical be used to center and celebrate Black communities’ relationships to love, beauty, desire, and self-determination in the face of a reality where these concepts are too often challenged?
schedule.title: Love in Color: Romantasy as Healing for Black Bodies

schedule.desc: More fantasy books feature queer characters as our discussions about queer identity grows. What are some books that showcase the LGBTQIA+ community well? What are the trends as more SFF includes queer characters and culture?
schedule.title: Queer Fantasy

schedule.desc: Stew Hotston has played and run LARPs for 25 years. As a man of color, he found LARPs to be super welcoming and inclusive. Yet, despite this, they failed to attract people like him to their games. This talk is about what happened when Stew sat down and picked apart what it was about the LARPs they were playing and running that stopped people from diverse backgrounds from coming along.
schedule.title: LARP, Race and How to Tell Inclusive Stories

schedule.desc: Join Hugo Finalists Inua Ellems (BDP-Short: Doctor Who) and Michael Damian Thomas (Editor - Short Form & Semiprozine: Uncanny Magazine) for an in-depth interview about Ellems' work as a screenwriter, poet, playwright, performer, graphic artist, and other creative passions.
schedule.title: Interview: Inua Ellems by Michael Damian Thomas

schedule.desc: The Kingdom of Caid, the SCA’s Southern California branch, brings its fighters to Worldcon for live combat demonstrations. See armored combat with rattan swords and rapier fencing in Renaissance style, both at full speed. Between bouts, fighters share how their armor and weapons are made, how bouts are won, and why honor is at the center of it all. Stop by, ask questions, and find out how you can try it yourself.
schedule.title: SCA Combat Demo - Saturday #1

schedule.desc: Authoritarianism can be part of fantasy worlds as the main form of government or a featured form. But how does authoritarianism work with magic systems, especially when it comes to corrupt governments? Panelists explore books that feature authoritarian elements in the fantasy genre.
schedule.title: Authoritarianism in Fantasy Worlds

schedule.desc: An overview of Diné Bizaad, the language of the Diné/Navajo people, its relation to other local indigenous languages, as well as its nearest linguistic relatives. Learn to speak a few words and phrases in this fascinating and beautiful language.
schedule.title: An Introduction to Diné Bizaad (Navajo Language)

schedule.desc: In only its second year, the Hugo Award for Best Poem looks like it might be here to stay! These poets have shown us their hearts, line by line, in this lyrical and moving format. Come hear them talk about their process for writing, how these poems came about specifically, and what it’s like to finally have their art form recognized by the Worldcon community in this way.
schedule.title: Counting Lines: Hugo Best Poem Finalists

schedule.desc: This meetup is for anyone in the community who identifies as Trans or Nonbinary and wants to meet other fans who similarly identify.
schedule.title: Meetup: Trans and Nonbinary

schedule.desc: Arkady Martine is the Hugo-winning author of the Teixcalaan duology, the novella Rose/House, and a multitude of short speculative fiction. She is also Dr. AnnaLinden Weller, a climate and energy policy analyst and a city planner. She is rarely bored but often tired. Come chat with her about any of the above - or something else entirely.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Arkady Martine

schedule.desc: Struggling to figure out the fight scenes in your books? Hear from folks trained in various fight forms about how to approach these complex scenarios. (This panel is for teens.)
schedule.title: And Now, I Die: Fight Choreography for Writing

schedule.desc: Children's Programming Staff Members will take the kids with parents/guardians through the Exhibits Hall. We might even find a few Specific Exhibits to stop to collect stamps for their Adventurers Club Passports.
schedule.title: Kids' Tour the Exhibits Hall

schedule.desc: We don't have a road atlas for Mars, but we have a significant amount of data, including official IAU names for many locations. How do Mars scientists name places on the Red Planet, and what's been happening in those places lately? Where do we imagine we'll celebrate Mars New Year on September 30, 2026?
schedule.title: Geography of Mars: Names, Places, and Updates

schedule.desc: A social gathering where attendees can dress in black, exchange shiny trinkets, and discuss their shared appreciation of corvids.
schedule.title: Meetup: Corvid Fans

schedule.desc: While it started as a mechanics-forward hobby, more and more games have turned to prioritising storytelling. At some tables, Game Masters have an absolute grip on the plot, and at others, the act of telling the story is more collaborative. And then we have “GM-less” games, in which GM authority can either rotate or is entirely replaced. How is the direction of plot changing at the table, and how do our panel use this to enhance their storytelling?
schedule.title: Cocreation and Storytelling at the Table (Virtual)

schedule.desc: The owners of big tech companies and other ultra-rich people are often science fiction fans. However, some of the future they seem to be building is troubling. Peter Thiel’s Palantir is working to create a surveillance society in line with Nineteen Eighty-Four. Larry Ellison is building a concentrated media empire. What if the oligarchy built ideas from positive SF, and fell in love with solarpunk? What would the panel like to see?
schedule.title: Can We Stop the Tech Oligarchy Making SF Warnings Real?

schedule.desc: Micaiah Johnson is an author and academic from the Mojave Desert whose interests span from string theory to ancient automatons. Join her as she endeavors to stay on topic while discussing the craft of writing, the specific research that went into her fictional worlds, and the unique challenges of creating art in our current hellscape *publishing landscape.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Micaiah Johnson

schedule.desc: Catherynne M. Valente is an internationally-bestselling author of science fiction and fantasy for adults and children, including Space Opera, Fairyland, Deathless, Palimpsest, The Past Is Red, and many more. Come talk about any of that or anything else, from knitting and ancient Greek, to politics and medieval Welsh, to movies, gardening, and terrifyingly large pets. Anything goes--you decide! And then we shall scheme...
schedule.title: Table Talk: Catherynne M. Valente

schedule.desc: This applies to new authors seeking traditional publication as well as to indie authors. Getting feedback on your story prior to pitching, submitting, and publishing is necessary, even vital. Panelists will define alpha readers, beta readers, other people who give you feedback, and the benefits they offer. How do you choose the right people to help you? What happens when your beta readers insist you're great, but nothing sells?
schedule.title: Alpha, Beta, ARC Readers and Editors: Know the Differences (Virtual)

schedule.desc: How does magic affect politics and vice versa in fantasy stories? How does the interplay of these two power structures impact the way a story is told? What media showcases this connection in interesting ways?
schedule.title: Magic and Politics

schedule.desc: How much is an original piece of art worth versus what an artist thinks people might be willing to pay? How do you factor in time, materials, and quality? What about prints or the equivalent? Is the first print really worth more? And how about those frames! It all adds up!
schedule.title: How Do You Price Your Art?

schedule.desc: We know AI can make videos. How is it used to support the creation of feature films or television series? Is it doing good or harm, or both? How is AI changing computer-generated special effects? Publishers have declined to publish books that they suspected contained AI generated content. Will the movie industry reject or embrace AI generated material?
schedule.title: Hollywood and AI: How is AI Being Used in the Film Industry?

schedule.desc: Writers and storytellers will help kids create their own adventure.
schedule.title: Create Your Own Adventure Live!

schedule.desc: Whether it’s glowing wands or swords, flashing energy weapons, or lit up costume pieces, our panelists will teach you the basics of homebrew lighting, including incorporating LEDs and batteries, fiber optics, and home-made light guides. Safety practices in assembling and powering your devices will be discussed in addition to how to add lighting.
schedule.title: Adding Lighting to Your Props and Costumes

schedule.desc: WorldCon brings together a blend of people interested in both science and writing. Unfortunately, there can be a breakdown between people performing the experiments and those making laws or the general public. Scientific research has a history of exploiting communities of color, poor people, and vulnerable populations. How can we bridge these groups of people while maintaining trust, for the benefit of all? Practical tips and philosophical discussion.
schedule.title: SciComm and You: How Do We Use Science for Good?

schedule.desc: There are many ways we learn to edit our own fiction, but few resources to help us become useful critique partners for other writers. With the greater level of invention in speculative fiction, this need is even more significant. The ability to poke holes in and reveal the weaknesses of both our own and our critique partners’ fiction is a learned one. We look forward to your contributions to the community and an exciting discussion.
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: How to Be a Good Critique Partner

schedule.desc: Join us on a journey across space and time at this virtual celebration as we bring the Worldcon spirit back to Dublin in 2029. Discover our vision for a Worldcon at the crossroads of storytelling, fandom, and imagination. Explore why Dublin is the perfect place to celebrate science fiction, fantasy, horror, art, gaming, and fan culture. Share the craic, play games, listen to stories, meet fellow fans, and have a brilliant time.
schedule.title: Dublin 2029 Virtual Party: Holding Slot

schedule.desc: You’re ready to use Kickstarter, BackerKit, Patreon, or other crowdfunding sources to grow your readership and help fund your projects. What are the secrets of a successful campaign? What are some pitfalls to avoid?
schedule.title: Successful Kickstarters and other Crowdfunders for Writers

schedule.desc: Dawson (she/they) is the Golden Crown-award winning author of The First Bright Thing and a Hugo, Nebula, and Sturgeon finalist this year for her short story, "Six People to Revise You". Her latest novel, The Lighthouse at the Edge of the World, won Best Novel for the Society of Midland Authors. Her short fiction has been seen in places such as Reactor, Uncanny, F&SF, Lightspeed, and others. She also works as a professor at the MFA Program for Creative Writing at Drexel University and a teaching artist at The Loft Literary Center. When she's not teaching or writing, she is traveling or looking after her chaotic dogs. Dawson's stories focus on queer empowerment, unlikely heroes, and hopeful resistance. She's also open to just talk about Disney for an hour.
schedule.title: Table Talk: J.R. Dawson

schedule.desc: In 1943, prominent Boston fan Art Widner designed and published a sophisticated SF board game. Earlier offerings based on Buck Rogers were simplistic and aimed at children but Widner’s game was aimed at adults. It combined elements of Monopoly and chase/race games. A few enterprising fans have attempted to resurrect Interplanetary over the years. We’ll trace the history of the game and introduce the latest, most ambitious reboot to date.
schedule.title: Interplanetary: The First Original SF Board Game

schedule.desc: Even with sales numbers dropping and the distribution channel scattered and shredded, it’s a great time to be a comics fan. Marvel and DC are doing some of the best work they’ve done in years, and there are strong stories from “second-rank” companies and a surge of independent publishers. We will look at how things are going, then become an audience-led “comic book sommelier,” where we match an individual with a perfect comic title or two.
schedule.title: The Comic Book Sommelier

schedule.desc: Russell Davis, a past President of SFWA and the current Operations Director, is also a multi-published novelist and short story writer under numerous pseudonyms, including Jenna Solitaire, Cliff Ryder, and David Cian. He has written in The Librarian and Transformers worlds, among others. In addition, he was the Director of the Genre Fiction MA/MFA program at Western Colorado University for nearly a decade, and helped create the MA in publishing.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Russell Davis

schedule.desc: Cecilia Eng is a Pegasus Award-winning filker who was inducted into the Filk Hall of Fame in 2013. She has performed on multiple Valdemar albums, wrote “Helva’s Song” based on Anne McCaffrey’s The Ship Who Sang, and is an active participant pretty much anywhere you find a music circle.
schedule.title: Concert: Cecilia Eng

schedule.desc: Saving the world isn’t reserved for people of a certain age, and adventure doesn’t come with an age limit. Join writers as they explore the universal desires that drive every great story, and the perspective and complexity that emerges when a story's heroes are older than the industry’s usual median age.
schedule.title: Experience Required: The Mature Main Character

schedule.desc: What happens when Hugo Best Fancast nominees share the mic? This live, performance style session brings voices from nominated fancasts together in a collaborative mash‑up. How do different shows approach criticism, humour, and community? Where do formats clash or harmonise? Expect lively exchanges, unexpected connections, and a celebration of fannish audio creativity.
schedule.title: Many Mics, One Stage: Hugo Fancast Mash‑Up

schedule.desc: It is not surprising that Colleen Doran has a lot of thoughts about storytelling: as she is someone who has been writing all her life, as well as translating other authors’ stories into images on the page, this should not come as a surprise to anyone. Join her as she talks about time, deconstruction, density, borders, and the manipulation of the reader’s senses.
schedule.title: Colleen Doran: Time in Storytelling

schedule.desc: Anarchism has often been an integral part of fantasy worlds. Explore how anarchy works with magic systems when the system is oppressive. Panelists discuss books that feature interesting anarchism in fantasy worlds.
schedule.title: Anarchy in Fantasy Worlds

schedule.desc: Daniel Gonzalez will share his artwork and journey as an Indigenous artist. He will discuss how his work is influenced by outhwestern iconography, culture, and the cosmos.
schedule.title: A Journey from the Reservation to Los Angeles

schedule.desc: Tia Tashiro, a Hugo, Locus, Sturgeon, and Astounding Award finalist for her short fiction, reads from her 2026 short story Archaeological Evidence for the Time Traveler.
schedule.title: Reading: Tia Tashiro

schedule.desc: Edward Carmien (edwardcarmien.com) reads from “The Assignment,” scheduled to appear in a future issue of Lovecraftiana.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Edward Carmien

schedule.desc: The contemporary fan community known as the furry fandom estranges fan practices as they are widely understood. In Untaming Fandom, a book currently under development, I blend Queer Theory, Fan Studies, Speculative Fiction Studies, and Print Studies to illustrate how fans’ numerous printed works illustrate fan communities’ overlooked texts and histories, challenging readers to accept fandom in all of its potential, making space for those layers
schedule.title: Untaming Fandom: Furry and Fan Communities

schedule.desc: Steven Popkes, the author of the recently completed Brother to Jackals trilogy, will read from the next novel in the Howard Cycle, The Apocalypse of Wind and Rain.
schedule.title: Reading: Steven Popkes

schedule.desc:
You are a flock of quasi-mystical crows. You have decided, among you, that a nearby human must die. Now, you will test your skills as a beast, an omen, and a trickster to ensure that this death occurs.

Steal keys, inflict curses, peck out the eyes of the unworthy, if need be. Humans are large and strong and clever, but you are swift and cunning, and you have the eye of Fate on you. The condemned will fall.
schedule.title: Murder of Crows

schedule.desc: Afterlife (USA), Eye for an Eye (USA), Invasion ’53 (USA, directed by Danielle Weinberg), The Data is Wrong (UK), Wake Up, Dolores! (USA, directed by Dan Rathke).
schedule.title: Even More Science Fiction Short Films

schedule.desc: There are things that go bump in the night, and horrors that plague the day. Join these leading Black and Indigenous authors for an exciting discussion of horror stories coming from Indigenous and Black communities.
schedule.title: Rue and Sage: Discovering Black and Indigenous Horror

schedule.desc: Kids of any age (parents are welcome too) take a walk to create a scale model of the solar system. Starting with a small soccer ball posing as our sun, we pace off the relative distances to place as many planets as we can walk to in the time we have, into their relative positions. Prepare to have your mind boggled.
schedule.title: Take a Stroll Through the Solar System

schedule.desc: We've had a bunch of new Star Trek options lately, in particular Which ones feel the most "Trek-like" and which take the franchise in new and interesting directions? This discussion circle will give you a space to express your opinions and engage with other fans of the franchise.
schedule.title: Geek Out About: New Star Trek!

schedule.desc: Diversity improves art. Representation matters. How can artists, particularly artists working in imaginative and fantastic imagery, improve the diversity in the people (and other beings) that they’re depicting? (Aside from incorporating ethnographic features, and not just changing skin tone.) What are the dos and don’ts?
schedule.title: Depicting Diversity in Visual Art

schedule.desc: What are the survival skills and supplies a teen needs to survive the zombie apocalypse? Grill the experts (not literally) about what they think are the critical must-haves. (This panel is for teens)
schedule.title: How Teens Can Survive the Zombie Apocalypse

schedule.desc: In this talk, Dr. Ross Mead will provide an overview of his research and development of fundamental social behaviors (such as speech, gestures, eye gaze, social spacing, etc.) that serve as building blocks for autonomous face-to-face human-robot interaction (HRI), and how his company (Semio) is using these behaviors to bring robots to life.
schedule.title: Bringing Robots to Life: Building Social Intelligence

schedule.desc: Immigrants have a unique perspective and often combine the experiences of both their origin country and their new home countries in a melange that illuminates the cracks in society. Come listen to authors as they share their journeys through countries and fiction alike.
schedule.title: We Get the Job Done: Immigrant Perspectives

schedule.desc: How do you create a fantasy farm setting? Join farmers, gardeners, and historians for tips on how to bring realism to that dimension of your writing. Can you grow enough wheat on just a few acres to supply flour for the winter? Fodder for a cow to take it through the winter and have milk? What preservation practices did people use before canning came along? Some practical advice for current growers might be included.
schedule.title: Farming in Fantasy: Practical Tips for Imagined Worlds

schedule.desc: The return to the Moon is both exciting and fundamentally different than in the Apollo era. Who all is going there and what are the potential risks and rewards of using public/private partnerships for lunar exploration? What new scientific questions do we expect to explore? Come and discuss all aspects of humanity’s return to the Moon!
schedule.title: Artemis II:Ii: Are We Going Back to the Moon to Stay?

schedule.desc: You’ve decided to GM for your RPG group. Maybe this is your first time, maybe you’re an old hand, but you want to tell your own story. How do you go about it? Plot out every little detail? Develop hundreds of NPCs? Or just write some notes on a few index cards and dive in? This workshop will help you make your own worlds and tell your own stories at the table.
schedule.title: How to Tell Your Own Stories at the Table

schedule.desc: Unlike early French filmmaker Méliès, the work of his contemporary, Catalan/Spanish filmmaker and cinematographer Segundo de Chomón (1871-1929) has only recently come under serious study. A pioneer of cinematographic techniques, Chomón is best known for his work in fantasy. Most interest has been shown in his films of high fantasy or the supernatural: demons and ghosts that terrify humankind; fairies and gnomes which populate the rural landscape; sorcerers and magicians that conjure whimsical phantasms into fleeting appearance. In this presentation I wish to focus on Chomón’s works that feature low fantasy, specifically the homely, prosaic kind. In such “normcore” films as Ah! la barbe, Le rêve des marmitons, La table magique, and Une excursion incohérente, we see characters going about their ordinary, quotidian lives, using commonplace items or performing menial tasks, when suddenly their world becomes infused with the fantastic, to the characters’ puzzlement, delight, or utter consternation.
schedule.title: The Films of Segundo de Chomon: Tripping the Normcore Fantastic

schedule.desc: A deep dive into tactics, strategies, and useful practices for revising novels and stories with Martha Wells and Kate Elliott.
schedule.title: The Revisions Process: Dialogue between Martha Wells and Kate Elliott

schedule.desc: Join representatives from Friends of the Island Fox (FIF), the only nonprofit dedicated exclusively to protecting and conserving the endangered Channel Island Fox. You will learn about the fox’s remarkable history, including its near‑extinction in the early 2000s. If you are curious about the adorable real‑world fox behind our convention mascot, this is a rare opportunity to learn directly from the people working to safeguard this unique species.
schedule.title: Meet the Island Fox: Conservation, Comeback, and Care

schedule.desc: Several of our pros have stories set in historical time periods or have created alternate timelines for their work. Find out how they tackled the research, how they decided what to change, and where history might take them in the future.
schedule.title: Where to Start? Researching History for Writing

schedule.desc: Hugo Award-winning author and table top role playing game enthusiast Amal El-Mohtar will choose which of her works to read at this event by rolling a d20. She may also take requests.
schedule.title: Reading: Amal El-Mohtar

schedule.desc: How do you create a realistic but fictional language from the ground up? Linguists and authors who have done just that discuss what it takes to create a convincing language, from cultural contexts to sound systems to grammars to vocabularies.
schedule.title: The Art and Science of Inventing Languages

schedule.desc: The Incomplete Worldcon Podcast-Some sci-fi fan news, a bit of Worldcon advice, and a brief look back at Worldcons of the past. Join us for a special LIVE episode of The Incomplete Worldcon Podcast! We're so excited to discuss a Worldcon AT the Worldcon WITH our Worldcon friends, including you! Sarah and Isabel will give you the lowdown on the convention so far, including our favorite things and THINGS WE DID NOT EXPECT!
schedule.title: Live Podcast: The Incomplete Worldcon Podcast

schedule.desc: Patrick and Teresa Nielsen Hayden are a married pair of writers, editors, and publishers who've been hanging around the SF&F world for over fifty years. They have edited award-winning SF&F novels, typed a manuscript for Joanna Russ, and looked at the sun through the Pope's solar telescope. Come chat with them about history, language, fandom, publishing, exposition, fiber arts, music, genealogy, copyediting, and whatever else happens to come up.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Teresa and Patrick Nielsen Hayden

schedule.desc: Ask a panel of agents about why writers need an agent, and the best way to get one.
schedule.title: What Does An Agent Actually Do For An Author?

schedule.desc: Is the internet and social media primarily driven by machines? Are bots, algorithms, and AI creating more content than people are? Are they driving human thinking? Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince predicts AI bot traffic will exceed human traffic by 2027. Once a fringe idea, the "dead internet theory" is beginning to look real. Can we identify machine interactions? Should we? Are humans leaving the public internet, and where are they going?
schedule.title: Is There A Man Behind The Curtain, Or Is The Internet Dead?

schedule.desc: First Person, Second Person, Third Person Limited, Third Person Camera-Eye, Omniscient with Narrator as Character, Omniscient with Narrator Off-Stage, Unreliable Narrator, all these possible perspectives are vital to telling a story. Panelists will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each, giving examples of where it's done well, or in a fresh way.
schedule.title: Point of View, What's the Point? (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Learn the mechanics of the audiobook process from a group of professionals who will outline all aspects of production, casting, and distribution of audiobooks, including rights issues, casting concerns, and marketing. Find out how writing lends itself to audio, and get tips from the narrators who bring words to life.
schedule.title: Audiobooks 101: The Process for Indie Authors and Rights Holders

schedule.desc: Harry Turtledove is an escaped Byzantine historian who writes alternate history, other sf, fantasy (a lot of it historically based), and, when he can get away with it, historical fiction. He can't sing but does make bad puns (as if there are any others). He has been known to talk about why fascism is right out and how cats are the secret masters of the universe. He may not this time, though, for fear they're listening.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Harry Turtledove

schedule.desc: Gaming criticism is in an odd place in 2026. Publications like Dicebreaker and Polygon have reduced their coverage, while indie sites like Rogue and Rascal are coming up. What does games criticism look like in 2026? Where is the best work being done in video game and tabletop criticism? Are the two in conversation or are they separate worlds?
schedule.title: Critical Success: How Critics Discuss Gaming

schedule.desc: We depend on science to understand the world. But science changes. For example, the best minds once considered Earth the center of the universe. Worse, this is a time full of deniers. The current American government is firing scientists. What is the place of science in society?
schedule.title: Science is Not Truth. It's Hypothesis and Hard Work

schedule.desc: Practice speaking the Navajo language with accomplished speakers and native speakers.
schedule.title: Conversation Practice in Navajo

schedule.desc: Kid attendees will take the created rockets to launch in an outdoor space using possibly a few scientific methods to launch them.
schedule.title: Launch a Rocket - Kids

schedule.desc: Join us for today’s feedback session. This is the best way to connect with the convention organizers and ask any questions you have about the con. Your participation will help us to address current issues and capture new opportunities that we might otherwise miss. Your feedback matters and will be heard by future Worldcon organizers as well!
schedule.title: Feedback Session - Saturday

schedule.desc: It’s after midnight in Providence, when the eccentric, problematic author H. P. Lovecraft receives three visitors: Fellow pulp writer Frank Belknap Long; Lovecraft’s estranged wife, Sonia Greene; and Nyarlathotep, a figment of Lovecraft’s feverish imagination. One part horror story, one part Dickensian Christmas panto, The Failure of the Century is the first play by Nick Mamatas, author of Move Under Ground, and the Lovecraftian crime novel I Am Providence.
schedule.title: "The Failure of the Century" (staged reading)

schedule.desc: John Wardale makes dozens of animals and other objects from long skinny balloons. These include dogs, dragons, giraffes, elephants, ninja turtles, mermaids, aliens, hats, motorcycles, and the starship Enterprise. He will teach us how to do balloon sculpting by helping everyone to make their own dog. (Allergy warning: balloons contain latex.)
schedule.title: Balloon Animal Sculpting Workshop (Saturday)

schedule.desc: Fandom has great potential to attract people. Many who found it stayed for years. Yet, many fans need to get away from it all or gafiate at some point. Some fans are not willing to join at all. Where does the magnetism of fandom lies? Our panelists will discuss how the entry points to fandom have changed over the years and what made them stay.
schedule.title: How I Found Fandom and Why I Stayed (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Fanart (here defined as art based on an existing creative property) isn’t limited to illustrative work. Fiber artists (quilters, knitters, crocheters, etc.), woodworkers building props/models, and other forms of handcrafts can be included under this umbrella. Can this type of work comment on, critique, expand upon, or otherwise transform the source media, and how? Let’s share and discuss our favorite examples!
schedule.title: Fan Crafting as Transformative Work

schedule.desc: Tammy Coxen is a conrunner and cocktail maven. Have a question about the history of cocktails and spirits? Want tips on how to stock your home bar and make great alcoholic or non-alcoholic cocktails at home? Want to know more about how the Hugo Awards are administered? Then this is the table talk for you!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Tammy Coxen

schedule.desc: All artists begin painting on their own easel while the audience watches. After a certain amount of time, they will change and begin painting on their neighbor's painting. This continues until every artist has painted on every easel.
schedule.title: Paint Around

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss the current relationship between traditional and indie publishing. What advantages and disadvantages are offered by each path? How are author expectations shifting? What myths still persist, and what does the future look like for hybrid careers?
schedule.title: Traditional vs. Indie Publishing—Changes and Why They Matter

schedule.desc: Watch award-winning artist Brittany Otto demonstrate how she creates Oneiroframes, combining layered paper and light into shadow box sculptures. Each line is painstakingly hand cut with a blade. Her work is influenced by her love of fantasy, biology, and struggles with mental health to create transformative, dream-like portals that draw the viewer into expressive worlds that shine brightest when surrounded by darkness.
schedule.title: Oneiroframes Demo

schedule.desc: Editors don't hate you. While the moment you open a critique and you find it covered in markups is never comfortable, editors are trying to make your work stronger. How can you establish a good working relationship with your editor? What sort of boundaries are healthy? When and where should you push back? Come find out!
schedule.title: Working with an Editor

schedule.desc: Whistling, night creatures, ghosts, and possessions—horror exists in every culture. How does contemporary horror from different communities build on the stories and legends our elders used to scare us and transform them into the chilling tales of today?
schedule.title: Oh the Horror: Horror from Diverse Perspectives

schedule.desc: E.G. Condé (Esteban) is a chronically queer and Puerto-Rican nerd who writes Indigenous Futurism (Taíno) and is pathologically obsessed with Final Fantasy. Join the author of Sordidez for unhinged rants about role playing games from the 90s, advice on how to fuse science and ancestral memory in your worldbuilding, the danger and joy of turning dreams into story fuel, and what it’s like to have a day job as an anthropologist of “the Cloud”.
schedule.title: Table Talk: E.G. Condé

schedule.desc: Gregg Castro is an activist in the California Native Community and has wide experience in the cultural, social, political and community revival of indigenous communities. He brings these experiences to the sci-fi con community on panels of diversity, equity, cultural aspects, storytelling, linguistics and indigenous ecological restoration efforts. He has written non-fiction articles on California Native culture.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Gregg Castro

schedule.desc: Much of today’s AI discussion rightly focuses on risks and ethical concerns: energy and water use, labor disruption, misuse, and inherent bias. This session looks at a different question: could AI contribute positively to shared societal goals? We’re interested in AI as a set of tools embedded in wider systems: energy, science, public infrastructure, climate, and health. This is not a hype panel but looking at it through a futurist lens.
schedule.title: AI Through a Hopeful Lens

schedule.desc: Early fans often tried their hands at poetry. Some of these hands were finely wrought inscribers of inspiring verse. Others were more like the clumsy paws of the grill chef who burns the toast. Regardless, it’s entertaining reading and worthy of remembrance. We’ll bring our favorites and invite the audience to recite selections of their own choosing.
schedule.title: Early Fan Poetry: From the Sublime to the Ridiculous

schedule.desc: You've pitched a project to an editor who is interested. Yay! But. They want to see an outline. You're a pantser! You like letting the story evolve through experimental writing! What are you going to do? Our panelists are those who outline plus those who usually don't outline but have learned to as they discuss strategies for developing an outline: How to keep the idea fresh in your mind, how to approach structure, how to infuse the outline with the passion you feel when pantsing the story, etc.
schedule.title: How to Change your Writing Process--When Pantsers have to Outline (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Using avant garde filmmaker and anthropologist Maya Deren’s writing about Balinese witchcraft in the 1940s, and Jerome Bruner’s notion of Narrative as Reality as overarching frameworks, I consider how “successful deviants” like me “rewrite” the rules of reality in ways that parallel the powers of Neo in The Matrix and the awakened mages in White Wolf’s Mage The Ascension. Magic isn’t esoteric: it is omnipresent in everything we do.
schedule.title: Transgender witching and storytelling

schedule.desc: Joe Haldeman will read from a hard-sf work in progress.
schedule.title: Reading: Joe Haldeman

schedule.desc: The best horror stories and thrillers thrive from perfectly timed quotable wisecracks or tension-breaking humor. Endless drama can get dull quickly unless there’s comic relief. This panel looks at “adding funny” to creative projects that aren't comedies but are in need for a dash of slapstick or cerebral wit at the right moment.
schedule.title: How to Add Funny to Your Prose

schedule.desc: From the Iridian war of Iain M. Banks' Culture novels to the Time War of Doctor Who, many of the major military conflicts in speculative fiction have a religious aspect. Religion offers a powerful narrative tool with which to create conflict. This panel will discuss what these depictions of religious conflict tell us about modern thoughts on faith and culture.
schedule.title: Muad'Dib Says Fight: Religious Wars in Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: Fanfic and other transformative works often challenge societal "norms." The primacy of canon and the views of the original author, the centering of the male gaze, and the heterocentrism of source texts are frequently subverted, satirized, or dismissed through these kinds of fanwork. What is it about these works that enables such freedom from modern conventions? Are there some kyriarchal norms that we are more inclined to reject than others?
schedule.title: Transformative Works as "Transgressive"

schedule.desc: How do you define your creative self, and how do you feel about how the rest of the world defines you and what you do? Every term for a person who creates has some assumptions and historical/cultural baggage attached. Do you feel that you had to “earn” the term you use to define what you do, or push back against gatekeeping? Are you a “real” artist? And yes, Impostor Syndrome will be part of this discussion too.
schedule.title: Artist, Craftsperson, Maker, Crafter, Hacker: What’s in a Name?

schedule.desc: Inconceivable! is the long-running game show of nerdery and nonsense, trivia and tribulations, hosted by author and podcaster Dan Moren. Each episode, we test our panelists’ knowledge of the nerdy, the useless, and the obscure as two teams face off over five rounds to answer diabolical questions about TV shows, comics, movies, games, and more.
schedule.title: Inconceivable! The Game Show of Nerdery and Nonsense

schedule.desc: Charlaine Harris has been a published writer for forty-five years. She has written in a wide variety of genres, and she's had three TV adaptations of her work (so far). If you're interested in sustaining a long career, or if you want to know about switching genres, she's the one to talk to.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Charlaine Harris

schedule.desc: Living in microgravity in cramped spaces is unlike anything that the general public has experienced. But for more than 120 years science fiction authors have described traveling in space in understandable and compelling ways. This paper explores how the methods of transport for visiting distant locations on earth shaped the stories and visual expressions of science fiction.
schedule.title: How then shall we travel in space?

schedule.desc: Feeling burdened or overwhelmed by all the work an indie writer has to do that is NOT writing? One option is publishing through a wriers' co-op. Book View Cafe has been running since 2008. Come listen to Book View Cafe members talk about how it got started, and how to keep it going. Panelists will discuss nuts and bolts, strategic planning, and how the co-op has evolved.
schedule.title: Writers' Co-Ops: Book View Cafe

schedule.desc: Are You There (USA), Autonomous (Canada - Jennifer Mosier), Battle Of LA (USA - Patrick Pizzolorusso), How to Prepare for Time Travelers in the Workplace (Canada - Grigory Luken), Lumen (Brazil), Mindhackers (Mexico), The Hum (Canada), The Passenger (USA), The Vagabond (USA), We Look Like You (USA)
schedule.title: Shorts, Shorts, and even more Shorts,

schedule.desc: So you've got a great idea for a space opera or a movie set in another solar system. How do you build your planets so they don't look like Earth in another place?
