What do you need to know about orbital mechanics, types of suns, and alien ecology? Starships and Dyson Spheres? How do you convince readers or watchers that you've got it right and deliver a sense of wonder? Who can help you? Who has done it right?
schedule.title: Making Fiction Planets Feel Real; Getting the Science Right!

schedule.desc: A welcoming gathering for costumers and cosplayers of color (Black, Indigenous, and other People of Color) attending LAcon V. Hosted by Gigi Coulson of the Costumers of Color nonprofit, this meetup is a relaxed space to connect with fellow makers, costumers, cosplayers, performers, and any fans of color who shares an interest in costume and creative expression. Everyone is invited to stop by, say hello, and meet others in the costuming community. Visit Costumers of Color’s website at https://costumersofcolor.org to learn more.
schedule.title: Costumers of Color Meetup

schedule.desc: Fear and lust have long been bosom buddies, and the current uptick in horror romance just reinforces that feeling of frightened arousal. How does one find the romance in a horrifying situation? How do those relationships grow? Do you stop running long enough to make out, or is that a death sentence? Come hear how these authors have tackled this age-old dichotomy.
schedule.title: Fear and Lust in Las Vegas: Horror Romance

schedule.desc: As fantasy has shifted over time, we still refer to some staples of the genre. If you're entering the fantasy genre for the first time, what old-school fantasy books should you read? Panelists explore ways to find foundational fantasy that holds up to a modern lens.
schedule.title: Foundational Fantasy You Should Read

schedule.desc: We are always trying to depict the alien, but how far do you have to go to be truly out of this world? What tools and techniques can help create believable creatures and technology? What in the natural order can you change? Are there rules you should never break?
schedule.title: Designing Things That Don’t Exist

schedule.desc: Although Lord of the Rings was written as a single book and then divided by its publisher, writers often copied its three-book structure (intro to the protagonists opposing evil, traveling the world, battle with the Big Bad). Panelists will discuss series types (one story arc vs. episodes), ending episodic books (cliffhanger? partial resolution?), and what happens when later books deviate from the structure, premise, or theme of earlier books.
schedule.title: Writing Series vs Standalones

schedule.desc: Have you ever wondered where LA place names like Topanga came from? Meet the Tongva (the Totoongvetam), the First People of the Los Angeles Basin and Southern Channel Islands, and learn the basics of our indigenous culture, beliefs, and Uto-Aztecan language, a relative of Hopi, Comanche, Ute, and Nahuatl. You will also learn to speak a few words and phrases.
schedule.title: Tongva 101, An Introduction to Tongva

schedule.desc: Want to build and shape the world 50 years into the future? Come imagine a brand new world or work on one you already have in progress in 60 minutes with published authors. (This workshop is for teens.)
schedule.title: Build a World in 60 Minutes: An Interactive Science Fiction Workshop

schedule.desc: Were you at LAcon I, II, III, or IV or are you interested in learning more about the earlier LAcons that led to this one? Join us for stories from those memorable Worldcons. Hear others and share your own.
schedule.title: LAcon Stories

schedule.desc: The Kingdom of Caid, the SCA’s Southern California branch, brings its fighters to Worldcon for live combat demonstrations. See armored combat with rattan swords and rapier fencing in Renaissance style, both at full speed. Between bouts, fighters share how their armor and weapons are made, how bouts are won, and why honor is at the center of it all. Stop by, ask questions, and find out how you can try it yourself.
schedule.title: SCA Combat Demo - Saturday #2

schedule.desc: Space Opera has become home to a plethora of stories exploring the boundaries of gender. This is only natural given the flexibility of alien biology and culture. Come dive into the wealth of stories blowing past the gender frontier.
schedule.title: Where No Man Has Gone Before: Sci-fi and Gender Exploration

schedule.desc: You’ve seen the art show and thought to yourself “I make fantasy and/or sci-fi artwork and it would be SO cool if I could show like all these amazing creators.” Art Show participants discuss how to research, apply for, and show work at conventions. Learn about portfolio development, and applications and all the steps right up until convention weekend setup and breakdown.
schedule.title: So You Want To Be In A Convention Art Show

schedule.desc: Holly Black, author of The Cruel Prince and Book of Night, will be reading a short story from her upcoming collection, A Conspiracy of Charming Monsters.
schedule.title: Reading: Holly Black

schedule.desc: Fiction loves to portray scientists in extreme conditions, but what is life really like for researchers? Experts talk about the weirdest things they have experienced in their day jobs. Is truth really stranger than fiction?
schedule.title: Tall Technical Tales: Stories from the Lab, Bench or Field

schedule.desc: Gregory A. Wilson, author of the award-winning graphic novel Icarus and award-winning Gray Assassin Trilogy, reads from Shade and Shadow, a novel manuscript going on submission in the fall.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Gregory A. Wilson

schedule.desc: Using your imagination make a tiara, crowd, wand, or animal.
schedule.title: Chenille Stem Creations

schedule.desc: Jennifer Hudak is a Nebula-winning and Hugo-nominated poet and writer, a yoga/movement teacher, and a mermaid far from her natural habitat. Come chat with her about the myth of "good posture," her 20-year old Siamese cat Loki, favorite teas, knitting pocket-sized animals, writing and publishing short stories and poems, and the quintessential dish of her adopted hometown of Rochester, New York: the Garbage Plate.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Jennifer Hudak

schedule.desc: Pirates are a romantic ideal in more ways than one, but the truth of piracy through history isn't so pretty. Authors talk about the reality of pirates and how they've hijacked the pirate ideals and truths for their own work.
schedule.title: Swab the Decks! Historically Accurate Pirates

schedule.desc: Explore urban fantasy and sci-fi inspired by Asian heritage and culture where traditional elements meet modern streets and futuristic skylines.
schedule.title: Heart of the City: Asian Urban SFF

schedule.desc: Join Guest of Honor Tim Kirk in Artist Alley! Head on down to the Exhibit Hall and visit with him as he draws.
schedule.title: Artist Alley with Tim Kirk

schedule.desc: Weyodi OldBear, Indigenous futurist, citizen of the Comanche Nation, author of As Many Ships As Stars will be reading from book one of her three book series (The Bees Made Honey In The Rich Man's Skull) The Root and The Seed and The Thief In Between. Be there or be square.
schedule.title: Reading: Weyodi OldBear

schedule.desc:
Journey into the wilderness between ten intergalactic societies and search for the source of rumors about an impossibility: a broken column made of unbreakable material.

Game system: Spells of the Symphony
schedule.title: The Broken Column

schedule.desc: Does extra-terrestrial life really need water? From the building blocks of galaxies and stars to the known environments of planets in our Solar System and beyond, we can seek clues about the nature of potential life. This panel will discuss these connections including elements in the universe, cells as factories, and extra-terrestrial habitats to see what life needs to survive: in science or in fiction.
schedule.title: Do Extraterrestrials Really Need Water?

schedule.desc: Concepts such as Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics have driven discussion of potential Artificial Intelligence (AI) for decades. Can such coded 'laws' give moral or practical guidance to robots and bodiless systems, ensuring that humanity won't come to harm? Can such laws still constrain beings who get smarter than us? Can SF tales help us protect ourselves from our own technology?
schedule.title: The Laws of Robotics and Other Ways AI Might Learn from SF

schedule.desc: Few creators have shaped television science fiction as profoundly as acclaimed writer and producer Ronald D. Moore. The creative force behind "Ba, Outlander, and For All Mankind, Moore's work examines humanity through its greatest challenges, in all its grief and hope. Join Tania Lotia as she explores a career that has helped define modern science fiction, creating worlds that inspire and endure.
schedule.title: From Deep Space to Alternate Histories: In Conversation with Ronald D. Moore

schedule.desc: Fiction has been flooded with cautionary tales of dystopias. However, when the real world seems already dystopian, how can speculative fiction provide a guiding light to get us through the turmoil? Which books should we reach for in order to help us plan our own path through the world?
schedule.title: Carrying the Torch During Times of Transition

schedule.desc: Dungeons and Dragons (D&D) is most tabletop roleplaying game groups’ default ruleset, and it works well for a lot of cases, but it has a focus on fantasy and magic. How do other rulesets portray the same subject matter, and how do other rulesets let us play in other genres and settings? What are the benefits of branching beyond the d20? And how do you pick a ruleset for the game you want to play?
schedule.title: Beyond D&D: How Do Other Rulesets Enable Play? (Virtual)

schedule.desc:
Thin IC is spoiled rotten, and he might have something a bit wrong with him, and maybe he does; but something definitely ain't right with him. If eyes are indeed the window to the soul, I think that thing sitting in the other room is straightfrom the depths of hell itself.

Character sheets, dice and pencils provided.
schedule.title: Shadowrun: Spoiled Rotten

schedule.desc: Infinite Branches is a round-robin anthology of queer disabled poets. Poets choose their own poems in response to the poet preceding them, and each group of poets concludes with a discussion of their work in the context of each other. Facilitation for choices, statements, and discussion is done by guest editor Toby MacNutt.
schedule.title: Interstellar Flight Press Presents Infinite Branches

schedule.desc: Make your own star map using glow in the dark stars or the pinhole technique. Star maps can be used to make the patterns more accurate.
schedule.title: Make A Star Map For Your Bedroom

schedule.desc: Come explore some of the easy techniques of tie dye with easy to use color concentrates that are safe for all ages.
schedule.title: Easy Tie-Dye Techniques

schedule.desc: A panel of award-winning visual effects artists turned science fiction and fantasy authors explore how the language of film translates into the written word. Just as quick cuts build tension on screen, short sentences accelerate pacing on the page. Close-ups become interior monologue. Wide shots become immersive worldbuilding. Discover how cinematic storytelling—timing, framing, rhythm, spectacle, and emotional focus—can shape unforgettable prose.
schedule.title: Cinematic Storytelling

schedule.desc: Diana M. Pho is a two-time Hugo Award-winning fiction editor with nearly 20 years of experience in publishing, She's an open book when it comes to talking about the book industry, from getting into the industry as a publishing professional to writing advice to favorite reads. She's always looking for a hobby to keep her off screens; the latest obsession is junk journaling and collage, audio drama podcasts, tactics for mutual aid, and cat pictures.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Diana M. Pho

schedule.desc: A lightly instructed life drawing workshop. Participants will draw a costumed figure beginning with quick gesture drawings and gradually progressing into longer poses using traditional techniques. Participants are also welcome to work with other drawing materials if desired.
schedule.title: Life Drawing Workshop

schedule.desc: Join artist Jacob John White in the Exhibit Hall for an in-depth examination of his large scale art exhibit, Bellringer, based on his graphic novel of the same name.
schedule.title: Docent Tour of the Bellringer Exhibit

schedule.desc: How do you craft vivid and complex cultures for your characters without forcing readers to sit through a lecture on economics? Whether it’s the price of an egg or the obstruction of a trade route, you want your readers to understand economic’s significance, but not at the cost of boring writing. Economics winds through almost every moment, a pattern glimpsed out of the corner of the reader’s eye. How do you explain it? How do you get it right?
schedule.title: Creating an Economy Without Inducing Math Anxiety

schedule.desc: A party of heroes becoming a new family unit is a staple of the fantasy genre. What makes this trope so likeable? And where can you read about fantasy found families?
schedule.title: Fantasy Found Families

schedule.desc: Arkady Martine is the Hugo-winning author of the Teixcalaan duology, the novella Rose/House, and a multitude of short speculative fiction. She is also Dr. AnnaLinden Weller, a climate and energy policy analyst and a city planner. She is rarely bored but often tired. She will read from her newest, unpublished novel.
schedule.title: Reading: Arkady Martine

schedule.desc: The British science fiction writer Adrian Tchalkovsky addresses these problems, at least obliquely, in many of his recent novels. In different volumes, he takes an overall evolutionary framework for granted, but examines different ways in which natural selection might work.
schedule.title: The Alternative Darwinisms of Adrian Tchaikovsky

schedule.desc: Shane Hawk, an enrolled Cheyenne and Arapaho horror writer and editor, reads from his short story "IVOЯIES," which was recently published in his latest project, Never Whistle at Night, Part II: Back for Blood. This tale is a direct descendent of his story "Behind Colin's Eyes," found in the original Never Whistle at Night anthology, as it follows the bloodline fifty years into the future.
schedule.title: Reading: Shane Hawk

schedule.desc: Maquel A. Jacob, Science Fiction and Horror author of the Curve of Humanity series reads from their short story collection, *Along the Curve*, which is based on that universe.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Maquel A. Jacob

schedule.desc: The podcast where we quiz the smartest celebrities we know and find out why they love what they love! In this episode, Bill Prady faces off vs. Mary Robinette Kowal. Who will fact themself better?
schedule.title: Go Fact Yourself Live - Prady vs. Kowal

schedule.desc: This round table will bring togethor authors for a discussion on what makes their female characters who blur the lines between what is wrong and what is justice unforgettable. From rage-fueled antiheroines to empathetic villians, explore how the women who challenge the idea of clear-cut morality—sometimes make us root for the chaos.
schedule.title: Lethal Ladies: Monstrous Women in SFF

schedule.desc: Terese Mason Pierre - acclaimed author, poet, and editor - is joined in conversation by Camille Hernandez, Poet Laureate of Anaheim. Together, they will explore Pierre’s creative journey, the intersections of poetry and speculative fiction, and the inspirations behind her award-winning work.
schedule.title: Special Guest Interview: Terese Mason Pierre

schedule.desc: An overview of Chumashan, the indigenous family of languages spoken along California’s Central Coast, from Malibu to San Luis Obispo, including the Northern Channel Islands. This course will focus on teaching the sound structure of Ventureño Chumash, and also on how words and sentences are made in the language. Learn to speak a few phrases in this unique and storied tongue, and learn about Chumash culture in the process!
schedule.title: An Introduction to the Chumash Language

schedule.desc: Works of horror have historically expressed truth to power, taking on inequality and unjust systems, and giving a good scare or two. In recent years, readers have been offered brilliant socio-political takedowns within the genre. How are writers currently taking on fascism, isolationism, weaponized nationalism, and authoritarianism? How do we balance the social and the political with the speculative and terrifying?
schedule.title: Horror Writing as Resistance

schedule.desc: Some stories feature fantastical librarians with even more fantastical libraries. What makes this setting and character so alluring? And where can you find these libraries and librarians in media?
schedule.title: Fantastical Librarians and Their Libraries

schedule.desc: An Indigenous Futurist, Weyodi OldBear, is a citizen of the Comanche Nation, retired professional baker, author of As Many Ships As Stars and The Root and The Seed and The Thief In Between (book one of a three book series) and two upcoming novels from Android Press. With an interest in alternative social and economic systems, Weyodi would be happy to chat about any old thing up to, and including, golden age science fiction and the best method for fry bread and/or deli halfsour pickle making.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Weyodi OldBear

schedule.desc: What does it mean to write speculative fiction in English while coming from a non-Anglophone country? How do geography, culture, and language shape the futures we imagine? This panel invites writers, especially those writing in English as a second language, to discuss the unique opportunities and constraints of working from outside the UK/US market.
schedule.title: Global Voices in an English-Language Market

schedule.desc: Catherynne M. Valente, Hugo nominee and internationally bestselling author of Space Opera, Fairyland, Deathless, and many more, will read from Nobody But Us, her upcoming SF thriller from Tor Books.
schedule.title: Reading: Catherynne M. Valente

schedule.desc: How do working scientists retain joy and curiosity is a difficult world. What tools do they use to come to breakthrough ideas, to slog through long experiments, and to stay passionate about sometimes difficult ideas?
schedule.title: Mind of a Child: A scientist’s curiosity about the world

schedule.desc: This panel of teens know their own minds and wants to tell you all about their thoughts and desires when it comes to the stories they want to see. This panel is for teen and adult writers who want to know more about what teens are interested in and enjoy seeing in story.
schedule.title: Teens Know What They Want: Hear from Teens on YA Topics

schedule.desc: The Voyager spacecraft discovered volcanoes on Io, studied the mysteries of Saturn’s Rings and now return data from outside our solar system. Join members of the Voyager Flight Team as they discuss these and many other daring feats of the twin spacecraft. This is an interactive session planned for people between 6 and 12 years old, but the parents in attendance with their child are welcome to participate.
schedule.title: The Daring Feats of the Voyager Spacecraft

schedule.desc: Many of us rely on regular medications or physical aids in our daily lives. What drugs and tech would be critical if civilization collapsed? How feasible would manufacturing be? What alternatives exist to modern drugs, and what are their drawbacks? Join us for a practical discussions of healthcare after the zombie, alien, robot, etc. apocalypse.
schedule.title: Medicine After The Apocalypse: Managing Chronic Conditions

schedule.desc: Building off our previous research on the description and inclusion of librarians in the works of Hugo nominees, we are continuing to interrogate the depictions of female-dominated professions in the genre. We hope to determine if librarianship is an outlier within other female-dominated professions or if the depictions of nurses, secretaries and teachers follow this trend by analyzing the text of Hugo award nominees and winners.
schedule.title: Pink Collar Galaxy: Feminized Professions In the Hugos

schedule.desc: Erin Brown is a poet and author of horror, fabulist, and weird fiction, with lots of experience in building, leading, and participating in critique groups and writers’ circles. Drop by to discuss what makes a great and sustainable critique group and writer’s circle, swap a few war stories- and maybe meet some potential accountability partners!
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Erin Brown

schedule.desc: Elizabeth Sandifer is a DIY critic hurling book-length essays into the gaping maw of the illiteracy crisis. It’s very punk rock. She’s got absolutely massive ADHD and has written about Doctor Who, British comics, occultism, They Might Be Giants, neofascism, 70s folk music, and the end of the world,. so really you can probably get her to talk about anything you want.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Elizabeth Sandifer

schedule.desc: Data centers are resource hogs, whether they are used for AI, crypto, or just storing iPhone pictures. It’s unethical to put them in under-resourced areas, it’s not fair for everyone to pay for the electricity, and they contribute to water bankruptcy. What are the solutions? Some people suggest data centers belong in the cold of space, others hope that they’ll drive energy breakthroughs. What are the privacy and national security implications?
schedule.title: Data Centers: Where Should They Go and How?

schedule.desc: More stories are migrating from fanfiction circles to bookstores either via traditional publishing channels or self-publishing, How is this changing the landscape of publishing? Are all these changes for good (new audiences, new subgenres, new marketing avenues)? What would we like to see more or less of in this space?
schedule.title: Filing Off the Serial Numbers

schedule.desc: Dave should have known: you put garbage in, you get garbage out. Let's talk about all those murderous robots and computers we love to hate in literature. This panel explores the ins and outs of machine mayhem, just don't start singing Daisy.
schedule.title: Killer Robots & Rogue Computers in Science Fiction

schedule.desc: The future of space science and exploration is diverse and inclusive: if we make it so! This panel will discuss topics both fact and fiction about shaping an inclusive future for space. Disabled, indigenous, queer, fat, old and young; space is for everyone. This panel will discuss topics both fact and fiction about shaping an inclusive future for space and the efforts being made towards (or away from) ideals envisioned in science fiction.
schedule.title: Crafting an Inclusive Future for Space Exploration

schedule.desc: Speculative fiction allows writers to imagine bodies, relationships, and desires that might not exist in the real world yet still reflect very deep and moving emotional truths. How do writers keep speculative sexuality grounded in character and culture rather than novelty? Our panelists will explore how fantasy and science fiction reshape desire, identity, and connection beyond the limitation of human bodies and culture.
schedule.title: You Want to Put That Where? Intimacy in Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: Andrew Ross is a master of parody, satire, and wit who has been cranking out new songs almost daily since 1997. He is a delightful performer and is a Pegasus Award winner for best composer.
schedule.title: Concert: Andrew Ross & The Possible Side Effects

schedule.desc: This workshop will focus on different forms of hair braiding: four strand “round” braids, classic (three-strand) French and (three-strand) Dutch (or inverted-French or underhand), crown braid (a modified three-strand French braid), and five and seven-strand fingering techniques. We might work on hearts, spirals and pullup-weaves. Which we use will be tailored to the desires and abilities of the participants.
schedule.title: Fancy Hair Braids Workshop (Saturday)

schedule.desc: Amal El-Mohtar is a writer, critic and table top role playing game enthusiast. Come along to chat about birding, deadlifting, Canada’s most important cultural export (Heated Rivalry), the current state of publishing, favourite episodes of Game Changer and many other delightful topics.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Amal El-Mohtar

schedule.desc: Professional artists tell us the things everyone should know coming into the art profession.
schedule.title: What's the Most Important Advice to Give Aspiring Artists?

schedule.desc: In this writing workshop, participants will learn how the ekphrasis poetic form focuses on using words to expressing a relationship with visual works of art. This writing wokrshop is for all levels.
schedule.title: What You See is What You Write

schedule.desc: We’re not changing our emissions fast enough to slow climate change. Geoengineering is about humans actively intervening in natural climate processes to change the outcomes. It’s risky, possibly foolish, and may be our only hope. What are the options, risks, and opportunities?
schedule.title: Geoengineering: Great danger and/or great opportunity?

schedule.desc: 2026 debut authors, indie and traditional, talk about getting their first project into print.
schedule.title: Meet Debut Authors of 2026! (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Latinx Diaspora writers in the Americas are pushing speculative fiction in bold directions, blending genres and drawing on the cultures of both the U.S. and countries of heritage. Across borders and genres, writers take on overlapping themes. Join this panel of Latin American and Latinx Diaspora writers as they discuss how they get innovative on the page.
schedule.title: Crossing Genres: Latin American and Latinx Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: Dragons! Depending on which mythology you draw on, dragons generally are benevolent and wise and also beautiful (Asia) or hideous, fire-breathing, and inimical to humanity (West). What about dragons in lesser-known mythologies? If you are designing your own dragons for your manuscript, what bioscience are you tweaking, and how will these dragons fit into your eco-system?
schedule.title: Dragons: Friends to Humanity or Evil Monsters?

schedule.desc: At different times throughout history, pivotal technological changes have changed the course of history. Panelists will choose an interesting piece of tech or scientific knowledge and explain its development and importance.
schedule.title: Technology through the Ages: a History of Science

schedule.desc: Panelists discuss how the world in which we set our stories is a character. Do our choices about setting drive the story? How does the setting shape culture and characters? How can we add the lived-in detail that makes a setting feel real? How do we know if our setting and story don’t work together?
schedule.title: Choose Wisely: Our Setting is Our First Character (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Tracey Baptiste will read from her superhero series BOY 2.0 which follows Coal, a kid in foster care who suddenly discovers he can turn invisible. Tracey will read a pivotal scene and answer Q&A.
schedule.title: Kids Reading: Tracey Baptiste

schedule.desc: Bring a current handwork project for a casual meetup of communal crafting and conversation.
schedule.title: Craft and Chat (Saturday)

schedule.desc: Come for the immortal slow burns, stay for the otherworldly magic. Explore the irresistible world of supernatural romance: where vampires brood, ghosts linger, storybook witches lust, and romance has a habit of doing the impossible.
schedule.title: Defying Reality: Supernatural Romance

schedule.desc: Here you are at Worldcon, right next door to Disneyland and the Black Spire Outpost, the Star Wars themed area. Join other fans sharing their best tips for getting the most out of your visit to Galaxy's Edge.
schedule.title: Welcome to Batuu: Visiting Galaxy's Edge

schedule.desc: Poets and editors discuss award winning speculative poems and collections exploring what elements stood out.
schedule.title: What Makes a Poem Award Worthy

schedule.desc: LitRPG has become extraordinarily popular. Panelists will discuss how this once-niche genre is moving into the mainstream in SFF.
schedule.title: LitRPG and Progression Fantasy

schedule.desc: See the latest installment in the Superhero series Surge of Power, followed by a question and answer session with the director, Vincent Roth. Feature: Surge of Power: Where There's Smoke (USA). Shorts: From the Wizard's Workbench (USA - Ed Greaves), Narrative (USA), The Black Smoke of Prediction... (Croatia)
schedule.title: Surge of Power and other tales

schedule.desc: Melinda Snodgrass, Star Trek :TNG writer and author of Imperials, Wild Cards and The Caroligian Series will be reading from her upcoming Loki novel. How do you survive in the modern world when you no longer have worshippers?
schedule.title: Reading: Melinda M Snodgrass

schedule.desc: Get Out (2017) was the first of a new wave of big budget horror movies directed by African Americans; an Academy Award nominated and winning movie; and a box office success. Another way to interpret Get Out is as a reworking of first zombie movie White Zombie. Get Out can be considered a Black-centered reframing of White Zombie, retelling the first zombie movie, as it reverses stereotypes about gender and race in horror and zombie media.
schedule.title: Unexpected Zombies: Get Out as White Zombie

schedule.desc: Every historic culture has included queer folks: people with non-normative experiences of love and desire. The stories of their lives are shaped by the varied ways in which their cultures understood gender and sexuality, which can sometimes seem as alien to us as a science-fictional setting. Authors talk about both situating their queer characters in their historic surroundings and rewriting those settings to create the stories they want to tell.
schedule.title: Stars on their Wrists: Queering History

schedule.desc: Despite having the word "war" in its title, Star Wars is not usually considered Military SF. Paul Atredes starts a galactic war, but most fans wouldn't class the novel Dune as Military SF, either. So what is military science fiction? This panel will discuss the conventions of the subgenre and why military science fiction continues to resonate.
schedule.title: What the heck is Military Science Fiction anyhow?

schedule.desc: The Astounding Award Finalists are all fresh from their first publication and chomping at the bit to dig into their next. Come hear from the next generation of incredible writers as they talk about their journeys, their advice to other beginning writers, and what they are planning next.
schedule.title: New on the Scene: Astounding Award Finalists

schedule.desc: Bring your kids to see, gently touch, and play many kinds of musical instruments. Meet the musicians who play them.
schedule.title: Musical Instrument Petting Zoo

schedule.desc: Humans are exploring two extreme environments at once: deep space and the deep ocean. Sophisticated environmental systems are required for both versions of the deep, and both can kill the unprotected. This panel explores the similarities and differences between deep-sea exploration and space exploration, and discusses how each discipline can learn from the other.
schedule.title: Extreme Environments: Space and the Deep

schedule.desc: Chris Rose and David O'Neill do a variation on the worldwide success gameshow Taskmaster. Creativity, improvisation, and rule‑bending are rewarded. Points are arbitrary. Hilarity is guaranteed.
schedule.title: Taskmaster

schedule.desc: Popular settings for science-fiction are space stations or remote outposts across the universe. What is so attractive about this? How much into the science do writers need to get when describing these settings. Can the space station itself serve as a plot device?
schedule.title: Stories Set on Space Stations/Outposts

schedule.desc: How has the evolution of music composition and technology affected the development of science fiction movie soundtracks? Panelists will share and discuss examples of movie music.
schedule.title: Evolution of Science Fiction Soundtracks (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Beginning authors, learn about aspects of self-publishing ranging from page layout to interior art for print and ebooks, plus publication requirements like ISBN numbers and copyrights. We'll cover pricing, hiring out vs. doing it yourself and the tools available, plus briefly touch on audiobooks. Find out how all these decisions affect expectations for income and getting your book into brick-and-mortar bookstores and libraries.
schedule.title: Your Manuscript Is Ready for Indie Publication. Now what?

schedule.desc: What have we learned from our experience with COVID-19? Panelists will discuss what we’ve learned in terms of disease monitoring, public health, and steps individuals can take to keep themselves healthy. We’ll also discuss some missteps in science communication, and accommodations that didn’t end up being helpful, such as tiny plastic screens.
schedule.title: COVID-19 Lessons: Practical Takeaways for the Next Pandemic

schedule.desc: Kath David is a puppeteer by trade, a writer by accident, and a book editor on purpose. Her puppets can be found in collections all over the world. She enjoys writing and editing. With her husband, Peter David, they edited a number of anthologies for Crazy 8 Press. Come have a chat about puppets and writing along with the business of writing. There will be puppets.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Kath O David

schedule.desc: What began as a 1966 Berkeley backyard party of history and sci-fi/fantasy fans became the Society for Creative Anachronism, or the SCA: a worldwide historical re-creation community celebrating 60 years of bringing the past alive. Welcome to Caid and the Current Middle Ages, where panelists with 2 to 58 years in the SCA share tales of combat, costuming, arts, pageantry, service, fandom, friendship, and how newcomers can join the adventure. The past is calling. Bring your curiosity.
schedule.title: 60 Years of the SCA: From Backyard Party to the Known World

schedule.desc: Panelists and the audience conspire to turn familiar stories, and maybe even some poetry, into unrecognizable hilarity. Panelists will be challenged to read the results out loud, in front of an audience, without totally cracking up.
schedule.title: MadLibs: Anything Goes

schedule.desc: Monte Lin is a ttrpg freelancer and Uncanny Magazine's nonfiction and managing editor. Come talk to him about table top role playing games (ttrpg), what kinds of writing you can do in ttrpgs, and tips on editing for ttrpgs! Or you can ask questions about Uncanny Magazine, writing nonfiction essays for them, or their production process. Or let's complain about the freelancing life in general. (And if you have tips on fountain pens and inks, when's your table talk?
schedule.title: Table Talk: Monte Lin

schedule.desc: Happy 25th to Studio Ghibli's classic, Spirited Away! At the time it was considered so good that it even won an Academy Award. How does it hold up today? What influence has it had on the genre?
schedule.title: Spirited Away At 25

schedule.desc: While folk horror originates from everywhere, mainstream Western publishing has gobbled up folklore from around the world and made it unrecognizable from its origins. The Slavic vampire, the Algonquian wendigo, and African vodou are prime examples. This international panel scratches the surface of varied regional horror inspired by folklore and how it all translates into fiction.
schedule.title: Global & Regional Horror: Monsters from Different Cultures

schedule.desc: Class is in session! Join panelists for a dynamic discussion about what it means to use their craft to bring historically underrepresented identities to YA and middle grade fantasy. Everyone deserves to grow up with a little magic.
schedule.title: Magic School is in Session: Representation in YA and MG Fantasy

schedule.desc: Xbox, PS5, Steamdeck, or your smartphone. All are welcome - come and meet other fans of video games!
schedule.title: Meetup: Video Gamers

schedule.desc: Join us to learn the basics of cell therapy: using living cells to treat diseases. Discover why you might want to use cells instead of standard medications, what types of cells doctors use, and different ways cells can be delivered to the body. We’ll talk about companies developing these treatments and how to tell legitimate trials from scams.
schedule.title: Cell Therapy 101: Treating Diseases with Living Medications

schedule.desc: A live recording of the Worldbuilding for Masochists podcast, where fantasy authors Marshall Ryan Maresca, Cass Morris, and Natania Barron talk about the craft of worldbuilding and answer questions from the audience. With new episodes every other Wednesday and frequent guest authors joining the co-hosts in conversation, the podcast explores history, culture, science, and more, encouraging writers to choose new and exciting ways to shape their invented worlds, rather than merely repeating assumptions, presumptions, and common tropes without interrogating them. Worldbuilding for Masochists is a six-time Hugo Finalist for Best Fancast.
schedule.title: Live Podcast: Worldbuilding for Masochists

schedule.desc: What happens when eroticized power is treated as personality rather than practice? This session looks at how consent cultures actually function, why dominance appears so frequently in stories about monarchy, magic, training systems, and immortality, and how speculative elements—magical control, brain implants, otherwordly bonds—can either illuminate or obscure real questions of agency.
schedule.title: Yes, Sir! BDSM, Consent, & Authority in Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: So many stories with fantastical creatures feature the well-known types: werewolves, dragons, faeries, and vampires. What other creatures should be featured? Where can we find stories, film, and TV shows that look at the lesser known magical or folkloric creatures?
schedule.title: Rare Fantastical Creatures and Where to Find Them

schedule.desc: GameLit, LitRPG and other sub-genres are an outgrowth of the wild popularity of video gaming in our culture today. Even if the story is not explicitly a gaming sub-genre, modern SFF has been influenced by the excellent worldbuilding, mechanics, and storytelling of games. The panelists will discuss how the influence of gaming is impacting SFF today and sparking writers' creativity.
schedule.title: How Videogames Inspire Writers' Creativity

schedule.desc: Conventions began as small, fannish events which have, over the years, evolved into diverse forms including big comic cons. Despite being the smaller, less-funded variety, fannish cons have survived till this day. Panelists will discuss the current challenges and whether this model is sustainable in the long run.
schedule.title: Is Fannish Convention Model Sustainable In The Long Run?

schedule.desc: Women were instrumental in shaping and developing speculative fiction for longer than the genre terms have existed. This panel celebrates the many women writers, artists, publishers, etc., who were responsible for creating what we know and love now.
schedule.title: Women Who Built the Genre (Before Anyone Noticed)

schedule.desc: As we all know, not all fantasy stories take place in completely different worlds. Many are set in alternate and often magically infused versions of our own from the actual five boroughs of New York to unnamed locales that are clear cutouts of real countries and cities. How do we best use the world around us when writing speculative fiction? How do we honor the history of a real place while still using the full breadth of our imaginations?
schedule.title: Writing Fantasy in Real Worlds

schedule.desc: Some transformative works creators seek validation through support from canon creators or sources. But others create shared "headcanons" and alternate universes that reject it, in part or in whole - where the finale didn't suck, their favorite characters never died, & everything seems "better." What's so appealing about this approach? Is there a pattern to the stories that inspire this reaction, and what fans decide to keep or discard?
schedule.title: How Important is Canon, Anyway?

schedule.desc: Young Adult Gothic fiction blends the spine-tingling atmospheres and rich diversity of the Gothic genre with the formative experiences of youth. Join our panelists as they explore what makes a story Gothic, drawing on settings and traditions from around the world. Discuss how the genre engages young readers, and how today's authors are reinventing classic Gothic traditions to haunt new generations.
schedule.title: Youthful Hauntings: A Journey through YA and YR Gothic

schedule.desc: From American Sign Language, to military handsign and theives' cant, humans have found ways to communicate without words through all of history. The use of gesture based languages has been found throughout much SF/F/H literature as well. Explore more about these languages and what they can bring to genre writing, with tips on how to create your own. (This is a panel for teens.)
schedule.title: Signs, Signals, & Secret Codes: Gestural Languages for Teens

schedule.desc: Many fans love collecting items. It may be books, art, trading cards, fanzines, textiles, or other fun stuff! Yet just obtaining the item may not be enough. Time may take its toll on the collection. Collections may be damaged by water, light, pests, and even dust. In this presentation we will show what we can do at home to improve the safety of our collection(s).
schedule.title: Caring for Your Collection(s)

schedule.desc: How do you create a realistic but fictional mythology from the ground up? Mythologists and authors who have done just that discuss what it takes to design a convincing belief system, from creation stories to deities to rituals.
schedule.title: The Art and Science of Inventing Mythologies

schedule.desc: Explore how SFF authors use heritage, inherited stories, traditions, and ancestral connections in their work—creating speculative fiction inspired by lineage and cultural markers rather than nation-states.
schedule.title: Roots on the Page: Writing Shaped by Heritage (Virtual)

schedule.desc: David Brin's Hugo winning novels include Startide Rising and The Uplift War and runners-up EARTH, Glory Season and The Postman (filmed by Kevin Costner.) A Caltech Distinguished Alumnus, David consults for NASA, companies, agencies and nonprofits about science and our onrushing future. The Transparent Society (nonfiction) won the Freedom of Speech Award. His new book on AI - AIlien minds - is about raising these new entities to be good citizens. David mentors new writers with his two series of YA SF novels for teens. His SF comedy is THE ANCIENT ONES. His play THE ESCAPE has its first full performance at LAConV.
schedule.title: Table Talk: David Brin

schedule.desc: Western Africa has a rich legacy of stories steeped in spirituality and mysticism that have endured the impact of colonial interference. Join these modern authors from across the global diaspora as they carry these narratives forward in today's book landscape, bringing larger-than-life West African inspired stories to the forefront of the genre.
schedule.title: West African Myth And Magic in Modern Fantasy

schedule.desc: Kendra Tornheim sings songs inspired by roleplaying games and books over decades expressing love, grief, and a sprinkle of antifascism.
schedule.title: Concert: Kendra Tornheim

schedule.desc: "May you live in interesting times" is a curse of sorts. Currently, we need to cope with a world that has become way too "interesting." Where we can find hope? How can one make a change? And last but not least, how do we accept things that are out of our control? Let's discuss the self-care, history, and lessons from fandoms in other times and places.
schedule.title: Fans Finding Hope in Difficult Times

schedule.desc: Veronica G. Henry reads from her Publishers Weekly-starred sci-fi novel The People's Library — where a futuristic library is powered by AI, and something's gone wrong with the algorithm.
schedule.title: Reading: Veronica G. Henry

schedule.desc: A meetup for Indigenous creators to be in community. Discuss topics, and address challenges faced specifically by Indigenous creators of all mediums.
schedule.title: Meetup: Indigenous Creators for Indigenous Creators

schedule.desc: Studio heads Eric Kaplan (Futurama) and Noel Belknap (Rick & Morty), with animator Mike Nordstrom, launch Kapknap Animation studio! Get a preview of My Friend Coffee, a dystopian animated workplace comedy about how capitalism takes the best of you and sucks ya dry. The team discusses building an indie studio, Patreon funding, and YouTube distribution. They will also debut Eric's new sci-fi novel and project, The Legend of the Wolf Whale!
schedule.title: Futurama to Indie Sci-Fi: Launching Kapknap Animation

schedule.desc: From guilty crushes to 'Enemies to Lovers' tropes, falling for the villain isn't unusual any more. Panelists explore why villainy is so attractive, from the wicked mindset to the tight black leather pants. Hear from authors who have embraced dark characters and decided to run with them, not away from them. Warning, these black-hearted characters cross your boundaries with abandon.
schedule.title: Villain for You, Never to You: Villains as Romantic Leads

schedule.desc: Leanne Schwartz, author of A Prayer for Vengeance, reads from her latest fantasy, To a Darker Shore, a Hadestown-meets-Dante’s Inferno-inspired katabasis that School Library Journal calls “a phenomenal work.” An autistic inventor travels to hell to avenge her friend sacrificed in her place, only to find him alive—but monstrously transformed. The work explores ableism, toxic beauty standards, moralizing of body size, and religious trauma.
schedule.title: Reading: Leanne Schwartz

schedule.desc: Reuben "Tihi" Hayslett is a queer author and activist who lives full time in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico. His debut short story collection was named Best Indie Fiction of 2019 by Kirkus and his 2026 novel, Orbital Bebop, is recieving critical acclaim as well. Join Tihi and chat about world-building, queer people of color characters, progressive politics and activism, Dothraki, High Valyrian and other conlangs, how to relocate out of the US, and how to write novels when you live with an attention-hungry cat.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Reuben "Tihi" Hayslett

schedule.desc: This roundtable discussion is for people interested in what speculative poetry is and are aiming to experiment or strengthen areas in current speculative poems by examining the works of speculative award winning poets.
schedule.title: Speculative Poetry 101 & 201

schedule.desc: David J. Peterson is a language creator best known for his work on HBO's Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon; Legendary's Dune films; Warner Bros. Superman and Supergirl; and the CW's The 100, among others. Join this table talk to chat about language creation, languages in general, linguistics, any of David's various TV/film projects (present or past), or whatever happens to be on your mind.
schedule.title: Table Talk: David J. Peterson

schedule.desc: What's the very first filk song you wrote or played or heard? Here's a fun opportunity to share songs no one might have ever heard from you before, or perhaps not in a very, very long time. If we run out of firsts, we may have time to share "old" filk songs or request ones you'd like to hear if anyone remembers them.
schedule.title: Theme Filk: My First Filk Song

schedule.desc: This is a critical look at gender roles in horror—from the evolution of the Final Girl to queer horror narratives and subverted tropes. How do we challenge, celebrate, and/or modify these storytelling conventions
schedule.title: The Final Girl and Beyond: Gender, Power, & Tropes in Horror

schedule.desc: Join Michael Cassutt for a viewing of his 2024 short film, The Summer Machine, based on a story by George R. R. Martin and starring Lina Esco, Matt Frewer, and Charles Martin Smith. Discussion will follow the viewing of this 35 minute film.
schedule.title: THE SUMMER MACHINE: Viewing / Discussion

schedule.desc: Alex Pheby is a writer and lecturer. Come along to chat about weird fiction, worldbuilding, surviving as a writer in academia, and anything else you feel like bringing up.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Alex Pheby

schedule.desc: Bruce McAllister, author of Dream Baby and The Village Sang to the Seat: A Memoir of Magic, will read two brand-new short stories.
schedule.title: Reading: Bruce McAllister

schedule.desc: By popular demand, the bananas are back! Join us as panelists perform dramatic readings of real Ig Nobel Award-winning and other Improbable Research papers, then attempt to answer audience questions. Celebrate “Research that makes people LAUGH… then THINK” in this science-based improv event.
schedule.title: Improbable Research: Ig Nobel Award Dramatic Readings

schedule.desc: Through the Syllable collective, Fabrice Guerrier, the Haitian author and painter, is helping create shared SFF settings for collaborative storytelling. The widely acclaimed Sauútiverse was Syllble's first brainchild, and there's more coming.
schedule.title: Landscapes of the Mind: Fabrice Guerrier (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Attending conventions is absolutely amazing. We can meet our friends, listen to panels, collect autographs, and enjoy the atmosphere. Yet there is no rose without thorns, from the con-crud, through the post convention blues, up to conrunners burnout and ecological impact. What are the dark sides of conventioning?
schedule.title: The Dark Side of Conventioning

schedule.desc: The divisions that lead to a conflict do not have to be geographic; sometimes they are economic. Wars between the rich and the poor, between industrial and agricultural, and between white collar and blue collar can all lead to violence and bloodshed. Let's talk about economic conflicts in science fiction and fantasy, from working class Belters to privileged elite elves.
schedule.title: There Will Be Class War

schedule.desc: Carolyn Ives Gilman, award-winning author of Touring with the Alien and The Ice Owl, reads from her new SF mystery story Testament of Leaves.
schedule.title: Reading: Carolyn Ives Gilman

schedule.desc: The Masquerade is one of the prime events at a Worldcon, rivaled only by the Hugo Award Ceremony. It is an onstage presentation extravaganza where genre costumers of all levels and abilities show off their skills and compete for awards. The event also includes a half-time show featuring belly dancing and other entertainment; to take place while the judges are conferring. Please join us for a night of excitement and wonder!
schedule.title: The Worldcon Masquerade

schedule.desc: Theodora Goss, award-winning author of the Athena Club series, as well as numerous short stories and poems, reads from a work in progress.
schedule.title: Reading: Theodora Goss

schedule.desc: Kel McDonald is an Eisner award winning comic editor and Eisner nominated comic creator. They have a wide experience in comics, whether self-published, a larger publisher, creative end of things, or administrative. Come chat about making comics that might be hard to fit into the growing landscape of the comic industries.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Kel McDonald

schedule.desc: Come test your wits with six rounds of geeky trivia questions and puzzles! You can play solo, but it's even more fun with a team of three to six people. Questions will cover topics from visual puzzles to wordplay to entertainment to quirky trivia, but you can expect a special focus on science fiction and fantasy for WorldCon! It's low stakes with fun as the goal. Come spend an hour testing your brain, scoring points, and groaning at all the lame jokes you'll hear.
schedule.title: Geektastic Trivia Spectacular

schedule.desc: The Oasis is a calm, welcoming place where you can rest and recharge at your own pace. You don’t have to talk to anyone unless you want to. You’ll find simple activities like coloring, short readings, and self-care supplies. If you need something, just ask—we’re here to help.
schedule.title: The Oasis - Saturday

schedule.desc: Join Cecilia Tan, Midori, and Laura Antoniou as they lead you through a smorgasbord of SM sci-fi and a farrago of fetishy fantasy fiction. Selections may include both published and unpublished works. All genders, orientations, and roles welcome, but you should be 18+ years of age!
schedule.title: Kink After Dark

schedule.desc: Filk music started out with people getting together in a circle in some random place at a convention to swap songs. We're official now and in a larger space, but it's still the same supportive tradition of sharing music together late into the night. All voices, instruments, and styles including a cappella welcome. Come by to sing or to listen!
schedule.title: Saturday Open Filk

schedule.desc: David J. Peterson is an author and constructed language (conlang) creator. Jessie Peterson has a Ph.D. in linguistics and was a professor of linguistics for 13 years, and is now a professional conlanger. She is the author of the book How to Create a Language: The Conlang Guide. Between them, they have created languages for Game of Thrones, Dune, Superman, and Elemental. They co-host LangTime Studio weekly on YouTube.
schedule.title: Creating Language: A Dialog Between David and Jessie Peterson

schedule.desc: The Future is Antifascist poet Brian U. Garrison reads from his 2026 chapbook. Join and practice building hope for the future!
schedule.title: Reading: Brian U. Garrison

schedule.desc: Director of Anaphora Literary Press and its three periodicals (Speculative: The Magazine). Routledge published her Introduction to the Attribution of Literature (2025, which changes the history of British literature with stylometry), and will soon publish a creative writing textbook completed while Assistant Professor of English at Dickinson State University: Writing Speculative Fiction. Seeking writing collaborators, offering writing consulting, and publishing and editing assistance.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Anna Faktorovich

schedule.desc: From consoles to keyboards, diverse writers from different disciplines will explore how their gaming lives reflect, and sometimes rewrite, their real ones. Join us to explore video games as sites of personal meaning and cultural discourse. We will discuss how it intersects with race, gender, and identity for those who live at the margins of the video game mainstream.
schedule.title: Avatars, Quests, and Extra Lives

schedule.desc: Jaymee Goh is a steampunk scholar, a fantasy writer, and an editor of some really great books. Come ask her questions about the editor/writer relationship, her favourite steampunk pet peeves, or what book production is like outside of writing/editing! Or talk about cooking, crafts, and cat rescue.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Jaymee Goh

schedule.desc: Na’vi language experts discuss compare how the language has been used, how often, and the differences in use between the three Avatar movies.
schedule.title: A Discussion of the Na’vi Language in the Avatar Movies

schedule.desc: The COVID-19 pandemic definitely reshaped our world and fandom was not an exception. For months, no conventions could take place in the “real world” but fans still found a way to meet: we moved cons online. What footprint did those months leave on fandom? Let's discuss what was lost because of the pandemic but also what we gained thanks to it.
schedule.title: Fandom in the Time of Pandemic: What We Got and What We Lost

schedule.desc: Join our language workshop where you will hear an overview of the creation of the Na'vi language from Avatar, and also learn to speak a few words and phrases.
schedule.title: Kaltxi! Learn "Hello" and More in Na'vi

schedule.desc: We just realized Heimdall is a tree! We found a lost Loki story on the Faroe islands! Hel isn’t black on one side after all, she’s blue! Mixing storytelling with fresh discoveries, Ada Palmer discusses advances in Norse myth research, what we’ve found and why it took so long to find it, a history of Medieval sources and 19th & 20th century scholarly (mis)adventures. New discoveries mean even cooler Norse myths for our fiction!
schedule.title: Norse Myth Research, or Why We've Been Wrong About Vikings

schedule.desc: Queer people have often only seen themselves in comics through metaphorical stories, like Marvel’s mutants. There is a clamor for explicitly queer people to be included, and furthermore, included outside of tragic narratives and integrated into the stories beyond focusing on their queerness. Is there still a place for metaphor? What comics have queerness done well? How are comics unique in combining representation with metaphor?
schedule.title: Queerness in Comics: Representation vs. Metaphor (Virtual)

schedule.desc: What makes a great review? What makes a gloriously scathing critique? Our panelists dig into the art of SFF criticism from a fan perspective: zines, blogs, social media, and beyond. We’ll share tips for reviewing well, explore how fan criticism shapes fandom culture, and tackle the tricky stuff: bias, spoilers, and beloved-but-flawed works.
schedule.title: Critiquing the Critics (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Cora Buhlert is a writer and translator from Bremen in North Germany and also the winner of the 2022 Hugo Award for Best Fan Writer. Come and virtually chat with her about science fiction and fantasy from the 1930s to today, self-publishing, blogging, translation, renewable energy, the Brisbane in 2028 Worldcon bid, toy collecting, Masters of the Universe and anything else that catches your fancy. There will be (virtual) coffee and cookies.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Cora Buhlert

schedule.desc: Angela Acosta, author of the Elgin nominated poetry collection A Belief in Cosmic Dailiness (Red Ogre Review, 2023) reads a selection of cozy speculative poetry about space station used bookstores and overzealous onboard toaster ovens.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Angela Acosta

schedule.desc: More fantasy books feature queer characters as our discussions about queer identity grows. What are some books that showcase the LGBTQIA+ community well? What are the trends as more SFF includes queer characters and culture?
schedule.title: Queer Fantasy (Virtual)

schedule.desc: With dozens of anime shows rushing at us every few months, it's easy for good stuff to be overlooked. What are your favorite less-discussed anime shows of recent years?
schedule.title: Hidden Gems of Anime (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Phoebe Barton, author of short stories and interactive fiction and part of the Hugo finalist Escape Pod team, reads from her unpublished science fiction noir novella A Land of Bad Decisions. It's noir, but on Mars!
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Phoebe Barton

schedule.desc: How can fiction and stories assist in assessing and developing policy, invite better research questions, and serve as a teaching tool? This interactive workshop demonstrates how African speculative fiction can be utilised in STEM educational settings and policy spaces to expose blind spots, navigate power imbalances, and remedy marginalisation in research and knowledge production. Participants will engage with stories from the Applied African SF Toolkit, organised by theme and accompanied by discussion frameworks modelled on seminars at Imperial College London, the University of Nairobi and University of Lagos. By the end of this session, participants will understand how to use fiction in research, policy, and education to challenge existing knowledge hierarchies and design more just, inclusive futures.
schedule.title: De-Risking Policy through Fiction: A Workshop from Applied African SF

schedule.desc: Lady Knights & Sword Lesbians are a popular trope in fantasy and sci-fi fiction, but what makes them so alluring? There are many ways to think about heroic positions and expansive gender expression in fantasy fiction. We can reclaim roles like knight/cavalier/jedi or we can find different ways for women & femmes to engage
schedule.title: Lady Knights & Sword Lesbians (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Tiffani Angus is a fiction and non-fiction writer, an editor, a book formatter, and a former academic who still has her hand in teaching newer writers how to stretch their wings. Come along and chat about subgenres of SFF/H, writing history (including historical fashion!), choosing writing workshops & university writing programs, the paths to publishing, fantastical & haunted gardens, women in apocalyptic fiction, and loads of other fun stuff.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Tiffani Angus

schedule.desc: Considering that you are all stars, meet at the hotel lobby for a leisurely 45-minute stroll around the venue. Get some fresh air, exercise, and chat with authors, editors, and artists in an informal setting. Hear about the interesting, fun, and maybe even unbelievable features of Anaheim.
schedule.title: Stroll with the Stars

schedule.desc: A good opening paragraph for a story or novel will carry the work to success. In this hands-on workshop, we will consider seventeen different ways to start a work of fiction, such as action, philosophy, frame, or setting. We'll explore how each one will affect the reader and evaluate the promise it sets for the story. Come ready to write and try out some new approaches. You'll leave with a handout to use these in your work!
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: It’s a Start – A Workshop On Your First Paragraph

schedule.desc: LA has fascinating history of literary SF and fandom from meetings of First Fandom at Clifton's Cafeteria, to those in the Ackermansion. Through the writing of Fahrenheit 451 at UCLA's library, Octavia Butler's bus rides to the Central Library, Harlan Ellison's Lost Aztec Temple of Mars, the invention of Steampunk and the first Latinxfuturist novel. Hear the stories and then plan your own tour of the 'Capital of SF'.
schedule.title: Los Angeles: A Visual Tour of the Capital of Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Are you creating a new world in a complex fantasy or science fiction setting? How do you make sure your ecology works? What can we learn from Earth’s ecology? Readers come to our genre partly for a sense of awe and wonder. How can we give them that through the settings we build, and how do we make those settings a character as well as believable?
schedule.title: Creating Believable Ecology: Getting Fantastic Worlds Right

schedule.desc: How do you channel fear, anxiety and trauma into your writing to reflect the ongoing threat of increasing climate disasters? In January 2025, over 12,000 homes were lost, and 150,000 Los Angeles residents were evacuated and displaced. This panel will spotlight local authors impacted by the recent L.A. wildfires, as well as writers facing other climate threats in their communities, including floods, hurricanes and extreme heat.
schedule.title: The World’s on Fire: Navigating Real Climate Catastrophes

schedule.desc: Star Trek depicted teleportation as moving a whole person (or more) from one place to another. In 2017, Chinese scientists successfully teleported a single photon. This year, Oxford researchers demonstrated the ability to use teleportation to link two quantum computers. How do current theories and approaches to teleportation reflect the science fiction we know? Are there new ways to think about teleportation?
schedule.title: Beam Me Up, Scotty! How Close Are We to Teleportation?

schedule.desc: Gentle morning Tai Chi session.
schedule.title: Morning Tai Chi - Sunday

schedule.desc: Most writers have dayjobs. Many have families or other responsibilities, but are still trying to fit writing into the crevices of busy lives. Likewise, some have no immediate demands, which means the day can slip by without one noticing--and nothing done beyond doomscrolling and staring at the screen. Panelists will offer suggestions for developing a daily writing schedule, including tips for breaking writer's block and getting right into it, how to use small units of time most effectively, how to work out compromises with living companions to get writing time, and how to still get those words out without robbing yourself of sleep.
schedule.title: How to Develop Good Writing Habits

schedule.desc: Most discussions of our evolving understanding of gender tend to revolve around western culture and history. But how does that evolution play out in other contexts? Have different cultures and histories led to different attitudes and touchpoints for gender studies? How have these differences made stories and spaces more or less inclusive?
schedule.title: Beyond the Gender Binary: Gender Around the World

schedule.desc: In this workshop, kids get to build their own science fiction exploration with help from world builders, song writers, and teachers. who will go around the room and everyone says one action they want to take" adventures that work like an old-style text adventure (think "adventure") or a modern day "escape room" but it's theater of the mind.
schedule.title: Science Fiction Worldbuilding for kids

schedule.desc: Alex Shvartsman reads from his brand-new space opera comedy The Best of All Possible Planets, written for the fans of Futurama and Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy.
schedule.title: Reading: Alex Shvartsman

schedule.desc: Sometimes you need to make your characters suffer without going over the top, having them survive the unsurvivable, or be unconscious the whole time. How can you write that sweet spot of pain and misery that can be endured or powered through while still being gut-wrenching to the reader? Which injuries lend themselves best to being healed and cared for by someone else, for the other side of hurt/comfort?
schedule.title: Best Whump Options: Injuries for Fiction (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Cozy SF and Fantasy boomed during the COVID-19 pandemic as we all reached for a warm, fuzzy spot in our genre. Panelists will discuss what we mean by cozy - how to create a cozy atmosphere and cozy characters while still preserving adventure and action. The panel will share examples of cozy SF/F books and short stories we love.
schedule.title: Snuggle up to Cozy SF/F

schedule.desc: Navigate your spaceships through the treacherous orbits of the Solar System, overcome all the difficulties, finance an expedition to Pluto, and be the first to bring back a cargo of immortality dust to Earth in this enhanced historical remake of one of the first science fiction board games ever created. It was originally designed and played by science fiction fans in 1943. To succeed, the players must guide their ships to secure valuable cargo from other planets while building wealth and avoiding dreadful hazards like meteors, pirates, and the deadly negasphere, in order to finance the dangerous game-winning mission to Pluto. Along the way, players may choose to be bold and lead the way into the outer reaches of the solar system, or lurk in waiting while others explore in hopes of pouncing on the final prize. Strategic choices can lead to victory... or calamity.
schedule.title: Interplanetary

schedule.desc: We use the term "Hard Sci-fi" to denote a story that is highly technical in nature. How does one make the divide between "hard" and "soft" sci-fi story? What are the hallmarks of a good hard vs. soft sci-fi story, and what are the best examples? Is this a useful dichotomy to hold? Our panelists have opinions and lists of recommendations to share.
schedule.title: How Hard is Too Hard? A Mohs Scale for Sci-fi "Hardness" (Virtual)

schedule.desc: SFF cons have a long tradition of costuming on and offstage. What makes a costume successful across different environments? What considerations should new costumers consider when creating an ensemble intended for hall wear versus masquerade competition? Join our panel to discuss the ins and outs of costumes for different contexts.
schedule.title: Hall Costume vs Masquerade Entry - What Are The Differences, And Can It Be Both?

schedule.desc: Carl edits sci-fi, fantasy, and horror at the Tor Publishing Group. He's a finalist for this year's Hugo for Editor — Long Form. His books have won the Nebula, Locus, and World Fantasy Awards, the Ursula K. Le Guin Prize, and many others. Join him for a chat about the industry, the state of fantasy and science-fiction, or your favorite punctuation marks. Carl won't buy a book at the table, but he may help you hone a pitch.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Carl Engle-Laird

schedule.desc: Let's face it, a lot of the Romantasy genre is written by straight white women, and while they do a good job (most of the time), we are still falling short on stories by and for diverse voices. Come hear about writing in the gaps and where we still need to find and encourage more voices to rise.
schedule.title: We Need More ______! Gaps in Romantasy

schedule.desc: Looking back, there is a long history of stealing someone's creative work. Make a copy or hire someone to make one. Use copy/paste for images on the internet. Take a photo and print it out. And now AI can be trained to work in your style for someone else's benefit. It's an increasingly challenging world for artists. How much protection do watermarks and copyright still give, and what are the options for protecting your work from AI?
schedule.title: You Stole My Art!

schedule.desc: A fragment from Writing Erudite Speculative Fiction uniquely combines the rules of literary criticism with the demands of maximizing sales in speculative genres. What structural rules can help raise the quality of speculative fiction? The origin of the relationship between character appearance and goodness is explained through physiognomy studies. The theory of the spectrum of gender and sex difference is applied to how writers can experiment with these possibilities in character and worldbuilding. Writers are invited to introduce surprising villains by incorporating many red herrings that detract reader attention away from the hidden culprit due to the magic trick of “inattention-blindness.” Prompts for designing places include: What elements of utopian biophilic design might positively connect residents with their environment instead of introducing pollutants that fight against it? What types of structures do animals build that human designers rarely borrow?
schedule.title: Building Wonderfully Strange Characters and Places

schedule.desc: The Hades and Persephone story is a classic romance we tell again and again. Why are we obsessed with this myth? How does the myth of Hades and Persephone reflect wester social reality? How has it shaped modern storytelling?
schedule.title: Hades and Persephone

schedule.desc: Mona Tewari is the author of Burn the Sea and Before I Bow (coming 4/13/27), and she has long been fascinated by the ways in which the narratives of legend and history shape our views of the present. Join her for a virtual chat about anything that catches your interest, whether it be writing as a part of the diaspora, managing chronic illness, pivoting careers or even baking, journaling, tea, gardening, or having too many hobbies.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Mona Tewari

schedule.desc: Folk horror is famous for its isolated locations, but does remote have to mean rural? Neil Williamson, editor of the award winning anthology Blood In The Bricks, will take you on a tour of the city's lonely corners and no-go zones, and introduce you to the off-kilter communities that inhabit them. The exercises in this workshop will help you re-imagine each of the iconic elements of a folk horror story from a fresh, urban perspective.
schedule.title: Neon Rites: Exploring Urban Folk Horror

schedule.desc: How do audio engineers and podcasters combine the spoken work with sound design to create effective audio dramas? Where do they find effects, music, and technical guides to layer these audio elements together? Our panel will talk about the art of the soundscape of audio dramas, and how to make yours work.
schedule.title: Words Without Pictures

schedule.desc: Storytelling through an immersive theatrical experience has more options than ever. We have LARPs, escape rooms, virtual reality games, and places such as Galaxy's Edge across the street from LAcon V. How has this storytelling technique evolved, and what do diverse perspectives and new technology bring to the experiences?
schedule.title: Immersive Experiences

schedule.desc: How can science fiction be used in the classroom? From elementary education to graduate-level classes, how is science fiction helping students learn?
schedule.title: How Are Teachers Using Science Fiction In The Classroom?

schedule.desc: Telling stories in video games is its own beast. It varies across genres, both in the literary sense of the word but also in the video game sense of the word: science fiction and fantasy, but also action and role-playing, and more. Different games use interactivity differently to tell stories, and even the extent to which a story is told linearly varies hugely. Stories told in games become collaborations between writer, artist, designer, voice actor, and others. Come and listen to two of the writers behind the Hugo Award finalists Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Hades II discuss how they approach the complexities of their playable stories.
schedule.title: Interactive Storytelling: Hugo Best Game Finalists

schedule.desc: Members of the Navajo nation discuss how the Navajo Code Talkers of WWII achieved their unique and critical communications, and its impact on the outcome of the war.
schedule.title: Navajo Code Talkers: How They Did It

schedule.desc: The magic circle is “the space in which the normal rules and reality of the world are suspended and replaced by the artificial reality of a game world”. It flows into the real world and vice versa, when character emotions bleed into player emotions. How can these concepts enhance our play, and how do we make sure we support each other in the magic circle? How can we have our characters fail, or even die, when their emotions are part of us?
schedule.title: Bleeding in the Magic Circle

schedule.desc: The idea of what constitutes a "war crime" has evolved over time as technology and human morality have shifted. As these frontiers of weapons and philosophy continue to develop, for better and for worse, how should and how will the laws of war adjust?
schedule.title: Rules of Interstellar Warfare: The Future of the Laws of War

schedule.desc: Interactive adventures in book form have been with us since 1930. Come take a look at some examples and their different approaches to solo gameplay.
schedule.title: Gamebook Show & Tell

schedule.desc: If you have magic in your stories, it's safe to say you've spent some time trying to lay out the rules. Hear from authors about building magic systems while asking questions about and working on your own. (This panel is for teens)
schedule.title: Thaumawhat? Teen Magic Systems Workshop

schedule.desc: Caitlin Starling, author of the bestselling The Starving Saints and other works of speculative horror, reads from her upcoming “what if vampires had to breastfeed” novel, Milkteeth.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Caitlin Starling

schedule.desc: Story structures in Eastern cultures often differ radically from Western story structures. This presentation examines how cultural values dictate structures: specifically, the four-act structure and circular/nested structures which naturally arise from Buddhist and collectivist values.
schedule.title: Cultural Values in Eastern Storytelling Structures

schedule.desc: Molly O'Neill, Astounding Award-shortlisted author of Greenteeth and Nightshade and Oak, reads from her forthcoming cosy fantasy book, A Summer of Storms. Join for a glimpse into 8th Century Lindisfarne.
schedule.title: Reading: Molly O'Neill

schedule.desc: Bring out your inner Trekkie with this networked computer game experience! 6–8 players take control of the spaceship Artemis, assuming various crew jobs: Helm, Weapons, Science, Communications, Engineering, Fighter Pilot(s), and Captain. The ship’s missions require the crew to work together to overcome challenges such as combat, puzzle-solving, diplomacy, and exploration. An educational (space science) teambuilding experience!
schedule.title: Artemis Space Bridge Simulator (Sunday)

schedule.desc:
Your group of goblins is in trouble. You've totally beefed the job the Dark Lord gave you. Now you're gonna have to scramble to fix things before someone finds out! Accidentally shoot yourself out of your own siege weapon. Pull strange and dangerous things out of your pockets. Set the Dark Lord's summer home on fire... again. Have a blast in this silly little game of goblin hijinks!

Players should be 13+ years old.
schedule.title: ShenaniGoblins

schedule.desc:
REMOTE (Or, Gallyvant's Finale): semiquincentennial = our word o' the year: 2026
A grandfatherly analog ghost and his namesake digital, female grandchild make a certain rural peace with post-Pandemic life's end, while representatives of the country's major institutions - church, state, and commerce - gather nearby to settle the climate crisis for good, their long-needed work neither far away in place nor time, for us the
hope at last. Fortunately, a lesbian lover has her limits and our protagonist Sonnie shows us the localest of remedies may be best, even in this particular conundrum that borders on being another rerun.
schedule.title: "Remote (Or Gallyvant's Finale)" Staged Reading

schedule.desc:
You’re not going back, but you were hired to do a job and they ain’t taking no for an answer. Are jobs and booze all there is? Come find out and play this legendary game!.

Character sheets, dice and pencils provided.
schedule.title: Shadowrun: Forty Ounces to Freedom

schedule.desc: Rounds have people singing different parts of the song at the same time, chasing each other around vocally, which creates harmony. From "Row, Row, Row Your Boat" to Renaissance pieces, singing in rounds is easy and fun for everyone! Facilitators will teach and lead some of their favorite, simple rounds to create amazing sound together. Participation is highly encouraged!
schedule.title: Singing in Rounds to Create Vocal Harmony

schedule.desc: Are two different collecting audiences emerging? One willing to buy prints, the other one satisfied only by paintings? This panel explores how to pursue the joy of collecting in the current era.
schedule.title: Collecting Fine Art in The Age of the Digital Print

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss what censorship is and isn’t, and the different methods used (both direct and indirect) when censoring materials. Panelists will also discuss what censorship in publishing looks like, and what impacts it has on the entire publishing pipeline, from creation to consumption.
schedule.title: Censorship and Publishing

schedule.desc: Dark Academia is unique in its versatility:it is both an aesthetic and a subgenre. It is present in fantasy, horror, literary fiction, romance, and more. Why do we keep wanting to return to school? Academia provides a plethora of tropes, and character archetypes for writers to explore. There is no doubt readers are hooked. This inclusive panel will discuss all of the ways young adault dark academia challenges the idea of school and keeps readers engaged.
