schedule.title: Young Adult Dark Academia: A Syllabus

schedule.desc: Louise Riofrio is educated in physics and astronomy, and worked as Scientist at NASA Johnson Space Center in Houston and in Hawaii studying the Moon. She is known worldwide for discovering change in The Speed of Light. She is author of two popular books, The Speed of Light and Discovery: Alaska to Hawaii. She is also an actress, winning awards from film festivals worldwide. At LAcon she will reveal a revolutionary discovery about gravity.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Louise Riofrio

schedule.desc: An increasingly visible subset of the set of designers today are the maker/users, who design, engineer, and construct objects for personal use. Close to the craftsperson in terms of aesthetic freedom, the maker/users’ have no one to answer to but her or his own client-selves. This project visually plots the design evolution of this project, Queen of the Killer Bees, from first inspiration through final design decisions.
schedule.title: Design Through Concept-Driven Investigation

schedule.desc: Whether traditionally published, indie published, or self published, every author is expected to do a tremendous amount of the lifting required to successfully promote their own books. For many authors, especially those of us who are introverts or struggle with imposter syndrome, this part of the job stirs up a lot of emotion. This session will explore how to build your own brand as an author and how to harness the power of enthusiasm to bypass the imposter syndrome and prioritize your own self-care as you find your audience.
schedule.title: Author Branding for Introverts and Imposters

schedule.desc: The age of women characters in fiction used to mostly skew young or old, with heroines in their prime making up the minority. This trend has reversed in recent years, as middle-aged protagonists have become increasingly popular in fiction. Panelists will discuss how middle-aged women have been portrayed throughout literary history, and how and why this representation has been changing in more contemporary works.
schedule.title: Bless Your Heart: Middle Aged Women as Epic Adventurers

schedule.desc: History was often recorded by the religion of the day, which means this history comes with its own religious lens. How does this affect the history we have and how we view it? Come hear authors talk about the effect religious history has had on their work.
schedule.title: Golden Idols: The Evolution of Religion

schedule.desc: A meetup for Pacific Islander creators to discuss topic and address challenges faced specifically by Pacific Islander creators of all media.
schedule.title: Meetup: Pacific Islander Creators for Pacific Islander Creators

schedule.desc: Scientists answer your questions about their respective fields, the state of science in the world today, and more!
schedule.title: AMA: Ask Me Anything with Scientists

schedule.desc: Not every fanfiction writer aims for professional publication, but some do. While fanfic builds valuable skills, it differs in important ways from writing for traditional publishing. This panel explores which fanfic skills translate well, which habits don’t, and how to adapt your strengths to create successful original work. If you love fanfiction and want to pursue traditional publishing, this session is for you.
schedule.title: Fanfic Can Get You Published (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Lorraine Wilson is a conservation scientist and award-winning author of books spanning and blending genres, most recently the connected science fantasies We Are All Ghosts In The Forest and The Salt Oracle. Come talk folklore, Scotland, climate fiction, genre-fluid writing, navigating publishing (particularly as a disabled author), and why every book is improved by a weird beastie. I can’t guarantee Zoom cats but I can promise salty opinions.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Lorraine Wilson

schedule.desc: Learn what first readers for short fiction magazines, agents, and editors look for in short and long form fiction. Panelists will share tips on common pet peeves in the industry so you’re better armed for submitting your work.
schedule.title: Editors’, Agents’, and Slush Readers’ Pet Peeves

schedule.desc: Create pages of stamps for a journal, notes, or a story.
schedule.title: Stamping Away

schedule.desc: Fantasy has had romantic elements as long as fantasy has been written, but the last three decades have seen an enormous rise in popularity of romantic fantasy--not just in English-language publishing but in non-Western publishing as well. Panelists will discuss popular plot tropes, redemptive arcs, character tropes, the immense popularity of m/m fantasy romance, sexy villains, and much more.
schedule.title: The Marriage of Fantasy and Romance

schedule.desc: Are your rough drafts a hot mess? Don’t worry, nobody has to see those first shaky attempts. With a few tricky techniques, you can turn your rough draft into a story polished enough to make your readers beg for more. (This panel is for teens.)
schedule.title: Diamond in the Rough: How to Revise Your Stories

schedule.desc: How do you craft vivid and complex cultures for your characters without forcing readers to sit through a lecture on economics? Whether it’s the price of an egg or the obstruction of a trade route, you want your readers to understand economic’s significance, but not at the cost of boring writing. Economics winds through almost every moment, a pattern glimpsed out of the corner of the reader’s eye. How do you explain it? How do you get it right?
schedule.title: Creating an Economy Without Inducing Math Anxiety (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Mightier Than the Sword. Join Audiobook’s Golden Voice, Stefan Rudnicki, as he takes you on a journey into the purpose, passion and power of the spoken (sometimes chanted and sung) word. This performance by the two-time Grammy winner invites you to witness a parade of excerpts from SF and Fantasy authors from The Bard to Harlan and from Brecht to Bova. Musical accompaniment by Alison Belle Bews and Gabrielle De Cuir.
schedule.title: Concert: Stefan Rudnicki, Alison Belle Bews, and Gabrielle de Cuir

schedule.desc: Join the Worldcon Cosplay Parade and bring your character to life as we make our way through the convention for all to admire! We’ll meet at [LOCATION TBD], then march, glide, or strut menacingly through the con before wrapping up in [LOCATION TBD] for a photo session and Cosplay Meetup. Whether you’re in screen-accurate armor, closet cosplay, or something wildly original, everyone’s invited to join the fun or come cheer and snap pics of your favorites!
schedule.title: Cosplay Parade and Photo Op

schedule.desc: Contrary to popular opinion, the Luddites didn't simply fear technological development. As Cory Doctorow argues, they asked "not what a technology does, but who it does it to and who it does it for." It's no wonder then that these ideas are found all throughout science fiction. Our panelists discuss this intersection and more!
schedule.title: Luddism and Science Fiction

schedule.desc: The Kingdom of Caid, the SCA’s Southern California branch, brings its fighters to Worldcon for live combat demonstrations. See armored combat with rattan swords and rapier fencing in Renaissance style, both at full speed. Between bouts, fighters share how their armor and weapons are made, how bouts are won, and why honor is at the center of it all. Stop by, ask questions, and find out how you can try it yourself.
schedule.title: SCA Combat Demo - Sunday #1

schedule.desc: Barbara Hambly has written fantasy, horror, historical murder mysteries, some “respectable” historical fiction, graphic novels, media tie-ins, and Saturday morning cartoons. She has also done costuming, belly-dancing, has taught community college, and holds black belts in karate and iaido. She is happy to talk about any of these, plus researching, world-building, and simply answering questions. She does not discuss politics.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Barbara Hambly

schedule.desc: Listen to an excerpt of Van Hoang's adult historical fantasy, The Monstrous Misses Mai, about four young women who accidentally become witches in order to pay rent in 1959 Los Angeles.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Van Hoang

schedule.desc: Oil prices climbed in 2026. The United States is supporting Big Oil. China is becoming a global leader in renewable energy. People can now buy rooftop or personal solar systems. Nuclear is enjoying another day or two of attention. What’s happening in renewable energy around the globe? What are the technologies, the breakthroughs, the hopes, and the possibilities?
schedule.title: Alternative Energy: Tools to Switch on Better Power

schedule.desc: Science fiction got a huge boost when Star Trek became mainstream with its strong moral lessons and long range missions. What works are continuing in that tradition and how do we continue to create new fables with strong moral centers?
schedule.title: Fables in Space: Spaceships with Moral Lessons

schedule.desc: Artist Yvonne Morton will present an overview of California's art tradition: En Plein Air. Artist Bernard Fallon will discuss how to adapt these techniques to produce En Plein Air-style moon- and planetscapes, as well as other celestial bodies. The En Plein Air workshop follows this presentation.
schedule.title: En Plein Air: A California Art Tradition Adapted for Other Planets!

schedule.desc: Classic science fiction imagines big computers waking up either evil, for example Hal9000 or Ellison’s “I Have no Mouth...”, or else super helpful like Heinlein’s Mike in Moon is a Harsh Mistress. Suppose today’s networks and AI wake up sentient. Who would they serve, and who would they replace? What would they value and what would be discarded?
schedule.title: What Happens if We Create Truly Sentient AI? (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Generative learning algorithms, known as Large Language Models, Attention Models, or just AI are the inescapable background radiation of digital life. We will cover the basics of how LLMs work, train one from scratch (on no unethically obtained material), and compare homemade models to large models such as ChatGPT. Finally, we'll discuss the dangers of unchecked AI content proliferation and when it makes sense to leave your Agent at home.
schedule.title: LLMs: What They Can Do, Can't Do, and Will Do Someday

schedule.desc: A panel of disabled writers discusses how their disabilities influence their worldbuilding and their characters. Writers often talk about “how to write a disabled character”: how do disabled writers write a non-disabled character?
schedule.title: Disability and Worldbuilding

schedule.desc: Join Tracey Baptiste, a bestselling author of acclaimed middle grade and young adult fiction, for an engaging conversation with Brandon O’Brien. Known for weaving Caribbean folklore, history, and imagination into unforgettable stories, Baptiste has inspired readers around the world. Together, they’ll discuss her creative process, the power of myth and storytelling, and her journey as a writer.
schedule.title: Special Guest Interview: Tracey Baptiste

schedule.desc: Join our Guest of Honor, Stan Sakai, and watch as he draws Usagi Yojimbo and talks through his process from beginning to end.
schedule.title: The Art Process of Stan Sakai

schedule.desc:
Reimagining Democracy for the 21st Century: Imagine that all of us—all of society—have landed on some alien planet and need to form a government: clean slate. We do not have any legacy systems from the United States or any
other country. We do not have any special or unique interests to perturb our thinking. How would we govern ourselves? It is unlikely that we would use the systems we have today. Modern representative democracy was the best form of government that eighteenth century technology could invent. The twenty-first century is very different: scientifically, technically, and philosophically.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Bruce Schneier

schedule.desc: Join us for a journey back to the Golden Age of SF when Robert A. Heinlein lived, worked, and played at several places around Los Angeles. Hear the panel talk about the places, people, and stories influenced by the City of Angels.
schedule.title: LA & Heinlein

schedule.desc: Leave any preconceptions at the door: Asian fantasy authors are challenging stereotypes about Asian characters and reimagining what strength looks like on the page. Join our panelists as they discuss moving beyond surface-level tropes to center resilience, complexity, and power in all its forms.
schedule.title: Redefining Strength: Asian Heroines Beyond the Stereotypes

schedule.desc: Welcome to ClockWerx. Hundreds of years into the future and far from Old Earth is Mendicant Station: a trading post and waystation made up of smugglers, long-haul ships, and independent-minded people, with a smattering of bureaucrats and tourist traps. The population is called human… but the term “human” encompasses more than your basic furless-primate. All manage to get along (more-or-less) and all of them have stories...
schedule.title: ClockWerx: A Science Fiction Web Series

schedule.desc: Make socks puppets, stuffed animals, or a Frankenstein’s monster of different stuffed animal parts.
schedule.title: Create a Friend

schedule.desc: Inez Ray reads from her much anticipated debut, Buzzard, a feminist dystopian sci-fi about abortion, prison reform, and overthrowing puritanical regimes. Buzzard will be out September 22nd with Left Unread and Bindery Books, enjoy a sneak peak of this Indies Introduce pick and the author's first ever public reading.
schedule.title: Reading: INEZ RAY

schedule.desc: Shapeshifter romance has been around since before Zeus thought a swan was a good shape to seduce women. Everything from werewolves to gelatinous changeling aliens have featured in romance in one form or another... or another. Explore why shifter romance continues to gain our attention.
schedule.title: Were Romance? There Romance! Shapeshifters in Romantasy

schedule.desc: Adapting science fiction and fantasy novels to the stage is a vastly different process than adapting to film. We have seen fannish and professional adaptations, such as the recent examples of Dune: The Musical at Glasgow 2024 and the National Theatre’s Frankenstein. What are the challenges inherent in adapting science fiction and fantasy to the stage? What characteristics lead to a better chance of success?
schedule.title: Adapting SFF for the Stage (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Children's Programming Staff Members will take the kids with parents/guardians through the Art Show. We might bump into members of the Adventurers Club and have a spot for the kids to collect a stamps for their Adventurers Club Passports.
schedule.title: Kids Tour of the Art Show

schedule.desc: Glass and metal, fiber and stone, leather and wood. These are all traditional combinations of materials for art and craft. What are more unusual or experimental combinations, including mixing 2D and 3D, and how do they work?
schedule.title: Adventures in Mixed Media

schedule.desc: Rajeev Prasad's first story was published in The Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction in 2021. He has gone on to publish regularly in F&SF, Clarkesworld, and other fabulous markets. He will be sharing a passage from "The Bone Garden", an urban fantasy novelette, out this month in F&SF.
schedule.title: Reading: Rajeev Prasad

schedule.desc: Award winning author and founding member of the Sauútiverse Collective, Xan van Rooyen, reads from their forthcoming neuroqueer, Afrocentric, dark fantasy novel Born of Malice!
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Xan van Rooyen

schedule.desc: Science Fiction (SF) Prototyping is a powerful method for fostering future-oriented thinking, but application in high school settings needs optimized facilitation strategies. This study quantitatively analyzes the impact of "divergence" (idea expansion) and "convergence" (idea synthesis) phases on the quality of student-generated narratives, with practical guidelines for using SF prototyping to boost students’ creativity and critical thinking.
schedule.title: High School SF Prototyping: Divergence-Convergence

schedule.desc: The Norwescon Speculative Film Festival has been running for six years in Seattle. Come and see some of the best shorts from the last few years.
schedule.title: Best of Norwescon’s Speculative Film Festival

schedule.desc: Marie Parks, emerging asexual fantasy author, winner of the New Mexico Book Award - Best LGBTQ Title, and founder of Sandia Starforgers workshops for speculative fiction writers, will read from her most recent novel, Flightless (Shadow Dragon Press, 2026). Flightless is a fantasy heist with strong social justice themes, and it features an aro/ace main character. Learn more about Marie and her writing at marieparks.com.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Marie Parks

schedule.desc: Shlomi has published several short stories, some Jewish-themed, in addition to an also Jewish-themed murder mystery series. He coordinates a critique group of published authors and collaborated with Elizabeth Moon on Horngard, the latest book in the Paksenarrion Universe this October. He's game to talk about SF, worldbuilding, cultural translation, and the upcoming book.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Shlomi Harif

schedule.desc: Contestants are encouraged to provide feedback to the masquerade staff, pick up submitted workmanship documentation and any last minute items.
schedule.title: Post-Masquerade Meeting for Contestants

schedule.desc: Brenda Cooper will read from her latest collection, When Mother's Dream: Stories. This collection is about strong women, family, and the environment, and includes science fiction and fantasy stories and poetry. All ages welcome.
schedule.title: Reading: Brenda Cooper

schedule.desc: Join Guest of Honor Tim Kirk for a richly illustrated journey through an extraordinary creative career spanning more than six decades. From his award-winning fantasy and science fiction art, including his beloved Tolkien-inspired visions of Middle-earth, to his influential career as a Disney Imagineer, Tim shares stories, artwork, and insights from a lifetime of imagination. Discover how a passion for storytelling shaped a remarkable career in art, fantasy, and themed entertainment.
schedule.title: Tim Kirk: A Lifetime of Imagination

schedule.desc: When writers ask how to market cross-genre, slipstream, experimental or other difficult-to-categorize works, they are usually told, “That’s what small presses are for!” The panelists will discuss writing outside the conventional marketing categories, and how to market such works.
schedule.title: Cross-Genre, Slipstream, and Difficult-to-Categorize Writing

schedule.desc: Cinema, television, and video games today heavily feature genre content - from cartoons to small indies to big budget franchises, they run the gamut of adaptations and remakes of both new and classic speculative works. Panelists will discuss what it means for geek culture to be this mainstream, how that’s influencing both the genre itself and, most importantly, fandom.
schedule.title: Geek Culture Is Mainstream - What Now?

schedule.desc: Sometimes the shortest stories hit the hardest. Come learn how to write an engaging and moving super short story. (This workshop is for teens)
schedule.title: Shorter is Better: Teen Flash Fiction Workshop
New and Indie Autographing: Tara Sim

schedule.desc: With the majority of the population living in light-polluted cities, it is becoming harder to look up and see constellations in the night sky. Ideas like beaming light to places on Earth from orbit, or orbital billboards are being seriously explored. How does losing access to the stars affect our sense of wonder and our understanding of our place in a vast universe?
schedule.title: Dark Skies: What Changes as the Stars Disappear?

schedule.desc: Recent advances in the study of Disaster Risk Reduction have shown that DRR policy implementation is not driven by experiencing loss, but by the mediated engagement of disasters through the news and related commentary. This paper shows how the thought experiment entertainment provided by Science Fiction can play the same role as the news and drive DRR implementation if it includes key narrative elements.
schedule.title: How SF Prevents Disasters: A socio-political model of action

schedule.desc: It's a truth universally acknowledged that "bad" characters wear black leather pants. What other costuming tropes exist in SFF media? As cosplayers, we ill discuss how these sorts of associates be leveraged to create recognizable ensembles even when the goal isn't to perfectly recreate the source material?
schedule.title: Storytelling By Costume

schedule.desc: In this workshop, we’ll make characters! Let’s discuss how to give our characters interesting flaws, how to sketch out potential arcs ahead of the game, and how to strike the balance between having an idea for your character and leaving room for development during play.
schedule.title: Making Interesting Characters in TTRPGs

schedule.desc: A demonstration and lesson on balloon sculpting for kids. We will also make balloon animals via request for the Camp Fuzzy members! (Allergy warning: balloons contain latex.)
schedule.title: Balloon Animal Sculpting Workshop (KIds' Edition - Sunday)

schedule.desc: In 1986, a student at Moscow State University called Dmitry Davidoff invented a game called Mafia, now known better as Werewolf, that defined a whole genre of tabletop games called social deduction games. The genre has expanded, with some games building on the original and others blending the concept with more traditional strategy games. Recently, others have started pushing the envelope. The panel suggests their favorite social deduction games.
schedule.title: The Evolution of Social Deduction Games

schedule.desc: In this workshop following the En Plein Air presentation, participants will enjoy creating a Mars-scape in the En Plein Air style by means of the depiction of light and shadow and other plein air techniques, taking into account the physical differences between Mars and Earth. Additional features such as rovers and objects visible in the Martian sky are optional! Participants can take their artwork with them after the workshop.
schedule.title: En Plein Air: Create Your Own Planetscape

schedule.desc: Ruth Frances Long / Jessica Thorne writes romance and fantasy from the heart which often strays into weird and wonderful liminal places. She works in a specialized library of rare & occasionally crazy books. A table talk to discuss all things from her books under both pen names, writing, folklore, historical oddities, rare books, bookbinding and early printing.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Ruth Frances Long / Jessica Thorne

schedule.desc: Max Gladstone is the author of many books, including the Hugo Best Series nominee Craft Wars (of which the most recent volume is Dead Hand Rule) and, with Amal El-Mohtar, the New York Times-Bestselling and Hugo Award-winning This is How You Lose the Time War. Come by to talk about writing, table top role playing games, coffee, and related subjects.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Max Gladstone

schedule.desc: How does a poet become an editor for a literary magazine or anthology? What should a poet expect when they transition from writing to editing? Poets who became guest editors of literary magazines and anthologies discuss their transition from generating writing to choosing what gets published.
schedule.title: From Poetry Writer to Guest Editor: Taking the Big Leap!

schedule.desc: Sapphic science fiction and fantasy isn't just about the romance. How do sapphic characters contribute to and shape worldbuilding, politics, as well as the overall plot in speculative fiction? Take a look at stories that have sapphic identities as part of the fabric of their world and not just as a subplot.
schedule.title: Do It for the Plot: Sapphic Stories in SFF

schedule.desc: Science is under fire. The United States has stepped back from climate research, energy conservation, and advanced medical research. On a fundamental level, citizens are being schooled to mistrust scientists and trust social media and political pundits. This disease is being deliberately spread by US money to other countries. How do we fight back and what change do we need to see?
schedule.title: SOS: Save Our Science

schedule.desc: Meet some of the writers, creatives, and fans who want to invite you to Edmonton / ᐊᒥᐢᑿᒌᐚᐢᑲᐦᐃᑲᐣ (Amiskwacîwâskahikan) for the Worldcon in 2030! We’re throwing a virtual bid party with interviews, a Q&A time, and the unveiling of our new bid mascots! Come get a taste of what it’s like “north of ordinary!”
schedule.title: Virtual Bid Party - Edmonton 2030

schedule.desc:
This panel will discuss the benefits of having your own website and what tools and services are available to build and maintain one. What should it include? How extensive must it be? Can/should you do direct sales from your website? What are the benefits of a newsletter and building a mailing list? We will discuss website and newsletter best practices based on the panelists’ experience.

(This is not a how-to for building your own website, etc.)
schedule.title: Do Self-Published Authors Need Their Own Website and Newsletter?

schedule.desc: Modern online platforms have made it easier to find, filter, and analyze trends in transformative works fanspaces. How is this data collected and reviewed? What patterns emerge from the results, and how have they changed over time? What are the challenges and benefits to seeing fandom through this kind of lens?
schedule.title: Transformative Works Data Analysis

schedule.desc: Want to start learning how to write in cursive? Any child who is comfortable writing may join us as we build cursive skills.
schedule.title: Cursive Club

schedule.desc: The Kingdom of Caid, the SCA’s Southern California branch, brings its fighters to Worldcon for live combat demonstrations. See armored combat with rattan swords and rapier fencing in Renaissance style, both at full speed. Between bouts, fighters share how their armor and weapons are made, how bouts are won, and why honor is at the center of it all. Stop by, ask questions, and find out how you can try it yourself.
schedule.title: SCA Combat Demo - Sunday #2

schedule.desc: Shibori is a Japanese dyeing technique that results in rich paterns. This workshop includes a series of historical binding dye techniques associated with Japan but found around the world. Workshop members will learn at least two techniques.
schedule.title: Shibori Binding Techniques

schedule.desc: Western storytelling traditions decree that a linear structure (along with the three act structure, the hero’s journey, and a rising self-esteem arc) are mandatory features of any satisfying story. This program challenges that assumption by exploring non-linear structures, specifically cyclic and nested structures, using examples from non-Western stories and films. Writers will come to understand how these non-linear structures allow for thematic stacking, embracing of moral complexity, and a synthesis between form and content to explode the idea that a straight line is the best way to tell every story.
schedule.title: Non-Linear Story Structures from Non-Western Storytelling

schedule.desc: One may have opinions on the quality of special effects and dialogue, but there is something about the science fiction films of the 1950s that still resonates with audiences today. Even audiences born in this millennium. What about those films still connects with today’s audience? Which ’50s films were your favorites? Forbidden Planet? The Day the Earth Stood Still? Cat-Women of the Moon?
schedule.title: SF Films of the '50s: A Look Back

schedule.desc: The panel of creatives of writers will discuss the pros and cons of social media. What is your social media presence for? How do you decide which platform and what are the best ways to choose social media?
schedule.title: Social Media and the Writer--2026

schedule.desc: JSY is the lead writer/creative producer for the critical hit Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Come join the Pancake Club meetup - Hugos Edition, where she’ll share some of her creative frameworks, explain why pancakes, and chat about stories, video games, and personal pet peeves. Pancake Club is for anyone with an interest in storytelling and is built on the belief that we enrich each other’s lives when we share our imaginations and perspectives.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen

schedule.desc: Critiquing is not the same thing to every writer. Some want strategic help while others need reactions on pacing, character, or prose. Good critiquers listen to what the author is asking for. Panelists will share their expertise in providing useful feedback not only on all aspects of the writing process, but how to constructively and collegially handle tricky situations, while always fighting the instinct to rewrite the person's work for them.
schedule.title: How to Provide an Excellent Critique

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss how queer characters navigate broken systems, authoritarian futures, and collapsing societies, and why dystopia can be a powerful space for imagining liberation.
schedule.title: Queerness in the Ruins: LGBTQ+ Identity in Dystopian Worlds (Virtual)

schedule.desc: We’ve done vampires. We’ve captained starships. The universe keeps expanding, and the Black imagination is limitless. Let’s talk cosmic horror from a Black perspective: what it is, what it isn’t, and how Black writers and artists do it differently. The Ballad of Black Tom is cosmic horror; is Ring Shout? What about Lilith’s Brood?
schedule.title: Afro-Cosmicism: Afrofuturism and Cosmic Horror

schedule.desc: In the early days of roleplaying, the heroic narrative assumed that all characters must be able-bodied and free of chronic conditions. How have tabletop roleplaying games evolved to make room for characters with a wider spectrum of abilities?
schedule.title: Disability Representation in TTRPGs

schedule.desc: Children's Programming Staff Members will take the kids with parents/guardians through the Exhibits Hall. We might even find a few Specific Exhibits to stop to collect stamps for their Adventurers Club Passports.
schedule.title: Kids' Tour the Exhibits Hall

schedule.desc: Over the years we learned that some of the “big names” in science fiction and fantasy were, and are, behaving in a very unethical way. Their works, however, may be important to us. Is it possible to separate the art from the artist? Should we try doing so, and if yes how can we achieve it? And last, but not least: how can we ethically enjoy such pieces of art?
schedule.title: Can We Enjoy the Art of Unethical People?

schedule.desc: Come hear from the Hugo Best Novel finalists and former finalists as they talk shop: how do they handle stories with such high plot stakes and involved storylines? How do they develop characters? Where do they find common ground in the act of storytelling, and where do they diverge?
schedule.title: Setting the Stakes High: Hugo Best Novel

schedule.desc: How can you take a trait that might have interfered with your creative productivity, and use it as an asset? The panel will discuss strategies for managing creative energy, working with (rather than against) neurodivergent tendencies, and balancing structure with spontaneity in artistic practice.
schedule.title: Creative Practice for Neurodivergent Artists

schedule.desc: There are movements afoot to give whole ecosystems, rivers, non-human species, and even AIs. Some of these rights already exists in some places. What does this mean? Will it change anything? And who or what should have rights?
schedule.title: When Everything Has Rights: Ecosystems, Animals and Robots!

schedule.desc: Dungeons and Dragons was originally an expansion of Chainmail, which is a medieval wargame. Early versions of the game relied heavily on othering the exotic and quantifying or gamifying racial characteristics. More recently, titles like Journeys through the Radiant Citadel show that Wizards of the Coast are trying to move past this. How are efforts to decolonize D&D going and what is there still to do?
schedule.title: Decolonizing D&D

schedule.desc: Much of today’s AI discussion rightly focuses on risks and ethical concerns: energy and water use, labor disruption, misuse, and inherent bias. This session looks at a different question: could AI contribute positively to shared societal goals? We’re interested in AI as a set of tools embedded in wider systems: energy, science, public infrastructure, climate, and health. This is not a hype panel but looking at it through a futurist lens.
schedule.title: AI Through a Hopeful Lens (Virtual)

schedule.desc: How scientists use light to understand the ultrasmall, there will be 3 or 4 stations for the kids to see how this is done.
schedule.title: Lighting up the nanoscale

schedule.desc: Astounding award-nominated speculative fiction author H.H. Pak reads from "Never Eaten Vegetables," their Hugo, Nebula, and Ignyte-nominated novelette about bioethics, sentient spaceships, and frogs.
schedule.title: Reading: H.H. Pak

schedule.desc: Solarpunk refers both to creative fictional works imagining hopeful climate futures and to a community of fans and activists inspired by these works. This ethnography explores the role of creative fictional works in the lives, communities, and online networks of self-identified solarpunks.
schedule.title: Between Art and Action: An Ethnography of Solarpunk

schedule.desc: Trang Thanh Tran, New York Times bestselling author of She Is a Haunting, reads from their Lodestar Award-nominated eco horror They Bloom at Night.
schedule.title: Reading: Trang Thanh Tran

schedule.desc: Scares come in all forms, this collection of short films should give you some goose bumps. A Nightmare on 34th Street (Canada), Bug (North Macedonia), Camp Evergreen (USA), Favela Amarela (Brazil), Furnaces (USA - Nick Dragon), Hide (USA), Selfless (USA - Will Anderson), The Plasticist (USA - Nick Dragon)
schedule.title: Horror Short Films

schedule.desc: Come listen to the finalists for the Hugo for Best Short Story talk shop. What tips do they have for keeping your short story short? What techniques do they use to make sure their story resonates with their audience? And, for the sake of all of our egos, how do they deal with rejection?
schedule.title: The Short Arc: Hugo Best Short Story Finalists

schedule.desc: Celebrate writers that embrace the big, curvy, and downright glorious bodies, crafting characters that throw out the one-size-fits-all rulebook and reflect the full, beautiful range of how humans actually exist within their bodies.
schedule.title: Let's Get Physical: Positive Body Representation in SFF

schedule.desc: Many tabletop games stem from a historical setting or scenario: from the War of the Roses to the Cold War, the Dark Ages to the Wild West. Our panelists discuss some of their favorite games in terms of both how they play and the real-life backdrop behind them. How can games teach and bring us closer to history, the pitfalls of representing more problematic parts of our past, and how can we use games to reclaim parts of our history?
schedule.title: Depictions of History in Board Games

schedule.desc: Join us for today’s feedback session. This is the best way to connect with the convention organizers and ask any questions you have about the con. Your participation will help us to address current issues and capture new opportunities that we might otherwise miss. Your feedback matters and will be heard by future Worldcon organizers as well!
schedule.title: Feedback Session - Sunday

schedule.desc: Many speculative fiction stories depict everyday people wearing everyday clothes, whatever that means for their particular setting. What are some unique considerations when crafting “common” clothing? How does that change when 21st century people might mistake your costume for your casual con outfit?
schedule.title: Everyday Clothing Costumes

schedule.desc: In his new book, AIlien Minds, David Brin explores how we might best coexist with artificial beings. How do we retain human agency and happiness and help our cyber-children become decent folks? So many current notions about AI, memes that are guiding genius innovators, are dangerous clichés cloned from feudalism or bad SF. David riffs off evolution and history and better SF to chart paths toward a future when humans and AIs may coexist peacefully and productively.
schedule.title: Concepts from David Brin’s New Book on AI: AIlien Minds

schedule.desc: Games, both tabletop and electronic, can be used at any age to make new friends, as an excuse to hang out with your friends, and social time with friends. We'll talk about, and hopefully even demo, some games that are great socializing opportunities for kids.
schedule.title: How Games are used as Social Gatherings

schedule.desc: So, you get on the elevator headed for the top floor, and a major editor in the field asks what you do. You tell them you’re a writer, and they say, we’re looking for stuff, tell me what you’re working on? You have one minute to get the editor excited about your work. Can you do it? That’s what's known as the “elevator pitch”—summarizing your work in one or two short sentences—and many writers can’t. Our workshop will introduce you to how an elevator pitch works (and what not to do). Bring your elevator pitch: our experts will discuss it, what works, what doesn’t work, and what might be done to punch it up and make it a winner.
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: Elevator Pitch Class

schedule.desc: Make a tote bag, infinity scarf or headband - so many possibilities
schedule.title: What Can You Make out of a T-shirt?

schedule.desc: Kate Elliott reads from her forthcoming The Flower Court (January 2027), a sapphic romantic fantasy in which a clever young scribe infiltrates the imperial consort quarters to search for a missing noblewoman, only to find herself forced to work with the Dowager Empress’s loveliest and most condescending servant.
schedule.title: Reading: Kate Elliott

schedule.desc: Join science fiction author and certified nerd Dr. Micaiah Johnson as she traces the history of robots from early automatons to today’s fraught AI discourse. She will discuss topics surrounding the mechanical human, from their unique role in society to their weird, haunted doll eyes. This talk will pay special attention to how historical shifts in race and politics continue to affect the legacy of these inventions.
schedule.title: Race & Robotics: A Not-so-brief History & Not-so-happy Ending

schedule.desc: From Saudi Arabia’s NEOM (The Line) to Toyota’s Woven City, what are some visions for livable and sustainable new cities? Are they a good idea? Why or why not? How economically and socially diverse will these cities be? How will they accommodate people with different physical abilities? Will they help solve sea level rise?
schedule.title: Future Cities: New Ideas For Dense and Workable Cities

schedule.desc: Writers from a minority perspective often get trapped into expectations that everything they write will be from and center their cultural and ethnic background. Yet, they have so much more to offer. Come hear these authors’ experiences escaping the pigeonhole and how you can, too.
schedule.title: Don't Pigeonhole Me: Writing From a Minority Perspective

schedule.desc: Christopher Caldwell writes fantasy fiction with queer and Black protagonists from a Black and queer lens. Come chat with them about: short fiction, poisons, home cooking, film noir, or anything else that piques your interest.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Christopher Caldwell

schedule.desc: Panelists who have assembled an anthology talk about what they learned from the experience - the challenges and discoveries, hard lessons about giving rejections, thrills of successful revise and resubmits, and advice they’d like those submitting to anthologies to really, really follow. Panelists will discuss how to choose the stories, including the nuts and bolts: rights, editing, copyediting, and types of royalties.
schedule.title: So You Think You Want to Do an Anthology, Eh? (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Fandom has great potential to attract people. Many who found it stayed for years. Yet, many fans need to get away from it all or gafiate at some point. Some fans are not willing to join at all. Where does the magnetism of fandom lies? Our panelists will discuss how the entry points to fandom have changed over the years and what made them stay.
schedule.title: How I Found Fandom and Why I Stayed

schedule.desc: California has been a hub for aero- and astronautics since their origins. From the Explorer 1, America’s first satellite built by JPL in 1958, to key components of spacecraft from Apollo to Artemis II being built right here in the Golden State, both NASA and the aerospace industry have made home bases here. Come talk about the history and the future of the space industry in California.
schedule.title: Space in LA: California Space Companies are Thriving!

schedule.desc: Sarah Pinsker reads from her Hugo nominated novelette "The Millay Illusion."
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Sarah Pinsker

schedule.desc: While it started as a mechanics-forward hobby, more and more games have turned to prioritising storytelling. At some tables, Game Masters have an absolute grip on the plot, and at others, the act of telling the story is more collaborative. And then we have “GM-less” games, in which GM authority can either rotate or is entirely replaced. How is the direction of plot changing at the table, and how do our panel use this to enhance their storytelling?
schedule.title: Cocreation and Storytelling at the Table

schedule.desc: We like to think of science as neat, methodical, and not particularly emotional. But real history suggests otherwise. Scientists fight over ideas and methods, they spend lifetimes trying to prove themselves right or someone else wrong. Come hear about historical science rivalries.
schedule.title: Grudges in Science: Science can be a tough competition

schedule.desc: The crew of Klingon ship IKV Stranglehold respond to a distress call from a Klingon ship that may be part of a nefarious plan by an old foe. Will the crew survive? Find out in the latest installment of Klingon Lifestyles, a fandom play that has been performed at San Diego Comic Con for 33 years. All life forms are welcome.
schedule.title: Klingon Lifestyles - Live!

schedule.desc: Bring your works in progress and let’s discuss how to get the feedback you need to improve them, and then do some playtesting! If you’ve got a game from the Game Design Jam, bring that!
schedule.title: Tabletop Game Playtesting Jam

schedule.desc: Many of us love stories featuring paranormal creatures and characters, but sometimes it’s hard to pick just one! Listen to authors who indulge in the paranormal side while they talk about ideas to consider when choosing your creature, as well as what difficulties you may face depending on those choices.
schedule.title: Choosing Your Paranormal Creature

schedule.desc: Many forms of art and craft are in a revolution driven by the wealth of new technology. These new technologies can be empowering, disruptive, or even both. Our panelists will discuss using technology as a tool to enhance an artist's ability to create. They will also cover what it's like to innovate new processes in well-established fields.
schedule.title: Technology and Art

schedule.desc: Join this panel of authors to explore how they create queer-normative and gender-fluid worlds that make space for people to exist fully. Consider how these worlds offer futures and fantasies that resist queer erasure and establish authenticity as the standard.
schedule.title: Queer Normative and Gender Expansive Worldbuilding in SF/F

schedule.desc: Fan art is creative work made for the love of an existing character, creative property, or genre. How has the definition been changing, and can it be commercial? This panel will include discussion on transformative works, the role of fan communities, artistic growth through fan art, and navigating questions of originality, ownership, and professional legitimacy.
schedule.title: What Is Fan Art?

schedule.desc: A place for current and past federal and JPL employees and contractors to meet and share experiences.
schedule.title: Meetup: JPL / NASA

schedule.desc: We may particularly love the new Wednesday Addams show, but she's always been awesome. Panelists explore Wednesday's evolution from 1930's cartoon character to modern day Netflix star. (This is a panel for teens)
schedule.title: Snap, snap! The Weird World of Wednesday Addams

schedule.desc: Many listeners access their podcasts through YouTube, and Spotify and Apple are adding video support. With listeners increasingly becoming viewers as well, what is the future for the audio podcast? Do you pivot to video, add a catchy thumbnail, or keep to audio only? And what happens when your favourite audio cast turns into a video talk show?
schedule.title: Video Killed the Podcast Star

schedule.desc: Stan Sakai has been creating art for over four decated. Happy to talk anything about comics, storytelling, Japanese history, working with six different publishers, or building the ever-growing Usagi Universe. From Space Usagi and Kaito '84 to the upcoming Last Yojimbo, Stan is happy to share stories from his career, creative process, and what's next for the rabbit ronin and his world.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Stan Sakai

schedule.desc: Fan Funds enable cultural exchanges between fandom in different parts of the world thanks to fannish generosity that covers the costs of travel (and sometimes also accommodation). Take advantage of this unique opportunity to support those endeavors by obtaining amazing items (or kipple) for yourself! Come and join our auction of extraordinary items!
schedule.title: Fan Funds Auction

schedule.desc: Redemption arcs are a staple of speculative fiction, but many stories confuse redemption with forgiveness, suffering, or a single dramatic gesture. This panel examines when redemption arcs fail, why audiences are often asked to accept moral closure without accountability, and what gets lost when harm is erased instead of reckoned with.
schedule.title: From Atonement to Aftermath: When Redemption Arcs Fail

schedule.desc: Sherlock Holmes has been inspiring authors since his conception. How has the Holmes canon moving into the public domain affected what stories authors feel able to tell? Explore how authors have riffed off this iconic character about how he has evolved through the years.
schedule.title: Stock-Holmes Syndrome: The Great Detective

schedule.desc: Holly Black is a writer of folkloric fantasy for kids, teenagers, and adults, including The Cruel Prince, The Spiderwick Chronicles, and the adult duology that begins with Book of Night. Come hang out and chat about wicked faeries, publishing, comics, games, planners, coffee, and schemes.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Holly Black

schedule.desc: Many creators today build worlds that span prose, film/TV, audio drama, theater, visual art, and music. Each form reveals different angles and imposes new creative, structural, and emotional possibilities. Come explore the craft and practice of multidisciplinary SFF storytelling: how to maintain coherence across formats, how stories evolve when adapted between them, and what new opportunities open up when worldbuilding becomes cross-media.
schedule.title: Multidisciplinary Futures: Creating SFF Across Media

schedule.desc: Come join those of Muslim faith for discussion, interaction, and community.
schedule.title: Meetup: Muslim Genre Fans

schedule.desc: Rebecca Matte is a literary agent and recovering attorney who represents young adult and adult SFF and romance. Come on by to talk all things publishing (queries, agents, editors, IP/WFH projects, contracts), IP law, big career pivots, balancing writing/publishing with chronic illness, or anything else that we happen to stumble across in our time together.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Rebecca Matte

schedule.desc: Jennifer Hudak, author of the Hugo-finalist poem "The World to Come," reads a selection of forthcoming poetry, and flash fiction that straddles the line between poetry and prose.
schedule.title: Reading: Jennifer Hudak

schedule.desc: Join our academics at their posters and chat about the research they’re presenting at Worldcon.
schedule.title: Academic Poster Session

schedule.desc:
You are a fairy, an incarnation of an idea, a collection of pixels ferrying magical data from one place to another. You're not just from the Pixie Verse; you're from The Club, the planetoid made of all ideas and experiences about going to the club. It's a 24/7 party, but this is the biggest party of the year: The clash of club! To determine the ruling archfey for the next year, each demifey representing a club will select champions to compete in this tournament of talent and taunting.

Game system: Thirsty Dungeons & Lesbian Dragons

Players should be 21+ years old.
schedule.title: Pixieverse: Clash of Clubs!

schedule.desc: Richard’s credits over 40+ years as a writer include: the Rowan Atkinson Schoolmaster sketch (The Secret Policeman’s Ball); libretti for the LA Opera; TV, radio and film scripts; his New Rock fantasy adventure series; graphic novels, song lyrics for talents as diverse as Dom de Luise, Eric Idle, Vanessa Williams, Plácido Domingo and Hello Kitty. Come and talk about all things writing—art, craft, collaboration, editing and audiobooks.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Richard Sparks

schedule.desc: tuds, safety pins, and combat boots? Come to this meetup for people who identify as punk!
schedule.title: Meetup: Punk

schedule.desc: From Something Wicked This Way Comes to Carnivàle, we have been fascinated by the dark possibilities of carnivals. Books like Veronica Henry's Bacchanal, Neal Shusterman's Full Tilt, and Sarah McNight's Carousel all wreak havoc with carnivals. What makes this supposed source of delight such a good vehicle for horrorifying stories?
schedule.title: Big Top Nightmares: Dark Carnivals

schedule.desc: Tired of the same old mythologies in your reading? Explore literature that utilizes pantheons and mythologies beyond Olympus.
schedule.title: Pantheons Around the World

schedule.desc:
Getting some herbs and spices sounds like a milk run. No big deal, they are offering you a fair amount of cred. What’s the worst that could happen? Join us playing this legendary game!

Character sheets, dice and pencils provided.
schedule.title: Shadowrun: Top Shelf Seattle

schedule.desc: H.H. Pak is a multi-award nominated writer of speculative fiction as well as co-editor of the terminally online newsletter, Wyrmhole Magazine. Come meet them to talk about space operas, genre tropes, the aptly named “sublime confusion” of being 20-something, subbing and pubbing, queerness, the very best places to eat in Los Angeles, and the mortifying necessity of making cringe art.
schedule.title: Table Talk: H.H. Pak

schedule.desc: Come join this meetup hosted by the Carl Brandon Society for fans who identify as Black, Latinx, AANHPI, or BIPOC for discussion, interaction, and community.
schedule.title: Meetup: Black, Latinx, AANHPI, BIPOC

schedule.desc: Kate Elliott is a writer and reader of sff, a genre she has loved since childhood. Think of this as a cozy AMA about her many books and worlds, the craft and profession of writing (including her favorite nerdy topic, world-building), outrigger canoe paddling, why Nirvana in Fire remains one of the best long-form tv shows ever made, barky schnauzers and other dogs, what folks are reading and watching lately, why history is cool, or some random unexpected question.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Kate Elliott

schedule.desc: The Kingdom of Caid, the SCA’s Southern California branch, brings its fighters to Worldcon for live combat demonstrations. See armored combat with rattan swords and rapier fencing in Renaissance style, both at full speed. Between bouts, fighters share how their armor and weapons are made, how bouts are won, and why honor is at the center of it all. Stop by, ask questions, and find out how you can try it yourself.
schedule.title: SCA Combat Demo - Sunday #3

schedule.desc: Come watch an animated feature film set in the War of the Worlds universe. Afterward we will have a question and answer session with the director Joe Bruce Pearson, who was an active member of Los Angeles Science Fantasy Society (LASFS) for close to 15 years.
schedule.title: War of the Worlds: Goliath

schedule.desc: Communication tools in tabletop roleplaying games have come a long way since Ron Edwards first developed lines and veils for Sex & Sorcery and John Stavropoulos invented the X-Card. Our panel will introduce the concept of communication tools and why they are important. Then we’ll discuss how we use them to work towards happier tables that work better for everyone playing.
schedule.title: Communication Tools in TTRPGs

schedule.desc: Creatives will explore what cultural appropriation really is and how to engage cultures purposely, ethically, and respectfully—centering connectivity while telling inclusive stories.
schedule.title: Inspiration Not Appropriation (Virtual)

schedule.desc: See how Daniel Gonzalez uses traditional oil painting techniques in his contemporary artworks. This demonstration will include approaches to composition, brushwork, color mixing, and layering. He will also share examples showing different stages of the painting process, from initial block-in to finished surface.
schedule.title: Oil Painting Demonstration

schedule.desc: A discussion of the challenges of making art in the these days of capitalism. What forms are available to artists to maintain greater control over their art, and how to balance ethical creation and consumption with the attention economy.
schedule.title: Life Goes On - Profit vs Sustainability in Creative Projects

schedule.desc: If you're a fan of Mary Robinette Kowal (MRK), you almost certainly know about Elsie the Cat. Elsie is MRK's 7-year-old calico cat, who has a 130-word vocabulary and uses Augmentative Interspecies Communication (AIC) to express herself. Join this virtual meetup with Elsie and Mary Robinette!
schedule.title: Meetup: Elsie the Talking Cat (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Classic science fiction imagines big computers waking up either evil, for example Hal9000 or Ellison’s “I Have no Mouth...”, or else super helpful like Heinlein’s Mike in Moon is a Harsh Mistress. Suppose today’s networks and AI wake up sentient. Who would they serve, and who would they replace? What would they value and what would be discarded?
schedule.title: What Happens if We Create Truly Sentient AI?

schedule.desc: From Victorian aliens on Doctor Who to airship pirates, the possibilities for "sci-fi-ifying" historical fashions are endless! Our panelists will go where no historian has gone before, and discuss what makes the process of taking an ensemble from history to science fiction successful.
schedule.title: Turning Your Historical Fashions Into SF/F Costumes

schedule.desc: Decorate a frame for your new creations or for gifts
schedule.title: Frame Decorating

schedule.desc: Fairy tale retellings are all the rage, but how do you add a twist to create your own spin on the story? Learn some new techniques and start breaking apart your own fairy tale to rebuild it better than ever. (This workshop is for teens.)
schedule.title: Fractured Fairy Tales: Teen Writing Workshop

schedule.desc: More than ever, diverse relationship types are critical for representation and inclusion beyond the monogamous heterosexuality of most mainstream fiction. Hear authors discuss the broad range of relationships and how they have approached the diverse relationships in their own work.
schedule.title: Diverse Relationships in Romantasy

schedule.desc: Even billionaires who run large foundations that support social causes mint more money every day than they can spend or give away. The top 1% own more than the bottom 99%. How do we fix this? This panel will explore alternative future economies and the choices we can make today to build a fairer future.
schedule.title: Future Economies: What If Everyone Had a Roof and Two Meals?

schedule.desc: Critiquing is not the same thing to every writer. Some want strategic help while others need reactions on pacing, character, or prose. Good critiquers listen to what the author is asking for. Panelists will share their expertise in providing useful feedback not only on all aspects of the writing process, but how to constructively and collegially handle tricky situations, while always fighting the instinct to rewrite the person's work for them.
schedule.title: How to Provide an Excellent Critique (Virtual)

schedule.desc: I am a retired physicist, former beam jockey, and long-time Chicago-area fan. You might have seen me give talks on spaceflight or astronomy. Recently I've spoken about Europa Clipper, various asteroid missions, lunar nomenclature, and Pluto. On Monday, I'll explain a whirlybird NASA's sending to Titan. I love to converse about the history of science fiction. Also the history of science. Have a seat and tell me what's on your mind!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Bill Higgins

schedule.desc:
An opportunity to ask questions of one of the leading literary agents in the field, in an intimate setting. Joshua has been representing favorite authors of sf/f/h fans in five decades, first selling a book by eventual number one bestseller Charlaine Harris in 1989 and in the 2020s representing number one bestseller Brandon Sanderson.
And he's sold debuts for authors he's met at a table talk.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Joshua Bilmes

schedule.desc: Found in the deep ocean, remote rainforest, isolated cave or just someone’s backyard. Panelists discuss some truly strange creatures and their “creative” adaptations, as well as the researchers and citizen scientists who look for them. Sea cucumber butt teeth, and other glories of nature. Inspired by Ursula Vernon and T. Kingfisher’s Hugo acceptance speeches.
schedule.title: Evolution is an Arms Race: Bizarre Plants and Animals

schedule.desc: Stories about incomprehensible forces of unimaginable magnitude with the power to destroy the world have existed in science fiction long before the arrival of atomic weapons. Many recent authors have used the JC 28/7: Minor copy edits, tagged as copy-edited. and cosmic horror to explore ideas around the most devastating types of warfare. This panel will talk about the best of these stories and what they tell us about our relationship to military conquest.
schedule.title: Eldritch Horror as a Nuclear Metaphor

schedule.desc: Marie Brennan and Alyc Helms, who write under the joint pen name of M.A. Carrick, read two selections from their recent Spanish Golden Age alternate history, The Eye of Leviathan!
schedule.title: Reading: Marie Brennan & Alyc Helms

schedule.desc: Science fiction inspired her journey. Space exploration made it real. Veteran NASA systems engineer, spacecraft whisperer, exoplanet hunter, and champion of curiosity, Tracy Drain grew up devouring science fiction in all its forms and then spent the next 25 years helping humanity explore the cosmos. Join Dr. Vidya Venkatesan as they discuss science fiction, science fact, and what keeps us looking up.
schedule.title: Boldly Going: A Conversation with Tracy Drain

schedule.desc: The Appalachian region of the United States has a rich folklore all its own. With examples from Old Gods of Appalachia to Deliverance to Pumpkinhead, these hills have inspired a long history of horrors–both fictional and real. Let's talk about Appalachians' contributions to our favorite genre.
schedule.title: Weird Tales Of Appalachia

schedule.desc: Why do dragons, in one form or another, show up in the oldest stories in nearly every culture around the world? Join mythologists and authors as they explore the origin stories of dragons and how they’re portrayed in a variety of cultures.
schedule.title: Dragons, Dragons, Everywhere!

schedule.desc: Deep space is a common setting in SF, but it poses unique challenges for sustaining human life. Is it even possible to assemble an ecology in which Earthborn life will thrive over thousands of years in something that began as a sterile shell? What solutions have researchers and writers suggested, and what do they think the biggest hurdles to creating a spaceborn ecology will be?
schedule.title: Deep Space Voyages: How Will Humans Thrive Between the Stars?

schedule.desc: In a time when most fantasy books featured male protagnoists and were geared towards adults, Tamora said hold my tankard. Her bold, brilliant, young female protagonists helped cement the beginnings of the young adult genre and she didn't hold back when it came to discussing uncomfortable topics with young readers such as war, loss, and (gasp!) periods. Come join the conversation about the impact her work has had on fantasy as a whole.
schedule.title: Lioness Rampant: Tamora Pierce 40 Years On

schedule.desc: What do you need to know before getting on a stage to perform a concert? Plan a strong set list, gauge timing and dynamics, head off stage fright, interact with your audience, promote merch without being obnoxious, keep your sound tech happy, and handle adoring fans? Our experienced panelists have handled it all, and share their off-stage secrets - including that P-word (PRACTICE!) - for on-stage success.
schedule.title: Stagecraft For Musicians

schedule.desc: Some countries are on the move from democracy towards authoritarianism. How will that change affect conventions and conrunning? What should conrunners do in the current landscape? Are the experiences of Eastern European SF groups prior to the fall of the Berlin Wall relevant now?
schedule.title: Conrunning in a Time of Dystopia

schedule.desc: Sophie Burnham, Astounding Award finalist and winner of the Sidewise Award, reads from their queer alt history Ex Romana trilogy.
schedule.title: Reading: Sophie Burnham

schedule.desc: Kevin is a costumer (creator of the Tiki Dalek), con runner, performer and just retired from IBM Research as a materials scientist, automation engineer, science lecturer, and IBM Quantum Ambassador. He’ll happily talk your ear off about costume design and construction (science fiction/fantasy/historical/drag/you name it), magnetoelectronics, spintronics, quantum computing, renaissance fairs, running conventions, Doctor Who, silly party hosting or just about anything. He’s done a lot and loves to talk about all of it.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Kevin Roche

schedule.desc: If a story is not a binary good vs evil, that leaves a gray area: or, politics! Panelists will discuss how political scheming and passions are a vital part of worldbuilding, and delve into how to write convincing politics that enhance the story.
schedule.title: Let’s Talk Spec Fic Politics! (Virtual)

schedule.desc: TV Tropes can clarify character, plot, etc, or freeze writers into self-conscious paralysis. This panel will show how familiar tropes aren’t the problem so much as unexamined tropes. Panelists will talk about how tropes function as shared language, when trope awareness improves storytelling, and when it turns into joy-killing metatextual anxiety. Panelists will discuss how to kill the panic, but keep the insight.
schedule.title: Oh No, It’s a TV Trope!

schedule.desc: Perhaps the most famous Tarot art is the Rider-Waite deck illustrated by Pamela Colman Smith, but there are a myriad of Tarot decks all with different gorgeous artwork. Our panel discusses how Tarot themes are represented by different artists and highlight some of their favourites.
schedule.title: Art of Tarot

schedule.desc: A meetup for women-identifying creators for discussion, interaction, and community, as well as to address challenges faced specifically by women-identifying creators of all media.
schedule.title: Meetup: Women Creators for Women Creators

schedule.desc: In this dye workshop, let’s explore what happens when we experiment. What happens when we put dye on dry fabric versus wet fabric? Fold fabric? Roll fabric? We’ll explore member suggestions to find out.
schedule.title: What Happens When I?

schedule.desc: Story podcasts are the short form cousin to audiobooks. Both podcasts and audiobooks have grown exponentially in the past years. How do podcast producers select the stories? What types of stories do listeners like to hear? Are story podcasts financially viable?
schedule.title: Tell Me a Story Every Week, and Make it Good

schedule.desc: Akua Lezli Hope, a SFPA Grand Master of Fantastic Poetry, speculative fiction writer, editor, presenter, wisdom seeker, and art maker, invites conversation about telepathy, consciousness, disclosure, reframing dis/ability, making mini anthologies, singing favorite anime tunes and using divination to prompt speculative poetry.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Akua Lezli Hope

schedule.desc: How will existing religions change as humans spread out into the galaxy? Are replicated bread and wine a worthy communion? Is praying in the vague direction of Earth acceptable? Will new religions arise as humanity's needs and fears change? Is eating food made from the proteins of recycled crew members' bodies a sacred ritual or just survival? These authors have explored these questions exhaustively.
schedule.title: Praying in Space: Religions of the Future

schedule.desc: This workshop will focus on different forms of hair braiding: four strand “round” braids, classic (three-strand) French and (three-strand) Dutch (or inverted-French or underhand), crown braid (a modified three-strand French braid), and five and seven-strand fingering techniques. We might work on hearts, spirals and pullup-weaves. Which we use will be tailored to the desires and abilities of the participants.
schedule.title: Fancy Hair Braids Workshop (Sunday)

schedule.desc: Is human history headed toward something like a world government? Many towering SF authors, such as HG Wells, Isaac Asimov, Gene Roddenberry, Liu Cixin, Ada Palmer, and Becky Chambers, have brilliantly portrayed the abolition of war through the unification of humankind. If SF writers can make that seem so believable, can we envision something like a world republic as part of the real unfolding future of humanity?
schedule.title: The World State: A Big Idea in the Legacy of Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Lavanya Lakshminarayan, Arthur C. Clarke Award-shortlisted author of The Ten Percent Thief, reads from her recent queer science fiction novel about food cultures in space, Interstellar MegaChef. If you like the sound of the Great British Bake-Off meets Star Trek with a South Asian twist, this one’s for you!
schedule.title: Reading: Lavanya Lakshminarayan

schedule.desc: Robin Hobb is the author of The Farseer Trilogy, and the volumes that follow to make up The Realm of the Elderlings. She will read from an unpublished (as of yet) Hobb ROTE story. If time permits, she will do a brief additional reading from an unpublished Megan Lindholm short story.
schedule.title: Reading: Robin Hobb

schedule.desc: Shay Kauwe, author of The Killing Spell reads from her forthcoming Hawaiian gothic, House of Salt.
schedule.title: Reading: Shay Kauwe

schedule.desc: Sarah Pinsker is the Hugo winning author of "Where Oaken Hearts Do Gather" and "Two Truths and a Lie" and a current finalist for her novelette "The Millay Illusion." Join her to chat about stories, music, stage magic, research, weird travel, and anything else you want to discuss. Since this is a virtual table talk, you can also request to tour her shelves or her art, and to meet her dogs.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Sarah Pinsker

schedule.desc: Interplanetary warfare is a staple of SF, but the realities of the technology required to survive and travel in space might render warfare moot. Come explore the physics and economics of interplanetary war - are the distances too vast for offensive operations to succeed? Might there be a point in time when the spread of technological civilization renders all forms of conflict that force an unwanted government on others effectively impossible?
schedule.title: Is Interplanetary War Possible?

schedule.desc: Meet several 2026 debut authors, indie and traditional, who talk about getting their first project into print.
schedule.title: Meet Debut Authors of 2026! 2nd Edition

schedule.desc: Great speculative fiction is built on a foundation of “what if?”, but the best “what if”s are backed by data. This session covers the practical tools for technical research: navigating academic databases, utilizing open-source technical manuals, and extrapolating current trends in STEM into future settings. Perfect for writers and readers who want to check their orbital mechanics or botanical ecosystems are more than just hand-waving.
schedule.title: Fact-Checking Your Fiction: Research for Speculative Worlds

schedule.desc: Stargate SG1 was on to a good thing: how can we combine archaeology/anthropology into science fiction? This panel looks at works where the science of the future is used to look at the past in new and meaningful ways on our planet and beyond.
schedule.title: The Ancients in Sci-fi: Archaeology and Anthropolgy in Space

schedule.desc: Asteroids, comets, the planets, and their moons abide in a complex dance around our Sun that has evolved over the last 4.5 billion years. We'll use computer simulations to introduce how orbital mechanics has shaped our solar system from present day resonance orbits to the Grand Tack hypothesis for Jupiter's migration. No equations needed.
schedule.title: How Orbital Mechanics Shape Our Solar System

schedule.desc: Paul Henry Fresco calls his art “neo-constructivism”: a combination of futurism, expressionism, android and human forms, and nature. His science fiction scenes are out of this world!
schedule.title: Art in Space: Paul Henry Fresco

schedule.desc: The last decade has given us all a taste of what a real dystopia can feel like, and you might be ready to channel that experience into your own writing. Hear from authors exploring different approaches to writing dystopias, apocalypses, and world breaking events. (This panel is for teens.)
schedule.title: Apocalypse Now: Dystopias for Teens

schedule.desc: Even for the Jedi, military life isn't all fighting all the time. Between battles, there's a lot of downtime, polishing of boots, and life on the military base. This panel will discuss how this is depicted in science fiction and fantasy, as well as identifying some of the best non-combat stories in military SFF.
schedule.title: When The Fighting Stops

schedule.desc: Longtime member Alan Anderson of the Klingon Language Institute will relate the history of the creation of the KLI, its purpose and goals, and its ongoing activities today.
schedule.title: Klingon Language Institute

schedule.desc: Whether you’re an artist with new work to show, or a collector who just got back from the Worldcon Art Show checkout, you want the best for your artwork. But framing and presenting artwork can be intimidating, and expensive, especially for more unique work. Fortunately, this panel of artists and framing experts have your back. The panel will consist of prepared questions as well as audience questions.
schedule.title: How to Frame Art

schedule.desc: The wild west is an incredibly vibrant setting that is useful for far more than just the western genre. Come hear from authors who are weirding the west in small and very large ways.
schedule.title: Wyvern Rustling: Weird Westerns

schedule.desc: Please join presenters from Japan for this year's Seiun Awards. These awards for the best science fiction works and achievements have been given annually since 1970. They will also provide an update on the state of SF in Japan and talk about what new and exciting SF we can look forward to seeing soon.
schedule.title: Seiun Awards / SF in Japan

schedule.desc: The stories that stick with us, that we rave about to strangers and friends with zealous fervor. The ones we return to, are rarely contained within a single page or chapter. From Homer’s epics to Octavia Butler’s Xenogenesis Trilogy. Star Wars episodes and anime arcs. The science fiction author and the poet are students of the same teacher. The format of the final project being the only difference between them, if anything. Enter serial poetry–a grouping of poems that stand alone to tell their own rich tale, but read together, build a universe that fandoms are born out of.
schedule.title: This Lore Runs Deep: Writing Serial Poems

schedule.desc: Two weeks before the opening of our Worldcon is the 80th anniversary of the death of H.G. Wells on August 13, 1946. So let's discuss his legacy. He was pretty good at science fiction and many consider him one of the inventors of our genre. And he apparently attended one of the weekly meetings of LASFS in Los Angeles not long before he died!
schedule.title: H.G. Wells 80 Years On

schedule.desc: Humans have always created myths as a way of meaning-making, to explore their humanity, relationships to power, authority, and creativity. It offers a language for grappling with the sacred, the artificial, and the human. From Talos to Westworld and beyond, we discuss how through myth, authors resist treating AI as inevitable or divine, instead revealing the human choices, values, and power structures embedded within these systems.
schedule.title: Modern Mythology in the Age of AI

schedule.desc: First Person, Second Person, Third Person Limited, Third Person Camera-Eye, Omniscient with Narrator as Character, Omniscient with Narrator Off-Stage, Unreliable Narrator, all these possible perspectives are vital to telling a story. Panelists will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each, giving examples of where it's done well, or in a fresh way.
schedule.title: Point of View, What's the Point?

schedule.desc: As we return to the Moon are we ready to start thinking about where Humans may start permanently living off Earth? We're talking not just a visit to the space station for a few months, but really moving out to stay. What are the hazards and hurdles? Where would be the best place to start an extra-Earth society?
schedule.title: Living in Space: Where Should We Go First?

schedule.desc: David Brin's Hugo winning novels include Startide Rising and The Uplift War and runners-up Earth, Glory Season and The Postman (filmed by Kevin Costner.) David will read excerpts from his SF comedy The Ancient Ones and from his two series of YA SF novels for teens. Also from his new nonfiction book on AI - AIlien minds. His play The Escape has its first full performance at LAConV. David is a many Hugo winner who also consults regularly on tech issues for NASA. (http://www.davidbrin.com)
schedule.title: Reading: David Brin

schedule.desc: The owners of big tech companies and other ultra-rich people are often science fiction fans. However, some of the future they seem to be building is troubling. Peter Thiel’s Palantir is working to create a surveillance society in line with Nineteen Eighty-Four. Larry Ellison is building a concentrated media empire. What if the oligarchy built ideas from positive SF, and fell in love with solarpunk? What would the panel like to see?
schedule.title: Can We Stop the Tech Oligarchy Making SF Warnings Real? (Virtual)

schedule.desc: How do you respectfully incorporate what you’ve seen into what you make? How does one thoughtfully create work inspired by cultures other than your own without appropriation or offense? Our panelists will discuss how they’ve done this, and what they’ve learned in the process.
schedule.title: Cultural Inspiration

schedule.desc: What is the difference between a hard and soft magic system? What books utlize each of these? When writing a book, how do you know where on the hard to soft scale your magic system should fall?
schedule.title: Hard and Soft Magic Systems (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Participants will cut out masks and decorate them. How beautiful or scary or beautifully scary do you want them?
schedule.title: Mask Making

schedule.desc: One of the great things about genre fiction is the tension between the new and the familiar. Tastes vary; some readers may prefer recognizable tropes while others want more innovation and unpredictability. Successful genre stories find a place between these poles. How do writers establish that balance? How do we write stories that include what we love, but make it our own? How do we both satisfy and subvert expectations?
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: Grafting Idea and Story

schedule.desc: 2027 is coming, and with it a plethora of new television and film offerings. What are we most looking forward to in 2027? Join our host in this discussion and share what you are excited to see next year!
schedule.title: Future Attractions: Media Coming in 2027

schedule.desc: Science fiction is a genre which challenges the human imagination by incorporating science into “what if” scenarios. In this paper, using LCATS, a LLM-based story analysis toolkit we developed, we compare science fiction stories with other kinds of stories (romance, mystery, adventure) to illuminate the techniques and quirks that make science fiction stories science fiction.
schedule.title: The Shape of Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Meteors. Volcanic eruptions. Worldwide flooding. Disaster movies have been around since the early days of film. We will discuss the tropes found in them and the cycles as well as evolution of the genre.
schedule.title: Disaster Movies: A Cathartic Reflection of Our Times

schedule.desc: Media and entertainment use a lot of digital storage and memory. The introduction of AI tools had generated a greater demand for storage. This panel will talk about the storage technologies used in professional media and entertainment. We’ll also share how digital storage is frequently used as a prop in video projects, such as the memory crystal in the last Mission: Impossible movie or the StorageTek magnetic tape library in Clear and Present Danger.
schedule.title: Digital Storage Use in Video Production and Movies

schedule.desc: A common criticism of both fantasy and science fiction is that the genre can be oblivious to the nuances of social class, and the way class influences how one experiences technological change or magical opportunities. Panelists will discuss the depiction of class, how the experience of class can vary from culture to culture, and the role of money, culture, education, and ideology in the experience and writing of class in sf and fantasy.
schedule.title: Social Classes in SF and Fantasy (Virtual)

schedule.desc: The writing process isn’t a binary, it’s a wide open universe. Panelists discuss different ways they approach story creation and the many metaphorical descriptions that people may find useful, including gardening, exploration, architecture, musical structures, outlining, “night driving,” and more.
schedule.title: Beyond the Pantsers and Plotters Spectrum

schedule.desc: Join the ruckus with the Idiot's Lantern troupe performing an out of this world comedy show! We explore the comical sides of various SciFi fandom/stories through a number of different sketches and styles.
schedule.title: The Idiot's Lantern: A SF/F Sketch Comedy Show
