schedule.desc: What's the one story you'd recommend to someone new to fanfiction? What's the story that haunts you, that you've gone back to reread multiple times? What's the story that you think is great enough to get awards? Our panelists answer these questions, as well as sharing their all-time favorite fanfiction works and where to find them.
schedule.title: Fanfic Recommendations

schedule.desc: Andy Dudak writes his own science fiction, translates it from the Chinese, and sometimes illustrates it. He's a Clarkesworld regular whose work has also appeared in Asimov's, Analog, and F&SF. Come talk to him about anything, including but not limited to climate fiction, evolution, police states, propaganda, translation as an act of writing, digital art, Cintiq tablets, cinema, or his forthcoming novel A Killing in Souls.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Andy Dudak

schedule.desc: Come and learn how to play some traditional card games!
schedule.title: Learn to Play Traditional Card Games

schedule.desc: In many cases bringing a costume to life requires creating texture and depth in the design. From handmade lace to beading and embroidery to painting, fine detail work can be an incredibly compelling element to include in an ensemble. Join our panel of crafters to learn about some of these techniques and how they can be used to best effect when building a costume.
schedule.title: It's All in the Details

schedule.desc: “We are the Ghor!” In Andor’s second season, we were introduced to the Ghor language. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll get comfortable with the sounds of Ghor, interact with basic phrases, then learn the planetary anthem that resounded through Palmo Square. You’ll leave ready for drinks at a fancy cafhouse — or a march against Imperial tyranny!
schedule.title: Languages of Resistance: An Introduction to Ghor

schedule.desc: Robert J. Sawyer is a best-novel Hugo Award winner and a past Worldcon guest of honor. The ABC TV series FlashForward was based on his novel of the same name, and His nonfiction collection Sawyer on Science Fiction debuts this weekend. Rob loves hard SF (Clarke! Pohl! Niven!), classic Star Trek, dinosaurs, Planet of the Apes, pizza — and puns!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Robert J. Sawyer

schedule.desc: Margaret is a writer and producer of television, animation, interactive media, and short fiction who worked on shows like The Middleman, Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance, Batman: Caped Crusader, Marvel Rising, Barbie Dreamhouse Adventures, Octonauts: Above and Beyond, Bladerunner: Black Lotus, and The Lizzie Bennet Diaries. Stop by to geek out, talk about weird career paths, writing in multiple media and genres, or what it's like to try out for and appear on Jeopardy!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Margaret Dunlap

schedule.desc: Gail Carriger, author of The Parasol Protectorate series reads from her forthcoming unpublished book in that universe. Just a classic tale of girl meets boy. Girl sticks her tail in boy’s eye. Werewolf meets kumiho.
schedule.title: Reading: Gail Carriger

schedule.desc: This paper explores the intertextual relationship of queer Colombian author LC Barragán Castro's fiction and Sufi aesthetics. I argue for the relevance of Sufi writings to understanding gender and sexuality beyond a strictly “Islamicate” context, intervening against the asphyxiating specter of continental philosophy in the critique of Latin American writing
schedule.title: Islamic Aesthetics in works of LC Barragán Castro

schedule.desc: Two short films including a fun take on Doctor Who fandom, as two fans try to save their favorite show. The One-Minute Problem (USA). Feature: WHO-Ligans: The Lost Fandom (UK)
schedule.title: WHO-Ligans and other tales

schedule.desc: Come by and chat in a friendly, casual group. Chat about what? Honestly—almost anything. So if you want to talk about music—mine or other people’s, already released or yet to come, great! Ask how to write songs! Or why a scene is beautiful. If you’d rather talk who we think is the greatest scientist of all time, or want to know about my latest adventures, or new info on AI in the arts, or deep magic behind all music, also great! You can decide.
schedule.title: Table Talk: David Raiklen

schedule.desc: Eliane Boey, author of Club Contango will read from Small Bites, her feminist horror novella, forthcoming from Space Cowboy Books 11.11.26. Small Bites is about a mother who has lost her hunger, and her belief that she is, in fact, totally fine; until she locks herself in with a large spider, and learns to recapture what she lost, and feel her appetite return; but not before things get really weird first.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Eliane Boey

schedule.desc: Consonance, OVFF, FilKONtario, FilkCONtinental, and more… Fannish music has gained a lot of popularity and currently we have multiple filk conventions in different parts of the world. How did this genre music came to be and how was it from a single typo?
schedule.title: Filk Fandom, or The Story of a Typo

schedule.desc: Dr. Theresa Jean Tanenbaum ("Tess") is an ex-professor of interactive storytelling, a poet, author, composer, game designer, illustrator, anarchist, actual player, podcaster, and disabled neurospicy transgender witch activist. She makes music as Moth Mother. Join her to talk about play, story, music production, disability, mutual aid, magic, gender, Maya Deren, brewing homemade ink, resilience, and surviving the death throes of capitalism.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Tess Tanenbaum

schedule.desc: The annual Otherwise Award celebrates genre fiction that expands our understanding of gender. To raise money, comedian Sumana Harihareswara auctions off rare books, vintage collectibles, discounts at retailers, wacky experiences, and more! Watch the livestream, bid in the chat, pay online - or just come to laugh! We'll also offer a special virtual gift bag to anyone who donates any amount during the auction. A WisCon tradition comes to Worldcon.
schedule.title: Otherwise Award Charity Auction (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Whether fairy tales are ancient stories collected over the centuries, magical stories fabulated by a single author, or tales and traditions about the elusive beings who drift in and out of our world, all are a fertile field for reinvention. Let's talk about how and why we "fracture" fairy tales, offer examples, and discuss how these in turn inspire new streams in the ever-changing river of literature Beyond the Fields We Know.
schedule.title: Fracturing Fairy Tales

schedule.desc: Character designs in fantasy and sci-fi settings often don't take earthly (or human) comfort into account. Panelists will discuss their experiences with heavy items, limited visibility, difficult shoes, and other uncomfortable elements, focusing on how they have ensured wearing their fabulous costumes doesn't ruin their con.
schedule.title: How To Stay Comfortable In Your Cosplay Clothing

schedule.desc: Small Publishing in a Big Universe is a podcast by, for, and about people involved in small presses and independent publishing. We talk about writing craft, cover art and audiobooks, and the business side of storytelling. At events from book festivals to WorldCons, SPBU creates space for authors to connect with readers. Here at LACon, we’re inviting indie and small-press authors to share their far-reaching ideas and latest WorldCon discoveries.
schedule.title: Live Podcast: Small Publishing in a Big Universe

schedule.desc: Dungeons and Dragons (D&D) is most tabletop roleplaying game groups’ default ruleset, and it works well for a lot of cases, but it has a focus on fantasy and magic. How do other rulesets portray the same subject matter, and how do other rulesets let us play in other genres and settings? What are the benefits of branching beyond the d20? And how do you pick a ruleset for the game you want to play?
schedule.title: Beyond D&D: How Do Other Rulesets Enable Play?

schedule.desc: Eric Linus Kaplan is a writer and philosopher and co-founder of Kapknap Animation an independent comedy animation studio whose dystopian science fiction workplace comedy My Friend Coffee is debuting on youtube at Kapknap Animation. He wrote the infamous dog episode of Futurama and his science fiction novel The Legend of the Wolf Whale is coming out next year. Come by to talk about comedy, SF, the biz, co-operative models of artistic scene creation, Dasein -- what have you!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Eric Linus Kaplan

schedule.desc: There are plenty of Western alternate histories, but what about when the rest of the world starts rethinking major battles and historical figures? Come hear from authors who enjoy playing in the sandbox of history as they talk about what they changed and why.
schedule.title: Alternate Histories from Global Perspectives (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Language can supercharge worldbuilding in SFF and act as powerful inspiration when shaping worlds that feel vibrant. Join authors to celebrate how the presence of first languages bring texture, longevity, and imagination to fictional worlds—and why the enduring nature of these voices matter.
schedule.title: Indigenous Languages in SFF

schedule.desc:
Andrea Stewart is the Sunday Times bestselling author of The Drowning Empire Trilogy and The Hollow Covenant Trilogy, and the author of a forthcoming thriller. Come chat about any topic that piques your
interest - whether that's building a career in writing, writing in multiple genres, data and money, the craft, or birds, cats, and parenting while writing.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Andrea Stewart

schedule.desc: Fantasy worlds are often judged—and constrained—by the phrase “back in those days,” as if imaginary societies are obligated to reproduce the norms of historical cultures, European or otherwise. This panel challenges the idea that oppression equals realism, and examines how shaky historical assumptions shape worldbuilding.
schedule.title: Dragons, Magic, and Somehow Still Sexism?

schedule.desc: Come dance the night away with other teens!
schedule.title: Shake it Off: Teen Dance Party

schedule.desc: From the first convention in 1936 to the mega events of today, join us for a 90 year journey as we look at the history and evolution of fandom and conventions. From First Fandom and Worldcon to the comic cons, the rise of Trekkies and multimedia cons, all the way to the anime and furry cons, and the virtual cons run by bronies today. While cons have exploded in the last 90 years, we are all still one giant family tree influencing each other.
schedule.title: Celebrating 90 Years of Conventions

schedule.desc: Pacificon I, the 4th World Science Fiction Convention, was originally planned for 1942 in Los Angeles, but the U.S.A.'s entry into World War II delayed it until July 1946. That Pacificon began an unbroken chain of Worldcons that continues to this day. What impact did the Pacificon have on the post-war science fiction community? Join us as we bring this pivotal moment in SF history to life.
schedule.title: How The 1946 Pacificon Saved Post-War Worldcons

schedule.desc: Bert-Oliver Boehmer writes military science fiction, political intrigue, and classic space opera in his Galacticide universe. Join him to chat about causality, alien minds and civilizations, religion and politics in SF, believable future wars, worldbuilding, Battlestar Galactica, the future of humanity, or the strange places a twenty-four-century story can go.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Bert-Oliver Boehmer

schedule.desc: What is it about vampires that we just find irresistable? They can be anything from cuddly to horrifying in the role of romantic lead, and yet we just keep returning for more. Come hear our panelists discuss their influences and the choices they made in their own work.
schedule.title: Bites and Bloodstains: Vampires in Romantasy

schedule.desc: Cecilia Tan is the founder of Circlet Press, a pioneering publisher in erotic science fiction and fantasy, and the award-winning author of over 35 novels ranging from BDSM romances published by the Big 5 to queer time travel fantasy. An early adopter of self-publishing techniques, she will happily talk about subjects including crowdfunding, queer visibility, the challenges publishing erotic material, digital publishing, and making it work as an author in our current world.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Cecilia Tan

schedule.desc: Fandom is broad and expresses itself in different forms. Each of those come with certain types of accessibility challenges. We made a big progress around accessibility, but are still far from perfection. What are the issues that fans face in formal and informal groups, while reading fanzines, at conventions, and within other fannish activities? How we can avoid pitfalls, and how each of us can make fandom a more welcoming, and accessible space?
schedule.title: What Can We Do to Make Fandom More Accessible For Everyone?

schedule.desc: Most science fiction and fantasy authors say naming people, places, and things is one of their toughest tasks. Just how do you go about creating evocative names for your work of art? Join entertainment industry naming experts, including anthropologists, linguists, and storytellers, for a discussion of the best approaches.
schedule.title: What’s In A Name? Creating Names in SFF

schedule.desc: From hive minds to distributed consciousness, alternative methods of cognition fill the pages of science fiction. These panelists will talk about the ins and outs of thinking from a vastly different mindset and some of the best examples in literature today as well as different forms of thought you might not have even heard of yet.
schedule.title: Unity Says Hi: Alternative Cognition in SciFi

schedule.desc: S. Qiouyi Lu, author of biocyberpunk novella In the Watchful City, reads from Razing Babel, a sociolinguistic scifantasy novel in progress set in the same universe as Watchful.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: S. Qiouyi Lu

schedule.desc:
Brenda W. Clough, Nebula and Hugo Award finalist, reads from her 2026 SF novel Off the Screen.
Could American democracy become a more perfect union? Will AI kill off live acting and theater? And, most importantly, can Edwin Barbarossa write the opening number of the first original musical in thirty years, before opening night?
schedule.title: Reading: Brenda W Clough

schedule.desc: Jean-Paul L. Garnier, owner of Space Cowboy Books and author of Cardboard Spaceship, In Each Other's Arms, and many other science fiction books and speculative poetry collections, will be reading from his dystopian satire Garbage In, Gospel Out, as well as selections from his Laureate Award winning and Elgin nominated speculative poetry collection Entropocene. https://spacecowboybooks.com/
schedule.title: Reading: Jean-Paul L. Garnier

schedule.desc: Come share songs about your favorite aliens, beasts, and creatures - oh my! Real or mythical, land-based or sea-faring, furred or feathered or scaled or winged, terrestrial or alien, we want to hear all your fluffy, scary, cuddly, beastly songs!
schedule.title: Theme Filk: A-B-C (Aliens, Beasts, and Creatures)

schedule.desc: From secret societies and spectral encounters to street vigilantes and savage superstitions, discover how these Singaporean authors explore manifestations of rage in their stories.
schedule.title: What Rages Beneath: SFF From Singapore

schedule.desc: Kemi Ashing-Giwa, the bestselling, award-winning author of The Splinter in the Sky, This World Is Not Yours, and The King Must Die, reads from one of her books! (The choice will be up to y'all—I'll give brief descriptions of all three at the start.)
schedule.title: Reading: Kemi

schedule.desc: Erin Brown, author of horror, fabulist, and weird fiction, reads a few very short, charmingly creepy stories that explore the power and fun of the untrustworthy, unreliable narrator.
schedule.title: Reading: Erin Brown

schedule.desc: Filk music started out with people getting together in a circle in some random place at a convention to swap songs. We're official now and in a larger space, but it's still the same supportive tradition of sharing music together late into the night. All voices, instruments, and styles including a cappella welcome . Come by to sing or to listen!
schedule.title: Sunday Open Filk

schedule.desc: The Oasis is a calm, welcoming place where you can rest and recharge at your own pace. You don’t have to talk to anyone unless you want to. You’ll find simple activities like coloring, short readings, and self-care supplies. If you need something, just ask—we’re here to help.
schedule.title: The Oasis - Sunday

schedule.desc: Cameron Reed, the author of The Fortunate Fall and What We Are Seeking, reads from her upcoming third novel. In Courting Hellfire, every star system has its own afterlife and its own criteria for judging the dead. The crew of a small starship, whose fates are complicated by a variety of sins, will risk damnation to find the secret of eternal youth.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Cameron Reed

schedule.desc: Wes Rist is a former diplomat, int'l human rights lawyer, and space law, ethics, and policy nerd. He's worked on preventing mass atrocities around the world and on the future of space exploration's impact on humanity. Come join a conversation about speculative fiction’s ability to help us make a better world, how we understand the current world we’re in, and what we should be thinking about as we aim for a future among the stars.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: D. Wes Rist

schedule.desc: Miguel O. Mitchell, author of the Elgin Award-winning scifi novel-in-verse Surrealia, will read from his forthcoming book of speculative poetry Lounging with Strange and from some of his published SFF flash fiction.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Miguel O. Mitchell

schedule.desc: Interested in asexual representation in speculative fiction? Working with small traditional presses? Cowriting? Marketing your books? Attending and/or running writing retreats? All of this and more is on the (virtual) table when you chat with Marie Parks. She is the award-winning author of The Grigori Cycle supernatural thriller series and Flightless, a social justice fantasy heist. She also founded Sandia Starforgers Writers Workshops.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Marie Parks

schedule.desc: What pieces of media seem to have disproportionate nostalgia attached to them, and what should have been left behind by the march of time? What makes it hard to let it go, and why do some works get this level of love where others don't? Come voice your opinions in this virtual discussion circle!
schedule.title: Nostalgia: I Just Can't Quit You (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Rachel Hartman, author of Tess of the Road and two-time Lodestar Award finalist, will read from her most recent young adult fantasy novel, Among Ghosts.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Rachel Hartman

schedule.desc: S. M. Hallow reads from her debut novel The Halls of the Dead, a gothic horror romance between three necromancers on a revenge quest against a corrupt judge in 1849 London.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: S. M. Hallow

schedule.desc: Considering that you are all stars, meet at the hotel lobby for a leisurely 45-minute stroll around the venue. Get some fresh air, exercise, and chat with authors, editors, and artists in an informal setting. Hear about the interesting, fun, and maybe even unbelievable features of Anaheim.
schedule.title: Stroll with the Stars

schedule.desc: The kids are “CAN WE GO DO THE CONVENTION?!” But parents are like “IT IS SEVEN IN THE MORNING NOTHING IS OPEN AND I NEED COFFEE.” Grab that coffee and bring the kiddos down to the Children’s Program for a family-friendly morning of board games.
schedule.title: Family Board Games: Morning Edition

schedule.desc: Reuben "Tihi" Hayslett will be reading from his queer afro-futurist novel Orbital Bebop. Six interconnected stories spread across both centuries and the solar system, Orbital Bebop shows how the unresolved -isms and schisms will follow us to the Moon, Mars and the stars, while also giving a glimpse into what hope and social healing could look like hundreds of years from now. Join Tihi as he reads a passage where two long lost childhood best friends reunite on the Moon, on opposite sides of a corporate hierarchy.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Reuben "Tihi" Hayslett

schedule.desc: From pristine first‑edition paperbacks to rare prop replicas, hand‑painted minis, comic runs, cosplay builds, and the sacred shelf of limited‑edition collectibles, you have built a universe of your very own. But what happens to your SFF treasures when you journey to the Great Convention Hall in the Sky?
schedule.title: Planning the Fate of Your Geeky Collection After You’re Gone

schedule.desc: Brandon O'Brien is a speculative poet, science fiction writer, and tabletop game designer from Trinidad and Tobago, the author of the SFPA Elgin Award-winning poetry collection Can You Sign My Tentacle?, and the Poet Laureate of Seattle Worldcon. Come chat with them about poetry, TTRPG writing, their love of tea, and their undying fandom for the Japanese tokusatsu franchise Kamen Rider.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Brandon O'Brien

schedule.desc: This paper examines how two speculative films challenge the imperative to cure bodies deemed defective. Through Tobin Siebers's complex embodiment theory, I analyze how both narratives construct disability not as inherent flaw but as a verdict imposed by systems reducing worth to measurable code. Juxtaposing genetic with cybernetic determinism, this study shows how both films subvert the romanticization of cure.
schedule.title: Refusing Cure: Disability and Agency in SF Film

schedule.desc: Atlin Merrick is a volcano of encouragement shaped a lot like a person. She's also fiction editor at Improbable Press and dearly wants to answer your questions about getting published. How can you catch an editor's attention with your story or novel? (There's a secret editors DO want you to know!) Why are publishers fussy about the font you use? (There's two really good reasons!) Bring your questions and Atlin promises none, none, none are dumb.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Atlin Merrick

schedule.desc: Looking to learn how to keep your costumes looking their best? How about choosing the right materials for a costume that will be easy to clean? Need to clean difficult materials, or get some laundry and stain-fighting tips? Or maybe you need something to last, or to store costumes and keep them in tip-top shape. Whatever your needs, if you’re in the costuming space, this is the panel for you!
schedule.title: Care and Feeding of Costumes

schedule.desc: Among Los Angeles fandom of the 1940s were the well-known LGBTQ+ activists, journalist James Kepner and Edythe Eyde, aka Tigrina. He was a prominent and provocative fan, artist, and writer, and she, a lesbian who published one of the first newsletters for gay women. Join us to explore the life and impact of Kepner and Tigrina on early fandom.
schedule.title: Kepner and Tigrina: Pioneering LGBTQ+ Activism in LA Fandom

schedule.desc: William Frank is an attorney specializing in intellectual property, especially trademark and copyright. While he isn't YOUR attorney and can't give you legal advice, he can provide background education and entertainment on IP law, fandom, the experience of expatriate life in Japan (he lived in the eastern Kobe suburbs in 2014, working on secondment), the convention experience, closet cosplay, anime and JRPGs...you name it.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: William Frank

schedule.desc: From songs of praise to tales of tragedies, poetry has carried humanity through every civilization. It is one of the first oral artforms and continues to be a pillar of the literary and music worlds. It is only right that we learn how speculative poetry builds the foundations for world bulding both in literature and online. In this workshop, participants will read poems that expand our knowledge of person, place, and pursuits to learn how we can use this writing form to expand the worlds we're making. This writing workshop is for all levels.
schedule.title: Poetry as World Building: Poems as Foundations for Gaming and Beyond

schedule.desc: Klingon language expert Alan Anderson discusses the growing body of Klingon literature, including translated works, poetry, and original fiction.
schedule.title: Shakespeare in the Original Klingon: An Overview of Translated and Original Fiction

schedule.desc: From “Somewhere Over the Rainbow” to “My Shot,” the “I Want” song crystallizes a character’s driving desire. This panel explores how musical theatre uses these songs to reveal motivation, stakes, and emotional arcs (including when "I Want" shouldn't have) and what writers of prose, film, and games can learn from this powerful storytelling tool.
schedule.title: The Magic of "I Want" Songs: Musical Character Motivation

schedule.desc: Whether the romance is front and center or side plot, less spicy stories are blossoming in fantasy. Whether your characters care less about sex or are just cautious about jumping in the sack, sex doesn't have to be in your face. Explore how authors are navigating the increasing demand for these slower burn romances.
schedule.title: Swords and Slow Burns: Closed Door Romantasy

schedule.desc: A lot of the time science fiction looks forward, but what about changing the path of scientific development in the past to create an alternate now? This panel looks at literature that has decided to address possible alternate scientific histories to create a different kind of science fiction.
schedule.title: Alternative Scientific History in Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Jennifer Brozek is a multi-talented author, editor, and media tie-in writer whose nominations and awards include: multiple Bram Stoker nominations, a British Fantasy Award nomination, multiple Hugo nominations, multiple Scribe Awards, and an Australian Shadows Award. Talk to Jennifer as an author or an editor. Get your questions answered. Find out what catches her attention. This is a safe space for all.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Jennifer Brozek

schedule.desc: As discussions about identities grow, neurodivergent fantasy is reflecting this space. What are some books that showcase multiple facets of neurodivergence well? And what are some trends in the space?
schedule.title: Neurodivergence in Fantasy

schedule.desc: In this workshop, kids get to build their own dungeon romp with help from worldbuilders, songwriters, and teachers. We will go around the room and everyone will say one action they want to take. This workshop works like an old-style text adventure (think Adventure) or a modern day escape room, but it’s theater of the mind!
schedule.title: Dungeon Worldbuilding for Kids

schedule.desc: Scott Edelman is a multi-faceted writer, editor, and podcaster. His career spans writing and editing for Marvel and DC Comics, editing Science Fiction Age magazine (which put him on the Hugo ballot four times for Best Editor) and Science Fiction Weekly, SCI FI Wire and Blastr at the Syfy Channel for 13+ years, plus publishing 135+ short stories. His Eating the Fantastic podcast is a 2026 Hugo Award finalist. And he's ready to chat about it all!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Scott Edelman

schedule.desc: Speculative fiction has a long history of combining the fantastic with the political. This genre is anything but apolitical. Authors will discuss the political themes they explore on the page and how these themes impact identity.
schedule.title: Reading Is Political: SFF as Political Conversation (Virtual)
New and Indie Autographing: Julia Bianco

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss SF/F/H influences from classical and mainstream art, and how mainstream art has been influenced in turn.
schedule.title: SF/F/H Influences from Classical and Mainstream Art

schedule.desc: This workshop covers the basics every short story writer should know when they’re ready to start submitting stories for publication. How to find publications, what to expect in response, how to handle different kinds of responses, and what happens after acceptance. Practical, hands-on demonstrations. Leave empowered to give your stories the best possible opportunity for success.
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: The Practice of Short Story Submissions

schedule.desc: Learn to make a stellated eight sided shape, an octahedron, by folding paper! It's simple, but looks super impressive!
schedule.title: Learn to Make a Stellated Octohedron

schedule.desc: The panel will explore what makes monsters so appealing to modern audience How do we approach using or adapting classic horror monsters in our work? How do we create our own?
schedule.title: Modern Monsters

schedule.desc: Internationally-published author Jeremy Szal reads from his debut novel Stormblood, the first book in a space opera trilogy that is for fans of Mass Effect and Red Rising and alien drugs. This will be his first ever reading in the US as an author.
schedule.title: Reading: Jeremy Szal

schedule.desc: Bert-Oliver Boehmer reads from the opening episode of Goddess of the Galacticide, his weekly science fiction serial. Linuka Omga remembers erasing her father from existence to spring a trap on their enemy. But if the plan worked, why does she remember him at all? The answer may be terrifying, beautiful, or both.
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Bert-Oliver Boehmer

schedule.desc: We often look to the heroes and their journeys to discuss the power of fantasy, but in doing so we overlook the setting that makes them who they are. Nature is not a passive place where heroes fulfil their duty, but rather it is the crucible that shapes and makes heroes. Through an examination of the role of nature throughout the Arthurian canon it is possible to recognize the power that nature holds and what it means to the fantasy genre.
schedule.title: Understanding Our Place in Nature

schedule.desc: Andrea Stewart, author of The Drowning Empire Trilogy, reads from the first book in her soon-to-be complete epic fantasy trilogy, The Hollow Covenant, a story of two sisters on opposite sides of a clandestine war between the gods.
schedule.title: Reading: Andrea Stewart

schedule.desc: Bring out your inner Trekkie with this networked computer game experience! 6–8 players take control of the spaceship Artemis, assuming various crew jobs: Helm, Weapons, Science, Communications, Engineering, Fighter Pilot(s), and Captain. The ship’s missions require the crew to work together to overcome challenges such as combat, puzzle-solving, diplomacy, and exploration. An educational (space science) teambuilding experience!
schedule.title: Artemis Space Bridge Simulator (Monday)

schedule.desc: What if your cat could tell you where it hurts — or thank you for helping? Mary Robinette Kowal shares her five-year journey with Elsie, an 8-year-old calico with a 130-word vocabulary who uses Augmentative Interspecies Communication (AIC) to express grief, coin phrases like "laser bird," and even self-report an undiagnosed injury. Learn the science behind button communication and how to start this life-changing conversation with your own pet.
schedule.title: The Talking Cat Journey

schedule.desc: Our sibling relationships are, statistically, the longest, closest familial relationship people will have in their lives, but they also aren't relationships anyone involved consciously chose. This makes them ripe both as emotional battlegrounds for your characters and for connection, support, and reconciliation. This question can include blended and found families, and the resulting dynamics.
schedule.title: Siblings: The Long Relationship Your Characters Don't Choose

schedule.desc: Eugene Randolph Young is an illustrator, graphic designer, and Assistant Professor of Design Visualization in the School of Design at San Francisco State University. He is known for his Afromancers IP and independent science fiction and fantasy art inspired by indigenous lore, 80s cyberpunk, mechs, and 50s pin-up art. His research interests include paper acoustics and trends in mecha color schemes.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Eugene R Young

schedule.desc: Fantasy and mystery are two genres that have been intersecting as long as the genres have existed. Panelists explore fantasy and mystery pairings, while discussing what makes the perfect balance.
schedule.title: Murderous Dragons: Fantasy Mystery

schedule.desc: Ever noticed that yellow plastic looking film in a pile of mulch or on a tree? That is an organism called a slime mold. These impressive critters are adept hunters of tasty treats and have confounded scientists and inspired writers for years. Join our panel as we talk about what we know, what we suspect, and what we hope might be true about these cute little single-celled amoeboid organisms.
schedule.title: Too Cool to be a Fungus: Slime Molds for the Win

schedule.desc: Jared Pechaček is the author and illustrator of The West Passage and other weird things. Your one-stop shop to talk about medieval art, monsters, fantasy, fashion, and anything else that takes our collective fancy, including perhaps some chatter about upcoming books!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Jared Pechacek

schedule.desc:
Journey into the wilderness between ten intergalactic societies and search for the source of rumors about an impossibility: a broken column made of unbreakable material.

Game system: Spells of the Symphony
schedule.title: The Broken Column

schedule.desc: Violence and combat play an important role in many speculative fiction stories. But given that most of us have never been in a real fight, and many of us lack combat training, how can we write fight scenes honestly and accurately? Our panelists experienced in martial arts or combat will discuss physical conflict's role in a story as well as how to properly blend it across individual, tactical, and strategic layers.
schedule.title: Using Violent Conflict in your Writing

schedule.desc: If your beta reader, mom, or spouse reads your manuscript, gives you the side-eye and says "This is really creepy," this panel is for you. Though audiences might be fascinated, do we need more Hannibal Lecters or Freddys? Cautionary, cathartic, or titillating? Do writers have a responsibility to readers when creating horrific humans? How far is too far? Panelists discuss exploring the dark side of humanity through their characters and fiction.
schedule.title: Writing Your Creepy Serial-Killer (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Lin Codega is an author, journalist, and screenwriter. Most recently, they were the Writers’ Room Assistant for The Vampire Lestat (Interview With the Vampire Season 3). They’ve been covering fandom, tabletop roleplaying games, and SFF-adjacent stories for over ten years, and have two novels: Motheater and Pasha the Storm. Come chat about genre-bending books, games, collaborative writing, vampires, pirates, and unhinged television.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Lin Codega

schedule.desc: Writers who want to pursue a career often find lots of conflicting advice. MFAs are one option, but there are many types, varying quality, and not all welcome speculative fiction writers. Join our Special Guests, Tracey Baptiste (who teaches at an MFA program) and Terese Mason Pierre (who got an MFA in 2025) as they share their thoughts on the different MFAs available, especially ones that are helpful and friendly for genre writers.
schedule.title: Should Writers Get an MFA (Master of Fine Arts)?

schedule.desc: Broad Universe is an international, non-profit organization dedicated to promoting, encouraging, honoring, and celebrating women. Their work also ecompasses those of marginalized genders who have been historically excluded from fields writing, editing and publishing in science fiction, fantasy, horror, and other speculative genres. Come hear our members read from their works and find your next favorite author!
schedule.title: Broad Universe Rapid-Fire Reading: Come Hear Broads Read!

schedule.desc: Jane Chambers Awardee Diana Burbano reads an excerpt from her post-apocalyptic Latinx speculative play Policarpa: Apocalypse Sur Amerikka, a vision of resistance and survival in the ruins of empire.
schedule.title: Reading: Diana Burbano

schedule.desc: Many of us have games that we own that we have never gotten to the table. The panel discusses the nature of the aspirational game, whether that’s a huge board game we’ve never got the people together to play, a tabletop roleplaying game that you’ve never quite got around to reading, or a video game that you want to play but never quite find time to do so.
schedule.title: Aspirational Games (or the Shelf of Shame)

schedule.desc: Writers of historical fiction who understand paradigms outside of modern Western rationalism often blend fantasy with historical fiction to represent worldviews of past times. Historical fiction combined with science fiction includes categories such as gears and steampunk. Panelists will discuss successful blends of historical fiction with SFF elements, how it is evolving and who is doing interesting things with it.
schedule.title: Historical Fiction meets SFF

schedule.desc: Draw a card from Magic: The Gathering or the Pokémon Trading Card Game, or create your own card game.
schedule.title: Create a Playing Card

schedule.desc: Science fiction and fantasy clubs were a great way to gather local fans and support each other in fanning and fanac. Some still exist today, but many have closed. Let’s take a look at the present day clubs and their history. How do new clubs get formed now and what value do they bring to their members? Are there new roles for such clubs to fulfill?
schedule.title: Are SFF Clubs Relevant Today?

schedule.desc: Scientists answer your questions about their respective fields, the state of science in the world today, and more!
schedule.title: AMA: Ask Me Anything with Scientists (Virtual)

schedule.desc: From assassin dolphins in The Day of the Dolphin to cybernetically-enhanced bunnies in We3, science fiction and fantasy have often depicted animals engaged in human-style military conflicts. Given the long history in the real world of bomb-sniffing dogs, cavalry charges, and other use of non-sapient combattants, this panel will delve into the tactics, feasibility, and ethics of using non-sentient beings in SFF combat.
schedule.title: Battle Cattle: Animals In Military Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Zoe is an award-winning medievalist, writer, and professional game designer. In her spare time, she co-hosts The Maniculum Podcast, where she is dedicated to breaking down the anachronisms of modern medievalist fantasy and bringing the magic of the Middle Ages to life for storytellers, GMs, and creatives alike. She also mentors and provides resources to aspiring narrative designers looking to get into the craft and is excited to chat!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Zoe Franznick

schedule.desc: Fan Funds are fan community–supported travel grants that enable cultural exchanges by sending fans as ambassadors between different fannish communities. This panel explores the history and current state of Fan Funds, with past and present delegates speaking about their journeys and how those experiences shaped their lives and their relationship to fandom.
schedule.title: Fan Funds as an Experience

schedule.desc: From weathered detail painted on miniatures, to sculptural frames for paintings that enhance or expand the story told by the painting, to painted or printed fabric that’s used to make clothing or costumes, there are many ways to cross over between 2D and 3D art. What are your go-to techniques? What are you curious about trying?
schedule.title: Crossing the Streams: Combining 2D and 3D Art Techniques

schedule.desc: Panelists will share their expertise on all aspects of creating and sustaining a critique group, including how to find members, how to choose a critique group style, how to moderate, how to create an inclusive and supportive critique environment, and whether or not members are expected to read material before meeting. All the nuts and bolts!
schedule.title: How to Set Up and Run a Critique Group

schedule.desc: Patricia McCracken is a long time fantasy artist of Japanese inspired watercolors having sold paintings and prints in convention art shows all over the country. While raising a family, she also managed to write and illustrate a book about, of all things, watercolor painting. Come join her to talk about watercolor painting, anything art related, being an author, self-publishing a book from start to finish, or just come on by and let’s chat.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Patricia McCracken

schedule.desc: Arley is an associate literary agent with kt literary and a senior editor at Locus Magazine. He is a two-time World Fantasy finalist, three-time Locus Award finalist for co-editing Fantasy Magazine. He does book reviews for Lightspeed, interviews for Clarkesworld, has a column with F&SF, and more. He has taught at Clarion West, critiqued for Odyssey, and been featured at many other programs. He also loves travel and food… but he’s vegetarian!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Arley Sorg

schedule.desc: It takes a lot of work to bring an idea to life and these panelists are here to tell you how to navigate that adventure. Learn how to take your ideas and turn them into books ready to share! (This panel is for teens)
schedule.title: From Idea to Book: A Realistic Guide for Teen Creators

schedule.desc: Some of the best speculative fiction out there imbues its setting with an attitude and personality all of its own. How do they accomplish this with and without going full AI? What are the best examples, and how can we apply it to our own work? Join these authors as they talk about the least lauded character: Place.
schedule.title: Ships and Cities with Attitude: Place as Character

schedule.desc: Take a last-minute field trip with Vanessa MacLaren-Wray, author of Shadows of Insurrection and Flames of Attrition. Step into a bizarre situation, one not at all inspired by real-world events, where a cabal of power-hungry lying patriarchists are working to overthrow a stable, balanced, matriarchal system. Can a reluctant general, a displaced accountant, and one or two Prime Directive violations foil the fake shamans’ evil plans?
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Vanessa MacLaren-Wray

schedule.desc: The age of women characters in fiction used to mostly skew young or old, with heroines in their prime making up the minority. This trend has reversed in recent years, as middle-aged protagonists have become increasingly popular in fiction. Panelists will discuss how middle-aged women have been portrayed throughout literary history, and how and why this representation has been changing in more contemporary works.
schedule.title: Bless Your Heart: Middle Aged Women as Epic Adventurers (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Egalitarianism is an ideal fandom aspires to, where fan spaces are open to everyone and everyone is an equal. Yet, we all know fandom often misses that mark. Panelists will discuss the unequal realities within fandom, and steps we can all take to make these spaces into more equal and welcoming places.
schedule.title: Is Fandom Really Egalitarian?

schedule.desc: Join us for an improvisational storytelling session: a round-robin where panelists build off what others in the panel have said, started by prompts from the audience.
schedule.title: An Improvisational Storytelling Session

schedule.desc: Gargoyles and grotesques have been a source of worldwide fascination for thousands of years. And yet, gargoyles in pop culture tend to be only side characters, playing bit parts in other heroes' stories. What does our enduring need for stone sentries reveal about our collective imagination and the stories we tell ourselves? And what tales would gargoyles tell if they were allowed to narrate? Is it time for more gargoyle futures?
schedule.title: Where my Gargoyles At? Giving Sidekicks Center Stage

schedule.desc: What does it mean to “create community” in a class where no one is ever in the room? This paper explores “podcast pedagogy” as an alternative to the sterile architectures of asynchronous online education. Rather than delivering information, the podcast format invites students into an unfolding dialogue that privileges curiosity and the lived process of collaborative thinking and understanding.
schedule.title: Reimagining Presence in Asynchronous Learning

schedule.desc: Panelists will discuss the nitty-gritty of writing proposals for grants and funding outside of the publishing world. How to focus your proposal, what language to use or avoid, what research to do first, and other elements.
schedule.title: Requesting Grants & Applying for Funding

schedule.desc:
Getting some herbs and spices sounds like a milk run. No big deal, they are offering you a fair amount of cred. What’s the worst that could happen? Join us playing this legendary game!

Character sheets, dice and pencils provided.
schedule.title: Shadowrun: Top Shelf Seattle

schedule.desc: Many TTRPG supplements exist to help us play our favorite stories at the table, but what if you want to play a story that nobody’s adapted? Bring your favorite work—short story, novel, TV episode, movie, or video game—and we’ll explore how to deconstruct it and play it at the table.
schedule.title: Playing Our Favorite Stories

schedule.desc: The majority of songs out there tell some kind of story but in far fewer words than even a short story. How do songwriters get their stories across succinctly and clearly in a way that interests the listener? Where do their ideas come from? Our songwriter panelists will share their processes for crafting well-told and memorable stories in songs.
schedule.title: Creating a Story in Song

schedule.desc: Every journey into space starts long before launch. It begins with imagining worlds beyond our own, continues through the breakthroughs that make exploration possible, and culminates with the teams who deliver missions across the solar system. Our guests discuss imagination and discovery, examining how vision, innovation, and execution shape the future of spaceflight, inspire those who pursue it, and influence the stories yet to be told.
schedule.title: From Storytelling to Spaceflight and Back Again

schedule.desc: From Shelley’s seminal creation to current depictions exploring feminism, transness, fatness, and deviation from Western beauty standards, monsters have served as stand-ins for bodies and souls that violate social norms and moral boundaries. Why is disability associated with morality? Whose body gets to be "right?" And why are cis and trans women kicking so much butt in the body horror subgenre right now?
schedule.title: Still More Monstrous: Monsters And the Transgressive Body

schedule.desc: Zain Memon, game designer and transmedia creator, reads from his forthcoming epic science-fantasy novel MAYA: Seed Takes Root. "A book of extraordinary riches, it offers provocative philosophical nuggets wrapped in a narrative both sweeping and immersive." - Anil Seth
schedule.title: Virtual Reading: Zain Memon

schedule.desc: Hugo and Nebula winner John Chu reads from his debut novel The Subtle Art of Folding Space. Unhinged physics in disrepair! Status reports in the form of egg tarts and soy-and-ginger glazed tilapia! Daily assassination attempts! Unreasonable parental expectations! Come and find out what I'm talking about.
schedule.title: Reading: John Chu

schedule.desc: Three short films based on the works of Howard Waldrop: The Ugly Chickens, Mary Margaret Road Grader, and Night of the Cooters. Waldrop was a Guest of Honor at Loscon 46 in 2019 and was honored with the World Fantasy Award for Life Achievement in 2021. The films were produced by Waldrop's close friend, George R.R. Martin, and released in 2024.
schedule.title: Howard Waldrop Films (produced by George R.R. Martin)

schedule.desc: The reader letters published Amazing Stories, reveal a wealth of popular visions of science and society from a time of great political and social upheaval. I argue that the roots of today’s world—from the present-day aesthetic of science, to the ubiquity of science fiction, and the modern tech industry’s fixation on speculation-driven growth—can be found in the 1920s and 30s through the readers, not the fiction, of Amazing Stories.
schedule.title: The New Popular Science of Amazing Stories

schedule.desc: Gabrielle is a multiple Audie Award winning narrator of audiobooks. She is known for her dexterity with characters and accents, and her instinctual talent at midwifing author intent. Sit back for a few minutes and let her take you to a sampling of the worlds she has created on audio for the likes of authors such as Ursula LeGuin, Virginia Woolf and C.L. Moore.
schedule.title: Reading: Gabrielle de Cuir

schedule.desc: If you identify as a person with a disability, please join other fans who do as well for this meetup.
schedule.title: Meetup: People With Disabilities

schedule.desc: Technology has always fascinated fandom. At first, the internet was going to save the world and connect us all. Has it? Did it? Maybe. But it's also full of bad user interfaces, obnoxious ads, and social media influencers. AI was fascinating until it was here, and messy, and we discovered it feeds on ugly datacenters. Quantum is coming. Come explore science fiction and fandom's ever-changing views of technology.
schedule.title: Fannish Views of Technology: Good, Bad, and In-Between

schedule.desc: Since early years of fandom, fans were recognizing others who contributed to the community. It have taken many forms – from being audience of someone’s fanac, through Fan Awards, to inviting fans as Guests of Honors. What is the importance of doing so? And do we recognize others enough?
schedule.title: Why Do We Need Fannish Recognition?

schedule.desc:
The Skiffy and Fanty Show is a four-time Hugo-finalist fancast and blog focusing on SFF, including reviews, interviews, and discussions.
LACon V says "Dare to Discover, Dare to Explore, Dare to be Uncharted!" Early SF’s discovery, exploration, and charting focused on outer space. Now, many interesting explorations in speculative fiction are about what it means to be human, or sentient, plus how we're transforming ourselves. What will we become?
schedule.title: Live Podcast: The Skiffy and Fanty Show- Strange New Selves!

schedule.desc: Scary stories distract us from the horrors of the world, and also help us process them. Writing and art are channels for the creator's trauma as well as the audience's, and also joyful distractions from it. Is there a line between entertainment and real trauma? What about the popularity of the True Crime genre? How dark is too dark?
schedule.title: Trauma vs Entertainment

schedule.desc: Join Eugene Young for A Song of Carbon & Water: The Magic of Water Soluble Graphite. Part presentation, part demonstration, and part workshop: you will learn the intriguing properties of the medium and how to incorporate it into your own art.
schedule.title: A Song of Carbon & Water

schedule.desc: Annalee Newitz, author of the Hugo finalist novella Automatic Noodle and editor-in-chief of Starlog, reads from their forthcoming sapphic slime mold novel A Wall Is Also a Road.
schedule.title: Reading: Annalee Newitz

schedule.desc: Panelists first will plunge into the pit by defining what is meant by "traditional," as most languages other than English have a variety of pronouns, not just for gender, plural, formal and informal, but for levels of society--and in ancient times certain people were not permitted a pronoun at all. Panelists will look at various pronouns that have been used and discarded in SFF and discuss gendered pronouns, non-gendered pronouns, and how writers might invent new forms--while creating cultures in which to fit them.
schedule.title: Non-Traditional Pronouns in SF and Fantasy

schedule.desc: Over the years, many fans have dreamed of becoming pro writers, artists, game designers, or other. The dream is still alive, and fulfilling it doesn't have to mean having to stop being a fan. How do pros keep up their fannish activities after going pro? In what ways can pros help out fandom? Let's discuss the ways and means of balancing the two.
schedule.title: From Fan to Pro and Back Again

schedule.desc: Evolution is a favorite tool of science fiction writers even though its results are so hard to predict. This panel explores literature that uses Darwinian theories to create aliens, monsters, and more!
schedule.title: But Why Not Radial Symmetry? Evolution in Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Writing advice often comes with an assumed "standard" of the writer: long periods sitting at a desk, hyper-focus, a routine and predictable process. Authors with disabilities know that isn't always how it goes. Let's discuss craft, access, process, and adaption for authors with disabilities.
schedule.title: The Writer's Life: Authors with Disabilities

schedule.desc: John Scalzi has absolutely no idea what he's going to read! He'll be almost as surprised as you will! Come anyway!
schedule.title: Reading: John Scalzi

schedule.desc: There is a lot of speculation going on in the WHOniverse right now. Join other fans of the Doctor in all their incarnations for a lively and fun discussion.
schedule.title: Geek Out About: Doctor Who

schedule.desc: Braid or weave a friendship bracelet using floss or yarn
schedule.title: More Friendship Bracelets

schedule.desc: Speculative romance revolves around the relationships people foster, not only romantically, but also familialy, socially, and politically. Stories about love have a long history of illustrating themes of resistance because those connections between people are often the first thing targeted by those who seek to control. Join our panelists for a discussion on romantasy and resistance.
schedule.title: Love Freely: Romantasy as Resistance

schedule.desc: Space is populated with a LOT of old satellites, broken satellites, and other debris, but no one is taking responsibility. The panel discusses what dangers are posed by this debris, who is paying attention, what we can do about it, and who is trying.
schedule.title: Junk in Space: What will we do with all the dead satellites?

schedule.desc: 19 years ago, singer/songwriter Janelle Monae released the EP "Metropolis Chase Suite." This began a six year journey through the story of Cindi Mayweather. Much like ancient epics -- The Epic of Gilgamesh, The Illiad, and The Odyssey -- this collection of musical poems recounts the extraordinary feats of metahumans amongst mortals. In this poetry writing and listening workshop: we'll go through the songs that drive the overall narrative of the Metropolis Chase Suite, analyze literary devices, asses Monae's creative decisions behind the hip hopera, and use writing prompts to develop first ideas for the modern poetry epic.
schedule.title: Gilgamesh, Odyssey, and Janelle Monae's Chase Suite

schedule.desc: Who doesn't like a romantic storyline? Come learn how to add romance to your writing from the first kiss and beyond. Whether you are writing Romantasy or Horror, learn to include romance that works for your genre and isn't too spicy to bring to your creative writing class at school. (This workshop is for teens)
schedule.title: Kiss and Tell: Writing Romance for Teens

schedule.desc: The rise of punk genres and stories is escalating in a delightful way, but what makes a story punk? What are the different punk subgenres? These panelists love to play in the punk landscape and are here to share what they think makes punk special.
schedule.title: Punk Me Up! Cyber, Steam, and Other Punks

schedule.desc: Michelle Witte is a literary agent with Mansion Street Literary Management. Michelle works with speculative fiction for all ages, though she has a soft spot for children's literature and loves working with author-illustrators. She is the author of The Craptastic Guide to Pseudo-Swearing and Happy Little Accidents: The Wit and Wisdom of Bob Ross. Come chat about books, writing, publishing, or any random tangent that the conversation takes us to.
schedule.title: Virtual Table Talk: Michelle Witte

schedule.desc: NASA’s whirlybird set to explore Titan is expected to launch in 2028. It will fly through the smoggy nitrogen-rich atmosphere, making periodic stops to sample the surface with its onboard geochemical lab. Heat from a radioisotope will recharge its batteries between flights, and keep its brain warm. Come and learn why scientists think Titan is such a fascinating place and a key location for studying prebiotic chemistry.
schedule.title: Dragonfly Over Titan: NASA’s Octocopter

schedule.desc: Autonomous drones, missile-destroying lasers, and other technological marvels have made the battlefield more complicated than ever. What might the depiction of military technology in science fiction tell us about what's next in the evolution of combat? Our panelists explore the near future of warfare and the role of science fiction in imagining it.
schedule.title: Near Future Warfare: Robots, AI, and Space Lasers!

schedule.desc: A panel discussion on the most interesting music videos telling SFFH stories. SFFH TV shows and movies are frequently recognized as part of the cultural zeitgeist and receive significant accolades come awards season. Why aren't music videos given the same attention when the production value and storytelling in music videos is just as impressive as feature film?
schedule.title: Music Videos Telling SFFH Stories

schedule.desc: Catherine Lucille Moore was an American speculative fiction author who started her career in the 1930s with a prolific publishing career that heavily influenced the science fiction and fantasy of the day. Why has Indiana’s genre pioneer been overlooked, and how do we reclaim her legacy?
schedule.title: C.L. Moore: The Midwest’s Queen of Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Seanan McGuire writes things. She likes to talk about them. She also likes things. She likes to talk about those, too. Come talk to Seanan. She may show you pictures of her cats. She will ask to see pictures of yours (if you have them).
schedule.title: Table Talk: Seanan McGuire

schedule.desc: First? Second? Third? Cinematic? Omniscient? Limited? Direct Address? Before you can begin to tell your story, you need to decide how to tell it. This crucial decision has important implications throughout the writing process since different points of view offer unique challenges and opportunities. This presentation will pass quickly over theory to hacks, tricks, checklists and other useful tips to staying on point when you’re narrating.
schedule.title: Clarion Presents: Your Guide to No Problem Point of View

schedule.desc: If you're a fan of Mary Robinette Kowal (MRK), you almost certainly know about Elsie the Cat. Elsie is MRK's 7-year-old calico cat, who has a 130-word vocabulary and uses Augmentative Interspecies Communication (AIC) to express herself. Join this meetup with Elsie and Mary Robinette! NOTE: This item will require a 10 minute walk to Elsie's hotel from the ACC North.
schedule.title: Meetup: Elsie the Talking Cat

schedule.desc: Colleen Doran, cartoonist, illustrator, and long time writer about the business of art making, with thousands of subscribers. Clear eyed discussions about contracts, money, funding, and whether or not student loans are worth the price. Let’s talk.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Colleen Doran

schedule.desc: Pokemon, Star Wars, Harry Potter, and Disney are some of the highest earning franchises of all time. Join us as we break down their paths to commercial success, perfect merch, and theme park lands. Explore more similarities between them than just the Hero’s Journey, Chosen Ones, and Dark Lords. Whether you like them or not, franchises are here to stay, so let's explore some of them in depth, and maybe get inspired to create your own media empire.
schedule.title: Storytelling in the Age of Franchise: Mechanics for Making a Hit Franchise

schedule.desc: Kemi Ashing-Giwa is an author, grad student, amateur kazooist, and shortbread enthusiast from Southern California. She writes multicultural queer science fantasy, often with a dash of horror. Her books include The Splinter in the Sky, This World Is Not Yours, and The King Must Die. Come chat about writing and publishing, favorite media, zines, science (I study mass extinctions and why they're worse for some species than others), cooking/baking, and honestly anything else!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Kemi

schedule.desc: Charlie Jane Anders reads from her upcoming novel Good Things Are Coming Your Way, about time travel, vampires and true love
schedule.title: Reading: Charlie Jane Anders

schedule.desc: Winning films from this year's film festival will be shown. (Note that not all films may be able to be shown.)
schedule.title: LACon Film Festival Winners Block

schedule.desc: Join our language workshop where you will hear an overview of the creation of the Dothraki and High Valyrian languages from A Game of Thrones, and also learn to speak a few words and phrases.
schedule.title: Rytsas! Learn "Hello" and More in High Valyrian and Dothraki

schedule.desc: Playing tabletop and card games
schedule.title: Game Time

schedule.desc: Panelists experienced with fiber arts discuss how they enrich stories already published. Who gets it right? For writers, how have they used fiber arts in their writing? What are some interesting avenues to learn about fiber arts for writers interested in this aspect of worldbuilding?
schedule.title: Fiber Arts in SF/F Fiction (Virtual)

schedule.desc: All members of the Silicon Web Costumers' Guild chapter of the International Costumers' Guild are welcome to come by, see each other in person, and have a little chat! Non-members are welcome if they are curious about our group and would like to learn more. Members of other chapters of the ICG are also welcome to stop by.
schedule.title: Meetup: Silicon Web Costumers' Guild

schedule.desc: Terese will read speculative poetry from her collection, "Myth," and an excerpt from her short story in the anthology, "As The Earth Dreams."
schedule.title: Reading: Terese Mason Pierre

schedule.desc: We're living in "interesting" times: between climate change, political upheavals, pandemics, AI, and, soon, quantum computing, what's a fan to do? How do we talk about this time of polycrisis? For example, do we prioritize political action or climate action, or try to make whatever we do do double duty? Is this as bad as it feels? How can we frame our thinking to pull a positive future that we want to live in out of these troubling times?
schedule.title: Polycrisis: Living Through Many Challenges At Once (Virtual)

schedule.desc: Fan communication began with fanzines and letters of comment, then evolved through in-person discussion at conventions, and then evolved again through the availability of the Internet, which brought mailing lists and forums, and now social media and podcasts. How do we communicate now? Do the "old ways" still work?
schedule.title: From Fanzines to Social Media – How Fans Communicate

schedule.desc: Bridget is an art addict, space painter, nature nut, mad gamer, and world traveler with no hope for recovery! Been an airbrush beach artist, ad agency A.D., plein aire painter, surviving Hollywood 46 years flinging paint on sets with fog machines, lights glaring, trap doors, wild animals, dancers kicking, singers crooning, & actors fighting, scenery crashing, and lived! Worked Heroes, AHS, Parks & Rec, Good Place, & more! Come tickle my brain!
schedule.title: Table Talk: Bridget Duffy

schedule.desc: From Shelley’s seminal creation to current depictions exploring feminism, transness, fatness, and deviation from Western beauty standards, monsters have served as stand-ins for bodies and souls that violate social norms and moral boundaries. Why is disability associated with morality? Whose body gets to be "right?" And why are cis and trans women kicking so much butt in the body horror subgenre right now?
schedule.title: Still More Monstrous: Monsters And the Transgressive Body (Virtual)

schedule.desc: How can using games potentially help kids to work out both physical and mental health issues going on with their lives?
schedule.title: Do Games Help Kids to Work Out Issues?

schedule.desc: Molly is a fantasy writer and engineering geologist, and the author of Greenteeth and Nightshade and Oak. Join her to talk about folklore, rocks, science in fantasy and fiction, construction, writing with spreadsheets, the wilds of Australia and the UK, having far too many hobbies, or to see photos of her foster kittens.
schedule.title: Table Talk: Molly O'Neill

schedule.desc: Neopaganism reveres the Triple Goddess, often described as the Maiden, the Mother, and the Crone. In some literary contexts, becoming a crone is marked with discontent, fear, loss, and anger, as well as interpersonal conflict between the crone, maiden, and mother. Where in literature is the crone accurately portrayed and explored? In what ways can becoming a crone be shaped differently than before?
schedule.title: Becoming the Crone
Virtual Table Talk: David Ian Salter

schedule.desc: We all know history is written by the victor, but what if the other side had won? Whether it’s a war, a technological race, or even the pie contest from 50 years ago, we can’t stop theorizing and writing about that other possibility.
schedule.title: But What if the Other Side Won? Alternate Histories

schedule.desc: Anuja Varghese, award-winning writer of literary fiction, fantasy, and erotica/romance where women of color get leading roles, reads from her debut medieval India-inspired romantasy A Kiss of Crimson Ash! D&D quest meets Bollywood love story (but make them queer!) in this first book in the Games of the Goddess trilogy.
schedule.title: Reading: Anuja Varghese

schedule.desc: Hugo and Nebula award winning writer James Patrick Kelly will be reading a robot story from his new collection The Book Of Bots.
schedule.title: Reading: James Patrick Kelly

schedule.desc: Barbara will read the first 25 minutes’ worth of a story she wrote back in 1996 for the Star Wars Adventure Journal, “Murder in Slushtime” – a Star Wars murder-mystery (centering on the love-lives of the Gamorrean Pig Guards). Or, if the audience prefers, she can read the first 25 minutes’ worth of the next Asher-Ysidro vampire novel, Nightfall’s Servants, due out next year. She regrets that she does not write anything much shorter than this.
schedule.title: Reading: Barbara Hambly

schedule.desc: David D. Levine, author of Nebula-winning novel Arabella of Mars and Hugo-winning short story "Tk'Tk'Tk," reads from his novel Vaudevaliens, a story about aliens on Broadway in 1910, which (at this writing) is currently seeking a publisher.
schedule.title: Reading: David D. Levine

schedule.desc: Do you look for hidden items, references, or characters in games, movies or elsewhere? For example, there are the hidden areas in Mario games, games where the player must look for the changes from one photo to the next or find all the items hidden within an image. Do you look for hidden images in Disney movies that relate to other movies? If so, this panel is for you!
schedule.title: Looking for "Easter Eggs" in Games, Movies, or Elsewhere?

schedule.desc: All good things must come to an end and sadly LAcon V must finish, although Worldcon goes on. That ending will come on Monday afternoon when we say goodbye to our Guests, say many thank-yous for all the contributions made, and share highlights of the convention and any final outcomes of votes held.
schedule.title: Closing Ceremony

schedule.desc: Sometimes the intro is longer than the song, or a performer feels compelled to sing all 27 verses to an epic musical tale. Not here! Each performer has two minutes or less (there will be a timer) to share their very short song, or just their favorite verse & chorus of a longer song if they like, no intro necessary! Also known as the "short attention span" circle, it will be friendly to younger performers.
schedule.title: Theme Filk: Short and Sweet!

schedule.desc: Before you start on your next adventure, come wish Fuzzy, our frazzled con mascot, a job well done by sharing music and camroderie late into the night before saying good bye. All voices, instruments, and styles including a cappella welcome. Come by to sing or to listen!
schedule.title: Monday Frazzled Fox Filk
